explanations.title: Speaking (Activities 8 and 9)
explanations.body: Scenario: you just bought a few items. Say 3 to 5 expressions with ang and kay, for example Ang mahal naman ng medyas!, then ask your partner the price of 2 to 4 items (Magkano ang medyas? / Isandaang piso ang medyas. / Ang mahal naman!). Guided Q and A, Dialog A: say you would like two towels; B asks the color; A asks for red and white; B says yes; A asks if they accept a credit card; B says no, only cash; A asks the cost; B says it. Dialog B: A asks if an item can be returned and why; B says yes and asks for a receipt; A shows it; B asks the size; A says the size and asks the cost; B says the price is the same and says the amount. Use honorifics such as kuya, ate, nanay, sir and ma’am.

explanations.title: Self-evaluation for Chapter 4
explanations.body: Check that you can: extract information about school supplies, clothes and accessories and shopping; transcribe and translate sentences and numbers about them; enumerate school supplies, clothes and accessories; ask and answer simple questions about them; use common shopping expressions; and buy and exchange items at the store. You should understand intensified adjectives with Set I and Set II markers, the enclitics na, pa, ba and lang, moderative adjectives, the prefix pang, exclamatory adjectives with ang and kay, the enclitic naman, location markers and the Set III personal pronouns.

explanations.title: Culture note: pasalubong
explanations.body: Pasalubong is the Filipino tradition of travelers bringing gifts from their destination to people back home. It can be any gift or souvenir for family or friends after being away for a period of time, or any gift given by someone arriving from a distant place. It is also associated with the balikbayan, overseas Filipinos returning to the Philippines, and may refer to items that migrant workers bring home to their families, friends, relatives, or even non-relatives they feel especially close to.

explanations.title: Notes
explanations.body: Pasalubong is a variant of pansalubong, from the root salubong, “to welcome”, “to meet”, “reception”. The prefix pa is short for pan/pang, roughly equivalent to the English suffix “-er”. Tumatanggap, umorder, pumili, bumili and tumawad are um verbs (see the grammar lessons). lessons.title: 82. C5 L1 · Um verbs: intransitive and transitive, and their tenses
lessons.subtitle: bumili, bumibili, bibili · tumanggap · pumili · umalis · umuwi

explanations.title: Um verbs
explanations.body: Um verbs are doer-focus verbs, just like mag verbs. Root words that take mag as a prefix can also take um; sometimes there is no difference in meaning, and sometimes there is (discussed in a future lesson). An intransitive verb does not require a direct object, a transitive verb does. English examples: I go home at 5:30 every day (intransitive); Imelda bought a fan (transitive).

explanations.title: How to conjugate
explanations.body: When the root begins with a consonant, um is infixed (inside the word): bili, bumili. The infinitive and the past tense have the same form (bumili). The future takes no affix and repeats the first syllable of the root (bibili). The present takes the affix and repeats the first syllable (bumibili). For roots beginning with a vowel, um goes in front: alis, umalis (infinitive and past), umaalis (present), aalis (future). Pawatas = infinitive, pangnakaraan = past, pangkasalukuyan = present, panghinaharap = future.

explanations.title: Sentences with um verbs
explanations.body: Intransitive: the doer follows the verb, with a prepositional phrase and time expression. Transitive: the Set II marker ng precedes the direct object (Humingi si Nanding ng resibo sa tindera).

explanations.title: Set III demonstratives
explanations.body: In the previous lesson personal pronouns replaced proper nouns. The names of places can also be replaced by demonstratives; these are the Set III demonstratives, or sa demonstratives, in English adverbs of place. Rito, riyan and roon are used in specific Tagalog regions; dito, diyan and doon are the common ones, but grammatically, the forms that start with d must be used at the beginning of a sentence or phrase (Dito ka dumaan).

rows: here (at this place, near the speaker)

there (at that place, far from both)

examples.text: Sige po, sir. Salamat po.
examples.translation: Woman: All right, sir. Thank you.

explanations.title: At a foreign exchange outlet (Activity 8, the book’s script)
explanations.body: Key: the man wants to exchange his dollars for pesos; the rate is ₱46.50 per dollar; the total is ₱93,000.00.

examples.text: Ma’am, magkano po ba ang palitan ng dolyar?

examples.text: Salamat po, ma’am.
examples.translation: Man: Thank you, ma’am.

examples.text: Walang anuman. Hanggang sa muli po.
examples.translation: Woman: You’re welcome. Until next time.

explanations.title: Speaking (Activities 9 and 10)
explanations.body: Dialog A at a store: A asks if they have a mestiza dress or terno; B says yes; A asks how much; B says the price; A asks if a credit card or check can be used; B apologizes and says the store accepts only checks. Dialog B: A asks what the best souvenir is; B says an embroidered handkerchief; A says he wants a dozen; B says they have it; A asks the price; B says it; A says it is very expensive, using the ang/kay expression. Activity 10 on R&R: A asks if they do foreign currency exchange; B says yes; A asks the rate; B says it; A says how many dollars to exchange; B gives the total in local currency; A thanks the clerk; B says no problem.

explanations.title: Getting started
explanations.body: The book opens with a mind map of bank transactions (mag-encash ng traveler’s check, mag-withdraw ng cash) and asks what types of bank transactions you will make in the Philippines (the mind map is left out).

explanations.title: Dialog A: a man transacts business at the bank

examples.text: Ma’am, puwede bang mag-encash ng Amerikanong traveler’s check dito?
examples.translation: Man: Ma’am, can I cash a U.S. traveler’s check here? (the book prints “U.S.”)

examples.text: Siyempre po, puwedeng-puwede po.
examples.translation: Woman: Of course, definitely.

examples.text: Magkano ang service fee n’yo?
examples.translation: Man: How much is your service fee?

examples.text: Limang porsiyento po ng halaga ng tseke.
examples.translation: Woman: Five percent (5%) of the value of the check.

examples.text: Ang laki naman!
examples.translation: Man: How big (exorbitant)!

explanations.title: Dialog B: a woman transacts business at the bank

examples.text: Mag-e-encash po ako ng Amerikanong traveler’s check. Ano po ang mga kailangan?
examples.translation: Woman 1: I will cash a U.S. traveler’s check. What are the requirements?

examples.text: Kailangan po ang orihinal na resibo, isang valid ID, at kopya ng pasaporte n’yo.
examples.translation: Woman 2: The original receipt, a valid ID and a copy of your passport are required.

examples.text: Eto po ang resibo, ID, at xerox ng pasaporte ko.
examples.translation: Woman 1: Here are my receipt, ID and a photocopy of my passport.

examples.text: Kailangan n’yo pong magbayad ng service fee.
examples.translation: Woman 2: You need to pay a service fee.

examples.text: Magkano po?
examples.translation: Woman 1: How much?

examples.text: Dose porsiyento po ng halaga ng tseke.
examples.translation: Woman 2: Twelve percent (12%) of the value of the check.

examples.text: Ang mahal naman!
examples.translation: Woman 1: How expensive!

explanations.title: Notes
explanations.body: In Dialog A, mag-cash out is a synonym of mag-encash; the book’s teacher note also mentions other uses of mag-cash out, for example choosing between a material prize and converting the prize to cash. Ang laki naman! and Ang mahal naman! mean “How exorbitant!”. Ano po ang mga kailangan (literally “What are the needs?”) means “What are the requirements?”. Filipinos widely use “xerox” to mean “photocopy”: Mag-xerox ka ng limang kopya (Make five copies). In the spoken lines here “U.S.” is written Amerikanong.

explanations.title: Mag verbs
explanations.body: Like um verbs, mag verbs can be transitive or intransitive: (1) transitive verbs require a direct object, (2) intransitive verbs do not, and (3) the direct object of doer-focus verbs (um and mag) is signaled by Set II markers, pronouns and demonstratives. Mag verbs are also doer-focus. When the subject is a pronoun the direct object cannot come right after the subject (so “Magbubukas siya ng savings account” cannot be rewritten with the subject at the very end).

explanations.title: Conjugation
explanations.body: Infinitive (pawatas): mag + root. Past (pangnakaraan): nag + root. Present (pangkasalukuyan): nag + first syllable of the root repeated + root. Future (panghinaharap): mag + first syllable repeated + root. After a vowel-initial root a hyphen is used (mag-aral). The book’s two foreign-word roots (wire transfer, cash) follow the same idea; the book prints their present and future as nagwa-wire transfer, magwa-wire transfer and nagka-cash, magka-cash.

explanations.title: The pseudo verb kailangan
explanations.body: Kailangan is a pseudo verb seen in earlier lessons. Pseudo verbs are usually followed by the infinitive form of the verb.

explanations.title: Cashing a traveler’s check (Activity 9)
explanations.body: Dialog A: A asks if he can cash a U.S. traveler’s check; B says yes for a fee; A asks how much the service fee is; B says the amount or equivalent percentage; A gives the traveler’s check and the fee; B gives the cash in pesos and thanks the customer. Dialog B: A asks what the requirements are; B says the original receipt, two copies of a valid ID and two copies of the passport; A hands over everything and asks if there is a service fee; B says yes and the amount; A asks if a credit card is accepted for the fee; B apologizes and says cash only.

explanations.title: Forgotten PIN (Activity 10)
explanations.body: You are on TDY in Quezon City and forgot your ATM PIN number. Go to the nearest bank and ask for help. Teller: it is noon, greet the customer. Client: return the greeting. Teller: ask what he/she needs. Client: say you forgot your ATM PIN number. Teller: say you need two copies of the passport and a valid ID. Client: give the documents.

examples.text: Magpapadala po ako ng sulat.
examples.translation: Man: I will send a letter.

examples.text: Dalawampu’t limang piso lahat.

examples.text: Eto po ang bayad.

examples.text: Eto po ang sukli.
examples.translation: Woman 2: Here is the change.

examples.text: Pabili rin po ng sobre.
examples.translation: Woman 1: I would also like to buy an envelope.

examples.text: Sorry po. Wala na po kaming sobre.

explanations.title: Notes
explanations.body: Para saan po? means “To where?” or “To which place?”. ’Pag is short for kapag. Kaya in Kailan kaya ang dating? is an enclitic (explained in the grammar lessons). Wala na po kaming sobre means “We don’t have mailing envelopes anymore.”

explanations.title: More mag verbs
explanations.body: This lesson reviews mag verbs and adds more. Sentences from the dialogs, with the root words:

examples.text: Magtatanong lang po.
examples.translation: I am just going to ask a question. (root tanong)

examples.text: May kartero po bang magpi-pick up ng sulat?
examples.translation: Will there be a postman to pick up the letter? (root pick up)

examples.text: Magdagdag lang po kayo ng singkuwenta pesos.
examples.translation: Just add fifty pesos, sir/ma’am. (root dagdag)

examples.text: Puwede bang maglagay ng pera sa sulat?
examples.translation: Can I place money in the letter? (root lagay)

explanations.title: Conjugation chart
explanations.body: The book’s Activity 1 asks you to complete the chart; the book’s key is shown with more roots. Infinitive: mag + root; past: nag + root; present: nag + first syllable repeated + root; future: mag + first syllable repeated + root.

explanations.title: Mag + a foreign word
explanations.body: A mag prefix can be attached to a foreign word to make it a Tagalog verb. The meaning comes from the action usually associated with the word: McDonald’s is an eating establishment, so mag-McDonald’s means “to eat at McDonald’s”. Mag-hamburger can mean either “eat hamburger” or “cook hamburger”; context decides.

examples.text: Nagma-McDonald’s sila gabi-gabi.
examples.translation: They eat at McDonald’s every night.

examples.text: Magpo-post office kami.
examples.translation: We are going to the post office.

examples.text: Magpi-pick up sila ng mga kahon.
examples.translation: They are going to pick up boxes.

explanations.title: Activity 2: the correct verb form (the book’s key)
explanations.body: 1 Nagdala; 2 Magtanong; 3 Magpi-pick up or Nagpi-pick up; 4 Magdagdag; 5 maglagay.

lessons.title: 93. C5 L3 · The enclitics kaya, nga, and din/rin
lessons.subtitle: Kailan kaya ang dating? · Pabili nga po · Meron din bang…? · Libre rin po

explanations.title: Kaya
explanations.body: Kaya as an enclitic expresses being puzzled; it means “I wonder” or “do you suppose”. A sentence with the enclitic kaya is a question (note the question mark). When kaya begins the dependent clause of a complex sentence with the meaning “so”, “therefore” or “that’s why”, it is not an enclitic but a conjunction.

examples.text: Kailan kaya ang dating?
examples.translation: I wonder when it will arrive?

examples.text: Darating kaya ngayon sa kanila ang kahon?
examples.translation: I wonder if (do you suppose) the box will arrive at their place today?

examples.text: Magpapadala kami sa inyo ng pakete, kaya matatanggap ninyo ito sa Lunes.
examples.translation: We are sending you a package, so you will receive it on Monday.

explanations.title: Nga
explanations.body: Nga confirms what has been said. It can be translated “really”, “it is true” or “to be sure”, and in some contexts it means “please”.

examples.text: Pabili nga po ng lima.
examples.translation: Please sell me five.

examples.text: Meron nga pong magpapadala ng pakete.
examples.translation: Someone will indeed send a package, sir/ma’am.

examples.text: LBC Padala nga po ito.
examples.translation: This is indeed LBC Padala.

explanations.title: Din and rin
explanations.body: Din and rin are variants. Rin is used after words ending in a vowel sound (a, e, i, o, u and y), din after all other sounds. They mean “also” or “too” in affirmative sentences and “either” or “neither” in negative ones. Like lang, rin and din are not used to start a sentence. Negative sentences begin with the adverb hindi.

examples.text: Meron din bang kumukuha ng pakete?
examples.translation: Is there someone also getting the package?

examples.text: Libre rin po ang pagpapadala ng pakete sa Metro Manila.
examples.translation: Sending packages in Metro Manila is also free.

examples.text: Puwede rin itong sukat ng kahon.
examples.translation: This box size is also allowed.

explanations.title: Two conversations at the post office (Activity 8, the book’s script)
explanations.body: Passage 1: books/documents/money/food for a niece or nephew to Laguna: land ₱615 in about 4 days, air ₱1,075 by tomorrow afternoon; he chooses air. Passage 2: a box of school supplies, clothes and food for a sibling to Palawan: ₱790, in about 8 to 10 days.

examples.text: Ma’am, gusto kong magpadala ng pera, dokumento, at mga pagkain para sa pamangkin ko.
examples.translation: Customer: Ma’am, I want to send money, documents and food for my niece/nephew.

examples.text: Para sa aling lugar?
examples.translation: Employee: To which place?

examples.text: Sa Laguna lang po. Hanggang ilang araw po?
examples.translation: Customer: Just to Laguna. Up to how many days?

examples.text: Mga apat na araw kung land rate. Bukas ng hapon kung air rate.
examples.translation: Employee: About four days by land rate. Tomorrow afternoon by air rate.

examples.text: Magkano ’yun?
examples.translation: Customer: How much is that?

examples.text: Animnaraa’t labinlimang piso kung land rate. Sanlibo’t pitumpu’t limang piso naman kung air rate.
examples.translation: Employee: Six hundred fifteen pesos (₱615) by land rate. One thousand seventy-five (₱1,075) by air rate.

examples.text: Sige, air rate na lang po para mas mabilis.
examples.translation: Customer: All right, air rate then, to be faster.

examples.text: Gusto kong magpadala ng isang kahon para sa kapatid ko, mga gamit pang-eskuwela, mga damit, at pagkain.
examples.translation: Customer: I want to send a box for my sibling: school supplies, clothes and food.

examples.text: Saan po papunta?
examples.translation: Employee: Where is it going?

examples.text: Sa Palawan. Mga kailan po kaya ang dating?
examples.translation: Customer: To Palawan. About when will it arrive?

examples.text: Mga walo hanggang sampung araw.
examples.translation: Employee: About eight to ten days.

examples.text: Magkano po lahat?
examples.translation: Customer: How much in all?

examples.text: Pitundaa’t siyamnapung piso po.
examples.translation: Employee: Seven hundred ninety pesos (₱790).

explanations.title: Speaking (Activities 9 and 10)
explanations.body: Dialog A: A says he is sending a letter; B asks the recipient’s location; A names a place in the U.S.; B asks if it is express or registered mail; A says registered and asks how much; B says the price. Dialog B: A asks the price of a mailing envelope; B says it; A says he wants ten pieces; B says the total; A says yes and thanks. Activity 10 at a package delivery service center in Manila: A asks if he can send a package to Davao City; B says yes; A says he is sending two packages and asks the rate; B says the amount per kilo; A asks the arrival date; B gives the estimate; A asks the total cost for both; B says it; A pays and says thank you.

explanations.title: Self-evaluation for Chapter 5
explanations.body: Check that you can: extract information about buying gifts and exchanging foreign currency, bank transactions and post office and package delivery transactions; transcribe and translate sentences and numbers about them; buy gifts, exchange foreign currency, cash a traveler’s check and ask simple questions about wire transfers; and ask and answer basic questions at the post office and a package delivery center. You should understand um verbs, mag verbs, the pseudo verb kailangan, the enclitics kaya, nga and rin/din, and Set III demonstratives.

units.title: Chapter 6 · Lesson 1: Renting a place

lessons.title: 95. C6 L1 · Looking for an apartment or a house
lessons.subtitle: Naghahanap ako ng apartment · Ano bang bahay ang gusto mo? · Gusto mo bang makita?

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: By the end of this lesson you can extract information about renting a place from reading and listening, transcribe and translate sentences and numbers about renting a place, and ask and answer questions about renting a house or an apartment. The structure is may and its various forms as “there is/are”.

explanations.title: Getting started
explanations.body: The book opens with a mind map of preferences when looking for a house or an apartment to rent (near the town, number of rooms, floors and so on) and asks you to add more concepts (the mind map is left out).

explanations.title: Dialog A: a client talks to a property manager

examples.text: Naghahanap ako ng apartment malapit sa bayan. May alam ka ba?
examples.translation: Man: I am looking for an apartment near the town. Do you know of one?

examples.text: May alam ako. Malapit sa lahat, sa palengke, sakayan ng bus, at sa trabaho mo.
examples.translation: Woman: I know of one. It is near everything: the wet market, the bus stop and your workplace.

examples.text: Magkano kaya ang upa?
examples.translation: Man: I wonder how much the rent is?

examples.text: Hindi ko rin alam. Magtanong na lang tayo. Kailan ka ba lilipat?
examples.translation: Woman: I don’t know either. Let’s just ask. When will you move?

examples.text: Sana sa susunod na buwan.
examples.translation: Man: Hopefully next month.

explanations.title: Dialog B: husband and wife talk about features of a house to rent

examples.text: Hon, ano bang bahay ang gusto mo?
examples.translation: Husband: Hon, what kind of house do you want?

examples.text: Gusto kong may tatlong kuwarto at dalawang banyo.
examples.translation: Wife: I want one with three rooms and two bathrooms.

examples.text: Ano pa?
examples.translation: Husband: What else?

examples.text: Gusto kong may dalawang palapag at malaking kusina at salas.
examples.translation: Wife: I want two floors and a big kitchen and living room.

examples.text: Gusto mo ba ng sahig na kahoy o marmol?
examples.translation: Husband: Do you want a wood or marble floor?

examples.text: Okey lang ang sahig na kahoy, pero dapat semento ang dingding.
examples.translation: Wife: A wood floor is okay, but the walls should be cement.

examples.text: May nakita akong paupahan. Gusto mo bang makita?
examples.translation: Husband: I saw a house for rent. Do you want to see it?

examples.text: Siyempre naman. May oras ako ngayon.
examples.translation: Wife: Of course. I have time now.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: May alam ka ba? means “Do you know of any (information)?”. A sakayan is a place designated for all forms of public transportation to pick up passengers: sakayan ng traysikel, sakayan ng jeepney, sakayan ng van. Terminal and istasyon are other terms for sakayan. Ano pa? means “What else?”.

explanations.title: Comprehension check (the book’s key)
explanations.body: The book’s question 5 asks for four things but its key lists five, and question 6 asks for three questions but its key lists four; the keys are given as printed.

rows: A1. What does the man want and what one thing is he specifically looking for?
He is looking for an apartment; he wants it close to the town.
A2. What two pieces of information does the woman know about an apartment?
It is close to the wet market and the bus station.
A3. What is one thing the woman doesn’t know?
A4. When does the man plan to move?
B5. What does the woman want in a house?
3 rooms, 2 bathrooms, 2 storeys, a big kitchen and a big living room.
B6. What questions does the man ask?
What kind of house do you prefer? What else? Do you prefer hardwood or marble? Do you want to see it?

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Maganda kung ganoon means “That’s good/great then” or “That’s good/great, if that’s the case.” Bakod na kongkreto means “concrete fence.” Unlike the U.S., the Philippines uses the metric system (since 1860), so metro kuwadrado (square meters) is used for the area of a property. The book prints the vocabulary entries meron(g) and isang taon(g): the g is the linker, which appears when the next word begins with a vowel (isang taong kontrata).

explanations.title: May / me and mayroon / meron
explanations.body: May and mayroon, with the colloquial forms me and meron, have three uses; this lesson covers one. Depending on context they are equivalent to the English existential phrase “there is / there are / there will be.” These verbs are not conjugated: time or tense comes from context or from the adverbs of time in the sentence. Wala is the negative counterpart and here means “there is/are/will be none.” The two other uses of may/mayroon and wala come in later lessons.

examples.text: Merong palaruan, at may dalawang day care center.
examples.translation: There is a playground, and there are two day care centers.

explanations.title: Rule 1: always link mayroon and meron to the noun
explanations.body: Mayroon and meron take the linker g (mayroong, merong) before the noun they refer to.

examples.text: Merong tatlong kuwarto at dalawang banyo sa bahay na ito.
examples.translation: There are three bedrooms and two bathrooms in this house.

examples.text: Mayroong sakayan ng bus malapit sa paupahang bahay.
examples.translation: There is a bus stop near the rental house.

explanations.title: Rule 2: may and maraming are never in the same sentence
explanations.body: English says “There are many rooms in the house”, but Tagalog says Maraming kuwarto sa bahay, not May maraming kuwarto sa bahay. Maraming already means “there are many”; note the linker ng with marami.

examples.text: Maraming kuwarto sa bahay.
examples.translation: There are many rooms in the house. (Not May maraming kuwarto.)

explanations.title: Rule 3: me / may cannot come before a monosyllabic word; meron / mayroon can
explanations.body: The book’s examples: Wrong Me/May raw bang paaralan sa paupahan? Right Meron/Mayroon raw bang paaralan sa paupahan? Wrong Me/May na tubig. Right Me/May tubig na. Right Meron/Mayroon nang tubig. Wrong Me/May po bang guwardiya rito sa sabdibisyon? Right Me/May guwardiya po ba rito sa sabdibisyon? Right Meron/Mayroon po bang guwardiya rito sa sabdibisyon? (Raw, na and po are one-syllable words.)

examples.text: Meron raw bang paaralan sa paupahan?
examples.translation: Is there reportedly a school at the rental? (Me/May raw is wrong; Meron/Mayroon raw is right.)

examples.text: May tubig na.
examples.translation: There is water already. (Not May na tubig.)

examples.text: Meron nang tubig.
examples.translation: There is water already. (Meron/Mayroon can come before a monosyllabic word.)

examples.text: May guwardiya po ba rito sa sabdibisyon?
examples.translation: Is there a guard here in the subdivision? (Not Me/May po bang guwardiya.)

examples.text: Meron po bang guwardiya rito sa sabdibisyon?
examples.translation: Is there a guard here in the subdivision? (Meron/Mayroon can come before po.)

explanations.title: Five sentences, true or false (Activity 5, the book’s script)
explanations.body: Key: 1 false (the speaker wants a big kitchen and a nice bathroom, not a large bedroom); 2 true; 3 false (the transportation is outside the subdivision); 4 true; 5 true (the question is probably about whether utilities are included in the rent). The book prints no key; the answers follow from the script.

explanations.title: Paulo and his sister Regine (Activity 6, the book’s script)
explanations.body: Paulo arrived in Los Baños, Laguna, a few days ago to study at the University of the Philippines Los Baños (UPLB). Key: four descriptions of the interior: a small bathroom, 2 bedrooms, a living room and a large kitchen (the room is painted white and Paulo likes it); two reasons it is expensive: near the university, and a quiet and safe place; the rent is ₱8,000 a month, including wi-fi and electricity.

examples.text: O, Paulo. Kamusta ang apartment mo?
examples.translation: Regine: Hey, Paulo. How is your apartment?

examples.text: Meron itong maliit na banyo, dalawang kuwarto, salas, at malaking kusina. Kulay puti ang kuwarto, at gusto ko ito.
examples.translation: Paulo: It has a small bathroom, two rooms, a living room and a big kitchen. The room is white, and I like it.

examples.text: Magkano naman ang upa?
examples.translation: Regine: How much is the rent?

examples.text: Medyo mahal kasi malapit lang dito sa UPLB. Tahimik at ligtas ang lugar, Ate.
examples.translation: Paulo: It is a bit expensive because it is close to UPLB. The place is quiet and safe, Ate.

examples.text: Magkano nga ang upa?
examples.translation: Regine: How much exactly is the rent?

examples.text: Walong libo isang buwan kasama ang wi-fi at kuryente.
examples.translation: Paulo: Eight thousand (₱8,000) a month including wi-fi and electricity.

explanations.title: A rental agency (Activity 7, the book’s script)
explanations.body: Key: the client wants a two-storey apartment close to restaurants, theatres, parks, public transportation and a wet market; the questions: Do you have a two-storey apartment? and How many months of deposit are needed?; the apartment is very safe with 24/7 security; the rent is ₱23,000 including electricity, water, internet and trash collection.

examples.text: Naghahanap ako ng apartment na may dalawang palapag. ’Yung malapit sa restawran, sa sinehan, parke, sakayan, at palengke.
examples.translation: Client: I am looking for an apartment with two floors, one near a restaurant, a cinema, a park, a bus stop and a wet market.

examples.text: Meron po kaming available. Kailangan po ng anim na buwang kontrata.
examples.translation: Agency: We have one available. A six-month contract is needed.

examples.text: Walang problema. Ilang buwan ang kailangang deposito?
examples.translation: Client: No problem. How many months of deposit are needed?

examples.text: Dalawang buwan lang po at isang buwang advance.
examples.translation: Agency: Only two months and one month advance.

examples.text: Magkano ang upa?
examples.translation: Client: How much is the rent?

examples.text: Dalawampu’t tatlong libo. Kasama ang kuryente, tubig, internet, at hakot ng basura.
examples.translation: Agency: Twenty-three thousand (₱23,000). Electricity, water, internet and trash collection are included.

examples.text: Ligtas ba ang apartment?
examples.translation: Client: Is the apartment safe?

examples.text: Ligtas na ligtas po. May guwardiya po kami, beynte kuwatro oras.
examples.translation: Agency: Very safe. We have a guard, twenty-four hours.

explanations.title: Note on UPLB
explanations.body: The University of the Philippines Los Baños is in the towns of Los Baños and Bay in Laguna, about 64 kilometers southeast of Manila. A full university since 1972, it traces its roots to the University of the Philippines College of Agriculture and has been influential in Asian agriculture and biotechnology through its plant breeding and bioengineering.

explanations.title: Activity 8, Dialog A: a friend knows of a place
explanations.body: The book gives the lines as English prompts for pair work; the Tagalog below is a sample of how the exchange can go.

examples.text: Alam mo ba kung may lugar na malapit sa trabaho?
examples.translation: A: Do you know of a place close to work?

examples.text: May alam akong lugar na malapit sa trabaho at malapit sa sakayan ng bus.
examples.translation: B: I know of a place close to work and close to the bus stop.

examples.text: Anong klaseng apartment ang gusto mo?
examples.translation: A: What type of apartment do you want?

examples.text: Okey na ang isang kuwarto.
examples.translation: B: A one-room apartment will do.

examples.text: Kailan ka lilipat?
examples.translation: A: When will you move?

examples.text: Sa susunod na buwan.
examples.translation: B: Next month.

explanations.title: Activity 8, Dialog B: a house near the town center
explanations.body: The book’s prompts: A says he knows a house near the town center; B asks if A knows the monthly rental; A says the amount; B asks how many floors, rooms and so on; A says the numbers; B asks if there is a big kitchen and living room; A says yes, a very big kitchen and a very beautiful living room. The amount line is a sample.

examples.text: May alam akong bahay na malapit sa sentro ng bayan.
examples.translation: A: I know of a house close to the town center.

examples.text: Alam mo ba kung magkano ang upa kada buwan?
examples.translation: B: Do you know how much the monthly rent is?

examples.text: Ang upa ay labinlimang libo kada buwan.
examples.translation: A: The rent is fifteen thousand a month. (sample amount)

examples.text: Ilang palapag at kuwarto ang meron?
examples.translation: B: How many floors and rooms are there?

examples.text: Malaki ba ang kusina at salas?
examples.translation: B: Are the kitchen and living room big?

examples.text: Oo, malaking-malaki ang kusina at napakaganda ng salas.
examples.translation: A: Yes, the kitchen is very big and the living room is very beautiful.

explanations.title: Activity 9: asking a realtor for details
explanations.body: The book’s prompts: square footage in meters; whether the place is safe; the deposit; a contract; whether cable and wi-fi are free. Sample exchange:

examples.text: Ligtas na ligtas po.
examples.translation: B: It is very safe.

examples.text: Magkano ang deposito?
examples.translation: A: How much is the deposit?

examples.text: Isang buwang deposito at isang buwang advance.
examples.translation: B: One month deposit and one month advance.

examples.text: May kontrata ba?
examples.translation: A: Is there a contract?

examples.text: Anim na buwang kontrata po.
examples.translation: B: A six-month contract.

examples.text: Libre ba ang cable at wi-fi?
examples.translation: A: Are cable and wi-fi free?

examples.text: Opo, pati tubig at kuryente.
examples.translation: B: Yes, including water and electricity.

examples.text: Maganda kung ganoon.
examples.translation: A: That’s great.

lessons.title: 100. C6 L2 · Asking for help to move
lessons.subtitle: Puwede bang humingi ng tulong? · Maghahakot kami ng gamit · Kailan tayo mag-iimpake?

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: By the end of this lesson you can extract information about moving from reading and listening, transcribe and translate sentences and numbers about moving, and ask and answer questions about moving. The structure is more um and mag verbs.

explanations.title: Getting started
explanations.body: In many rural places in the Philippines houses made of light materials are literally transferred from one location to another with the help of neighbors, family and friends (searching “bayanihan moving house Philippines” shows videos). The book asks whether this is true in your culture too; the video is left out.

explanations.title: Dialog A: two friends are talking

examples.text: Pare, puwede bang humingi ng tulong? Maghahakot kami ng gamit.
examples.translation: Woman: Pare, may I ask for help? We will haul our things.

examples.text: Oo naman, mare. Lilipat na ba kayo sa bagong bahay? Kailangan mo ba ng pick-up?
examples.translation: Man: Of course, mare. Are you moving into the new house already? Do you need a pick-up truck?

examples.text: Oo, pare, at mga lalaking magbubuhat ng mga muwebles.
examples.translation: Woman: Yes, pare, and men who will carry the furniture.

examples.text: Walang problema. Magsasama ako ng mga kapitbahay dito.
examples.translation: Man: No problem. I will bring along some neighbors from here.

explanations.title: Notes on MERALCO and PLDT
explanations.body: MERALCO (Manila Electric Railroad and Light Company) is the largest distributor of electric power in the Philippines. PLDT (Philippine Long Distance Telephone Company) is the largest telecommunications and digital services company in the Philippines.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Pick-up refers to a pick-up truck. Mga lalaking magbubuhat are male haulers. Tapos na po means “It’s already done, sir/ma’am.” Pare and mare are friendly forms of address between friends (the book glosses nothing more).

rows: A1. What is the woman asking the man to do and why?
To help her move her things because she is moving to a new house; to lend her a pick-up truck; she needs male helpers to carry the furniture.
A2. What two forms of help are mentioned?
A pick-up truck and male helpers to help move the stuff.
B3. What is the man doing?
He is starting to pack things.
B4. Who will help with moving?
Tita and Tito (aunt and uncle). (The book prints no key; the answer follows from the dialog.)
B5. What three questions does the woman ask?
When will we pack? Have you called MERALCO and PLDT? Have you asked Tita and Tito for help? (The book prints no key; the answers follow from the dialog.)

explanations.title: Culture note
explanations.body: Moving companies are available only in big cities. Residents in the provinces rely mostly on family, friends and neighbors when moving to a new place in the area. Payment is not necessarily expected: drinks or snacks are enough to show appreciation for the help. It is also common to rent jeepneys from neighbors or friends instead of calling movers.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Saan po galing means “Where from, sir/ma’am?” and Saan papunta means “Where to?”. Para saan? means “For what?” or “For what purpose?”. Mag-iimpake (root impake) and maghahakot (root hakot) are verbs used with the marker ng (or ang in other contexts) to indicate the person(s) who will do what the verb says; in the dialog they are “person/s who will pack and haul.” Maganda kung ganoon is another way of saying Mabuti kung ganoon.

rows: A1. What does the woman want to do?
She is moving things and she is asking for a quote.
A2. How much does she need to move?
Just enough to fit in a regular-size truck.
A3. How much is the estimated cost?
B4. What is the woman asking?
She wants to know if Cris knows of a rental truck service.
B5. What two types of services does the woman want?
Packing and hauling of her belongings.

explanations.title: Um verbs that convert to mag verbs
explanations.body: Some verbs can be conjugated both ways. A native speaker usually uses the um form, which sounds more natural, but speakers also switch between forms.

explanations.title: Conjugation (Activity 1)
explanations.body: The book’s key conjugates pumunta, lumipat, magbilang and magsama. The chart shows all seven roots. Um verb: past = infinitive, present = um + first vowel repeated (pumupunta), future = first syllable + root (pupunta). Mag verb: past nag + root, present nag + first syllable + root, future mag + first syllable + root.

explanations.title: Verbs used in only one form
explanations.body: Not every um verb can be conjugated in mag, or the reverse. These are used in one form only:

explanations.title: Verbs with different meanings in um and mag
explanations.body: Magtira and magtabi are used interchangeably.

explanations.title: Passage 1: two siblings (Activity 7, the book’s script)
explanations.body: Key: she is asking for help because she is moving to a new place; the apartment is close to her school; the move is Saturday at around 1:00 p.m.; her brother and his friends will help.

examples.text: Oo naman. Kailan ka ba lilipat?

examples.text: Walang problema. Magsasama ako ng mga kaibigan ko. Marami ka bang gamit?

examples.text: Marami-rami din po.
examples.translation: Sister: Quite a lot, too.

explanations.title: Passage 2: a woman and a man on the telephone (Activity 7, the book’s script)
explanations.body: Key: the purpose is to ask her friend for help because she is moving; she is moving to Barangay Siyete, about five kilometers from her current location; the services she wants are truck rental, hauling and packing; the company is fast and reliable.

examples.text: Mabuti kung ganoon.
examples.translation: Woman: That’s good then.

units.title: Chapter 6 · Lesson 3: Furnishing and decorating

lessons.title: 105. C6 L3 · Furnishing a house: furniture and household items
lessons.subtitle: Bumili ka na ba ng gamit pambahay? · Meron ka na bang kalan? · Magbabaratilyo sa Linggo

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: By the end of this lesson you can extract information about furnishing and decorating, transcribe and translate sentences and numbers about it, enumerate household items, and ask and answer simple questions about furnishing and decorating. The structures are may/me/mayroon/meron as the verb “to have”, wala in response to may/me/mayroon/meron questions, and more mag verbs.

explanations.title: Getting started
explanations.body: The book opens with a mind map of household items and asks you to provide as much vocabulary as possible (the mind map is left out).

explanations.title: Dialog A: two friends are talking

examples.text: Bumili ka na ba ng gamit pambahay?
examples.translation: Man: Have you bought household items already?

examples.text: Kahapon pa. Bumili ako ng tokador, kama, bentilador, mesa, at upuan.
examples.translation: Woman: Since yesterday. I bought a dresser, a bed, an electric fan, a table and chairs.

examples.text: Bumili ka na rin ba ng bagong pridyider at telebisyon?
examples.translation: Man: Have you also bought a new refrigerator and television?

examples.text: Wala pa. Sa Sabado na.
examples.translation: Woman: Not yet. On Saturday.

examples.text: Meron ka na bang kalan at ibang gamit pangkusina?
examples.translation: Man: Do you already have a stove and other kitchen things?

examples.text: Wala pa rin. Bukas na ako bibili.
examples.translation: Woman: None yet either. I will buy tomorrow.

explanations.title: Dialog B: siblings talk on the phone

examples.text: Yanyan, meron ka na bang silya at mesa?
examples.translation: Brother: Yanyan, do you already have chairs and a table?

examples.text: Wala pa po, Kuya. Hihiram na po muna ako.
examples.translation: Sister: Not yet, Kuya. I will borrow some for now.

examples.text: Magbabaratilyo sa Linggo sa SM. Sumama ka. Ano pa ba ang mga kailangan mo?
examples.translation: Brother: There will be a sale on Sunday at SM. Come along. What else do you need?

examples.text: Marami pa po. Unan, punda, kobre kama, kumot, muskitero, at plantsa po.
examples.translation: Sister: Plenty more. Pillow, pillow case, bed cover, blanket, mosquito net and flat iron.

examples.text: Marami nga. Maglista ka nga. Magkita tayo sa labas ng SM, alas-diyes ng umaga.
examples.translation: Brother: That is a lot indeed. Make a list, please. Let’s meet outside SM at ten in the morning.

examples.text: Opo, Kuya.
examples.translation: Sister: Yes, Kuya.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Gamit pambahay is the general term for furniture and other household items. Gamit pangkusina is the general term for kitchen appliances and utensils. Kobre kama is also spelled kubre kama. Tokador, kama, bentilador, mesa and telebisyon are Spanish cognates.

rows: A1. What five household items did the woman buy?
Dresser, bed, electric fan, table, chair.
A2. What three items does the woman need to buy?
A3. When did the woman buy a few of the items and when does she plan to buy the rest?
B4. What two items will the woman borrow?
B5. What event will take place on Sunday?
B6. What six items does the woman need?
Pillow, pillow case, bed cover/bedsheet, blanket, mosquito net, flat iron.

lessons.subtitle: Mag-aayos ka na ba ng bahay bukas? · Ako na ang bahala · Pahiram naman

explanations.title: Dialog A: two friends are talking

examples.text: Mag-aayos ka na ba ng bahay bukas?
examples.translation: Man: Are you going to arrange the house tomorrow?

examples.text: Oo. Maglilinis ako ng bahay, magliligpit ng kalat, at magkakabit ng kurtina.
examples.translation: Woman: Yes. I will clean the house, put away the mess and hang curtains.

examples.text: Tutulong ako. Ako na ang magpapako at magsasabit ng mga kuwadro.
examples.translation: Man: I will help. I will do the nailing and hanging of the picture frames.

examples.text: Salamat naman. Medyo malaki ang kuwadro ng medalya. Marami ring mga sertipiko.
examples.translation: Woman: Thank goodness. The frame for the medal is a bit big. There are also many certificates.

examples.text: Ako na ang bahala. Walang problema.
examples.translation: Man: I’ll take care of it. No problem.

explanations.title: Dialog B: a man and a woman are talking

examples.text: Meron ka bang walis tingting at bunot? Puwede bang humiram?
examples.translation: Woman: Do you have a walis tingting and a coconut husk? May I borrow?

examples.text: Wala akong walis tingting at bunot. Meron akong walis tambo.
examples.translation: Man: I don’t have a walis tingting and a coconut husk. I have a walis tambo.

examples.text: Magwawalis ako ng bakuran at magtatanggal ng agiw. Kailangan matigas ang walis. Meron ka bang panlampaso? Pahiram naman. Maglalampaso din ako ng sahig.
examples.translation: Woman: I will sweep the yard and remove the cobwebs. The broom has to be hard. Do you have a mop? Let me borrow it. I will also mop the floor.

examples.text: Wala din, e.
examples.translation: Man: None either, you see.

explanations.title: Culture note
explanations.body: In Filipino homes it is very common to see family pictures, medals, diplomas and certificates of honor prominently displayed on the living room wall. These objects are sources of pride and honor for the family.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: In another context magkakabit (as in magkakabit ng kurtina, “will hang curtains”) means “will connect, fasten, attach.” Ako na ang bahala means “I’ll take charge” or “I’ll take care of that.” Pahiram naman means “Let me borrow” or “Lend me.” Kurtina, kuwadro, medalya, sertipiko, problema and lampaso are Spanish cognates.

Clean the house, put away the mess, hang curtains.
A2. What two things will the man do to help?
Nail nails into the wall and hang the picture frames.
A3. Two descriptive details about the medal and certificates
The frame for the medal is a bit big; there are many certificates.
B4. What three things does the woman plan to do?
Sweep the yard, remove cobwebs, mop the floor.
B5. What does the woman need?
A broom stick (walis tingting), a walis tambo, a mop or rag, bunot (coconut husk).

lessons.subtitle: Meron ka bang panlampaso? · Wala akong walis tingting · May walis tambo ako

explanations.title: May as the verb “to have”
explanations.body: In Chapter 6 Lesson 1 you learned may/me/mayroon/meron as “there is/are/was/were/will be.” In this lesson they mean “to have.” Wala is the negative answer. Examples from the presentations, each with the question and the answer:

examples.text: Meron ka na bang kalan at ibang gamit pangkusina? Wala pa rin.
examples.translation: Do you already have a stove and other kitchen things? None yet also.

examples.text: Meron ka na bang silya at mesa? Wala pa po, Kuya.
examples.translation: Do you already have chairs and tables? None yet, Kuya.

examples.text: Meron ka bang walis tingting? Wala akong walis tingting. Meron akong walis tambo.
examples.translation: Do you have a broomstick? I don’t have a broomstick. I have a walis tambo.

examples.text: Meron ka bang panlampaso? Wala din, e.
examples.translation: Do you have a mop? None, too.

explanations.title: Linker rules in questions
explanations.body: In an interrogative sentence meron/mayroon always needs the linker ng on the enclitic ba (bang). With may/me you do not need the linker. Right: Meron ka na bang kalan at ibang gamit pangkusina? Wrong: Meron ka na ba kalan at ibang gamit pangkusina? Right: Me/May kalan ka na ba at ibang gamit pangkusina? Wrong: Me/May kalan ka na bang at ibang gamit pangkusina?

examples.text: Meron ka na bang kalan at ibang gamit pangkusina?
examples.translation: Right: meron needs the linker ng on ba.

examples.text: May kalan ka na ba at ibang gamit pangkusina?
examples.translation: Right: with may/me, ba takes no linker.

explanations.title: Linker rules in statements
explanations.body: In a declarative sentence meron and mayroon always need the linker ng or g with the personal pronoun that follows immediately (akong). You do not need a linker with may. Right: Meron akong walis tambo. Wrong: Meron ako walis tambo. Right: May walis tambo ako. Wrong: May walis tambo akong. With meron/mayroon the personal pronoun subject follows the verb; with may/me it follows the direct object (walis tambo), not the verb.

examples.text: Meron akong walis tambo.
examples.translation: Right: meron needs the linker ng/g with a following personal pronoun.

examples.text: May walis tambo ako.
examples.translation: Right: with may, the pronoun follows the object and no linker is needed.

explanations.title: Conjugation chart (Activity 1, the book’s key)
explanations.body: The book prints magligpit as “to fix”; in the dialog it means to put things away in an orderly manner. Infinitive: mag + root; past: nag + root; present: nag + first syllable repeated + root; future: mag + first syllable repeated + root.

rows: to put away (the book prints “to fix”)

explanations.title: Activity 2: choose the correct form (the book’s key)
explanations.body: The correct verb forms are, in order: magwawalis, nagtatanggal, naglista, maglampaso, magpako, nagligpit. Activity 3 gives their translations:

examples.text: Bukas magwawalis kami sa bagong bahay.
examples.translation: Tomorrow we will sweep at the new house.

examples.text: Kasalukuyan silang nagtatanggal ng mga agiw sa lumang bahay.
examples.translation: Today they are removing the cobwebs from the old house.

examples.text: Kahapon naglista sina Henry ng mga gamit nila.
examples.translation: Yesterday Henry and company listed their things.

examples.text: Kailangang maglampaso tayo ng banyo at sahig.
examples.translation: We need to mop the bathroom and floor.

examples.text: Kailangan nating magpako at magsabit ng kuwadro.
examples.translation: We need to nail and hang the picture frames.

examples.text: Umalis na ang mga bisita at nagligpit na rin sila.
examples.translation: The visitors already left and they also cleaned up.

examples.text: Maghihiram ka ba ng panlampaso, walis tingting, at basahan?

examples.text: Tutulong akong magkabit ng kurtina at magsabit ng kuwadro.
examples.translation: I will help put up the curtain and hang the picture frame.

explanations.title: Passage 1: chores for the next day (Activity 7, the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: tomorrow she will fix her things, clean the house, hang curtains, hang picture frames, clean the backyard and remove cobwebs (the book asks for five and lists six); the man offers to help clean her house; she needs a broom stick and a mop from him.

examples.text: Ano ang gagawin mo bukas?
examples.translation: Man: What will you do tomorrow?

examples.text: Maraming-marami. Mag-aayos ako ng gamit, maglilinis ng bahay, magkakabit ng kurtina, magsasabit ng mga kuwadro, magwawalis ng bakuran, at magtatanggal ng agiw.
examples.translation: Woman: A great deal. I will arrange my things, clean the house, hang curtains, hang the picture frames, sweep the yard and remove cobwebs.

examples.text: Ang dami nga. Tutulong ako. May kailangan ka bang gamit?
examples.translation: Man: That is a lot indeed. I will help. Do you need any tools?

examples.text: Puwede bang magdala ka ng walis tingting at lampaso?
examples.translation: Woman: Can you bring a walis tingting and a mop?

examples.text: Oo naman.
examples.translation: Man: Of course.

examples.text: Salamat.
examples.translation: Woman: Thank you.

explanations.title: Passage 2: the brother’s new apartment (Activity 7, the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: the older sister is asking her brother if he has complete household items; he has a bed, a table and a chair; she asks about a pillow, pillow case, bed cover, mosquito net and flat iron; she suggests buying the things he needs tomorrow (there is a sale in Divisoria) and they will meet at 5:00 p.m.

examples.text: O, Junjun, kumpleto ka na ba ng gamit diyan sa apartment mo?
examples.translation: Sister: Hey, Junjun, do you have all your things there in your apartment?

examples.text: Hindi pa po, Ate. Meron lang akong kama, mesa, at silya.
examples.translation: Brother: Not yet, Ate. I only have a bed, a table and a chair.

examples.text: Me gamit pangkusina ka na ba?
examples.translation: Sister: Do you have kitchen things yet?

examples.text: Wala pa po. Kahapon lang po ako lumipat.
examples.translation: Brother: Not yet. I only moved yesterday.

examples.text: Meron ka na bang unan, punda, kobre kama, muskitero, at plantsa?
examples.translation: Sister: Do you already have a pillow, pillow case, bed cover, mosquito net and flat iron?

examples.text: Wala pa rin po.
examples.translation: Brother: None yet either.

examples.text: Sige, magkita tayo bukas, alas singko ng hapon. Bibili tayo ng mga gamit mo. May baratilyo sa Divisoria.
examples.translation: Sister: All right, let’s meet tomorrow at five in the afternoon. We will buy your things. There is a sale in Divisoria.

examples.text: Opo, Ate.
examples.translation: Brother: Yes, Ate.

explanations.title: Lorna’s new house, segment 1 (Activity 9, the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: two bedrooms and a bathroom, with a bed, chair and small table; the house is about 10 minutes’ walk from the school.

examples.text: O, Lorna, kamusta ang bagong bahay?
examples.translation: Older sister: Hey, Lorna, how is the new house?

examples.text: OK lang, Ate. May dalawang kuwarto, isang banyo. Merong kama, isang silya, at maliit na mesa.
examples.translation: Lorna: It’s okay, Ate. There are two rooms and one bathroom. There is a bed, a chair and a small table.

examples.text: Malapit ba iyan sa eskuwelahan?
examples.translation: Older sister: Is it near the school?

examples.text: Opo. Mga sampung minuto lang kung maglalakad kayo.
examples.translation: Lorna: Yes. Only about ten minutes if you walk.

explanations.title: Lorna’s new house, segment 2 (Activity 9, the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: the place is nice and safe, near the mall, hospital and bus station; the monthly payment is ₱10,500; the older sister says it is very expensive. The book calls the payment a mortgage in the key; in the script Lorna says bayad (payment).

examples.text: Magkano naman ang bayad mo sa bahay?
examples.translation: Older sister: How much do you pay for the house?

examples.text: Medyo mahal, Ate. Maganda at ligtas ang lugar. Malapit ito sa lahat, mall, ospital, restawran, at sakayan ng bus.
examples.translation: Lorna: It is a bit expensive, Ate. The place is nice and safe. It is near everything: mall, hospital, restaurant and bus stop.

examples.text: Magkano nga ang bayad mo buwan-buwan?
examples.translation: Older sister: How much exactly do you pay every month?

examples.text: Sampunlibo’t limandaan isang buwan.
examples.translation: Lorna: Ten thousand five hundred (₱10,500) a month.

examples.text: Ang mahal-mahal naman!
examples.translation: Older sister: That is so expensive!

explanations.title: Six true-or-false statements (Activity 8)
explanations.body: The book prints only the statements (for example “The speaker needs a bed, pillows, and blankets for the room”) and plays the sentences on audio; the script and key are not printed, so this activity is left out.

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: The audio and the tick boxes.

explanations.title: Self-evaluation for Chapter 6
explanations.body: Check that you can: extract information about renting a place, moving, and furnishing and decorating, in reading and listening; transcribe and translate sentences and numbers about them; ask and answer questions about renting a house or apartment, about moving, and about furnishing and decorating; and enumerate household items. You should understand may and its forms as “there is/are/will be”, um and mag verbs, may/me/mayroon/meron as the verb “to have”, and wala in response to may/me/mayroon/meron questions.

units.title: Chapter 7 · Lesson 1: Sports

lessons.title: 111. C7 L1 · Sports expressions and a vacation dialog
lessons.subtitle: Ang galing-galing ng manlalaro! · Nagbasketbol, nag-arnis, nagkarate · Nag-wakeboarding kami

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: By the end of this lesson you can extract information about sports from reading and listening, transcribe and translate sentences and numbers about sports, enumerate popular sports, and ask and answer simple questions about sports. The structures are intensified/exclamatory adjectives and mag verbs related to sports.

explanations.title: Getting started
explanations.body: The book asks what your favorite sport is and shows a few popular sports in the Philippines (pictures, left out); you add more.

examples.text: Ang galing-galing ng manlalaro!
examples.translation: How very good the player is!

examples.text: Ang tapang-tapang ng coach!
examples.translation: How very brave the coach is!

examples.text: Ang lakas-lakas ng boksingero!
examples.translation: How very strong the boxer is!

examples.text: Ang liksi-liksi ng manlalangoy!
examples.translation: How very agile the swimmer is!

examples.text: Ang sakit-sakit ng kalamnan ko sa karate!
examples.translation: How very painful my muscles are from karate!

examples.text: Ang layo-layo ng basketball court!
examples.translation: How very far the basketball court is!

examples.text: Ang sipag-sipag ng basketbolista!
examples.translation: How very hardworking the basketball player is!

examples.text: Ang hirap-hirap tumakbo!
examples.translation: How very difficult it is to run!

examples.text: Hello, Marvin. O, kumusta ang bakasyon mo? Nag-enjoy ba ang anak mo?
examples.translation: Woman: Hello, Marvin. So, how was your vacation? Did your child enjoy it?

examples.text: Sobrang nag-enjoy. Sumubok ako ng maraming klaseng sports kasama ng panganay ko. Nagbasketbol, nag-arnis, nag-football, nagkarate, at nagboksing. Ikaw, kumusta ang bakasyon mo?
examples.translation: Man: Very much. I tried many kinds of sports with my oldest child: basketball, arnis, football, karate and boxing. And you, how was your vacation?

examples.text: Naku, ang saya-saya! Nagbakasyon ako sa ’Pinas kasama ng dalawang anak ko. Nag-wakeboarding kami.
examples.translation: Woman: Oh my, how very enjoyable! I vacationed in the Philippines with my two children. We did wakeboarding.

explanations.title: Culture note: arnis
explanations.body: Arnis, also known as eskrima and kali, is the national sport and martial art of the Philippines. The three names are roughly interchangeable umbrella terms for the traditional Filipino martial arts (FMA), which emphasize weapon-based fighting with sticks, knives, bladed weapons and improvised weapons. Arnis also includes hand-to-hand combat, joint locks, grappling and weapon-disarming techniques. Emphasis is generally on weapons, but some systems focus on empty hands and some old-school systems do not teach weapons at all.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Ang galing-galing, ang tapang-tapang, ang lakas-lakas, ang liksi-liksi, ang sakit-sakit, ang layo-layo, ang sipag-sipag and ang hirap-hirap are intensified/exclamatory adjectives, explained in the grammar lesson. Ang sipag-sipag literally means “how very industrious”; in the list it means “How very diligent the basketball player is!”, and in another context “how hard-working!”. Panganay ko means “my oldest child.” Nagbasketbol, nag-arnis, nag-football, nagkarate and nagboksing are mag verbs used for sports activities.

explanations.title: Comprehension check A: the adjective for each noun (the book’s key)
Comprehension check B: the dialog (the book’s key)

rows: What two questions did the woman ask?
How’s your vacation? Did your son enjoy it?
What five sports did the man enjoy doing?
Basketball, arnis, football, karate and boxing. (The book’s key prints “baseball” for arnis; the dialog says nag-arnis.)
Where did the woman spend her vacation and who was with her?
In the Philippines, with her two children.

lessons.title: 112. C7 L1 · Joining a gym and becoming a good swimmer
lessons.subtitle: Paano ba maging miyembro ng gym? · Libre ang pool · Gaano kadalas?

explanations.title: Dialog A: a man inquires about gym membership

examples.text: Hello, Laila. Paano ba maging miyembro ng gym?
examples.translation: Remo: Hello, Laila. How do I become a member of the gym?

examples.text: Madali lang. Mag-fill-up ka lang ng membership form. Ipakita mo ang valid ID mo at magbayad ka ng membership fee.
examples.translation: Laila: It’s easy. Just fill up a membership form. Show your valid ID and pay a membership fee.

examples.text: Magkano ang membership fee?
examples.translation: Remo: How much is the membership fee?

examples.text: Sanlibo’t limandaan para sa buong taon.
examples.translation: Laila: One thousand five hundred (₱1,500) for the whole year.

examples.text: Anu-ano ang benepisyo?
examples.translation: Remo: What are the benefits?

examples.text: Marami. Libre ang paggamit ng kagamitang ng gym. Libre din ang pool, at kasama sa bayad ang dalawang miyembro ng pamilya.
examples.translation: Laila: Many. Use of the gym equipment is free. The pool is also free, and two family members are included in the payment.

explanations.title: Dialog B: two siblings talk about swimming

examples.text: Kuya, paano bang maging magaling na manlalangoy, tulad mo?
examples.translation: Sister: Kuya, how can one become a good swimmer, like you?

examples.text: Madali lang. Dapat malakas ang katawan mo at sapat ang tulog mo. Kailangan mo ring mag-ensayo palagi.
examples.translation: Brother: It’s easy. Your body should be strong and you should get enough sleep. You also need to practice all the time.

examples.text: Gaano kadalas, Kuya?
examples.translation: Sister: How often, Kuya?

examples.text: Sa simula, puwede nang isang beses isang linggo.
examples.translation: Brother: At the start, once a week is fine.

examples.text: Kuya, puwede mo ba akong turuan?
examples.translation: Sister: Kuya, can you teach me?

examples.text: Oo naman.
examples.translation: Brother: Of course.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Miyembro, benepisyo, beses and libre are Spanish cognates. In Dialog B, manlalangoy is a noun (“swimmer”); another example is manlalaro (“player”). The membership fee in Dialog A is sanlibo’t limandaan, ₱1,500 for the whole year. The book’s Dialog A also says paggamit ng kagamitang ng gym as printed.

rows: A1. What does the man ask the woman?
How to become a member of the gym.
A2. What three requirements are mentioned?
Fill up the membership form; show a valid ID; pay the membership fee.
A3. How much is the membership fee?
A4. What are three benefits of membership?
Free use of the gym’s equipment; free use of the pool; the payment includes 2 members of the family.
B5. What does the sister want to know?
How to be a good swimmer.
B6. What four pieces of advice does her brother give?
Be physically fit; have enough sleep; practice often; at the start, once a week is fine.

explanations.title: Intensified / exclamatory adjectives
explanations.body: In Chapters 3 and 4 you learned adjectives. One way to form an intensified/exclamatory adjective is to duplicate the root word, put a hyphen between the two, place ang at the beginning and end the sentence with an exclamation point. The eight sentences from the presentation (the book’s key):

examples.text: Ang galing-galing ng manlalaro!
examples.translation: How very good the player is!

examples.text: Ang tapang-tapang ng coach!
examples.translation: How very brave the coach is!

examples.text: Ang lakas-lakas ng boksingero!
examples.translation: How very strong the boxer is!

examples.text: Ang liksi-liksi ng manlalangoy!
examples.translation: How very agile the swimmer is!

examples.text: Ang sakit-sakit ng kalamnan ko sa karate!
examples.translation: How very painful my muscles are from karate!

examples.text: Ang layo-layo ng basketball court!
examples.translation: How very far the basketball court is!

examples.text: Ang sipag-sipag ng basketbolista!
examples.translation: How very hardworking the basketball player is!

examples.text: Ang hirap-hirap tumakbo!
examples.translation: How very difficult it is to run!

examples.text: Ang bilis-bilis ng manlalangoy!
examples.translation: How very fast the swimmer is!

examples.text: Ang saya-saya ng bakasyon!
examples.translation: How very enjoyable the vacation is!

explanations.title: Review of mag verbs related to sports
explanations.body: Identify the mag verbs and translate. Except for the last sentence, the verbs are in the past tense.

examples.text: Nag-enjoy ba ang anak mo?
examples.translation: Did your child enjoy it?

examples.text: Nagbasketbol, nag-arnis, nag-futbol, nagkarate, at nagboksing siya.
examples.translation: He/she played basketball, did arnis, played football, did karate and boxed.

examples.text: Nag-wakeboarding kami.
examples.translation: We did wakeboarding.

examples.text: Kailangan mo ring mag-ensayo palagi.
examples.translation: You also need to practice all the time.

explanations.title: Extended conjugation table (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Foreign words are hyphenated (mag-basketball, mag-football). Tagalized words are spelled together (magfutbol, nagfutbol, nagfufutbol). For magkarate the book also gives nag-karate / nag-karate / magka-karate.

explanations.title: Activity 2: choose the right tense and the time word (the book’s key)
explanations.body: The correct verb is in each sentence below, with the time word that justifies it:

examples.translation: This coming Saturday, we father and child will do karate. (magkakarate, sa darating na Sabado)

explanations.title: Translate the sentences (Activity 4, the book’s key)
explanations.body: Efren “Bata” Reyes (billiards) and Manny “Pacman” Pacquiao (boxing) are famous Filipino sports figures. The Tagalog lines drop the quotation marks around the nicknames.

examples.text: Ang sipag-sipag mag-ensayo ni Efren Bata Reyes!
examples.translation: How very hardworking Efren “Bata” Reyes is in training!

examples.text: Gusto mo bang maging magaling na boksingerong tulad ni Manny Pacman Pacquiao?
examples.translation: Do you want to be a good boxer like Manny “Pacman” Pacquiao?

examples.text: Ate, puwede mo ba akong turuang lumangoy?
examples.translation: Big Sister, can you teach me how to swim?

examples.text: Ipakita mo ang valid ID mo, mag-fill-up ka ng membership form, at magbayad ka ng membership fee.
examples.translation: Show your valid ID, fill up the membership form, and pay the membership fee.

examples.text: Kasama ba sa bayad ang ibang miyembro ng pamilya?
examples.translation: Does the fee include other members of the family?

explanations.title: Passage 1: two friends in the gym (Activity 6, the book’s script)
explanations.body: Key: the man asks how to become a member; the requirements are filling up a form, a valid ID and payment of the membership fee; the fee is ₱1,200 for one year; the membership fee includes up to four members of the family.

examples.text: Liza, gusto kong maging miyembro ng gym. Paano ba?
examples.translation: Man: Liza, I want to become a member of the gym. How?

examples.text: Ang dali lang. Magdala ka lang ng valid ID at mag-fill up ka ng form.
examples.translation: Woman: It’s very easy. Just bring a valid ID and fill up a form.

examples.text: Hindi ba malaki ang membership?
examples.translation: Man: Isn’t the membership big?

examples.text: Hindi naman. Sanlibo’t dalawandaan lang buong taon.
examples.translation: Woman: Not really. Only one thousand two hundred (₱1,200) for the whole year.

examples.text: Libre ba ang asawa’t anak ko?
examples.translation: Man: Are my wife and child free?

examples.text: Libre hanggang apat na miyembro ng pamilya mo.
examples.translation: Woman: Free for up to four members of your family.

explanations.title: Passage 2: a man and a woman on the phone (Activity 6, the book’s script)
explanations.body: Key: they talk about their respective vacations; the man did boxing, karate and wakeboarding with his cousin; his two questions: How was your vacation in Lake Tahoe? and Isn’t it expensive (the book’s key says “Is the ski equipment expensive?”); the woman says the rental is cheap.

examples.text: Hello, James. Kumusta na ang bakasyon mo? Nag-enjoy ba kayo ng pinsan mo?
examples.translation: Woman: Hello, James. How was your vacation? Did you and your cousin enjoy it?

examples.text: Naku, ang saya-saya! Sobra kaming nag-enjoy. Nagboksing kami, nagkarate, at nag-wakeboarding. Ikaw, kumusta ang bakasyon mo sa Lake Tahoe?
examples.translation: Man: Oh my, how very enjoyable! We enjoyed ourselves a lot. We boxed, did karate and did wakeboarding. And you, how was your vacation at Lake Tahoe?

examples.text: Ang saya din. Nag-ski kami ng mga bata.
examples.translation: Woman: It was a lot of fun too. We skied with the children.

examples.text: Hindi ba mahal?
examples.translation: Man: Isn’t it expensive?

examples.text: Mura lang ang renta ng gamit.
examples.translation: Woman: The equipment rental is cheap.

explanations.title: Dennis and his cousin Manny (Activity 8, the book’s script)

lessons.subtitle: Paano po maging miyembro ng gym? · Puwede mo ba akong turuan? · Glossary

explanations.title: Activity 9: joining a gym in Manila
explanations.body: The book gives English prompts for pair work; the Tagalog below is a sample of how the exchange can go (the book’s fee is ₱750 a month).

examples.text: Magandang araw po.
examples.translation: You: Good day.

examples.text: Magandang araw din po.
examples.translation: Receptionist: Good day to you too.

examples.text: Paano po maging miyembro ng gym?
examples.translation: You: How can I become a member of the gym?

examples.text: Madali lang po. Mag-fill up lang kayo ng membership form, ipakita ang dalawang valid ID, at magbayad ng membership fee.
examples.translation: Receptionist: It’s pretty easy. Just fill up the membership form, show two valid IDs and pay a membership fee.

examples.text: Magkano po ang membership fee?
examples.translation: You: How much is the membership fee?

examples.text: Pitong daan at limampung piso po kada buwan.
examples.translation: Receptionist: Seven hundred fifty pesos a month (₱750).

examples.text: Ang mura naman! Ano po ang mga benepisyo?
examples.translation: You: How affordable! What are the benefits?

examples.text: Marami po. Libre ang paggamit ng kagamitan, libre ang pool, at kasama ang isang miyembro ng pamilya.
examples.translation: Receptionist: A lot. Free use of the equipment, free use of the pool, and one family member is included.

examples.text: Magaling! Gusto kong maging miyembro.
examples.translation: You: Great! I would like to become a member.

explanations.title: Activity 10: learning karate from a friend
explanations.body: The prompts: ask how to excel in karate; the friend says you need a healthy body and regular practice; ask how often (for a beginner, twice a week); ask if the friend can teach you; meet at the gym.

examples.text: Paano ba maging magaling sa karate, tulad mo?
examples.translation: You: How can one excel at karate, like you?

examples.text: Kailangan malusog ang katawan mo at dapat kang mag-ensayo palagi.
examples.translation: Friend: You need a healthy body and must practice regularly.

examples.text: Gaano kadalas ang ensayo?
examples.translation: You: How often is the practice?

examples.text: Para sa nagsisimula, puwede na ang dalawang beses isang linggo.
examples.translation: Friend: For a beginner, twice a week is fine.

examples.text: Puwede mo ba akong turuan?
examples.translation: You: Can you teach me?

examples.text: Oo naman. Magkita tayo sa gym.
examples.translation: Friend: Of course. Let’s meet at the gym.

examples.text: Salamat. Kita tayo mamaya.
examples.translation: You: Thank you. See you later.

Ang sakit-sakit ng ___! Ang layo-layo ng/ni ___! Ang sipag-sipag ng/ni ___! Ang hirap-hirap ng/mag(verb) ___! Fill them with your own words.

units.title: Chapter 7 · Lesson 2: Hobbies

lessons.title: 116. C7 L2 · Favorite hobbies: music, reading, mahjong, fishing
lessons.subtitle: Ano po ang paborito n’yong libangan? · Nakikinig na lang ako ng musika · Gustung-gusto kong mangisda

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: By the end of this lesson you can extract information about hobbies from reading and listening, transcribe and translate sentences and numbers about hobbies, enumerate hobbies, and ask and answer simple questions about hobbies. The structures are ma verbs and more um and mag verbs.

explanations.title: Getting started
explanations.body: The book shows two common hobbies (pictures, left out) and asks what your hobbies are; you add more.

explanations.title: Dialog A: a niece talks to her uncle about his favorite pastimes

examples.text: Tito, ano po ba ang paborito n’yong libangan?
examples.translation: Niece: Uncle, what is your favorite hobby?

examples.text: Dati, tumutugtog ako ng piano at saxophone. Miyembro kasi ako ng banda.
examples.translation: Uncle: Before, I played the piano and saxophone. I was a member of a band, you see.

examples.text: E, ngayon po, ano po ang libangan n’yo?
examples.translation: Niece: And now, what is your hobby?

examples.text: Ngayon, nakikinig na lang ako ng musika, nagbabasa ng diyaryo o libro, at nanonood ng balita.
examples.translation: Uncle: Now I just listen to music, read the newspaper or books, and watch the news.

examples.text: Hindi na po kayo nagpa-piano at nagsa-saxophone?
examples.translation: Niece: You no longer play the piano and the saxophone?

examples.text: Madalang na lang. Napapagod na ako.
examples.translation: Uncle: Only seldom now. I am already tired.

explanations.title: Dialog B: a goddaughter talks to her godfather about favorite pastimes

examples.text: Ninong, ano po ang paborito n’yong libangan ni Ninang?
examples.translation: Goddaughter: Ninong, what is your and Ninang’s favorite hobby?

examples.text: Paminsan-minsan, nagmamadyong at nagbabaraha kami.
examples.translation: Godfather: Sometimes we play mahjong and cards.

examples.text: Saan po?
examples.translation: Goddaughter: Where?

examples.text: Sa bahay lang.
examples.translation: Godfather: Just at home.

examples.text: ’Nung kabataan n’yo po, ano po ang gustung-gusto n’yong libangan?
examples.translation: Goddaughter: When you were young, what hobby did you like very much?

examples.text: Gustung-gusto kong mangisda. Nag-aalaga din ako ng hayop at nagtatanim ng halaman.
examples.translation: Godfather: I liked fishing very much. I also raised animals and grew plants.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Paborito, musika and baraha are Spanish cognates. Pinakagusto is another word for gustung-gusto in Dialog B. A synonym of mangisda is mamingwit.

rows: A1. What two questions does the niece ask her uncle?
Uncle, what is your favorite hobby? Nowadays, what is your hobby?
A2. What were the uncle’s favorite hobbies before and what are they now?
Before, he played the piano and saxophone; now he listens to music, reads newspapers and books and watches the news.
A3. How often does the uncle play the piano and saxophone now, and why?
Very seldom, because he is tired.
B4. What two questions does the goddaughter ask?
What are your and Ninang’s favorite hobbies? When you were younger, what hobby did you like most?
B5. What two hobbies does the godfather currently enjoy?
B6. What three hobbies did the godfather enjoy most when he was younger?

lessons.subtitle: nakikinig, napapagod, matututo, masasanay · tumutugtog, nagbabasa, nagbibisikleta

explanations.title: Ma verbs
explanations.body: Some ma verbs focus on the doer and others on the object. This lesson covers ma verbs that focus on the doer: the prefix ma means “to do something” and expresses various kinds of action. Examples from the presentation:

examples.text: Nakikinig na lang ako ng musika at nanonood ng balita.
examples.translation: I just listen to music and watch the news.

examples.text: Napapagod na ako.
examples.translation: I am already tired.

examples.text: Masasanay ka rin.
examples.translation: You will get used to it, too.

examples.text: Interesado akong matuto.
examples.translation: I am interested in learning.

explanations.title: Ma verb conjugation
explanations.body: Ma verbs are conjugated like mag verbs. Past tense: change ma to na. Present: keep na and reduplicate the first syllable of the root. Future: ma plus the first syllable of the root repeated plus the root.

explanations.title: Sentence pattern of ma doer focus
explanations.body: The pattern is: ma verb, marker (if any), doer, marker, rest of the sentence. Set III markers are used if the action is directed toward a person or a place, and Set II markers if there is a direct or indirect object in the sentence. The book’s examples:

examples.text: Nakikinig na lang ako ng musika.
examples.translation: I just listen to music.

examples.text: Nakikinig na lang si Lolo kay Lola.
examples.translation: Grandfather just listens to Grandmother.

examples.text: Napapagod na ako.
examples.translation: I am already tired.

examples.text: Matututo kayo ng Tagalog.
examples.translation: You will learn Tagalog.

examples.text: Matututo kami kay Ginang Vargas.
examples.translation: We will learn from Mrs. Vargas.

examples.text: Nanonood si Mercedita ng sine.
examples.translation: Mercedita watches a movie.

explanations.title: Review: um and mag verbs about hobbies
explanations.body: Identify them and their tenses, and translate (the book’s key):

examples.text: Dati, tumutugtog ako ng piano at saxophone.
examples.translation: In the past, I played the piano and saxophone.

examples.text: Ngayon, nakikinig na lang ako ng musika, nagbabasa ng diyaryo o libro, at nanonood ng balita.
examples.translation: Now I just listen to music, read the newspaper or books and watch the news.

examples.text: Hindi na po kayo nagpa-piano at nagsa-saxophone?
examples.translation: You no longer play the piano or the saxophone?

examples.text: Napapagod na ako.
examples.translation: I am already getting tired.

examples.text: Paminsan-minsan, nagmamadyong at nagbabaraha kami.
examples.translation: From time to time, we play mahjong and cards.

examples.text: Gustung-gusto kong lumangoy sa ilog.
examples.translation: I like to swim in the river very much.

examples.text: Nag-aalaga din ako ng hayop at nagtatanim ng halaman.
examples.translation: I also take care of animals and grow plants.

examples.text: Mahilig ka palang maggantsilyo?
examples.translation: So you are fond of crocheting?

examples.text: Si Nanay ang nagturo sa akin.
examples.translation: Mother was the one who taught me.

examples.text: Marunong ka bang magbisikleta?
examples.translation: Do you know how to ride a bike?

examples.text: Interesado akong matuto.
examples.translation: I am interested in learning.

examples.text: Turuan mo naman akong magbisikleta.
examples.translation: Teach me how to ride a bike, please.

explanations.title: Activity 2: choose the correct form (the book’s key)
explanations.body: The book’s key is: nagbibisikleta, magtatanim, any of the three forms, nagmadyong, mag-exercise, nagbabasa, makinig, magpiyano, masanay, nanonood. Completed sentences:

examples.text: Paminsan-minsan, nagbibisikleta ako sa parke.
examples.translation: Sometimes I ride a bike in the park. (nagbibisikleta: habit, paminsan-minsan)

examples.text: Bukas, magtatanim kami ni Lola ng halaman.
examples.translation: Tomorrow Grandmother and I will plant plants. (magtatanim, bukas)

examples.text: Tumutugtog ka ba ng saxophone sa Club Marine?
examples.translation: Do you play the saxophone at Club Marine? (the book’s key says all three forms fit: tumugtog, tumutugtog, tutugtog)

examples.text: Nagmadyong ang mga matatandang babae kagabi.
examples.translation: The elderly women played mahjong last night. (nagmadyong, kagabi)

examples.text: Ayaw niyang mag-exercise kasi madali siyang mapagod.
examples.translation: He/she doesn’t want to exercise because he/she gets tired easily. (mag-exercise)

examples.text: Tuwing hapon, nagbabasa si Roberto ng nobela.
examples.translation: Every afternoon Roberto reads a novel. (nagbabasa, tuwing hapon)

examples.text: Mahilig ka bang makinig ng musika?
examples.translation: Are you fond of listening to music? (makinig)

examples.text: Hindi ako marunong magpiyano.
examples.translation: I don’t know how to play the piano. (magpiyano)

examples.text: Gusto kong masanay sa pagtugtog sa banda.
examples.translation: I want to get used to playing in the band. (masanay)

examples.text: Alam kong nanonood si Lolo ng sine tuwing Sabado.
examples.translation: I know that Grandfather watches movies every Saturday. (nanonood, tuwing Sabado)
