explanations.title: Translate the sentences (Activity 4, the book’s key)

examples.text: Interesado akong matutong lumangoy.
examples.translation: I am interested in learning to swim.

examples.text: Marunong ka bang tumugtog ng piyano?
examples.translation: Do you know how to play the piano?

examples.text: Puwede mo ba akong turuang magbisikleta tuwing Sabado?
examples.translation: Can you teach me how to ride a bike every Saturday?

examples.text: ’Pag weekend, nanonood lang ako ng balita o nakikinig ng musika.
examples.translation: On weekends I just watch the news or listen to music.

examples.text: Nag-aalaga ako ng hayop at nagtatanim ng halaman tuwing bakasyon ko sa probinsiya.
examples.translation: I raise animals and garden every time I go on vacation in the province.

explanations.title: Numbers (Activity 5)
explanations.body: The book’s number tables for this activity are empty (the audio gives the numbers and no key is printed), so they are left out.

explanations.title: Passage 1: a woman talks to her uncle (Activity 6, the book’s script)
explanations.body: Key: she asks when he started playing the saxophone and piano; he started in his younger years, when he was in a band; he rarely plays now that he is old because he gets tired easily.

examples.text: Tito, mahilig pala kayong tumugtog ng saxophone at piano. Kailan pa po?
examples.translation: Niece: Uncle, so you are fond of playing the saxophone and piano. Since when?

examples.text: Dati, ’nung kabataan ko. Miyembro kasi ako ng banda.
examples.translation: Uncle: Before, when I was young. I was a member of a band, you see.

examples.text: Hindi po ba mahirap tumugtog ng piano at saxophone?
examples.translation: Niece: Isn’t it difficult to play the piano and saxophone?

examples.text: Sa umpisa, mahirap. Masasanay ka rin.
examples.translation: Uncle: At the start, it’s difficult. You will get used to it, too.

examples.text: Ngayon po, nagpa-piano at nagsa-saxophone pa rin ba kayo?
examples.translation: Niece: Now, do you still play the piano and the saxophone?

examples.text: Madalang na lang. Napapagod na ako.
examples.translation: Uncle: Only seldom now. I am already tired.

explanations.title: Passage 2: a woman calls a friend (Activity 6, the book’s script)
explanations.body: Key: she wants the man to teach her how to ride a bike; he likes biking, swimming and playing billiards (the book asks for two and lists three); he is willing to teach her to ride a bike; they meet Friday afternoon at the park close to the man’s house.

examples.text: Hello, Randy, marunong ka bang magbisikleta?
examples.translation: Woman: Hello, Randy, do you know how to ride a bike?

examples.text: Oo, naman. Magbisikleta, lumangoy, at magbilyar ang paborito kong libangan.
examples.translation: Man: Of course. Biking, swimming and playing billiards are my favorite hobbies.

examples.text: Interesado akong matutong magbisikleta. Puwede mo ba akong turuan?
examples.translation: Woman: I am interested in learning to ride a bike. Can you teach me?

examples.text: Siyempre naman. Bakante ako tuwing Biyernes ng hapon.
examples.translation: Man: Of course. I am free every Friday afternoon.

examples.text: Sige, bakante din ako sa Biyernes. Saan?
examples.translation: Woman: All right, I am free on Friday too. Where?

examples.text: Sa parke, malapit sa bahay namin.
examples.translation: Man: At the park, near our house.

examples.text: Sige. Salamat.
examples.translation: Woman: All right. Thanks.

explanations.title: The Macapagal family’s hobbies (Activity 7, the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: The book’s chart: grandfather plays mahjong; grandmother plays mahjong and cards; father reads books and listens to music; mother crochets and gardens; oldest sister bikes; oldest brother plays basketball; youngest brother plays basketball, karate and boxing.

explanations.title: Liza and her mother (Activity 8, the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: they vacation next Saturday, December 20, in the Philippines; Liza’s youngest son wants to learn karate; the kids look forward to wakeboarding. The book labels the speaker “Aunt” while the question calls her Liza’s mother; Liza calls her ’Nay.

examples.text: O, Liza, kamusta? Kailan ang bakasyon n’yo sa Pilipinas?
examples.translation: Aunt: Hey, Liza, how are you? When is your vacation in the Philippines?

examples.text: Sa susunod na Sabado po, sa a-beynte po ng Disyembre, ’Nay. Sobrang excited na nga po ang mga bata.
examples.translation: Liza: Next Saturday, on the twentieth of December, ’Nay. The children are very excited already.

examples.text: Pupunta ba kayo ng Nuvali?
examples.translation: Aunt: Will you go to Nuvali?

examples.text: Opo, ’Nay. Gustung-gusto ng mga batang mag-wakeboarding.
examples.translation: Liza: Yes, ’Nay. The children love wakeboarding.

examples.text: Tamang-tama, paboritong libangan yan ng mga pinsan nila doon.
examples.translation: Aunt: Perfect, that is their cousins’ favorite hobby there.

examples.text: Oo nga, ’Nay. Si Bunso nga, magpapaturo daw rin ng karate sa Tito niya.
examples.translation: Liza: Yes indeed, ’Nay. Bunso will reportedly ask his uncle to teach him karate, too.

examples.text: Ang hilig-hilig naman kasi ni Tito niya sa karate. O, sige, ingat kayo. Kamusta na lang sa mga bata. Good luck sa bakasyon.
examples.translation: Aunt: His uncle is very fond of karate, you see. All right, take care. Say hello to the children. Good luck on the vacation.

explanations.title: Activity 9: hobbies with your host family
explanations.body: The book gives English prompts for pair work; the Tagalog below is a sample of how the exchange can go.

examples.text: Ano po ang paborito n’yong libangan?
examples.translation: You: What are your favorite hobbies?

examples.text: Noong bata pa ako, nagbibisikleta, naglalakad sa bundok, lumalangoy, at naggagantsilyo ako.
examples.translation: Host: When I was younger, I biked, hiked, swam and crocheted. (the book’s prompt: biking, hiking, swimming, crocheting)

examples.text: Ano po ang mga bagong libangan n’yo?
examples.translation: You: What are your new hobbies?

examples.text: Nagbabasa ako ng libro at diyaryo, nanonood ng TV, at nakikinig ng musika.
examples.translation: Host: I read books and newspapers, watch TV and listen to music.

examples.text: Mahilig po ba kayong magluto?
examples.translation: You: Are you fond of cooking?

examples.text: Oo, gustung-gusto kong magluto.
examples.translation: Host: Yes, I like cooking very much.

examples.text: Puwede po ba ninyo akong turuang magluto?
examples.translation: You: Can you teach me how to cook?

examples.text: Oo naman, puwede.
examples.translation: Host: Yes, of course, I can.

explanations.title: Activity 10: a friend who is a professional biker

examples.text: Paano ba maging magaling sa pagbibisikleta, tulad mo?
examples.translation: You: How can one be good at biking, like you?

examples.text: Madali lang. Kailangan mo lang ng oras para mag-ensayo.
examples.translation: Friend: It’s easy. You just need time to practice.

examples.text: Gaano kadalas ang ensayo?
examples.translation: You: How often is the practice?

examples.text: Para sa nagsisimula, puwede na ang isang beses isang linggo.
examples.translation: Friend: For a beginner, once a week is fine.

examples.text: Puwede mo ba akong turuan?
examples.translation: You: Can you teach me?

examples.text: Oo naman. Magkita tayo sa parke sa Sabado.
examples.translation: Friend: Of course. Let’s meet at the park on Saturday.

examples.text: Salamat. Hanggang sa Sabado.
examples.translation: You: Thanks. Until Saturday.

lessons.subtitle: Ang dami-daming tao sa konsiyerto! · Sulit ang bayad ko sa sine! · Punta tayo ng konsiyerto

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: By the end of this lesson you can extract information about entertainment from reading and listening, transcribe and translate sentences and numbers about entertainment, use common expressions about entertainment, and ask and answer simple questions about entertainment. The structures are more ma, mag and um verbs, a review of may as “to have” and its other uses, and more intensified adjectives.

explanations.title: Getting started
explanations.body: The book shows common forms of entertainment (pictures, left out) and asks for more. The teacher note explains that hobbies and entertainment use the same Tagalog term, libangan, and that there is a thin line between entertainment and hobbies.

explanations.title: Common expressions
explanations.body: The book prints expression 4 as “Ang mahal mahal”; the lesson writes the doubled adjective with a hyphen as in the earlier lessons.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Ang dami-dami, ang mahal-mahal, ayaw na ayaw, gustung-gusto and ang galing-galing are intensified adjectives. Tiket, konsiyerto, karera, paborito, Miyerkules, Huwebes and Biyernes are cognates. ’Di bale is the shortened Hindi bale (“It’s okay”). Palabas means “theater production” or “movie” in expression 5, and pelikula means “movie” in expression 7.

examples.translation: I really dislike watching scary shows!

examples.translation: I like watching children’s movies very much!

explanations.title: Review: may as the verb “to have”
explanations.body: May has the forms me, mayroon and meron and many uses; one is “to have.” Meron and mayroon always need the linker g; in Meron na akong tiket the linker has moved to the pronoun right before the noun meron is linked to. You do not need a linker with may/me. Right: Meron na silang tiket para sa konsiyerto. Wrong: Meron na sila tiket para sa konsiyerto. Right: May tiket na sila para sa konsiyerto. Wrong: May tiket na silang para sa konsiyerto. With meron/mayroon the personal pronoun subject follows right after the enclitic (na); with may/me it follows the direct object. Right: May tiket ako. Wrong: May akong tiket. / May na akong tiket. Right: Meron akong tiket. / Meron na akong tiket. Wrong: Meron ako tiket. / Meron na ako tiket.

examples.text: Meron na akong tiket sa karera ng kabayo.
examples.translation: I already have a ticket to the horse race.

examples.translation: They already have a ticket for the concert.

examples.translation: They already have a ticket for the concert.

examples.translation: I have money.

examples.text: May tiket ako.
examples.translation: I have a ticket.

examples.translation: I already have a ticket.

explanations.title: Review: may as “there is / there are”
explanations.body: The verb phrase “there is / are / was / were / will be” refers to the existence of something or someone in a place. May is not conjugated: tense comes from context or time expressions (kahapon, noong isang taon, noong isang buwan, noong isang linggo, kaninang umaga, kaninang madaling araw, mamayang gabi, mamayang hatinggabi, and so on).

examples.text: ’Di bale, may konsiyerto pa naman sa Huwebes at Biyernes.
examples.translation: It’s okay, there is still a concert on Thursday and Friday.

examples.translation: Is there a cockfight today?

explanations.title: Nell and her cousin (Activity 10, the book’s script)
explanations.body: Key: the conversation is mainly about a recently concluded concert; two descriptive ideas: the line is very long, and the ticket is a bit expensive but worth it; Nell’s last question is whether her cousin wants to watch the concert again; the cousin will watch it again if Nell pays for her ticket. The script prints konsiyeto in the first line; the lesson spells it konsiyerto.

lessons.title: 127. C8 L1 · Eid al-Fitr: Sitti’s blog and a conversation on Hari Raya
lessons.subtitle: Mahalagang-mahalaga ang pagdiriwang ng Eid · Abalang-abala ang lahat · Meron ka na bang ginawa?

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: By the end of this lesson you can recognize and use vocabulary about religious holidays in the Philippines, extract information about Christian and Muslim holidays and celebrations from reading and listening passages, transcribe and translate sentences about holidays and celebrations, and talk about celebrations and holidays. The structures are adjectives and adverbs with reduplicated syllables, and may as an indefinite pronoun.

explanations.title: Getting started
explanations.body: The book shows pictures of Philippine holidays and celebrations (Eid al-Fitr or Hari Raya Puasa, Araw ng Pasko and Undas) and asks what the holiday seasons depict (pictures, left out).

explanations.title: A. Sitti’s blog
explanations.body: A blogger narrates her experience celebrating Eid al-Fitr in her hometown in the province of Lanao del Norte.

examples.text: Sa mga Muslim, mahalagang-mahalaga ang pagdiriwang ng Eid al-Fitr o Hari Raya Puasa.
examples.translation: For Muslims, the celebration of Eid al-Fitr or Hari Raya Puasa is very important.

examples.text: Pagtatapos ito ng isang buwang pag-aayuno, o Ramadan.
examples.translation: It is the end of a month of fasting, or Ramadan.

examples.text: Araw ng pasasalamat din ito kay Allah.
examples.translation: It is also a day of thanksgiving to Allah.

examples.text: Bisperas pa lang ng Hari Raya, nagdadasal na kami sa moske.
examples.translation: Already on the eve of Hari Raya, we pray at the mosque.

examples.text: Tumatagal nang tatlong araw ang pagdiriwang ng Eid.
examples.translation: The Eid celebration lasts three days.

examples.text: Sama-sama kaming lahat sa kapistahan ng Eid.
examples.translation: We are all together at the Eid feast.

examples.text: Sa mismong araw ng Hari Raya, sabay-sabay kaming mag-anak na pumupunta ng moske at nagdadasal.
examples.translation: On the very day of Hari Raya, our whole family goes to the mosque together at the same time and prays.

examples.text: Abalang-abala ang lahat sa paghahanda ng masasarap na pagkain.
examples.translation: Everyone is very busy preparing delicious food.

examples.text: May mga regalo rin para sa mga kaibigan at kamag-anak.
examples.translation: There are also gifts for friends and relatives.

examples.text: Sunud-sunod ding dumarating ang mga bisita.
examples.translation: The guests also arrive one after another.

explanations.title: B. A conversation about Hari Raya
explanations.body: The book gives questions and sample answers:

examples.text: Meron ka na bang ginawa para sa Hari Raya?
examples.translation: Have you done anything for Hari Raya yet?

examples.text: Oo. Meron na akong ginawa.
examples.translation: Yes. I have already done something.

examples.text: Wala. Wala pa akong ginawa.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Ramadan is the month of fasting observed by Muslims throughout the world. Eid al-Fitr, Eid or Hari Raya Puasa is the Muslim celebration that marks the end of Ramadan; it is a regular holiday in the Philippines, and in many Muslim places in Mindanao, even in Manila, there are programs showcasing traditional Muslim dance and music. Mahalagang-mahalaga, sama-sama, sabay-sabay, abalang-abala, sunud-sunod and parehong-pareho are adjectives and adverbs with reduplicated syllables (grammar lesson). Sa mismong araw means “on the same day.” In part B, meron is an indefinite pronoun (grammar lesson).

rows: A1. What two reasons were given why Eid is important to Muslims?
It marks the end of fasting (Ramadan); it is a day of thanksgiving to Allah.
A2. What one activity is mentioned a day before Eid?
A3. What four activities are mentioned on the day of Eid?
The family gathers as one; they go to the mosque together and pray; everyone is busy preparing delicious food; gifts are handed out to family and friends.
B. What were the two questions about?
Whether the listener has done anything for Hari Raya; whether Hadja Normina said something about her plan for Hari Raya.

explanations.title: A. Leonora’s notes about holidays in the Philippines

examples.text: Mahabang-mahaba ang Pasko sa Pilipinas.
examples.translation: Christmas in the Philippines is very long.

explanations.body: The book gives questions and answers:

examples.translation: Will someone watch the house later?

examples.text: Wala po. Wala pong magbabantay. May pupuntahan silang lahat.
examples.translation: No, sir. No one will watch it. They are all going somewhere.

examples.translation: You, are you going anywhere?

examples.translation: Is anyone coming tomorrow to help prepare for Noche Buena?

examples.translation: I’m sure someone is coming tomorrow.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Mahabang-mahaba, magandang-maganda, iba’t-iba and masayang-masaya are adjectives with reduplicated syllables; walang-walang and sama-samang are adverbs with reduplicated syllables (grammar lesson). Undas is “All Saints’ Day.” In the Philippines, November 1 is Araw ng mga Patay (Day of the Dead), also known by the Spanish term Todos los Santos. Families visit the cemetery, tombs are cleaned or repainted, candles are lighted and flowers are offered; family members and visitors also play cards, eat and drink at the cemetery. It is a national holiday. In part B, the first may means “someone or somebody” and the third means “somewhere”; me and meron in lines 5 and 6 mean “someone or somebody.” Wala means “no one” or “nobody” in lines 2 and the last sentence, and “nowhere” in line 4.

rows: Christmas or New Year’s eve dinner
incomparable; can’t hold a candle to (idiom)
A1. What are the three holidays mentioned?
Christmas, New Year and the Day of the Dead (All Saints’ Day; the book’s key also writes All Souls’ Day).
A2. Describe Christmas in the Philippines.

examples.text: Sa gabi ng mismong araw ng Pasko, magluluto ako ng paborito ni Lolo na kare-kare. May misa sa gabi kaya magsisimba ako. Tapos, maghahapunan kasama ang lolo at lola ko. Tatawagan ko rin si Nanay at Tatay sa Amerika.
examples.translation: On the night of Christmas Day itself, I will cook Grandfather’s favorite kare-kare. There is a night mass so I will attend mass. Then I will have dinner with my grandfather and grandmother. I will also call Mother and Father in America.

examples.text: Excited na ako sa Hari Raya Puasa dahil magluluto rin si Ina ng mga paborito kong pagkain. May salu-salo sa bahay. Pupunta ang mga kamag-anak at mga kaibigan ko.
examples.translation: I am already excited about Hari Raya Puasa because Mother will also cook my favorite foods. There is a feast at home. My relatives and friends will come.

examples.text: Sa Undas pupunta kami ng mga pinsan ko sa sementeryo. Magluluto rin ako ng kakanin. Sabay-sabay kaming magdadasal. Wala kaming gagawin kundi magkuwentuhan, magtawanan, at magkantahan.
examples.translation: On Undas my cousins and I will go to the cemetery. I will also cook rice cakes. We will pray together. We will do nothing but chat, laugh and sing.

explanations.title: Reduplicated syllables
explanations.body: In Chapter 4 lesson 2 you met matibay-tibay (root tibay), marami-rami (root dami), malaki-laki (root laki) and maliit-liit (root liit): adjectives with a hyphen and duplicated syllables. In other words only the first syllables are duplicated, and if there are more than two syllables, only the first two. Examples: sari-sarili = just for the person concerned and nobody else; kani-kanila = respectively, individually; pake-pakete = by the pack.

explanations.title: Adjectives with reduplicated syllables
explanations.body: An adjective describes or clarifies a noun or a pronoun. Identify the reduplicated adjective and the noun it describes in each sentence from the presentations:

examples.text: Mahalagang-mahalaga ang pagdiriwang ng Eid al-Fitr o Hari Raya Puasa.
examples.translation: The celebration of Eid al-Fitr or Hari Raya Puasa is very important.

examples.text: Parehong-pareho ang Eid sa kapistahan ng Pasko.
examples.translation: Eid is exactly the same as the Christmas feast.

examples.text: Abalang-abala ang lahat sa paghahanda.
examples.translation: Everyone is very busy with the preparations.

examples.text: Mahabang-mahaba ang Pasko sa Pilipinas.
examples.translation: Christmas in the Philippines is very long.

examples.text: Magandang-maganda ang mga parol sa mga bahay.
examples.translation: The lanterns on the houses are very beautiful.

examples.text: Sari-saring panregalo at pake-paketeng paputok ang ibinebenta.
examples.translation: Assorted gifts and firecrackers by the pack are sold.

examples.text: Masayang-masaya rin ang putukan tuwing Bagong Taon.
examples.translation: The fireworks every New Year are also very merry.

explanations.title: Adverbs with reduplicated syllables
explanations.body: Adverbs qualify or modify verbs; they do not describe nouns or pronouns. Sabay-sabay and sama-sama tell how an action was done or how something happened. Identify the reduplicated adverb and the verb it modifies:

examples.text: Sama-samang pumupunta sa sementeryo ang bawat pamilya.
examples.translation: Each family goes to the cemetery together.

examples.text: Sama-samang nagsisimba ang bawat pamilya sa araw ng Pasko.
examples.translation: Each family attends mass together on Christmas Day.

examples.text: Sabay-sabay kaming mag-anak na pumunta ng moske at magdasal.
examples.translation: Our whole family went to the mosque and prayed at the same time.

examples.text: Walang-walang sinabi ang Pasko sa Amerika sa Pasko sa Pilipinas.
examples.translation: Christmas in America cannot compare with Christmas in the Philippines.

examples.text: Minu-minuto naming naririnig ang putukan.
examples.translation: We hear the fireworks every minute.

examples.text: Sunud-sunod ding dumarating ang mga bisita.
examples.translation: The guests also arrive one after another.

explanations.title: Activity 2: choose the adjective or adverb
explanations.body: The book gives seven items with choices such as gabi-gabi / sabay-sabay / unti-unti and prints only the labels ADV (items 1 to 5) and ADJ (items 6 and 7) with no key for the underlined choices, so it is left out; the sentences above show how the forms are used.

lessons.title: 130. C8 L1 · May as an indefinite pronoun: someone, something, somewhere
lessons.subtitle: May pupuntahan ka ba? · Meron akong ginawa · Walang nag-imbita kay Mayor

explanations.title: May as an indefinite pronoun
explanations.body: In earlier lessons you learned may and its variants me, mayroon and meron as “there is/are” and as “has, had, have.” As an indefinite pronoun, may means someone, somebody, anyone, anybody, something, anything, somewhere and anywhere. Wala, the negative form, means no one, nobody, nothing and nowhere. Sample sentences from the presentations:

examples.text: Meron bang sinabi si Hadja Normina tungkol sa balak niya sa Hari Raya?
examples.translation: Did Hadja Normina say anything about her plans for Hari Raya?

examples.text: Oo. Merong sinabi si Hadja Normina tungkol sa balak niya sa Hari Raya.
examples.translation: Yes. Hadja Normina said something about her plans for Hari Raya.

examples.text: Meron ka na bang ginawa para sa Hari Raya?
examples.translation: Have you done anything for Hari Raya?

examples.text: Oo. Meron na akong ginawa.
examples.translation: Yes. I have done something.

examples.text: May pupuntahan ka ba?
examples.translation: Are you going somewhere?

examples.text: May nagbabantay ba sa bahay ngayon?
examples.translation: Is someone watching the house today?

examples.text: May pupuntahan silang lahat.
examples.translation: They are all going somewhere.

examples.text: Meron bang darating bukas para sa paghahanda sa Noche Buena?
examples.translation: Is someone coming tomorrow for the Noche Buena preparation?

examples.text: Sigurado akong me darating bukas.
examples.translation: I’m pretty sure someone is coming tomorrow.

examples.text: Mayroon na bang nag-imbita kay Mayor para sa salu-salo bukas?
examples.translation: Has someone already invited the Mayor to the feast tomorrow?

examples.text: Opo. Mayroon nang nag-imbita kay Mayor.
examples.translation: Yes. Someone has already invited the Mayor.

explanations.title: Wala as the negative counterpart
explanations.body: Wala has no variant and requires the linker ng at all times.

examples.text: Wala. Walang sinabi si Hadja Normina tungkol sa balak niya sa Hari Raya.
examples.translation: No. Hadja Normina has not said anything about her plans for Hari Raya.

examples.text: Wala. Wala pa akong ginawa.
examples.translation: No. I haven’t done anything yet.

examples.text: Wala akong pupuntahan.
examples.translation: I’m not going anywhere.

examples.text: Wala. Walang nagbabantay.
examples.translation: No. No one is watching.

examples.text: Walang nag-imbita kay Mayor.
examples.translation: No one has invited the Mayor.

lessons.subtitle: Pinakamatagal at pinakamagarbong piyesta ang Pasko · Pansit at inihaw na isda · May salu-salo sa bahay namin

explanations.title: Activity 6: an authentic text (adapted from philstar.com)
explanations.body: The book asks for the main idea and two to four supporting details. Key: the main idea is that Filipinos celebrate Christmas for the longest time and in the grandest way; supporting details (any two): each house and street is adorned with lanterns, lights and other decorations; the Christmas celebration starts in September; stores overflow with gifts, decor, toys and so on; people crowd the stores to buy gifts for their loved ones.

examples.text: Pinakamatagal at pinakamagarbong piyesta ang Pasko sa mga Pilipino.
examples.translation: Christmas is the longest and grandest feast for Filipinos.

examples.text: Bawat bahay at mga lansangan ay punung-puno ng mga naggagandahang parol na napapaligiran ng makulay na Christmas lights at iba’t-ibang dekorasyon.
examples.translation: Every house and street is full of beautiful lanterns surrounded by colorful Christmas lights and various decorations.

examples.text: Walang tatalo sa Pilipinas sapagkat mula Setyembre ay sinisimulan nang ipagdiwang ang Pasko.
examples.translation: Nothing beats the Philippines because Christmas celebrations begin in September.

examples.text: Ang mga tindahan ay umaapaw sa dami ng mga iba’t-ibang klase ng laruan, mga damit, sapatos at mga panregalong pamasko kung kaya’t siksikan ang mga ito ng mga taong naghahanap ng ibibigay sa kanilang mga minamahal sa buhay lalo na sa kanilang mga inaanak.
examples.translation: The stores overflow with many kinds of toys, clothes, shoes and Christmas gifts, so they are crowded with people looking for something to give to their loved ones, especially their godchildren.

explanations.title: Activity 7: authentic radio excerpts (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: The book’s key for the holiday heard in each excerpt: 1 New Year; 2 Eid al-Fitr / Hari Raya Puasa; 3 All Saints’ Day; 4 Christmas Day. The percentage in the fourth excerpt is written in words.

examples.text: Ganito palagi ang eksena tuwing magbabagong taon. Walang tigil ang pagdating ng mga napuputukan. Para mabawasan ang ganitong insidente ngayong darating na bagong taon, sama-sama na ang DOH, PNP, MMDA at pamahalaan ng Bulacan.
examples.translation: The scene is always like this at New Year. The arrival of firecracker victims never stops. To reduce such incidents this coming New Year, the DOH, PNP, MMDA and the government of Bulacan are working together. (holiday: New Year)

examples.text: At sa paglabas ng bagong buwan o ’yung new moon kagabi sama-samang nagdarasal ang libu-libong kapatid nating Muslim sa Blue Mosque sa Maharlika Village sa Taguig para sa pagdiriwang ng pagtatapos ng buwan ng Ramadan o yung tinatawag na Eid al Fitr.

explanations.title: Activity 8, Passage 1: an aunt and her niece (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Key: the occasion is All Saints’ Day; three dishes (the book’s key): grilled fish, beef stew and stir-fry noodles; the aunt asks Mely to buy flowers at the market before proceeding to the cemetery.

examples.text: Hello po Tita, ano po ang dadalhin n’yo sa Undas?
examples.translation: A: Hello, Tita, what will you bring for Undas?

examples.text: O Mely, salamat at napatawag ka. Pansit at inihaw na isda.
examples.translation: B: Oh Mely, thank you for calling. Pancit and grilled fish.

examples.text: Tamang-tama, magdadala ako ng nilagang baka, kanin at kakanin.
examples.translation: A: Perfect, I will bring boiled beef, rice and rice cakes.

examples.text: Puwede ka bang bumili ng bulaklak sa palengke bago ka pumunta ng sementeryo?
examples.translation: B: Can you buy flowers at the market before you go to the cemetery?

examples.text: Opo, Tita. Walang problema.
examples.translation: A: Yes, Tita. No problem.

explanations.title: Activity 8, Passage 2: a mother and her daughter overseas (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Key: the occasion is Christmas; having everyone in the family together at Christmas will make the mother happy; Charice arrives on December 23. The script says a-23 for the date; the lesson writes it in words.

examples.text: Charice, tuloy ba kayong magpasko dito ng pamilya mo?
examples.translation: A: Charice, are you and your family still spending Christmas here?

examples.text: Opo, Nanay. Naka-book na nga kami e. Sa a-beynte tres po ng Disyembre ang dating namin mula San Francisco.
examples.translation: B: Yes, Mother. We are already booked. Our arrival from San Francisco is on the twenty-third of December.

examples.text: Tamang-tama na-mi-miss ko na ang mga apo ko.
examples.translation: A: Perfect, I already miss my grandchildren.

examples.text: Ano po bang pasalubong ang gusto n’yo?
examples.translation: B: What kind of pasalubong do you want?

examples.text: Hindi na kailangan. Ang mahalaga sama-sama tayong lahat sa pasko. Masaya na ako.
examples.translation: A: It’s no longer necessary. What matters is that we are all together at Christmas. I’m already happy.

explanations.title: Activity 9: Darwisa invites Susana (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Darwisa, a Muslim native of Bongao, Tawi-Tawi, invites her Christian friend Susana to a feast. In the dialog, sir and ma’am are honorifics referring to Susana’s parents. Key: the invitation is to the Eid celebration for Susana and her family; Susana and her siblings will most likely accept; gifts for Susana’s siblings and Susana’s favorite food await; Susana’s parents will not be on hand.

examples.text: Hello, Susana. Bisi ka ba bukas? May salu-salo sa bahay namin. Isama mo sina sir at ma’am, at mga kapatid mo.
examples.translation: Darwisa: Hello, Susana. Are you busy tomorrow? There is a feast at our house. Bring sir and ma’am, and your siblings.

examples.text: Ay, opo nga pala. Tapos na ang Ramadan. Sila Dad, nasa Maynila. Sa susunod na linggo pa ang dating nila. Pero, mga kapatid ko siguradong sasama sila.
examples.translation: Susana: Oh, yes, that’s right. Ramadan is over. Dad and the others are in Manila. They arrive next week. But my siblings will surely come.

examples.text: Tamang-tama naghanda ako ng regalo para sa mga kapatid mo. Nagluto rin ako ng paborito mong ulam.
examples.translation: Darwisa: Perfect, I prepared gifts for your siblings. I also cooked your favorite dish.

explanations.body: The book gives English prompts for pair work; the Tagalog below is a sample of how the exchange can go.

examples.translation: Host: Yes, it is also big. Different firecrackers are sold and there are lots of fireworks on New Year’s Eve.

explanations.title: Activity 11: role-play, Sitti invites Cristina
explanations.body: Sitti is a Muslim, older than her friend Cristina; Ramadan has just ended. Sitti greets Cristina and invites her to a small celebration at her house; says one or two things about Ramadan and Eid (fasting, thanksgiving); says the celebration is tomorrow at 12 noon and that she will pick Cristina up; thanks her for accepting. Cristina greets back, accepts the invitation, asks what Ramadan and the celebration are about, asks when and at what time, says she will wait, and thanks Sitti. Use the honorifics Hadja, Hadji, Tita, Tito, Kuya or Ate; the expressions Salamat po, Hanggang bukas, Pakiulit, Walang problema, Pasensiya na po; and the intensifiers gustung-gusto and masayang-masaya as appropriate (role-play, left out).

explanations.title: Activity 12: challenge yourself
explanations.body: Share one important celebration in your country and give three to five details about what you do with friends or loved ones (individual work, left out).

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: By the end of this lesson you can recognize vocabulary commonly used in engagements and weddings, answer comprehension questions in reading and listening about superstitious beliefs about weddings, talk about weddings and engagements using honorifics and the Tagalog expressions you have learned, and transcribe and translate sentences about engagements and weddings. The structures are the core vocabulary and a review of may/me, mayroon/meron and wala.

explanations.title: Culture note
explanations.body: Traditionally the groom is expected to spend more for the wedding than the bride; nowadays the bride and the groom may share the wedding expenses equally. In selecting witnesses (sponsors or godparents) some Filipino parents are concerned about the positions, titles or ranks of the witnesses; this is considered family pride.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Sagrado, importante, modista and irerekomenda are Spanish cognates. Sasaksi (root saksi) means “will witness”; saksi refers to a “witness” or “godparent.” Abay is the informal word for bridesmaid (abay na babae) and groomsman (abay na lalaki).

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Sukob is a Filipino superstitious belief that siblings cannot marry in the same year; it is believed that something unfortunate will happen to either sibling if the custom is violated. Kumpisal (confession) is a requirement of the Catholic Church for couples before matrimony. Traje de boda (also trahe) is the wedding dress. May masamang mangyayari means “something bad will happen.”

explanations.title: Comprehension check A: who or what each activity is for (the book’s key)

rows: Call the church or parish and change the wedding date; set a schedule for confession.
Go to the printing press and ask for a discount.
Make a reservation for two hundred people.
Call immediately; change the motif of the wedding to gold.

explanations.title: Comprehension check B: superstitious beliefs (the book’s key)

rows: Do not allow the candle to burn out.
Do not allow the veil to fall off.
Do not fit the wedding dress before the wedding.

explanations.title: Activity 1: an authentic text about a small-town wedding (summary)
explanations.body: The book prints a newspaper-column excerpt by Juan M. Flavier about the wedding day of Pitoy (source: philstar.com) and four multiple-choice items. The excerpt is not copied here. In short: the narrator is one of Pitoy’s ninong (godfather and sponsor); the bride’s parents were very strict and superstitious; right after leaving the church the couple had to eat sugar so that their life together would be sweet; the wedding had to begin at exactly 6:30 a.m.; and the narrator teased Pitoy that he could still back out. The book’s four items ask who the narrator is (godfather), what someone told the groom (that he could still back out), how the bride’s parents were described (strict) and what the couple had to eat after the ceremony (sugar).

lessons.title: 135. C8 L2 · Review of may/me, mayroon/meron and wala
lessons.subtitle: May kasalan sa simbahan · Wala kaming litrato · Meron ka bang pera?

explanations.title: Brief review of may/mayroon and wala
explanations.body: You studied may/mayroon and its negative wala in Chapter 6 Lesson 1. True or false (the book’s key, with the corrections):

rows: False. Delete maraming or may (May bisita rito / Maraming bisita rito).
The word maraming makes a sentence negative.
May is the translation of the word “to be.”
False. May is not the translation of “to be.”
With may or me we can use linkers.
False. Linkers are not used with may/me.
With mayroon you need a linker.
With may you need a main verb.
False. A main verb is not needed.

explanations.title: Translate with may/me, mayroon/meron or wala (the book’s key)

examples.text: May kasalan sa simbahan ng Santo Domingo.
examples.translation: There is a wedding at Santo Domingo Church. (also Mayroong kasalan sa simbahan ng Santo Domingo.)

examples.text: May limang pares ng ninong at ninang.
examples.translation: There are five pairs of sponsors. (also Mayroong limang pares ng ninong at ninang.)

examples.text: May magandang babaeng ikakasal sa labas ng simbahan.
examples.translation: There is a beautiful bride waiting outside the church. (also Mayroong magandang babaeng ikakasal sa labas ng simbahan.)

examples.text: May pareng naghihintay sa loob ng simbahan.
examples.translation: There is a priest waiting inside the church. (also Mayroong pareng naghihintay sa loob ng simbahan.)

examples.text: May puting kotse sa harap ng simbahan.
examples.translation: There is a white car in front of the church. (also Mayroong puting kotse sa harap ng simbahan.)

examples.text: Walang mga bulaklak sa loob ng simbahan.
examples.translation: There are no flowers in the church.

explanations.title: Sentences from Presentation 1 and 2 (the book’s key)

examples.text: Meron akong kilalang modista at parentahan.
examples.translation: I know a dressmaker and a rental place. (literally: I have knowledge of a dressmaker and a rental place.)

examples.text: May kakilala rin akong caterer.
examples.translation: I also know a caterer.

examples.text: Kung hindi pa, meron akong irerekomenda.
examples.translation: If not yet, I can recommend someone.

examples.text: Sabihin mo lang anak, kung ano pang wala o kulang.
examples.translation: Just tell me, child, what else you lack or don’t have.

examples.text: Huwag isukat ang trahe de boda at may masamang mangyayari.
examples.translation: Don’t try on the wedding dress because something bad might happen.

examples.text: Walang mawawala kung susundin ang pamahiin.
examples.translation: Nothing will be lost if the superstitious practices are followed.

explanations.title: Activity 2: negate these may/mayroon sentences (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Negating may/mayroon is done with wala (walang before a linked word).

rows: May natanggap kaming imbitasyon sa kasal nina Jose at Josefa.
Wala kaming natanggap na imbitasyon sa kasal nina Jose at Josefa.
Mayroon kaming litrato at video ng kasalan nila.
Wala kaming litrato at video ng kasalan nila.
May malaking regalo kami para sa bagong kasal.
Wala kaming malaking regalo para sa bagong kasal.
Mayroon silang isang linggong pulotgata sa Boracay.
Wala silang isang linggong pulotgata sa Boracay.
May malaking handaan sa Manila Hotel ngayon.
Walang malaking handaan sa Manila Hotel ngayon.
Mayroon ba kayong pupuntahang kasalan mamayang gabi?
Wala ba kayong pupuntahang kasalan mamayang gabi?

explanations.title: Activity 3: complete with may/me, mayroon/meron or wala
explanations.body: The book lists eight sentences with choices (for example 1 __ bulaklak sa kotse ng ikakasal, 6 __ na raw pagkain para sa handaan, 7 __ belo ang babaeng ikakasal) and prints no key, so the exercise is left out; Activities 2 and 4 show the patterns.

explanations.title: Activity 4: switch may/me and mayroon/meron (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Add linkers where needed: meron needs the linker (ba bang, ka bang), may does not.

rows: May pera ba kayo para sa kasal ninyo?
Meron ka bang pera para sa kasal ninyo?
May kakilala ba kayong mananahi ng trahe de boda?
Meron ba kayong kakilalang mananahi ng trahe de boda?
Mayroon na bang balita sa handaan sa kasal ni Jack?
May balita na ba sa handaan sa kasal ni Jack?
May pamahiin ka bang alam tungkol sa pag-aasawa?
Meron ka bang alam na pamahiin tungkol sa pag-aasawa?

explanations.title: Activity 5: um and mag verbs found in the presentations (the book’s key)
explanations.body: The book’s chart gives the infinitive, past, present and future: for magschedule it prints nag-ii-schedule and mag-iischedule.

explanations.title: Notes on the chart
explanations.body: Meron and me are colloquial forms of mayroon and may. Tawagan (to call on the phone) and palitan (to exchange) are -an/han/nan verbs taken up in later lessons.

explanations.body: None beyond the audio.

explanations.title: Transcribe five sentences (Activity 6)
explanations.body: The book plays five sentences (with wedding pictures); here are the sentences.

examples.text: May regalo ang ninong at ninang para kina James at Susan.
examples.translation: The godfather and godmother have a gift for James and Susan.

examples.text: Mayroong trahe de boda si Jessica galing sa Estados Unidos.
examples.translation: Jessica has a wedding dress from the United States.

examples.text: May mamamanhikan sa bahay nina Josefa sa Miyerkules.
examples.translation: Someone will come for the pamamanhikan at Josefa’s house on Wednesday.

examples.text: Mayroong isandaang bisita sa kasalan nina James at Nadine.
examples.translation: There are one hundred guests at James and Nadine’s wedding.

examples.text: May bulaklak ba sa simbahan sa araw ng kasal ninyo?
examples.translation: Are there flowers in the church on your wedding day?

explanations.title: Translate the sentences (Activity 7, the book’s key)

examples.text: Kailangan ng basbas ng mga magulang ninyo bago kayo magpakasal.
examples.translation: You need the blessing of your parents before you get married.

examples.text: Sundin ninyo ang mga pamahiin ng matatanda.
examples.translation: Follow the superstitious beliefs of the elders.

examples.text: Nagpareserba na si Chito ng hotel para sa tatlundaang katao.
examples.translation: Chito already made hotel reservations for three hundred people.

examples.text: May dalawandaang bisita ang dumalo sa aming kasal sa Baguio.
examples.translation: Two hundred guests attended our wedding in Baguio.

examples.text: Wala kaming wedding planner, kasi gusto naming magtipid sa gastos.
examples.translation: We have no wedding planner because we wanted to save on expenses.

explanations.title: A monolog about a wedding (Activity 8, the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: The book asks for two to four essential elements of information (EEIs) and the numbers heard. Key: Felisa Cruz is from Manila but lives in California now; she and Gene got married in Santa Clara, California; the wedding took place on June 27, 1999 at 11:00 in the morning; the reception was at the Santa Clara Marriott Hotel; there were 100 guests; there were two witnesses (her sister and Gene’s best friend); the wedding celebration was happy; they went to Las Vegas the day after. Numbers: June 27, 1999; 11:00 a.m.; 2 witnesses; 100 guests.

examples.text: Ako si Felisa Cruz.
examples.translation: I am Felisa Cruz.

examples.text: Taga-Maynila ako pero nakatira ako ngayon sa California.
examples.translation: I am from Manila but I live in California now.

examples.text: Gene Smith ang pangalan ng aking asawa.
examples.translation: My husband’s name is Gene Smith.

examples.text: Ginanap ang kasal namin sa Santa Clara, California.
examples.translation: Our wedding was held in Santa Clara, California.

examples.text: Ang seremonya at handaan ay ginawa sa Santa Clara Marriott Hotel.
examples.translation: The ceremony and reception were held at the Santa Clara Marriott Hotel.

examples.text: Noong ika-dalawampu’t pito ng Hunyo mil nobesiyentos nuwebe, alas-onse ng umaga ang kasal namin.
examples.translation: Our wedding was at eleven in the morning on the twenty-seventh of June, 1999.

examples.text: Isang daan ang mga bisita namin.
examples.translation: We had one hundred guests.

examples.text: Dalawa ang saksi, ang kapatid kong babae at ang matalik na kaibigan ni Gene.
examples.translation: There were two witnesses: my sister and Gene’s best friend.

examples.text: Masaya ang kasal.
examples.translation: The wedding was happy.

examples.text: Kinabukasan, pumunta kami sa Las Vegas.
examples.translation: The next day we went to Las Vegas.

lessons.title: 137. C8 L2 · Listening: Leah and her godmother, renting a wedding dress
lessons.subtitle: Iwasan mo ang sukob · Walang mawawala kung susundin ang mga pamahiin · Mas mura kung kasama ang mga abay

explanations.title: Activity 9, segment 1: the motif and the discount (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Key: the colors mentioned are yellow, red and blue; Leah got a discount by mentioning her godmother’s name to the owner of the printing press (the godmother is a friend of the owner).

examples.text: O, Leah, nagdesisyon ka na ba sa motif ng kasal mo, dilaw ba, pula o asul?
examples.translation: A: So, Leah, have you decided on your wedding motif, yellow, red or blue?

examples.text: Ay Ninang, pula na po.
examples.translation: B: Oh Ninang, red already.

examples.text: A, ganun ba?
examples.translation: A: Oh, is that so?

examples.text: Opo.
examples.translation: B: Yes.

examples.text: Humingi ka na ba ng diskuwento sa imprenta? Binanggit mo ba ang pangalan ko?
examples.translation: A: Did you ask for a discount at the printing press? Did you mention my name?

examples.text: Opo, Ninang. Magkumare raw nga kayo e kaya ho malaki ang diskuwento ko. Salamat ho, ha?
examples.translation: B: Yes, Ninang. They said you are comadres, so my discount is big. Thank you, okay?

explanations.title: Activity 9, segment 2: sukob (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Key: sukob was mentioned: when two members of the family get married in the same year, the superstition says something bad will happen to either of the brides; Leah is going to get married first.

examples.text: O, mabuti naman. E di ba may plano ring ikasal ang ate mo? Iwasan mo ang sukob.
examples.translation: A: Oh, good. Doesn’t your older sister also plan to marry? Avoid sukob.

examples.text: Sabi nga po, Ninang, bawal daw ikasal ang magkapatid sa iisang taon kaya nga po sa susunod na taon na po ang kasal nila Ate. Ang bait nga ni Ate, e.
examples.translation: B: That’s what they say, Ninang, siblings are not allowed to marry in the same year, so Ate’s wedding is next year. Ate is so kind.

examples.text: A, o, nauna kayo ’no? Okey.
examples.translation: A: Oh, so you go first, right? Okay.

examples.text: Opo.
examples.translation: B: Yes.

explanations.title: Activity 9, segment 3: more superstitions (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Key: do not fit the wedding dress before the wedding or the wedding might not happen; on the wedding day the bridal veil should not fall nor the candle’s flame go out; Leah says she will follow all the superstitions even when she thinks they are not true; her godmother says there is nothing wrong with obeying customary traditions.

examples.text: Hindi mo rin dapat sinusukat ang traje de boda baka hindi matuloy ang kasal mo. At saka tandaan mo, sa mismong kasal hindi dapat malaglag ang belo mo ni mamatay ang apoy ng kandila.
examples.translation: A: You also shouldn’t try on the wedding dress, or your wedding might not push through. And remember, at the wedding itself your veil must not fall nor the candle flame go out.

examples.text: Opo, Ninang. Susundin ko pong lahat ’yan kahit na minsan parang hindi naman totoo.
examples.translation: B: Yes, Ninang. I will follow all of that even if sometimes it doesn’t seem true.

examples.text: Aba, walang mawawala kung susundin ang mga nakaugaliang pamahiin.
examples.translation: A: Well, nothing will be lost if the customary superstitions are followed.

explanations.title: Activity 10, segment 1: renting a wedding dress (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Key: the bride-to-be is looking for a quality but affordable bridal gown for rent; the rent is cheaper if it includes the clothes of the bridesmaids and groomsmen and cheapest if it includes the clothes of the witnesses.

examples.text: Manang Gloria meron po ba kayong pinaparentahang mura pero de-kalidad na traje de boda?
examples.translation: A: Manang Gloria, do you have a cheap but quality wedding dress for rent?

examples.text: De-kalidad na traje de boda pero mura.
examples.translation: B: A quality wedding dress but cheap.

examples.text: Opo, opo.
examples.translation: A: Yes, yes.

examples.text: Oo, meron naman, kumpleto. Mas mura kung kasama ang mga isusuot ng mga abay na lalaki at abay na babae. Lalong mura kapag kasali ang damit ng mga saksi sa kasal.
examples.translation: B: Yes, there is, complete. It is cheaper if the clothes for the groomsmen and bridesmaids are included. It is cheapest when the clothes of the wedding witnesses are included.

explanations.title: Activity 10, segment 2: the pamamanhikan (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Key: the couple agreed that the fiancé would do the pamamanhikan, accompanied by his parents, to formally ask her parents for her hand in marriage; the fiancée believes in it because she thinks it is important to get her parents’ blessing; the shop owner agrees, saying it is important to get the parents’ blessing because marriage is sacred.

examples.text: E, namanhikan na ba siya? Importante ’yan.
examples.translation: B: Well, has he done the pamamanhikan? That’s important.

examples.text: Ay, siyempre po, Manang Gloria. Napag-usapan na ho namin. Mamamanhikan po siya kasama ng kanyang mga magulang. Siyempre po kailangan naman ng basbas ng mga magulang ko.
examples.translation: A: Of course, Manang Gloria. We have already discussed it. He will do the pamamanhikan with his parents. Of course, my parents’ blessing is needed.

examples.text: Kailangan talaga ang basbas ng mga magulang. Alam mo ang pag-aasawa, e, sagrado ’yan.
examples.translation: B: The parents’ blessing is really needed. You know, marriage is sacred.

explanations.title: Activity 11: inviting a friend to a wedding
explanations.body: Student A (PFC Martinez in the book’s card) invites PFC Cristobal (Student B) to his son’s wedding: ceremony at San Roque Parish Church, reception at A’s house afterward, April 15 at 10 a.m., children are okay. The Tagalog below is a sample of how the exchange can go.

examples.text: Ikakasal na ang anak ko at gusto kong imbitahan ka, Cristobal.
examples.translation: A: My son is getting married and I want to invite you, Cristobal.

examples.text: Salamat po. Kailan po at saan ang kasal?
examples.translation: B: Thank you. When and where is the wedding?

examples.text: Sa Abril kinse, alas-diyes ng umaga, sa San Roque Parish Church. Sa bahay namin ang handaan pagkatapos.
examples.translation: A: On April fifteenth, at ten in the morning, at San Roque Parish Church. The reception is at our house afterward.

examples.text: Gusto ko pong pumunta pero wala po ang asawa ko sa araw na iyon. Puwede ko po bang isama ang dalawang anak ko?

units.title: Chapter 8 · Lesson 3: Expressions related to life events

lessons.title: 139. C8 L3 · Post-it notes about a death and a baptism
lessons.subtitle: Pumanaw na si Ninong Serafin · Nanganak na si Mareng Dolor · Idaan mo sa bahay nila agad

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: By the end of the lesson you can recognize and use vocabulary commonly used in daily conversations about birth, death and baptism; answer comprehension questions related to births, baptisms, funerals and condolences; become familiar with the Filipino customs in life events; and ask and respond to questions about social occasions. The structures are the core vocabulary and a review of gerunds.

explanations.title: Getting started
explanations.body: The book shows pictures of important life events and asks you to add related expressions and traditional practices in Tagalog (the pictures are left out).

explanations.title: Presentation 1: post-it notes of a mother to her kids
explanations.body: Three notes: 1 for Noy, 2 for Tisay and 3 for Ding.

examples.text: Noy, umikot ka sa bahay-bahay at humingi ka ng abuloy.
examples.translation: Noy, go from house to house and ask for donations.

examples.text: Pumanaw na si Ninong Serafin mo.
examples.translation: Your godfather Serafin has passed away.

examples.text: Pakisabi mo sa mga makikiramay na sa punerarya Villa ang burol.
examples.translation: Please tell those who will extend condolences that the wake is at Villa Funeral Home.

examples.text: Ipaalala mo, magpapamisa din tayo.
examples.translation: Remind them that we will also offer a mass.

examples.text: Tisay, bumili ka ng lobo.
examples.translation: Tisay, buy a balloon.

examples.text: Nanganak na si Mareng Dolor.
examples.translation: Mareng Dolor has given birth.

examples.text: Iniluwal niya nang normal ang bata.
examples.translation: She gave birth to the child normally.

examples.text: Hawig daw sa ama.
examples.translation: The baby reportedly looks like the father.

examples.text: Binyag pala ni Xavier.
examples.translation: So it is Xavier’s baptism.

examples.text: Bumili ka ng keyk. Idaan mo sa bahay nila agad.
examples.translation: Buy a cake. Drop it off at their house right away.

examples.text: Ding, dumaan ka sa bahay ni Tinoy, ’yung naulilang anak ni Aling Ining.
examples.translation: Ding, pass by the house of Tinoy, the orphaned child of Aling Ining.

examples.text: Ibigay mo ’yung koronang bulaklak.
examples.translation: Give him the floral wreath.

examples.text: Pakisabi na nakikiramay ang buong barangay sa pagyao ni Aling Ining.
examples.translation: Please say that the whole barangay extends its condolences on the passing of Aling Ining.

examples.text: Itanong mo na rin kung kailan ang libing.
examples.translation: Also ask when the burial is.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: In note 1, bahay-bahay (literally house to house) means “neighborhood.” Umikot, humingi, pumanaw, bumili and dumaan are um verbs. Makikiramay and nanganak are ma verbs. Naulilang anak in note 3 means “orphaned child” or “surviving child” and pagyao means “death.” Idaan means to “drop something off”: Idaan mo ang keyk sa bahay nila agad means “Drop the cake off at their house right away.” Dumaan means to “pass by”: Dumaan ka sa bahay ni Tinoy means “Pass by Tinoy’s house.”

rows: 1. What three instructions were asked of Noy?

To go from house to house and ask for donations; to inform those who wanted to grieve with the family of Serafin that the wake will be at Villa Funeral Homes; and to remind Noy’s mom that they will also offer a mass for Serafin.
2. What is Noy’s relationship to the deceased?
The orphaned child of Aling Ining.
4. What four instructions were asked of Ding?
To pass by Tinoy’s house; to bring the wreath for the dead; to kindly inform Tinoy that the entire barangay is grieving for the loss of his mom; and to ask Tinoy when the burial will be.
5. From whom did the newborn get his or her features?
6. What two things were asked of Tisay to buy?

explanations.title: Culture note
explanations.body: According to Muslim burial traditions, the dead should be buried within twenty-four hours, before sunset. In the Christian tradition in the Philippines, there is first a nine-day prayer period and then a mass and celebration on the fortieth day after the person has died. It is believed that on the fortieth day the soul of the deceased departs from the body and goes to an afterlife: heaven, purgatory or hell.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Ang isinusuot means “the clothes they are wearing”; here it refers to the white or black color. Pag-eembalsamo, pagpanaw, pagbababang-luksa, pagsusuot, pagdadalamhati and paggunita are gerunds (taken up in the grammar section). Kristiyano, puwede, simbolo, misa, nobena, seremonya and oras are Spanish cognates.

explanations.title: Comprehension check (the book’s key)
explanations.body: 1. Muslim burial rituals (four details): the ritual is simple; the remains are bathed and shrouded in white cloth; this is followed by a prayer; the body is buried within twenty-four hours; embalming is prohibited. 2. Christian burial practices (at least four): embalming is allowed; black or white clothing symbolizes grief; after a year, grief is supposed to end (pagbababang-luksa); there is food and gambling during the wake; other answers: nine days of novena prayer, and a mass and celebration on the fortieth day in remembrance of the deceased.

lessons.title: 141. C8 L3 · Gerunds from um and mag verbs
lessons.subtitle: Pag + salitang-ugat · pagdadalamhati · paggunita · pagyao

explanations.title: Gerunds from um and mag
explanations.body: Gerunds are words derived from verbs but used as nouns. English gerunds end in -ing: from go we get going, from vote voting, from run running (Marcie and I enjoyed going around the city; My favorite exercise is running). Tagalog gerunds are also derived from verbs but are formed differently. Examples from the reading:

examples.text: Simbolo ito ng pagdadalamhati.
examples.translation: This is a symbol of mourning.

examples.text: Ang pagbababang-luksa ay nag-uumpisa pagkatapos ng isang taon.

examples.translation: To Christians embalming is allowed.

examples.text: Bawal ang pag-eembalsamo sa labi.
examples.translation: Embalming the remains is forbidden.

examples.text: Pakisabi na nakikiramay ang buong barangay sa pagyao ni Aling Ining.
examples.translation: Please inform that the entire barangay is extending its condolences on the passing of Aling Ining.

explanations.title: Rules for forming gerunds
explanations.body: 1. Tagalog gerunds use the prefix pag. Pag is a constant: it does not change whether the verb is doer-focus or object-focus, and it is followed by the root word of the verb. 2. When the gerund comes from a verb conjugated with mag, duplicate the first syllable of the root (magdalamhati → pagdadalamhati). 3. When the gerund comes from an um verb, do not duplicate the first syllable (gumunita → paggunita). 4. Not every word that begins with pag is a gerund: pagkatapos (after) is not; pagkain (food) is not a gerund depending on its use; pag-alis is not when it is used in the recent perfective tense; pagsusulit (test) is a noun. 5. The gerund is usually translated as a regular noun: pagpanaw, from pumanaw (die), is literally “dying,” but we simply say “death.” 6. The pattern in a phrase or a sentence is Ang/ng/sa + gerund + ng/ni/kay.

lessons.subtitle: Isinilang na niya ang unang anak · Binyag at kaarawan sa a-kinse · Pakisabi na nakikiramay kami

explanations.title: Activity 6, segment 1: the birth announcement (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: the report is about the birth of Luis Miguel (son of Julia Santamaria and Francis Arcilla). The two dates are September 10, the expected due date, and September 8, the actual date of birth.

examples.text: A-diyes ng Setyembre ang takdang panganganak ni Julia Santamaria.
examples.translation: The tenth of September was Julia Santamaria’s due date.

examples.text: Pero kahapon, a-otso ng Setyembre, bago mag-alas-kuwatro ng hapon, isinilang na niya ang unang anak nila ni Francis Arcilla sa Asian Hospital, sa Alabang, Muntinlupa.
examples.translation: But yesterday, the eighth of September, before four in the afternoon, she gave birth to her first child with Francis Arcilla at Asian Hospital in Alabang, Muntinlupa.

explanations.title: Activity 6, segment 2: the baby’s name (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: the parents are Julia Santamaria and Francis Arcilla; the baby took his name from the deceased fathers of his parents.

examples.text: Luis Miguel ang pangalan ng panganay na anak ng mag-asawa.
examples.translation: Luis Miguel is the name of the couple’s firstborn.

examples.text: Ang pangalang Luis Miguel ay mula sa mga pumanaw na ama nina Julia at Francis, sina Luis Santamaria at Miguel Arcilla, mga kilalang artista ng kanilang kapanahunan.
examples.translation: The name Luis Miguel comes from the late fathers of Julia and Francis, Luis Santamaria and Miguel Arcilla, well-known artists of their time.

explanations.title: Activity 7, segment 1: the baptism invitation (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Key: baptism of the eldest child of Leo; November 15; 10 a.m.; Golden Meadows Clubhouse, Sta. Rosa, Laguna.

examples.text: Anak, eto ang imbitasyon ng binyag ng panganay na anak ni Leo. Hindi ba isa ka sa mga ninang?
examples.translation: Mother: Child, here is the invitation to the baptism of Leo’s firstborn. Aren’t you one of the godmothers?

examples.text: Oho, Ma. Kailan nga ba ’yon?
examples.translation: Daughter: Yes, Ma. When is that again?

examples.text: Sabi dito sa imbitasyon, sa a-kinse ng Nobyembre, alas-diyes nang umaga sa Golden Meadows Club House, Sta. Rosa, Laguna.
examples.translation: Mother: It says here in the invitation, on the fifteenth of November, at ten in the morning at Golden Meadows Club House, Sta. Rosa, Laguna.

examples.text: Naku, a-kinse rin pala!
examples.translation: Daughter: Oh no, it’s the fifteenth too!

explanations.title: Activity 7, segment 2: the birthday (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Key: birthday celebrant Jake; November 15; 7 p.m.; the celebrant’s house; Carmona, Cavite.

examples.text: E, Ma, a-kinse din ang kaarawan ni Jake.
examples.translation: Daughter: Well, Ma, Jake’s birthday is on the fifteenth too.

examples.text: Pero ’di bale, sa gabi naman ata ’yung handaan kay Jake.
examples.translation: Mother: But never mind, Jake’s party is at night, I think.

examples.text: Sigurado po ba kayo, Ma?
examples.translation: Daughter: Are you sure, Ma?

examples.text: Alas-siyete nga ng gabi ang alam ko e, sa bahay lang nila ng Ate mo sa Carmona, Cavite. Malapit lang naman.
examples.translation: Mother: Seven in the evening is what I know, at the house of your sister and them in Carmona, Cavite. It’s close.

explanations.title: Activity 8, passage 1: a teacher and a colleague (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: the donation for Usman’s family was handed to Ms. Vicente; the Muslim tradition of burying the remains within twenty-four hours was mentioned; the deceased is married, is Muslim and has no child.

examples.text: Ms. Vicente, eto ’yung abuloy ng klase para kay Usman. Pakisabi sa naulila niyang asawa na nakikiramay kami. Mabuti at wala pa silang anak.
examples.translation: A: Ms. Vicente, here is the class’s donation for Usman. Please tell his surviving wife that we extend our condolences. It is good that they have no child yet.

examples.text: Salamat po, Ginang Topacio. Opo sasabihin ko po.
examples.translation: B: Thank you, Mrs. Topacio. Yes, I will tell her.

examples.text: Ngayon na ba ang libing?
examples.translation: A: Is the burial today?

examples.text: Opo. Sa tradisyong Islam, kailangan pong ilibing ang labi ni Usman sa loob ng beynte kuwatro oras.
examples.translation: B: Yes. In the Islamic tradition, Usman’s remains must be buried within twenty-four hours.

explanations.title: Activity 8, passage 2: an OFW in the US calls her sister (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: the question asked was whether the food for the wake is enough; two traditions: the novena for the dead and embalming the remains; two instructions to Melissa: buy two wreaths and have a mass said for the deceased mother.

examples.text: Melissa, hindi ba kulang ang pagkain sa lamay?
examples.translation: A: Melissa, isn’t the food at the wake insufficient?

examples.text: Hindi po, Ate. Tama lang po kasi isang araw na lang po ang nobena.
examples.translation: B: No, Ate. It’s just right because there is only one day of the novena left.

examples.text: Magpapadala ako ng pera. Bumili ka ng isa pang koronang bulaklak at magpamisa ka na rin.
examples.translation: A: I will send money. Buy one more floral wreath and have a mass said as well.

examples.text: Okey po, Ate. Sa Sabado na po ang libing. Napaembalsamo na po ang labi ni Nanay.
examples.translation: B: Okay, Ate. The burial is on Saturday. Mother’s remains have already been embalmed.

examples.text: Huwag kang mag-alala, bunso, darating ako.
examples.translation: A: Don’t worry, little one, I will come.

explanations.title: Activity 9: guided conversation
explanations.body: Melissa calls her friend Tina to express condolences on the death of Tina’s oldest sister. A: express your condolences, ask the date and time of death and the cause; B: say the cause and the date and time; A: ask when the burial is scheduled; B: say there is no schedule yet, that the remains will be embalmed and that the nine-day novena starts tonight; A: ask Tina to extend condolences to her parents and siblings; B: say yes, say goodbye and thank her for the call. A sample of how the exchange can go:

examples.text: Nakikiramay ako sa pagyao ng panganay ninyong kapatid, Tina. Kailan at anong oras siya pumanaw? Ano ang ikinamatay niya?
examples.translation: Melissa: I extend my condolences on the passing of your eldest sibling, Tina. When and at what time did she pass away? What did she die of?

examples.text: Salamat, Melissa. Pumanaw siya kagabi, alas-diyes ng gabi, dahil sa sakit sa puso.
examples.translation: Tina: Thank you, Melissa. She passed away last night at ten o’clock because of a heart condition.

examples.text: Kailan ang libing?
examples.translation: Melissa: When is the burial?

examples.text: Wala pang iskedyul. Ie-embalsamo ang labi at magsisimula ang siyam na araw na nobena mamayang gabi.
examples.translation: Tina: There is no schedule yet. The remains will be embalmed and the nine-day novena starts tonight.

examples.text: Pakisabi sa mga magulang at kapatid mo na nakikiramay ako.
examples.translation: Melissa: Please tell your parents and siblings that I extend my condolences.

examples.text: Sige, sasabihin ko. Salamat sa tawag. Paalam.
examples.translation: Tina: Okay, I will. Thank you for the call. Goodbye.

explanations.title: Activity 10: role play, an invitation to a baptism
explanations.body: Student A (Severino) invites Pauleen, her husband and children to his son’s baptism: the son’s name is Severino III; April 20 at 10 a.m. at St. Joseph’s Parish in Tandang Sora, Quezon City; reception at Jollibee, a three to five minute walk from the church. Student B (Pauleen) accepts, asks the date, time and the baby’s name, asks where the reception is, thanks Severino and says goodbye. A sample:

examples.text: Pauleen, iniimbitahan kita, ang asawa mo at mga anak mo sa binyag ng anak ko.
examples.translation: Severino: Pauleen, I am inviting you, your husband and your children to my son’s baptism.

examples.text: Salamat, Severino. Kailan at anong oras ang binyag? Ano ang pangalan ng sanggol?
examples.translation: Pauleen: Thank you, Severino. When and at what time is the baptism? What is the baby’s name?

examples.text: Severino Ikatlo ang pangalan niya. Sa a-beynte ng Abril, alas-diyes ng umaga, sa St. Joseph’s Parish sa Tandang Sora, Quezon City.
examples.translation: Severino: His name is Severino the Third. On the twentieth of April, at ten in the morning, at St. Joseph’s Parish in Tandang Sora, Quezon City.

examples.text: Saan ang handaan?
examples.translation: Pauleen: Where is the reception?

examples.text: Sa Jollibee, tatlo hanggang limang minuto lang ang lakad mula sa simbahan.
examples.translation: Severino: At Jollibee, just a three to five minute walk from the church.

examples.text: Salamat sa imbitasyon. Magkita tayo roon. Paalam.
examples.translation: Pauleen: Thank you for the invitation. See you there. Goodbye.

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: By the end of the lesson you can recognize vocabulary commonly used in relation to the weather, answer comprehension questions about weather-related passages in reading and listening, describe the weather conditions of specified places and talk about weather conditions using the vocabulary learned. The structures are the core vocabulary and ma adjectives related to weather conditions.

explanations.title: Getting started: a radio weather forecast for the week in Manila
explanations.body: The book plays a radio forecast and asks you to label five pictures for the days Lunes (Monday) to Biyernes (Friday) with makulimlim (overcast), maulan (rainy), maaraw (sunny), maulap (cloudy) and bahagyang maulap (partly cloudy). The pictures are left out; the forecast script is:

examples.text: Ngayong Lunes magiging makulimlim ang panahon.
examples.translation: This Monday the weather will be overcast.

examples.text: Sa Martes, ang panahon ay magiging maulan.
examples.translation: On Tuesday the weather will be rainy.

examples.text: Masarap mamasyal sa Miyerkules dahil maaraw.
examples.translation: It is nice to go out on Wednesday because it is sunny.

examples.text: Magiging maulap naman sa Huwebes.
examples.translation: It will be cloudy on Thursday.

examples.text: Bahagyang maulap naman sa Biyernes.
examples.translation: It will be partly cloudy on Friday.

explanations.title: Presentation 1: weather updates from a government website
explanations.body: Weather updates from the PAGASA site.

examples.text: Maaraw at maaliwalas ang panahon sa Hilagang Luzon.
examples.translation: The weather in Northern Luzon is sunny and clear.

examples.text: Maulan at maulap naman ang panahon sa Silangang Visayas.
examples.translation: The weather in Eastern Visayas is rainy and cloudy.

examples.text: May pulu-pulong pag-ulan sa Katimugang bahagi ng Cebu na tatagal ng isa hanggang dalawang oras.
examples.translation: There will be isolated rain showers in the southern part of Cebu that will last one to two hours.

examples.text: Samantala, patuloy ang pag-iral ng hanging amihan sa Silangang Visayas.
examples.translation: Meanwhile, the northeast monsoon continues to prevail in Eastern Visayas.

examples.text: Ang Kalakhang Maynila naman ay makakaranas ng maulap na papawirin na may pag-ulan at ang agwat ng temperatura ay naglalaro mula beynte singko hanggang trenta y tres antas na sentigrado.
examples.translation: Metro Manila will experience cloudy skies with rain and the range of the temperature is estimated from twenty-five to thirty-three degrees centigrade.

examples.text: Nalusaw na ang namumuong sama ng panahon.
examples.translation: The developing low-pressure area has dissipated.

examples.text: Umiiral na lamang ngayon sa bansa ang habagat na nagdudulot ng mga pag-ulan.
examples.translation: Only the southwest monsoon, which is causing rains, now prevails in the country.

examples.text: May kalat-kalat na pag-ulan sa ilang bahagi ng Kanlurang Mindanao at medyo may kalakasan ang hangin.
examples.translation: There are scattered rain showers in some parts of Western Mindanao and the wind is moderately strong.

explanations.title: Note on PAGASA
explanations.body: The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) is part of the Department of Science and Technology (DOST). It is responsible for monitoring, analyzing, forecasting and giving warnings about tropical weather systems.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: The Tagalog term for DOST is Kagawaran ng Agham at Teknolohiya; the cognate for agham (science) is siyensiya. Learn the directions: Hilaga (north), Silangan (east), Timog (south) and Kanluran (west). In maulap na papawirin, papawirin literally means “atmosphere”; idiomatically the phrase is “cloudy skies.” Naglalaro literally means “playing”; in this context it means “estimated.” Pulu-pulong pag-ulan (isolated rain showers) means only 10 to 20 percent of the forecast area will receive measurable rainfall, while kalat-kalat na pag-ulan (scattered rain showers) refers to 30 to 50 percent. The other term is manaka-nakang pag-ulan (paminsan-minsang pag-ulan), meaning “sporadic” or “occasional” rain showers.

explanations.title: Presentation 2: a Facebook post of a Filipino nurse in Japan
explanations.body: Marynol writes about the different seasons and weather changes.

examples.text: Taglamig na dito sa Japan.
examples.translation: It is winter already here in Japan.

examples.text: Tuwang-tuwa ako nung nagniyebe.
examples.translation: I was very happy when it snowed.

examples.text: Ilang buwan na lang at tagsibol na rin.
examples.translation: In a few months it will be spring too.

examples.text: Excited na akong makakita ng mabulaklak na cherry blossom.
examples.translation: I am already excited to see the blooming cherry blossoms.

examples.text: Naalala ko nung taglagas, manghang-mangha ako sa makukulay na mga puno.
examples.translation: I remember that during fall I was very amazed at the colorful trees.

examples.text: Parang kailan lang sa Pilipinas, matinding bagyo at pagbaha lang ang nararanasan ko.
examples.translation: It seems not so long ago that in the Philippines I was experiencing only severe typhoons and flooding.

examples.text: Pero siyempre miss ko rin ang tag-init sa Pilipinas kasi lagi akong nasa beach.
examples.translation: But of course I also miss the summer in the Philippines because I am always at the beach.

examples.text: O sige, ’nay bukas ulit at matutulog na ako.
examples.translation: Okay, Mom, until tomorrow again; I will go to sleep now.

examples.text: Natuwa lang talaga ako kaya napasulat nang mahaba-haba.
examples.translation: I was just really delighted so I ended up writing quite a lot.

explanations.title: Note on Philippine seasons
explanations.body: The Philippines generally has only dry and wet weather. There is no winter, fall or spring. Cold weather conditions are experienced only in places at high elevations, such as Baguio City or Tagaytay City in Luzon and Bukidnon in Mindanao.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Napasulat (wrote unintentionally) is from a ma verb with the infix pa, signifying involuntary action. The mapa combination verbs are both actor- and doer-focused. The phrase parang kailan lang is idiomatically “it seems not so long ago.” ’Nay is a contracted form of nanay. Natutuwa, matutulog and namumulaklak are ma verbs.

lessons.title: 147. C9 L1 · Ma adjectives related to weather
lessons.subtitle: Maaraw · Maulan · Maulap · Mahangin · Makulimlim

explanations.title: Ma adjectives
explanations.body: Most adjectives start with the prefix ma. Ma is affixed to abstract nouns such as strength and other qualities that the root word expresses, and to concrete nouns to mean having much or many of the thing expressed in the root word.

explanations.title: Practice: identify the adjectives and their root words (the book’s key)

rows: The view on the mountain is beautiful.
Hindi masama ang magtapon ng asin.
It is not bad to throw salt.
Alam namin na marunong ang mga estudyante.
We know that the students are knowledgeable.
Hindi ko kaya ang mabigat na sako ng bigas.
I cannot carry the heavy sack of rice.

explanations.title: Ma adjectives used with weather conditions
explanations.body: Ma adjectives are also used with acts of nature related to weather conditions. Study these sentences from the presentations:

examples.text: Ngayong Lunes magiging makulimlim ang panahon.
examples.translation: This Monday the weather will be overcast.

examples.text: Sa Martes, ang panahon ay magiging maulan.
examples.translation: On Tuesday the weather will be rainy.

examples.text: Masarap mamasyal sa Miyerkules dahil maaraw.
examples.translation: It is nice to go out on Wednesday because it is sunny.

examples.text: Magiging mahangin naman sa Huwebes.
examples.translation: It will be windy on Thursday.

examples.text: Bahagyang maaraw naman sa Biyernes.
examples.translation: It will be partly sunny on Friday.

examples.text: Maaraw at maaliwalas ang panahon sa Hilagang Luzon.
examples.translation: The weather in Northern Luzon is sunny and clear.

examples.text: Ang Kalakhang Maynila ay makararanas ng maulap na papawirin.
examples.translation: Metro Manila will experience cloudy skies.

examples.text: Excited na akong makita ang mabulaklak na cherry blossom.
examples.translation: I am excited to see the blooming cherry blossoms.

examples.text: Naalala ko noong taglagas, manghang-mangha ako sa makukulay na puno.
examples.translation: I remember that during fall I was very amazed at the colorful trees.

explanations.title: Meanings
explanations.body: Except for masarap, mabulaklak and makukulay, most of the ma adjectives in these sentences are related to weather. Makulimlim means “cloudy, dark or overcast.” Maulan means “rainy.” Maaraw means “sunny.” Maulap means “cloudy,” and maaliwalas means “clear.”

explanations.title: Activity 1: complete with ma adjectives (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Word box: maulap, mahina, maalon, maaraw, malakas, maaliwalas. The completed sentences with the book’s translations (Activity 2):

examples.text: Darating ang bagyo kaya bukas magiging maulap ang tabing-dagat.
examples.translation: There will be a storm, so tomorrow the seashore will be cloudy.

examples.text: Mararanasan natin ang malakas na bagyo bandang alas-singko ng hapon.
examples.translation: We will experience a strong typhoon around five o’clock in the afternoon.

examples.text: Makakaranas ang Metro Manila ng maaliwalas na papawirin dahil wala na rito ang bagyo.
examples.translation: Metro Manila will experience clear skies because the storm is no longer in this area.

examples.text: Tumigil na ang bagyo, at maaraw na ang Kalakhang Maynila.
examples.translation: The storm ended and the Metro Manila area is already sunny.

examples.text: Ayon sa PAGASA, maalon na sa tabing-dagat sa Manila Bay dahil sa bagyong Lando.
examples.translation: According to PAGASA, the seashore will have huge waves due to typhoon Lando.

examples.text: Mukhang mahina ang hangin dahil wala na ang bagyo.
examples.translation: It looks like there will be light winds because the storm has passed.
