explanations.title: Culture note: the jeepney
explanations.body: The jeepney is the most popular and widely recognized form of transportation in the Philippines, called the “king of the road” because of its bulky box-type frame and the way drivers jostle in and out of traffic. It is actually a remnant of World War II: hundreds of American Willys jeeps were left behind, and Filipinos attached a roof, extended the length by two meters and added two rows of seats to carry more passengers, creating the earliest “share shuttle.” It dominated the narrow streets because it was flexible enough to weave through them despite its heavy frame, and sturdy enough to hold anything from fruits to animals on its roof.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Sana(ng), kaya, kasi(ng), na, yata, din, pang and muna are enclitics (explained in the grammar sections). Dakak is a famous beach resort in Dapitan in the southern Philippines. Habal-habal is a customized motorcycle which can carry up to twelve passengers. Roro in magroro is short for “roll-on/roll-off ships.” Mga in mga ilang oras and mga anim na oras means “about.”

explanations.title: Comprehension check, Dialog A (the book’s key)

rows: 1. What was the main idea of the conversation?
To know the cheapest way to travel to Dakak.
2. Which mode of transportation is the most expensive?
3. What five types of transportation were mentioned?
Airplane, roll-on/roll-off vessel, boat, customized motorcycle, jeepney.
4. What two advantages were mentioned for the alternative travel plan?
It is economical and there are many more places to see.
6. What did speaker 1 say about the alternative travel plan?
That the travel is a bit long and she will think about it.

explanations.body: The questions asked about the airline: which airline do you prefer; which airline do you not like; which of the two airlines is on time; which one is cheap; which one has quality service; which airline is grandma’s and grandpa’s; which airline did you choose.

explanations.title: Presentation 2: a telephone exchange between a travel agent and a client

examples.text: DDR Travel and Tours, magandang umaga po. Ano po ang maipaglilingkod ko sa inyo?
examples.translation: A: DDR Travel and Tours, good morning. How can I help you?

examples.text: Magpapa-book po sana ako ng biyahe mula Manila papuntang Kalibo.
examples.translation: B: I would like to book a trip from Manila to Kalibo.

examples.text: Balikan po ba? Kailan po ang alis?
examples.translation: A: Is it roundtrip? When is the departure?

examples.text: Balikan ho. Sa a-beynte ng Nobyembre ang alis at sa a-beynte singko na po ang balik.
examples.translation: B: Roundtrip. Departure is on the twentieth of November and the return is already on the twenty-fifth.

examples.text: Ilan po ang pasahero?
examples.translation: A: How many passengers?

examples.text: Dalawa lang kami ng asawa ko.
examples.translation: B: Just the two of us, my spouse and I.

examples.text: Magkano po lahat?
examples.translation: A: How much is it altogether?

examples.text: Tatlong libo’t dalawang daan kasama na po ang buwis.
examples.translation: B: Three thousand two hundred, tax already included.

examples.text: Tumatanggap po ba kayo ng credit card?
examples.translation: A: Do you accept credit cards?

examples.text: Opo. Siyempre po. Puwede rin pong cash. May opisina po kami sa mismong paliparan.
examples.translation: B: Yes. Of course. Cash is also fine. We have an office right at the airport.

explanations.body: Ano po ang maipaglilingkod ko sa inyo? means “How can I help you?” The other way of saying it is Ano po ang maitutulong ko sa inyo? Balikan means “roundtrip”; there is no equivalent term for a one-way flight in Tagalog. explanations.title: A. The enclitics: review
explanations.body: We took up some enclitics at the beginning of Semester I. Ho, po and ba are enclitic particles. Po and ho signal politeness and are equivalent to sir/madam; po is more formal and more polite than ho. Ba is an enclitic particle signaling a question. Opo and oho are not enclitics: they are complete words equivalent to a polite “Yes, sir/madam.” To say “No” politely, say Hindi ho.

rows: Na kina Tita po ang mga bata.
Where are the children? The children are at Auntie’s, sir or ma’am.
Are you from Missouri? No, I am from California.

explanations.title: Culture note: politeness
explanations.body: Filipinos place great emphasis on politeness and respect for elders. The first words taught to a child are opo and oho. They are also used by adults when addressing anyone older or higher in rank, and when meeting for the first time. Use these words until the person addressed urges you not to; this is a signal that the getting-acquainted stage is progressing to a more familiar level.

explanations.title: What each enclitic means
explanations.body: Sana means “hopefully, I hope or wish.” Yata signifies what on the surface someone or something is, “it seems,” “looks,” “appears”: Uulan yata is “It looks like it will rain”; Siya yata ang piloto is “It seems he or she is the pilot.” Yata never starts a sentence but can be used as a one-word answer: Uulan ba? Yata. (Will it rain? Looks like.) Native speakers say Tila yata (literally “It looks like it seems”). Sometimes yata means something else, as in Ako yata ang bumili niyan: it can be “It seems I was the one who bought that” or “After all, I was the one who bought that”; an exclamation mark instead of a period most definitely means the latter, the emotional meaning of yata. Muna implies “before you do or say something”; even though muna means “first,” it is not a substitute for the ordinal number “first” (una or pang-una, also pangunahin). Kasi means “because, it is because.” Na means “now” or “already” in affirmative sentences, and “anymore” or “not anymore” in negative sentences. Na is used with the past tense to show all the perfect tenses. The combination na naman means “again.”

explanations.title: B. The question word alin
explanations.body: Alin means “which” and signifies a choice, implied or otherwise. The uses with examples from the reading: 1. Alin with nouns and adjectives, followed by ang (Alin ang mura?); 2. Alin with numbers and with personal and demonstrative pronouns, followed by sa (Alin sa dalawang airline ang on time?); 3. Alin with verbs (Alin ang pinili mo?); 4. Alin as a modifier, with the linker (Aling airline ang gusto mo?).

lessons.title: 167. C10 L1 · Practice with enclitics: matching, completing, transcribing, a dialog
lessons.subtitle: Teka muna po · Sana may discount · Mga senior citizen yata ang mga boss

explanations.title: Activity 2: match the enclitics (the book’s key)
Activity 3: complete with the right enclitic (my key)
explanations.body: The book’s printed key for items 1, 3 and 7 is only a list of choices, so these are left out. The remaining items:

rows: Huwag naman sanang maraming tao sa istasyon ng tren.
I hope there will not be many people at the train station.
Hindi sana kami mag-eeroplano, pero sige na nga.
We were not going to take a plane, but okay then.
Wala yatang biyahe ngayon, hindi ho ba?
It seems there is no trip today, isn’t that so?

explanations.title: Activity 4: enclitics in five statements heard at airports and stations (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Write all the enclitics you hear and translate them.

rows: Mag-ingat po kayo sa mga bagahe ninyo.
Tapos na po ako sa security. Ikaw muna.
po, politeness; na, already; muna, first
Dumating na ba ang flight isandaa’t dalawampu? Sana dumating na.
na, already or now; sana, it is hoped that
May sukli ka na ba? Oo yata.
na, already; yata, it seems; ba, question enclitic
Sana hindi ka tumakbo, kasi nagmamadali kang umakyat.
sana, hope; kasi, it is because

explanations.title: Activity 5: write four questions with alin
explanations.body: Write four questions using the different uses of alin (the teacher gives feedback; the answers are open and left out).

examples.text: Sana bumili ka ng dalawang balikang tiket para sa paglipad natin sa Maynila.
examples.translation: I hope you bought two roundtrip tickets for our flight to Manila.

examples.text: A las sais y medya na ng gabi nang dumating ang tren sa Bikol.
examples.translation: It was already half past six in the evening when the train arrived in Bicol.

examples.text: Isang daang piso ang pera ko at sana makarating ako sa Maynila.
examples.translation: My money is one hundred pesos and I hope I can reach Manila.

examples.text: Sumakay kami sa taksi kasi huli na kami sa trabaho namin.
examples.translation: We rode in a taxi because we were already late for our work.

examples.text: Mag-ingat kayo sa mga paliparan, istasyon ng bus, at dyipni.
examples.translation: Be careful at the airports, bus stations and jeepneys.

explanations.title: Activity 7: read the dialog and translate the underlined parts (the book’s key)
explanations.body: The underlined parts, in order: 1. gusto ko sanang magpareserba ng biyahe papuntang Baguio (I would like to make travel reservations to Baguio); 2. teka muna po at titingnan ko kung mayroon kayong discount (wait first, sir, and I will see if you can get a discount); 3. nagbibigay ng discount sa mga senior citizen (gives discounts to senior citizens); 4. mga senior citizen yata ang mga boss (I will have you know that we senior citizens are the bosses); 5. heto na po, tatlundaang piso ang lahat (here, sir, three hundred pesos altogether).

examples.text: Mabuhay Travel, magandang hapon po. Ano po ang maipaglilingkod ko sa inyo?
examples.translation: Linda: Mabuhay Travel, good afternoon. How can I help you?

examples.text: Gusto ko sanang magpareserba ng biyahe papuntang Baguio. Airline tiket po.
examples.translation: Jose: I would like to make travel reservations to Baguio. An airline ticket.

examples.text: O, sige po. Ilan pong tiket ang bibilhin ninyo?
examples.translation: Linda: Okay. How many tickets will you buy?

examples.text: Dalawang balikan. Magkano po ba ang lahat?
examples.translation: Jose: Two roundtrip. How much is it altogether?

examples.text: Teka muna po at titingnan ko kung mayroon kayong discount.
examples.translation: Linda: Wait first, sir, and I will see if you can get a discount.

examples.text: Senior citizen po kami. Sana may discount.
examples.translation: Jose: We are senior citizens. I hope there is a discount.

examples.text: Ang Mabuhay Travel po nagbibigay ng discount sa mga senior citizen.
examples.translation: Linda: Mabuhay Travel gives discounts to senior citizens.

examples.text: Mabuti naman! Mga senior citizen yata ang mga boss!
examples.translation: Jose: That’s good! I will have you know that we senior citizens are the bosses!

examples.text: Heto na po, tatlundaang piso ang lahat. May discount na isandaang piso po.
examples.translation: Linda: Here, sir, three hundred pesos altogether. With a discount of one hundred pesos.

lessons.title: 168. C10 L1 · Listening: a voice mail, travel plans, a field trip and a booking call
lessons.subtitle: Magpareserba ka ng flight para sa akin · Matutuloy ba kayo sa Cebu? · Walo kami sa isang habal-habal

explanations.title: Activity 8: a voice mail by a mother to her son (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key (essential elements of information): the mother wants her son Andres to book a flight for her to the Philippines; she wants to go as soon as possible; the flight should be booked through PAL, leaving Saturday evening; the son can withdraw from their joint account to pay for the ticket; she asked him to call her after booking.

examples.text: Andres, puwede ka bang magpareserba ng flight para sa akin?
examples.translation: Andres, can you reserve a flight for me?

examples.text: Kailangan ko munang pumunta sa Pilipinas sa lalong madaling panahon, anak.
examples.translation: I need to go to the Philippines first as soon as possible, child.

examples.text: Tawagan mo ang PAL at kung puwede sa Sabado nang gabi ang alis ng eroplano.
examples.translation: Call PAL and if possible the plane leaves on Saturday night.

examples.text: Gamitin mo muna ang pera sa joint account natin para sa pambayad ng tiket.
examples.translation: Use the money in our joint account first to pay for the ticket.

examples.text: O, sige anak, tumawag ka sa akin kapag nakapag-book ka na.
examples.translation: Okay, child, call me when you have booked.

explanations.title: Activity 9, passage 1: an overheard conversation (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: the purpose of the call is to ask if the flight to Cebu will push through; the people traveling: mother, father, grandmother, uncle, aunt (not mentioned but implied), older sister, older brother, cousins, sister-in-law and brother-in-law; the caller’s flight is this coming Saturday.

examples.text: Oh, Charice, matutuloy ba kayo sa Cebu sa susunod na linggo? Sinu-sino kayo?
examples.translation: A: Oh, Charice, will you go through with Cebu next week? Who are you?

examples.text: Si Mama, Papa, Lola Belen, sina Kuya at Ate, at ’yung hipag at bayaw ko po.
examples.translation: B: Mama, Papa, Grandma Belen, Kuya and Ate, and my sister-in-law and brother-in-law.

examples.text: Lahat pala kayo aalis?
examples.translation: A: So all of you are leaving?

examples.text: Opo. Kayo po. Matutuloy po ba kayo ni Tito?
examples.translation: B: Yes. And you? Will you and Uncle go through with it?

examples.text: Siyempre naman kasama ng dalawang pinsan mo. Pero ngayong Sabado na ang flight namin. Kayo kailan?
examples.translation: A: Of course, with your two cousins. But our flight is already this Saturday. When is yours?

examples.text: Sa Martes na po, sa susunod na linggo.
examples.translation: B: It is already on Tuesday, next week.

examples.text: O sige, ingat sa biyahe.
examples.translation: A: Okay, take care on the trip.

explanations.title: Activity 9, passage 2: a mother and a daughter (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: Mom is asking her daughter to cancel her trip to Zamboanga; the reason is that the mother heard there will be a typhoon the next day and feels it is not safe for her daughter to travel; the mom’s suggestion is to take a plane to Zamboanga tonight.

examples.text: Anak, mabuti pa i-cancel mo na lang ang biyahe mo sa Zamboanga.
examples.translation: A: Child, it is better to just cancel your trip to Zamboanga.

examples.text: Nay, hindi po puwede. Kaarawan po ni Lolo Goryo. Hindi po puwedeng wala ako.
examples.translation: B: Mom, I can’t. It is Grandpa Goryo’s birthday. I can’t be absent.

examples.text: Hindi ka ba natatakot? May bagyo daw bukas. Medyo malakas ang alon, tatlumpu’t anim na oras pa ang biyahe. Matagal-tagal din iyon.
examples.translation: A: Aren’t you scared? They say there will be a typhoon tomorrow. The waves are rather strong and the trip is still thirty-six hours. That’s quite long.

examples.text: Mama, ika-cancel naman po ng coastguard ang biyahe kung talagang malakas ang bagyo.
examples.translation: B: Mama, the coast guard will cancel the trip if the typhoon is really strong.

examples.text: Ang tigas tigas talaga ng ulo mong bata ka. Mabuti pa mag-eroplano ka na lang ngayong gabi. Mabuti na ang sigurado.
examples.translation: A: You really are so hardheaded, child. It is better to just take a plane tonight. Better to be sure.

explanations.title: Activity 10, segment 1: a travel narration (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: the purpose of the travel was a field trip to Dapitan in Mindanao; the student took a jeepney from Dipolog to Dapitan, a distance of 21 kilometers or about 27 minutes.

examples.text: Taga-Batangas ako. Pero estudyante ako sa Maynila.
examples.translation: I am from Batangas. But I am a student in Manila.

examples.text: Unang beses kong bumiyahe papuntang Mindanao.
examples.translation: It is my first time traveling to Mindanao.

examples.text: Field trip namin sa Dapitan, Zamboanga del Norte.
examples.translation: Our field trip is to Dapitan, Zamboanga del Norte.

examples.text: Unang beses kong sumakay ng eroplano mula Manila papuntang Dipolog.
examples.translation: It was my first time riding a plane from Manila to Dipolog.

examples.text: Tapos nag-dyip kami mula Dipolog papuntang Dapitan.
examples.translation: Then we rode a jeepney from Dipolog to Dapitan.

examples.text: Malapit lang, mga dalawampu’t pitong minuto ang biyahe, dalawampu’t isang kilometro lang kasi ang layo.
examples.translation: It is near, the trip takes about twenty-seven minutes because the distance is only twenty-one kilometers.

explanations.title: Activity 10, segment 2 (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: it was scary but fun to ride a habal-habal for the first time, with eight people on one, from Dapitan to Dakak; the weather was nice because the field trip was in December, a good month to travel, not that warm, and the wind a bit cold.

examples.text: Unang beses din akong sumakay ng habal-habal papuntang Dakak.
examples.translation: It was also my first time riding a habal-habal to Dakak.

examples.text: Walo kami sa isang habal-habal.
examples.translation: There were eight of us on one habal-habal.

examples.text: Nakakatakot pero masaya.
examples.translation: It was scary but fun.

examples.text: Maaliwalas ang panahon dahil Disyembre nung bumiyahe kami.
examples.translation: The weather was clear because it was December when we traveled.

examples.text: Magandang bumiyahe kapag Disyembre.
examples.translation: It is good to travel in December.

examples.text: Medyo malamig ang hangin. Hindi masyadong mainit.
examples.translation: The wind is a bit cold. It is not too hot.

explanations.title: Activity 11: a client and a receptionist (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Main idea: the client wants to book a flight. Details: a one-way flight for three people from Laoag, Ilocos Norte to Manila; the passengers are two senior citizens, one student and a one-year-old infant; ten percent discount for the senior citizens and the student, the infant is free; the call took place in the afternoon.

examples.text: Magandang hapon po, magpapabook po sana ako ng flight papuntang Manila.
examples.translation: A: Good afternoon, I would like to book a flight to Manila.

examples.text: Saan po galing ma’am?
examples.translation: B: Where from, ma’am?

examples.text: Sa Laoag, Ilocos Norte po.
examples.translation: A: From Laoag, Ilocos Norte.

examples.text: Balikan po ba?
examples.translation: B: Is it roundtrip?

examples.text: Papuntang Maynila lang po.
examples.translation: A: Only to Manila.

examples.text: Ilan po ang pasahero?
examples.translation: B: How many passengers?

examples.text: Dalawang senior citizen po, isang estudyante, at isang taong gulang na bata.
examples.translation: A: Two senior citizens, one student and a one-year-old child.

examples.text: May diyes porsiyentong diskuwento po ang senior citizen at ang estudyante basta may ID lang. Tapos libre po iyong bata.
examples.translation: B: Senior citizens and the student get a ten percent discount as long as they have an ID. And the child is free.

explanations.title: Activity 12: guided conversation, booking a flight
explanations.body: Call a travel agency and book a flight for two from Manila to Cebu. A (travel agent): say the agency’s name and greet the client; ask the destination and dates; ask which time they prefer to travel; say 7,590.50 pesos including tax; say yes to credit card. B (client): return the greeting and say you would like to book a flight for two; say you want a roundtrip ticket for two on December 20 to 28; say in the morning between 5 and 10 a.m. and ask the total cost; ask if they accept credit cards. A sample:

examples.text: Magandang umaga po. DDR Travel and Tours po ito. Ano po ang maipaglilingkod ko sa inyo?
examples.translation: Travel agent: Good morning. This is DDR Travel and Tours. How can I help you?

examples.text: Magandang umaga rin po. Gusto ko pong mag-book ng biyahe para sa dalawang tao.
examples.translation: Client: Good morning too. I would like to book a trip for two people.

examples.text: Saan po ang pupuntahan ninyo at kailan po ang biyahe?
examples.translation: Travel agent: Where will you go and when is the trip?

examples.text: Papuntang Cebu po. Balikan po para sa dalawa, mula ika-beynte hanggang ika-beynte otso ng Disyembre.
examples.translation: Client: To Cebu. Roundtrip for two, from the twentieth to the twenty-eighth of December.

examples.text: Anong oras po ang gusto ninyong bumiyahe?
examples.translation: Travel agent: What time do you want to travel?

examples.text: Sa umaga po, mula alas-singko hanggang alas-diyes. Magkano po lahat?
examples.translation: Client: In the morning, from five to ten. How much is it altogether?

examples.text: Pitong libo limandaan at siyamnapung piso at singkuwenta sentimos po kasama ang buwis.
examples.translation: Travel agent: Seven thousand five hundred ninety pesos and fifty centavos, tax included.

examples.text: Tumatanggap po ba kayo ng credit card?
examples.translation: Client: Do you accept credit cards?

examples.text: Opo.
examples.translation: Travel agent: Yes.

explanations.title: Activity 13: role play, how to reach Boracay
explanations.body: You are a U.S. foreign language student in Manila who wants to visit Boracay; ask your teacher about the cheapest way. A (student): greet your teacher and say you plan to go to Boracay; ask about the cheapest way; ask the total travel time from Batangas to Aklan; ask how much; ask which month is good; thank her and say you will think about it. B (teacher): return the greeting and say Boracay is one of the most visited places by local and foreign tourists; say he can take a roro from Batangas to Calapan, Oriental Mindoro, then transfer to another roro to Caticlan, Aklan; travel time is about five and a half hours; the total cost for first class is only 1,400 pesos; any time except the rainy seasons of June and July. A sample:

examples.text: Magandang umaga po, Ma’am. Balak ko pong pumunta sa Boracay. Ano po ang pinakamurang paraan?
examples.translation: Estudyante: Good morning, ma’am. I plan to go to Boracay. What is the cheapest way?

examples.text: Magandang umaga rin. Isa ang Boracay sa pinakabinibisita ng mga lokal at dayuhang turista. Puwede kang magroro mula Batangas hanggang Calapan, Oriental Mindoro. Tapos lumipat ka sa isa pang roro papuntang Caticlan, Aklan.
examples.translation: Guro: Good morning too. Boracay is one of the most visited by local and foreign tourists. You can take a roro from Batangas to Calapan, Oriental Mindoro. Then transfer to another roro to Caticlan, Aklan.

examples.text: Ilang oras po ang biyahe mula Batangas hanggang Aklan?
examples.translation: Estudyante: How many hours is the trip from Batangas to Aklan?

examples.text: Mga lima at kalahating oras.
examples.translation: Guro: About five and a half hours.

examples.text: Magkano po?
examples.translation: Estudyante: How much?

examples.text: Isang libo’t apatnaraang piso lang ang kabuuan para sa first class.
examples.translation: Guro: Only one thousand four hundred pesos in total for first class.

examples.text: Anong buwan po ang magandang bumisita?
examples.translation: Estudyante: Which month is good to visit?

examples.text: Kahit anong buwan maliban sa tag-ulan ng Hunyo at Hulyo.
examples.translation: Guro: Any month except the rainy season of June and July.

examples.text: Salamat po. Iisipin ko po muna.
examples.translation: Estudyante: Thank you. I will think about it first.

explanations.title: Activity 14: ask each other questions about places to visit
explanations.body: With your partner ask each other questions about places to visit, with emphasis on alin. Refer to Presentation 1B as a model (open pair work, left out).

explanations.title: Activity 15: challenge yourself
explanations.body: Assume you have toured the islands of the Philippines. Using the images as a guide, narrate your experiences using different modes of transportation and include one or two weather conditions. Use habal-habal, roro, bangka, barko, eroplano, traysikel, nakakatakot, maganda, masaya, mahal, mura, tanaw ang dagat and other words (individual work, left out).

explanations.title: Words and phrases used for travel: sample sentences
explanations.body: The book’s sample sentences (clock times written out):

examples.text: Dahil alas-diyes ang alis ng bus, dumating siya sa istasyon nang alas-nuwebe y medya.
examples.translation: Because the bus departs at ten o’clock, he arrived at the station at half past nine.

examples.text: Sa Disyembre pa ang balik ko sa States. Magtatagal pa ako dito sa Pinas.
examples.translation: My return to the States is not until December. I will stay longer here in the Philippines.

examples.text: Kumuha ka ng balikang tiket. Mas matipid iyon.
examples.translation: Get a roundtrip ticket. That is more economical.

examples.text: Labindalawang oras ang biyahe mula Maynila hanggang Banaue.
examples.translation: The trip from Manila to Banaue is twelve hours.

examples.text: Kasama na po ang buwis sa halaga ng tiket ninyo.
examples.translation: Tax is already included in the price of your ticket.

examples.text: Hindi po kasama ang bayad sa drayber kung aarkila kayo ng van.
examples.translation: The driver’s fee is not included if you rent a van.

examples.text: Magpapa-book na ako ng dalawang kuwarto sa hotel ngayong gabi.
examples.translation: I will book two rooms at the hotel tonight.

examples.text: Upang makarating sa pulo, kailangan nating sumakay ng bangka.
examples.translation: To reach the island, we need to ride a boat.

examples.text: Pagdating sa pulo, manananghalian muna tayo.
examples.translation: Upon arrival at the island, let’s have lunch first.

examples.text: Isa ito sa pinakamalaking paliparan na napuntahan ko.
examples.translation: This is one of the biggest airports I have been to.

examples.text: Siksikan ang mga turistang pasahero sa roro.
examples.translation: The tourist passengers are packed in the roro.

examples.text: Walang-walang sinabi ang kalidad ng serbisyo ng Coron Gateway dito sa Busuanga Seadive Hotel.
examples.translation: The quality of service of Coron Gateway cannot compare with that of the Busuanga Seadive Hotel here.

examples.text: Sumakay kami ng balsa para makarating sa Nagata Falls sa Aklan.
examples.translation: We rode a raft to reach Nagata Falls in Aklan.

examples.text: Mas matipid ang magbarko kaysa mag-eroplano mula Batangas hanggang Caticlan.
examples.translation: Riding a ship is more economical than riding a plane from Batangas to Caticlan.

examples.text: Mag-eroplano ka na lang. Hindi naman malaki ang diperensiya sa presyo ng tiket sa barko.
examples.translation: Just take a plane. The difference in the ticket price to the ship is not big.

examples.text: Puwede ring mag-RORO mula Bicol patungong Kabisayaan at Palawan. Araw-araw ang biyahe, may air-con, higaan, kainan, disco, at bar o sports facilities.
examples.translation: You can also take a roro from Bicol to the Visayas and Palawan. The trip is daily, with air-conditioning, beds, a canteen, a disco and a bar or sports facilities.

examples.text: Malapit lang ang Basilica del Santo Niño sa hotel namin kaya hindi na namin kailangang magkotse.
examples.translation: The Basilica del Santo Niño is near our hotel so we no longer needed to take a car.

examples.text: Kung marami ang sasama sa biyahe natin, mas masaya sigurong magbus na lang ang buong tropa.
examples.translation: If many will join our trip, it is probably more fun for the whole gang to just take a bus.

examples.text: Isang oras na lang ang magtren mula Tutuban hanggang Clark.
examples.translation: Riding the train from Tutuban to Clark is now only one hour.

examples.text: Tuwang-tuwa ang kaibigan kong Intsik nang magkalesa kami sa paglilibot sa Intramuros at Binondo.
examples.translation: My Chinese friend was very happy when we rode a calesa touring Intramuros and Binondo.

examples.text: Puwede ka ring mag-taxi, mag-UBER, o mag-GRAB mula NAIA hanggang Bonifacio Global City kung hindi mo alam mag-commute.
examples.translation: You can also take a taxi, an Uber or a Grab from NAIA to Bonifacio Global City if you don’t know how to commute.

examples.text: Subukan nating maghabal-habal sa Palawan. Ito raw ang the best kung gusto nating mag-river crossing.
examples.translation: Let’s try riding a habal-habal in Palawan. They say it is the best if we want river crossing.

examples.text: Magtraysikel na lang tayo papunta sa Tagaytay Ridge.
examples.translation: Let’s just take a tricycle to Tagaytay Ridge.

examples.text: Mas mabilis kang makakarating sa simbahan kung magdyi-dyip ka.
examples.translation: You will get to the church faster if you take a jeepney.

examples.text: Kung high tide, puwedeng magbangka o kaya naman maglakad sa lumang footbridge papuntang Caloco Beach.
examples.translation: At high tide you can take a boat or else walk on the old footbridge to Caloco Beach.

examples.text: Kailangan naming magbalsa upang matawid ang talon sa Pagsanjan.
examples.translation: We needed to ride a raft to cross the falls at Pagsanjan.

units.title: Chapter 10 · Lesson 2: Lodging and accommodations

lessons.title: 170. C10 L2 · A hotel reservation and choosing a hotel
lessons.subtitle: Magpapareserba sana ako ng isang kuwarto · Alin ang malinis na hotel? · Libre ang almusal

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: By the end of the lesson you can recognize vocabulary commonly used in lodging and accommodations; answer comprehension questions about short reading and listening passages on lodging; transcribe and translate sentences about lodging; speak about lodging using the expressions learned; and use time words and phrases. The structures are the core vocabulary, the enclitics lang/lamang, raw/daw and rin/din, adverbial time words and phrases (part I) and a review of the question word alin.

explanations.title: Getting started
explanations.body: The book shows alternating hexagons with ideas about preferences of hotels and lodging houses in the Philippines and asks you to add related concepts in Tagalog (the hexagons are left out).

explanations.title: Presentation 1A: exchanges between a receptionist and a client

examples.text: Magandang hapon po. Ano po ang maitutulong ko sa inyo?
examples.translation: Receptionist: Good afternoon. How can I help you?

examples.text: Magpapareserba sana ako ng isang kuwarto.
examples.translation: Client: I would like to reserve one room.

examples.text: Kailan po?
examples.translation: Receptionist: When?

examples.text: Mula a-uno ng Enero hanggang a-siyete.
examples.translation: Client: From the first of January to the seventh.

examples.text: Para sa ilang tao po?
examples.translation: Receptionist: For how many people?

examples.text: Para lamang sa tatlong tao. Kaming mag-asawa at anak ko. Limang taong gulang lang siya.
examples.translation: Client: For only three people. My spouse and I and my child. He is only five years old.

examples.text: Narinig ko na may diskuwento raw kayo para sa mga sundalo?
examples.translation: Receptionist: I heard that you reportedly have a discount for soldiers?

examples.translation: Client: Yes. Also for teachers. Both have a ten percent discount.

examples.text: Ang galing naman! Tamang-tama ang promong iyan sa amin. Sundalo ako at guro naman ang asawa ko.
examples.translation: Receptionist: That’s great! That promo is perfect for us. I am a soldier and my spouse is a teacher.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Lamang, lang, raw, rin and naman are enclitics (discussed in the grammar section). Ang galing naman means “That’s great!” Promo(ng) is short for “promotion.” In hatid-sundo, hatid means “to escort or accompany” and sundo means “to pick up,” so hatid-sundo here means a free pick-up to and from the airport. Microtel and Sogo are two popular chains of hotels in the Philippines.

explanations.title: Comprehension check, Dialog A (the book’s key)
explanations.body: The book’s key is a little at odds with the dialog (it is the receptionist who says she is a soldier); the answers are printed as the book gives them.

rows: Magpapareserba sana ako ng isang kuwarto. (I would like to make a reservation for one room.)
2. Who will stay in the hotel?
Husband, wife and daughter (the book’s key says daughter; the dialog only says child).
3. What four promotional benefits are offered?
A 10% discount for soldiers and teachers, a free stay for kids, free breakfast, and free pick-up to and from the airport.
4. What is the occupation of the caller?
Soldier (the book’s key; in the dialog the receptionist is the soldier and the caller is her guest).
5. What is the occupation of the caller’s spouse?

explanations.body: The questions asked: which hotels are cheap; which one is Lucas and company’s hotel; which one is clean; which one has free breakfast; which did you choose.

examples.text: Sabi nila wala raw katulad ang Mission Bay Resort at Casino.
examples.translation: They say Mission Bay Resort and Casino has no equal.

examples.text: Nasa dulong timog ng Isla ng Cagraray at tatlumpu’t pitong kilometro lamang ang layo mula sa kabisera ng Albay.
examples.translation: It is at the southern tip of Cagraray Island and only thirty-seven kilometers away from the capital of Albay.

examples.text: Tanaw ang Dagat Pasipiko mula sa kuwarto ko.
examples.translation: The Pacific Ocean can be seen from my room.

examples.text: Kumpleto at moderno ang mga kagamitan sa loob. Pati ang pasilidad ng gym.
examples.translation: The furnishings inside are complete and modern. Also the gym facility.

examples.text: Malapit din ito sa daungan at paliparan.
examples.translation: It is also close to the port and the airport.

examples.translation: The place is quiet and peaceful.

examples.text: Malapit din ito sa kilalang Spice Market. Dito ko naman natikman ang iba’t ibang luto ng Timog-Silangang Asya.
examples.translation: It is also close to the famous Spice Market. It was here that I tasted the different dishes of Southeast Asia.

examples.text: Nandiyan din ang De La Playa. Para ito sa mga mahilig sa pagkaing-dagat.
examples.translation: De La Playa is also there. It is for those fond of seafood.

examples.text: Medyo may kamahalan ang presyo pero sulit naman.
examples.translation: The price is a bit expensive but it is worth it.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions (A)
explanations.body: Wala raw katulad means “incomparable.” Sabi nila means “they say” or “according to them.” Medyo may kamahalan ang presyo means “a little bit pricey or expensive.” “Gym” has no Tagalog equivalent.

explanations.title: Presentation 2B: two siblings book accommodation for the family
explanations.body: In the book each answer has many possible alternatives, listed in the table below; this sample dialog uses one of them each.

examples.text: Mag-book ka na ng hotel kina Mama at Papa.
examples.translation: A: Book a hotel for Mama and Papa already.

examples.text: Tapos na.
examples.translation: B: Already done.

examples.text: Kailan ka nag-book?
examples.translation: A: When did you book?

examples.text: Kahapon.
examples.translation: B: Yesterday.

examples.text: Nag-book ka na ba para kina Tita at Tito?
examples.translation: A: Have you booked for Auntie and Uncle?

examples.text: Hindi pa.
examples.translation: B: Not yet.

examples.text: Kailan ka magbu-book?
examples.translation: A: When will you book?

examples.text: Bukas nang umaga.
examples.translation: B: Tomorrow morning.

explanations.title: Adverbial time words and phrases (part I)
explanations.body: Other possible answers to Kailan ka nag-book? include ngayon lang, ngayung-ngayon lang, kahapon, kamakalawa, kagabi, kaninang umaga, noong linggo, noong isang linggo, noong nakaraang linggo and kamakailan lang. Answers to Kailan ka magbu-book? include ngayon din, ngayong araw na ito, ngayung-ngayon din, ngayong mga araw na ito, ngayon ding araw na ito, mamaya, mamayang gabi, bukas and bukas nang umaga. Noong linggo, noong isang linggo and noong nakaraang linggo (last week) are synonyms.

examples.text: Ngayong Biyernes, simula na ang Biyahe ni Drew sa tag-init at ang unang destinasyon ng ultimate biyaherong si Drew ay Pagudpud, Ilocos!
examples.translation: This Friday the summer Biyahe ni Drew begins, and the first destination of ultimate traveler Drew is Pagudpud, Ilocos!

examples.text: Puwedeng magmaneho nang sampu hanggang labindalawang oras.
examples.translation: You can drive for ten to twelve hours.

examples.text: Pero kung may pang-eroplano naman, apatnapu’t limang minuto lang ito mula Manila hanggang Laoag, tapos dalawa hanggang tatlong oras na lang ang biyahe sa daan.
examples.translation: But if you can afford a plane, it is only forty-five minutes from Manila to Laoag, then only two to three hours of travel on the road.

examples.text: Pagdating naman sa accommodations, may mga rekomendasyon si Biyahero Drew.
examples.translation: As for accommodations, Traveler Drew has some recommendations.

examples.text: Una sa kanyang listahan ay ang high-end Hannah’s Beach Resort and Convention Center. Sunod ang Kapuluan Vista Resort.
examples.translation: First on his list is the high-end Hannah’s Beach Resort and Convention Center. Next is Kapuluan Vista Resort.

examples.text: At kung talagang kapos ang budget puwede kang mag-homestay sa isang pamilya.
examples.translation: And if the budget is really tight you can do a homestay with a family.

examples.text: Pagdating naman sa kainan, hindi rin magpapahuli ang Pagudpud.
examples.translation: As for dining, Pagudpud will not be left behind either.

examples.text: Bukod sa tradisyonal na lutuing Ilocano sa Evangeline’s, sasampulan din ni Drew ang lutuing Aleman sa Bergblik at ang Italian fare sa Tartarugas.
examples.translation: Besides the traditional Ilocano cooking at Evangeline’s, Drew will also sample the German cuisine at Bergblik and the Italian fare at Tartarugas.

examples.text: At bago siya bumalik ng Maynila, dadaanan muna niya ang Kangkang para matikman ang crispy lechon at pinakbet!

lessons.title: 172. C10 L2 · The enclitics lang, rin/din, raw/daw and naman; review of alin
lessons.subtitle: Lang · Rin at din · Raw at daw · Naman · Alin

explanations.title: Review: use the earlier enclitics in sentences
explanations.body: Make your own sentences with sana, yata, muna, kasi and na (open answers, left out). Examples from the last lesson: Sana makarating ang eroplano kaagad; Tiket yata ni Gregorio iyan; Maghintay ka muna; Hindi kami natuloy kasi maulan; Huli na tayo.

explanations.title: a. Lang/lamang
explanations.body: Lang is the short form of lamang, which means “only.” Lang is never used to start a sentence. Occasionally na is added to lang, but the meaning does not change; na lang as a phrase is still translated “only” or “just.”

examples.text: Para lamang sa tatlong tao.
examples.translation: Only for three persons.

examples.text: Limang taong gulang lang siya.
examples.translation: He is only five years old.

examples.text: Tatlumpu’t pitong kilometro lamang ang layo mula sa kabisera ng Albay.
examples.translation: It is just thirty-seven kilometers away from the capital of Albay.

examples.text: Tubig na lang.
examples.translation: Just water.

explanations.title: b. Rin/din
explanations.body: Rin and din are variants. Rin is used after words ending in vowel sounds (a, e, i, o, u and y); din is used with all other sounds. Rin and din mean “also” or “too” in affirmative sentences. In negative sentences they translate as “either” or “neither.” Like lang, rin and din are not used to start a sentence. (Negative sentences begin with the adverb hindi.)

examples.text: Pati rin po sa mga guro.
examples.translation: Including also the teachers, sir or ma’am.

examples.text: At libre rin po ang anak ninyo. Libre rin po ang almusal.
examples.translation: And your child is free too, sir. Breakfast is also free, sir.

examples.text: Malapit din ito sa pamosong Spice Market.
examples.translation: This is also near the famous Spice Market.

examples.text: Malapit din ito sa daungan.
examples.translation: This is also near the port.

examples.text: Nandiyan din ang De La Playa.
examples.translation: De La Playa is also there.

explanations.title: c. Raw/daw
explanations.body: Raw and daw follow the same rule as rin/din in the choice of r or d. They are used in repeating what has just been said or read and for stating a general truth or a popular saying.

examples.text: Sabi nila wala raw katulad ang Mission Bay Resort at Casino.
examples.translation: They say Mission Bay Resort and Casino has no equal.

examples.text: Narinig ko na may diskuwento raw kayo para sa mga sundalo.
examples.translation: I heard that there is a discount for the soldiers.

examples.text: Ikaw daw ang nagtanong tungkol sa resort.
examples.translation: They say you asked about the resort.

examples.text: Marami raw ang nagpapareserba sa Discovery Bay sa Boracay.
examples.translation: They say many are making reservations at Discovery Bay in Boracay.

examples.text: Hindi raw mabuti ang manatili sa Taal Vista Lodge.
examples.translation: They say it is not good to stay at the Taal Vista Lodge.

explanations.title: d. Naman
explanations.body: Naman can mean “instead,” “on the other hand,” “well enough,” “in turn,” or “after all.” It can also convey a mild reproach. It is also used to state something earlier; in such instances the conjunction “and” can be added to the English statement. Context is always a good guide to how it translates. Naman can also indicate “please,” as in Bumili ka naman ng tiket. The verb needs to be in the command form; in Tagalog the infinitive is also the command form.

examples.text: Sundalo ako at guro naman ang asawa ko.
examples.translation: I’m a soldier and my wife is a teacher.

examples.text: Medyo may kamahalan ang presyo pero sulit naman.
examples.translation: It’s a bit expensive but (on the other hand) you get your money’s worth.

examples.text: Bumili ka naman ng tiket.
examples.translation: Please buy a ticket.

explanations.title: B. Adverbial time words and phrases
explanations.body: Past: kahapon, kagabi, noong linggo, noong nakaraang linggo, kamakalawa, kaninang umaga, noong isang linggo, kamakailan (lang). Present: ngayon lang, ngayung-ngayon lang, ngayon din, ngayung-ngayon din, ngayong mga araw na ito, ngayon ding araw na ito. Future: mamaya, mamayang gabi, bukas, bukas nang umaga. For future time words you can surmise that mamayang hapon means “this afternoon,” bukas nang tanghali “tomorrow at lunch time” and bukas nang gabi “tomorrow night.”

explanations.title: Activity 2: underline the enclitics and translate (the book’s key)

rows: Napakamahal naman ng hotel na ito kaya doon tayo sa Dusit Hotel.
This hotel is very expensive so let’s go to Dusit Hotel.
Sinabi mo raw na tumawag kami ng taksi at nagmamadali ka.
They say you asked us to call a taxi because you were in a hurry.
Ikaw lang daw ang naiwan sa kuwarto dahil maysakit ka.
You were the only one left in the room because you were sick.
Hindi raw sila tumatanggap ng bata sa resort na ito.
They say they are not accepting children in this resort.
Ikaw na lang ang sumama sa mga turista sa bus na iyan.
You are the only one who should go with the tourists in that bus.

explanations.title: Activity 3: correct the enclitics or write TAMA (the book’s key)

rows: Opo, narito na ang susi sa kuwarto ninyo sa room bilang kuwatro singko dos.
Yes, the key to your room, room number 452, is here.
Si Jojo naman ang bibili ng pagkain natin bukas.
Jojo will be the one to buy our food tomorrow.
Malapit raw ang Manila Hotel sa Marriott Hotel.
Malapit daw ang Manila Hotel sa Marriott Hotel.
They say the Manila Hotel is close to the Marriott Hotel (daw after a consonant sound).
Tatlong putahe lang ang nakalista sa restawrang ito.
Only three dishes are listed in this restaurant.
Bakit hindi daw nila nilinis ang kuwarto ninyo?
Bakit hindi raw nila nilinis ang kuwarto ninyo?
Why is it that they supposedly did not clean your room? (raw after a vowel sound)
Maganda sa resort na iyon kasi natulog rin kami doon.
Maganda sa resort na iyon kasi natulog din kami roon.
It is nice at that resort because we also slept there (din after a consonant sound, and roon after a consonant word).

explanations.title: Activity 4: write the correct enclitic (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Some items accept more than one answer, as the book notes.

rows: Gusto ko po ___ magpareserba ng dalawang kuwarto.
I would like to reserve two rooms.
Matagal-tagal ___ pala ang paghintay ng taksi dito.
It turns out waiting for a taxi here also takes quite a while.
Si Alfredo ___ ang tumawag sa restawran upang magpareserba.
They say Alfredo is the one who called the restaurant to reserve (also acceptable: rin).
Wala rin ___ siyang pambayad sa hotel.
They say he also has nothing to pay for the hotel.
Si Maria ___ ang puwedeng makipag-usap sa kanya.
Only Maria can talk with him (also acceptable: raw).
Handa na ___ kayo sa biyahe natin?
Are you ready already for our trip?
Ikaw ___ ang mag-order at may gagawin ako.
You order first because I have something to do.
I hope there is a discount.

explanations.title: Activity 6: translate the phrases of the paragraph (the book’s key)
explanations.body: The book’s paragraph, in sentences, with my translations of the whole sentences:

examples.text: Gusto rin naming magbakasyon sa Boracay at nag-book kami rito sa Discovery Shores sa Boracay.
examples.translation: We also wanted to take a vacation in Boracay and we booked here at Discovery Shores in Boracay.

examples.text: May kamahalan daw ang hotel na ito pero itinuloy namin dahil gusto naming mag-enjoy.
examples.translation: They said this hotel is a bit expensive but we went ahead because we wanted to enjoy ourselves.

examples.text: Sabi rin ng mga kaibigan namin na hindi raw masyadong masarap ang pagkain.
examples.translation: Our friends also said that the food is reportedly not very delicious.

examples.text: Hindi totoo ito dahil masarap ang pagkain at binigyan din kami ng diskuwento sa restawran.
examples.translation: This is not true because the food was delicious and we were also given a discount at the restaurant.

examples.text: Mabuti rin ang serbisyo at napakalinis ng mga kuwarto!
examples.translation: The service was also good and the rooms were so clean!

examples.text: Nasiyahan kami sa bakasyon namin at babalik rin kami sa Discovery sa susunod na taon.
examples.translation: We enjoyed our vacation and we will also come back to Discovery next year.

lessons.title: 174. C10 L2 · Listening: choosing a hotel, two overheard talks and two reservation calls
lessons.subtitle: Sa Heritage Hotel may diskuwento · Tanaw ang dagat · Magpapareserba po sana ako ng dalawang kuwarto

explanations.title: Activity 7: a conversation about a vacation (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key (essential elements of information): Josie is planning to go on vacation to the Philippines; Marina encouraged Josie to choose Heritage Hotel because of the 25% discount and other amenities; Josie liked the amenities and the discount so she will book at Heritage Hotel; Marina had a brochure with information about Heritage Hotel and gave it to Josie; Josie is excited about staying at the Heritage Hotel.

examples.text: Ate Marina, may tiket na ako sa PAL sa bakasyon ko.
examples.translation: Josie: Ate Marina, I already have a PAL ticket for my vacation.

examples.text: Sa PAL rin kami. Gusto mo ba ng diskuwento sa hotel?
examples.translation: Marina: We are on PAL too. Do you want a discount at the hotel?

examples.text: Opo naman. Gusto ko rin ng diskuwento. May alam po ba kayong hotel?
examples.translation: Josie: Of course. I also want a discount. Do you know of a hotel?

examples.text: Sa Heritage Hotel may diskuwento at maraming amenities.
examples.translation: Marina: At Heritage Hotel there is a discount and many amenities.

examples.text: Ganun po ba? Sige, mag-bo-book ako sa Heritage Hotel at malapit nga sa lahat, sa paliparan, sa Great Mall of Asia, at sa pasyalan. Tamang-tama lang ang pagbabakasyon natin!
examples.translation: Josie: Is that so? Okay, I will book at Heritage Hotel and it is close to everything, the airport, Great Mall of Asia and the tourist spots. Our vacation is just perfect!

examples.text: Sa Heritage, beynte singko porsiyento ang diskuwento at libre ang almusal. Isa pa, malinis at maganda rin ang Heritage. Heto, may brochure ako.
examples.translation: Marina: At Heritage the discount is twenty-five percent and breakfast is free. Also, Heritage is clean and beautiful too. Here, I have a brochure.

explanations.title: Activity 8, passage 1: a conversation between friends (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: the caller asked if a room reservation has been made, the distance between the hotel and the airport, and if there are tourist spots, nice places and restaurants nearby; the hotel is very close to the port and airport and close to tourist spots and restaurants; the reservation was made last week.

examples.text: Hello, Mare, nagpareserba ka na ba ng kuwarto para sa atin?
examples.translation: A: Hello, friend, have you already reserved a room for us?

examples.text: Noong isang linggo pa.
examples.translation: B: Since last week.

examples.text: Hindi ba malayo sa paliparan ang hotel?
examples.translation: A: Isn’t the hotel far from the airport?

examples.text: Malapit talaga at malapit din sa daungan.
examples.translation: B: It is really close and also close to the port.

examples.text: May malapit bang mga pasyalan at restawran?
examples.translation: A: Are there tourist spots and restaurants nearby?

examples.text: Oo naman, Mare.
examples.translation: B: Of course, friend.

explanations.title: Activity 8, passage 2: an overheard conversation (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: the room overlooks the sea; the price is expensive but worth it; the package includes free breakfast and free pick-up and drop-off at the airport.

examples.text: Ang ganda naman nitong kuwartong napili mo!
examples.translation: A: How beautiful this room you chose is!

examples.text: Oo, siyempre, tanaw ang dagat, e.
examples.translation: B: Yes, of course, it overlooks the sea.

examples.text: Pero medyo mahal.
examples.translation: A: But it is a bit expensive.

examples.text: Hindi bale, sulit naman. Libre pa ang almusal.
examples.translation: B: Never mind, it is worth it. Breakfast is even free.

examples.text: Libre din ba ang hatid-sundo sa paliparan?
examples.translation: A: Is the airport pick-up and drop-off free too?

examples.text: Oo, kasama sa bayad iyon.
examples.translation: B: Yes, that is included in the payment.

explanations.title: Activity 9: an excerpt of a conversation (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: the purpose of the call is to reserve a room or make a reservation at a hotel; the total cost is 15,250 pesos including tax; the package includes free internet, free breakfast, free use of the gym and free pick-up from the airport.

examples.text: Hello, Ma’am, para po ba sa mga estudyante? Kasi may promo po kami.
examples.translation: A: Hello, ma’am, is it for students? Because we have a promo.

examples.text: Oo. Mga estudyante sila. Mabuti’t may promo. Magkano lahat?
examples.translation: B: Yes. They are students. It’s good there is a promo. How much is it altogether?

examples.text: Kinse mil, dos siyentos singkuwenta lang po kasama na ang buwis. Libre internet, almusal, at libre ang gamit sa gym, at pati na ang pagsundo sa paliparan.
examples.translation: A: Only fifteen thousand two hundred fifty, tax included. Free internet, breakfast, free use of the gym, and the airport pick-up too.

explanations.title: Activity 10: a client and a receptionist (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Main idea: the caller is making a room reservation. Details: two rooms for four people (the caller, her husband and two children); the children are 20 and 14 years old, both males; the reservation is from June 18 to 25.

examples.text: Ma’am, magandang tanghali po. Magpapareserba po sana ako ng dalawang kuwarto.
examples.translation: A: Ma’am, good noon. I would like to reserve two rooms.

examples.text: Para kailan po?
examples.translation: B: For when?

examples.text: Mula a-dise-otso hanggang a-beynte singko ng Hunyo.
examples.translation: A: From the eighteenth to the twenty-fifth of June.

examples.text: Para sa ilang tao po?
examples.translation: B: For how many people?

examples.text: Apat. Kaming mag-asawa at dalawa kong anak.
examples.translation: A: Four. My husband and I and my two children.

examples.text: Ano po ang mga edad nila?
examples.translation: B: What are their ages?

examples.text: Beynte at katorse anyos. Pareho silang lalaki.
examples.translation: A: Twenty and fourteen years old. Both are boys.

explanations.title: Activity 11: guided conversation, booking a hotel
explanations.body: Call a travel agency and book a hotel. A (travel agent): say the agency’s name and greet the client; ask the dates of stay; ask for how many people; say the senior citizen has a 20% discount and her son stays for free; say you also offer free internet, use of the gym, free breakfast and free pick-up at the airport. B (client): return the greeting and say you want to book a hotel for two people (the book’s card says three in the next line); say May 10 to 15; say three people: you, your mom, a senior citizen, and your three-year-old son; say that’s great. A sample:

examples.text: Magandang umaga po. Ito po ang Mabuhay Travel and Tours. Ano po ang maitutulong ko sa inyo?
examples.translation: Travel agent: Good morning. This is Mabuhay Travel and Tours. How can I help you?

examples.text: Magandang umaga rin po. Gusto ko pong mag-book ng hotel para sa dalawang tao.
examples.translation: Client: Good morning too. I would like to book a hotel for two people.

examples.text: Kailan po kayo mananatili?
examples.translation: Travel agent: When will you stay?

examples.text: Mula a-diyes hanggang a-kinse ng Mayo.
examples.translation: Client: From the tenth to the fifteenth of May.

examples.text: Para sa ilang tao po?
examples.translation: Travel agent: For how many people?

examples.text: Para sa tatlong tao po, ako, ang nanay kong senior citizen at ang tatlong taong gulang kong anak.
examples.translation: Client: For three people: myself, my mother, who is a senior citizen, and my three-year-old son.

examples.text: May beynte porsiyentong diskuwento po ang senior citizen at libre po ang anak ninyo.
examples.translation: Travel agent: The senior citizen has a twenty percent discount and your son stays for free.

examples.text: Ang galing naman!
examples.translation: Client: That’s great!

examples.text: Mayroon din po kaming libreng internet, gamit sa gym, almusal at hatid-sundo sa paliparan.
examples.translation: Travel agent: We also have free internet, use of the gym, breakfast and airport pick-up and drop-off.

explanations.title: Activity 12: role play, planning a trip to Palawan
explanations.body: You are a U.S. foreign language student in Manila who wants to go to Palawan and asks a classmate for details. A: greet your classmate and say you plan to go to Palawan; ask for a recommendation, the name of a hotel; ask how much per night; ask about the good things the hotel offers, proximity to the airport, restaurants, the beach and the town proper; say the price is worth it then; say thank you and you will think about it. B: return the greeting and say Palawan is a very nice place; say El Nido Beach Resort Hotel; say 82 dollars per night or almost 4,000 pesos; say it is very close to the airport, about 3.3 kilometers, the hotel is right on the beach and just a 2-minute walk to the town proper, it has its own restaurant and there are other restaurants nearby. A sample:

examples.text: Magandang umaga. Balak kong pumunta sa Palawan.
examples.translation: Estudyante: Good morning. I plan to go to Palawan.

examples.text: Magandang umaga rin. Napakaganda ng Palawan.
examples.translation: Kaklase: Good morning too. Palawan is very beautiful.

examples.text: Anong hotel ang irerekomenda mo? Magkano kaya sa isang gabi?
examples.translation: Estudyante: Which hotel would you recommend? How much might it be per night?

examples.text: Ang El Nido Beach Resort Hotel. Walumpu’t dalawang dolyar sa isang gabi o halos apat na libong piso.
examples.translation: Kaklase: El Nido Beach Resort Hotel. Eighty-two dollars per night or almost four thousand pesos.

examples.text: Ano ang magagandang alok ng hotel? Malapit ba sa paliparan, restawran, beach at bayan?
examples.translation: Estudyante: What good things does the hotel offer? Is it near the airport, restaurants, the beach and the town?

examples.text: Napakalapit nito sa paliparan, mga tatlong kilometro. Nasa tabing-dagat mismo ang hotel at dalawang minuto lang ang lakad papunta sa bayan. May sarili itong restawran at may iba pang restawran sa malapit.
examples.translation: Kaklase: It is very close to the airport, about three kilometers. The hotel is right on the beach and only a two-minute walk to the town. It has its own restaurant and there are other restaurants nearby.

examples.text: Kung ganoon, sulit ang presyo. Salamat, iisipin ko muna.
examples.translation: Estudyante: In that case the price is worth it. Thank you, I will think about it first.

units.title: Chapter 10 · Lesson 3: Experiences at the airport

lessons.title: 176. C10 L3 · Lost luggage and waiting at the airport
lessons.subtitle: Nawawala po ang bagahe ko · Madalas bang nahuhuli ang PAL? · Parang walang hanggan

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: By the end of the lesson you can recognize vocabulary commonly used in air travel experiences; answer comprehension questions about short reading and listening passages on air travel experiences; transcribe and translate sentences about air travel; and talk about situations in the airport or airplane using the expressions learned. The structures are the core vocabulary, the enclitics pa, pala, nga, kaya and tuloy, and adverbial time words and phrases (part II). In the book a mind map of airline travel concepts opens the lesson and you add related words in Tagalog (the mind map is left out).

explanations.title: Presentation 1, Dialog A: a passenger and an airport employee

examples.text: Sir, saan po ba ang lost and found section? Nawawala po kasi ang bagahe ko.
examples.translation: A: Sir, where is the lost and found section? My luggage is missing.

examples.text: Dito po. Kailan pa po ba nawawala at anong flight?
examples.translation: B: Here. When did it go missing and what flight?

examples.text: PAL PR isa sero singko po mula San Francisco hanggang dito sa NAIA. Kanina lang pong alas-kuwatro y medya ng umaga.
examples.translation: A: PAL PR one-oh-five, from San Francisco to here at NAIA. Just earlier, at four-thirty in the morning.

examples.text: Anong oras nga po pala ulit?
examples.translation: B: What time was it again?

examples.text: Alas-kuwatro y medya. Kulang yata ako sa tulog kaya tuloy namalikmata ako.
examples.translation: A: Four-thirty. I seem to have lacked sleep so I ended up distracted.

examples.text: Ano po ang itsura ng bagahe n’yo at ano ang mga laman?
examples.translation: B: What does your luggage look like and what are the contents?

examples.text: Kulay tsokolate. May sukat na beynte singko por disi-otso por onse. Mahahalagang dokumento, titulo ng lupa at sertipiko ng kasal.
examples.translation: A: Chocolate in color. It measures twenty-five by eighteen by eleven. Important documents, a land title and a marriage certificate.

examples.text: O sige po. Titingnan ko po kung nasa loob ang bagahe n’yo.
examples.translation: B: All right. I will check whether your luggage is inside.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions (Dialog A)
explanations.body: The enclitics pa, pala, nga, kaya and tuloy are discussed in the grammar section. NAIA is Ninoy Aquino International Airport. PR 105 is one of the flight numbers of Philippine Airlines (PAL), the flag carrier of the Philippines and the oldest airline in Asia. The names of the various departments and sections of NAIA are all in English. In the book the measurements are printed in inches (25”x18”x11”); in the spoken lines they are written in words.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions (Dialog B)
explanations.body: PAL and Cebu Pacific are the two biggest airlines in the Philippines. Nahuhuli (is late), mahuli (to be late) and “late” are used interchangeably; it is not uncommon to hear a native speaker mix Tagalog and English, especially in Manila and the surrounding areas. The answer parang walang hanggan means “seems endless.”

explanations.title: Comprehension check, Dialog A (the book’s key)

rows: 1. What was the main topic of conversation?
The passenger is reporting lost luggage.
2. What are the two items inside the missing luggage?
Important documents: a land title and a marriage certificate.
3. What description is given of the missing object?
The dialog says chocolate in color and the size is 25 x 18 x 11 (the book’s key says red, which does not match the dialog).
5. What could have been a contributing factor?
The passenger said he might have overlooked his luggage because of lack of sleep.
6. What action did the airport employee take?
He said he will check whether the luggage is inside (the office).

explanations.title: Comprehension check, Dialog B (the book’s key)
explanations.body: The man asked about the time of the woman’s flight and whether PAL is often late. The woman asked a confirmation question whether the man always takes Cebu Pacific, and asked how often Cebu Pacific flies late.

explanations.title: Presentation 2, Dialog A: an immigration officer and a traveler

examples.text: Nasaan po ang inyong pasaporte?
examples.translation: A: Where is your passport?

examples.text: Eto po.
examples.translation: B: Here it is.

examples.text: Malapit nga palang mapaso ito kaya kailangan mong kumuha ng bago. Balido ito hanggang sa katapusan lang nitong buwan.
examples.translation: A: This is about to expire, I see, so you need to get a new one. It is valid only until the end of this month.

examples.text: Opo, sir. Gagawin ko po.
examples.translation: B: Yes, sir. I will do it.

examples.text: Ano nga pala ang pakay mo sa pagbisita dito sa Pilipinas? Saan ka tutuloy?
examples.translation: A: By the way, what is your purpose in visiting the Philippines? Where will you stay?

examples.text: Mamasyal lang po. May kaibigan po ako dito sa Lipa, Batangas.
examples.translation: B: Just to go around. I have a friend here in Lipa, Batangas.

examples.text: Gaano ka katagal dito?
examples.translation: A: How long will you be here?

examples.text: Dalawang buwan at kalahati lang po.
examples.translation: B: Only two and a half months.

examples.text: Meron ka pa bang ibang ID?
examples.translation: A: Do you have any other ID?

examples.text: Opo meron akong driver’s license. Kaya lang po malapit na rin pong mapaso.
examples.translation: B: Yes, I have a driver’s license. But it is also about to expire.

examples.text: Patingin nga? Asikasuhin mo ’yan agad, sir.
examples.translation: A: Let me see. Take care of that right away, sir.

examples.text: Opo.
examples.translation: B: Yes.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions (Dialog A)
explanations.body: The phrase may bisa pa is a synonym of balido. Gaano ka katagal dito means “How long will you stay here?” ID is used in spoken language; in written Tagalog the term pagkakakilanlan (“identity” or “identification”) is used. Driver’s license is commonly used; the Tagalog lisensiya ng pagmamaneho is very seldom used.

explanations.title: Presentation 2, Dialog B: Mila sees her friend Sergio off at the airport
explanations.body: In the book Mila has alternative answers: for “when will you return” she can say Sa isang taon pa, Sa susunod na taon, Sa darating na taon, Balang-araw or Sa hinaharap; for “when will you get a passport” she can say Sa makalawa, Sa Biyernes, Sa Linggo, Sa Lunes or Sa linggong darating.

examples.text: Ingat ka sa lakad mo.
examples.translation: Mila: Take care on your trip.

examples.text: Salamat. Ikaw, kailan ka uuwi sa Pilipinas?
examples.translation: Sergio: Thanks. You, when will you return home to the Philippines?

explanations.title: Notes and expressions (Dialog B)
explanations.body: Sa isang taon pa, sa susunod na taon, sa darating na taon, balang-araw, sa hinaharap, sa makalawa, sa Biyernes, sa Linggo and sa linggong darating are time words. Note the difference between Linggo in Sa Linggo (Sunday) and sa linggong darating (this coming week): Linggo (Sunday) is capitalized. The last sentence, Ano kaya kung sasama na lang ako sayo?, means “I wonder if I could go with you?” or “How about or what if I go with you?”

explanations.title: Activity 1: an email about lost baggage (the book’s key)
explanations.body: From Baggage_tracing at the PAL address, to Lucy. Subject: nawawalang bagahe. In the book the email gives two phone numbers (a hotline, 632-851-3011, and a number to call back, 632-223-3345); here the numbers are not read out. Key: 1. a follow-up inquiry about lost luggage; 2. the passenger reported the loss to the lost and found section, then called the hotline but nobody answered; 3. inside the airplane; 4. important documents, a laptop, and presents for her husband and children.

lessons.subtitle: Pa · Pala · Nga · Kaya · Tuloy · Ang ayos ng mga enclitic

explanations.title: A. Review: complete the sentences with an enclitic you know (the book’s key)
explanations.body: The enclitics learned so far: ba, po, muna, sana, lang, raw, rin.

rows: Teka ___ po at nasa telepono ako.
Ikaw ___ ang sasakay sa PAL at hindi kami.
Wala ___ silang libreng almusal sa motel na ito.

explanations.title: B1. Pa
explanations.body: In certain contexts pa may mean mockery, sarcasm or exasperation. It can be translated as “still” or “even” in the English sentence. With another enclitic, pala, pa means “even” or “too.”

examples.text: Kailan pa po ba nawawala at anong flight?
examples.translation: When was it (still) missing?

examples.text: Nagbigay ka ng regalo at may cake pa pala!
examples.translation: You have already given a gift and there’s even a cake, too!

examples.text: Bakit ka bagsak sa test? Nag-review pa tayo maghapon!
examples.translation: Why did you flunk the test? We even reviewed all day!

explanations.title: B2. Pala
explanations.body: Pala is an expression of mild surprise. It is roughly equivalent to “oh, I see” and “so.” With nga it means “oh, by the way.” Sometimes the word itself is not translated in English but is signaled by an exclamation point.

examples.text: Anong oras nga po pala ulit?
examples.translation: What time is it really?

examples.text: Malapit nga palang mapaso ito.
examples.translation: So, this will soon expire.

examples.text: Ano nga pala ang pakay mo sa pagbisita dito sa Pilipinas?
examples.translation: Oh, really, what is your purpose in visiting here in the Philippines?

explanations.title: B3. Nga
explanations.body: Nga is used to confirm what has just been said. It can also be translated as “really,” “it is true” or “to be sure.” It also means “please” in certain contexts. See the examples under pala as well.

examples.text: Siya nga ang pumasok sa eroplano.
examples.translation: She is really the one who boarded the plane.

examples.text: Naglakbay na nga si Leandro kasama ang pamilya niya.
examples.translation: Leandro really left already with his family.

explanations.title: B4. Tuloy
explanations.body: Tuloy conveys the idea that something or some action resulted in something else. It is translatable as “as a result” or “ended up.”

examples.text: Kulang yata ako sa tulog, kaya tuloy namalikmata ako.
examples.translation: It looks like I lacked sleep, that’s why, I ended up distracted.

examples.text: Matagal ang serbisyo sa paliparang ito, nahuli tuloy ako sa biyahe ko.
examples.translation: The airport service was slow, as a result I was late for my travel.

examples.text: Nasira ang kompyuter sa paliparan, hindi tuloy umalis ang mga eroplano sa wastong oras.
examples.translation: The computers at the airport broke down, as a result, the airplanes did not leave on time.

examples.text: Hindi umuwi ang piloto sa wastong oras, nagalit tuloy ang asawa niya.
examples.translation: The pilot did not come home on time, as a result, his wife got mad.

explanations.title: B5. Kaya
explanations.body: Kaya is used to express bewilderment or puzzlement. It is similar to the perplexed tone of “I wonder” and “do you suppose.”

examples.text: Ano kaya kung sasama na lang ako sayo?
examples.translation: I wonder if I could go with you?

explanations.title: B6. Rules about the order of enclitics
explanations.body: a. Enclitics are usually placed after the first full word or unit of the sentence. However, the monosyllabic pronouns ko, mo and ka are positioned before the enclitics. b. The first full word may be preceded by the markers ang, ang mga, si, sina, or the words sa and nasa. So the order is: marker + first full word + ko, mo or ka + enclitic(s) + rest of the sentence. c. When two or more enclitics are used, they follow the column order in the table below. Some words in column 3 can also be positioned after column 4 in certain sentences. Na and pa are mutually exclusive: they cannot be used in the same phrase. d. When hindi is used in a question, it precedes all the enclitics used in the sentence. Ko, mo and ka precede the enclitics. Ho and po occur right after hindi; ho and po cannot be used with ko, mo and ka (the plural of these pronouns is used with ho and po). The pattern is: Hindi ho/po + ba + full word or unit + other enclitics + rest of the sentence.

explanations.title: Activity 7: a pilot’s announcement (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Write the numbers you hear. Key: 1. flight number 104; 2. 33,000 feet (the altitude now); 3. 400 miles per hour (the speed); 4. 15 (minutes early at arrival).

examples.text: Magandang hapon po, mga pasahero. Ito po ang inyong kapitan.
examples.translation: Good afternoon, passengers. This is your captain.

examples.text: Una, gusto namin kayong batiin sa PAL Flight Number isa sero apat papuntang Maynila.
examples.translation: First, we want to greet you on PAL Flight Number one-oh-four to Manila.

examples.text: Kasalukuyang lumilipad tayo sa taas na tatlumpu’t tatlong libong talampakan at bilis na apatnaraang milya bawat oras.
examples.translation: We are currently flying at an altitude of thirty-three thousand feet and a speed of four hundred miles per hour.

examples.text: Maganda raw ang panahon at inaasahan nating lumapag sa Maynila na mas maaga nang mga labinlimang minuto.
examples.translation: The weather is said to be good and we expect to land in Manila about fifteen minutes early.

explanations.title: Activity 8, passage 1: a conversation between relatives (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: 1. she lost her luggage at the airport and asks her aunt for help or does not know what to do; 2. the caller and her daughter or son; 3. Romeo Magtalas is the aunt’s godson at his wedding, works at the lost and found section of NAIA, and was referred to by the aunt to help the caller.

examples.text: Tita, nawala po ang isang bagahe ko! Ano po ang gagawin ko?
examples.translation: A: Auntie, one of my bags is lost! What should I do?

examples.text: Nasaan ka? Kailan lang?
examples.translation: B: Where are you? When just now?

examples.text: Nasa paliparan pa po dito sa NAIA. Kararating lang namin mula Cotabato.
examples.translation: A: I’m still at the airport here at NAIA. We have just arrived from Cotabato.

examples.text: Paano ba nawala?
examples.translation: B: How did it get lost?

examples.text: Kasama ko po kasi itong anak ko. Namalikmata ako. Akala ko kumpleto na ang bagahe ko.
examples.translation: A: I am with my child. I got distracted. I thought my luggage was complete.

examples.text: OK, relax ka lang. Pumunta ka sa lost and found section. Hanapin mo si Romeo Magtalas. Inaanak ko ’yan sa kasal. I-report mo at humingi ka ng tulong sa kanya. Sabihin mo ang pangalan ko.
examples.translation: B: OK, just relax. Go to the lost and found section. Look for Romeo Magtalas. He is my godson at his wedding. Report it and ask him for help. Say my name.

examples.text: Opo, Tita. Thank you po talaga.
examples.translation: A: Yes, Auntie. Thank you so much.

explanations.title: Activity 8, passage 2: a traveler and an immigration officer (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: 4. the passport expires on December 20 (the book adds 2018, which is not in the script); 5. the officer asked for additional identification, the length of stay, whether the traveler has a relative in the Philippines and where he will live; 6. passport, driver’s license and company ID; 7. he has a house in the Philippines and his wife and children live there.

examples.text: Ma’am, sa Disyembre a-beynte paso na ang pasaporte n’yo. Isang buwan na lang po ’yun.
examples.translation: A: Ma’am, your passport expires on December twentieth. That is only one month away.

examples.text: Aasikasuhin ko po agad sir.
examples.translation: B: I will take care of it right away, sir.

examples.text: May iba ka pa bang ID?
examples.translation: A: Do you have another ID?

examples.text: Meron po. ID ng kumpanya kung saan ako nagtatrabaho at driver’s license ko po.
examples.translation: B: Yes. The ID of the company where I work and my driver’s license.

examples.text: Patingin nga. Uhm. OK ito. Hanggang kailan ka dito sa Pilipinas?
examples.translation: A: Let me see. Hmm. This is OK. Until when will you be here in the Philippines?

examples.text: Hanggang bagong taon lang po.
examples.translation: B: Only until New Year.

examples.text: May kamag-anak ka ba? Saan ka titira?
examples.translation: A: Do you have relatives? Where will you live?

examples.text: Opo. May bahay po kami dito. Nandito po ang asawa’t mga anak ko.
examples.translation: B: Yes. We have a house here. My wife and children are here.

explanations.title: Activity 9: siblings talking about travel plans (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: 1. the sister was invited to be bridesmaid at Aby’s wedding and asks her brother to pay for her plane ticket to Manila; 2. the brother’s reminders are to make sure she has a valid passport, not to bring plenty of luggage and to check whether a storm is coming; 3. she will stay in Manila for four days, fly to Manila on Friday, attend the wedding on Sunday morning and fly back to San Francisco on Sunday night. The book’s script misprints the brother’s last question as Ilang raw ka ba; the sensible reading is Ilang araw ka ba.

examples.text: Kuya, kinuha po akong abay sa kasal ni Aby. Sa Manila daw po ang kasal. Puwede’ng ikaw na ang magbayad ng pamasahe ko sa eroplano?
examples.translation: A: Big brother, I was chosen as a bridesmaid at Aby’s wedding. The wedding is said to be in Manila. Could you pay for my plane fare?

examples.text: Walang problema, bunso. Kailan ba ang kasal?
examples.translation: B: No problem, little sister. When is the wedding?

examples.text: Sa susunod na buwan na po.
examples.translation: A: Next month already.

examples.text: Siguraduhin mo lang na balido ang pasaporte mo. At saka huwag ka nang magdala ng maraming bagahe. I-check mo rin kung may bagyo ba. Ilang araw ka ba sa Manila?
examples.translation: B: Just make sure your passport is valid. And don’t bring a lot of luggage. Also check whether there is a storm. How many days will you be in Manila?

examples.text: Apat na araw lang po. Plano kong lumipad ng Biyernes. Linggo kasi ng umaga ang kasal. Balik San Francisco na ako agad Linggo ng gabi.
examples.translation: A: Only four days. I plan to fly on Friday. The wedding is Sunday morning. I go back to San Francisco right away on Sunday night.

explanations.title: Activity 10: a voicemail (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: Gloria, Georgina’s godmother, left a voicemail. She did not know right away that Georgina is going home to the Philippines and would have bought presents for Georgina’s siblings. She asks Georgina to drop by her house to get money to buy the presents, and will also send the land title and marriage certificate through Georgina, to be given to Gloria’s brother in the Philippines.

examples.text: Hello, Georgina, si Ninang Gloria mo ’to.
examples.translation: Hello, Georgina, this is your Ninang Gloria.

examples.text: Aalis ka daw sa Sabado papuntang Pilipinas.
examples.translation: They say you are leaving on Saturday for the Philippines.

examples.text: Bakit naman hindi mo sinabi agad?
examples.translation: Why didn’t you tell me right away?

examples.text: Sana nakabili ako ng regalo sa mga kapatid mo.
examples.translation: I wish I had been able to buy gifts for your siblings.

examples.text: Hindi bale, dumaan ka na lang dito sa bahay.
examples.translation: Never mind, just drop by the house.

examples.text: Bibigyan na lang kita ng pera.
examples.translation: I will just give you money.

examples.text: Ikaw na ang bahalang bumili ng regalo sa kanila.
examples.translation: You will be in charge of buying them gifts.

examples.text: Ipapadala ko rin pala ang titulo ng lupa at sertipiko ng kasal namin ng Ninong mo.
examples.translation: By the way, I will also send the land title and the marriage certificate of your Ninong and me.

examples.text: Ibigay mo sa kapatid ko.
examples.translation: Give them to my brother.
