explanations.title: Activity 11: guided conversation at the immigration counter
explanations.body: You are at the immigration counter of Ninoy Aquino International Airport. An immigration officer asks about your travel documents and purpose of visit; your partner plays the officer. Use honorifics, then switch roles. A: ask for passport and a valid ID; ask about the purpose of stay and the address in the Philippines; ask about the length of stay; say he needs to get a new and valid passport because it is about to expire and so is the ID. B: show your documents; say you will visit your relatives and give your complete address; say about a month; say you will do so when you return to your country and thank the officer. A sample:

examples.text: Magandang umaga po. Pakipakita po ang pasaporte at balidong ID ninyo.
examples.translation: Immigration Officer: Good morning. Please show your passport and a valid ID.

examples.text: Magandang umaga po. Heto po.
examples.translation: Traveler: Good morning. Here you are.

examples.text: Ano po ang pakay ng pagbisita ninyo at saan kayo tutuloy sa Pilipinas?
examples.translation: Immigration Officer: What is the purpose of your visit and where will you stay in the Philippines?

examples.text: Bibisitahin ko po ang mga kamag-anak ko. Tutuloy po ako sa bahay nila sa Lipa, Batangas.
examples.translation: Traveler: I will visit my relatives. I will stay at their house in Lipa, Batangas.

examples.text: Gaano po kayo katagal dito sa bansa?
examples.translation: Immigration Officer: How long will you stay in the country?

examples.text: Mga isang buwan po.
examples.translation: Traveler: About a month.

examples.text: Kailangan po ninyong kumuha ng bago at balidong pasaporte dahil malapit na pong mapaso ito, pati ang ID ninyo.
examples.translation: Immigration Officer: You need to get a new and valid passport because it is about to expire, and your ID as well.

examples.text: Gagawin ko po iyon pagbalik ko sa bansa ko. Salamat po.
examples.translation: Traveler: I will do that when I return to my country. Thank you.

explanations.title: Activity 12: role play, reporting missing luggage
explanations.body: You travelled from Davao to Manila via Cebu Pacific and on arriving home discovered one piece of luggage is missing. You call the airline’s hotline (the book’s picture of the Davao airport is left out). Student A, the receptionist: it is 2 p.m., greet the caller, say the airline’s name and ask how you may help; say sure, then ask again for the passenger’s full name, flight number, date and number of bags; ask for the luggage’s description; thank the passenger and ask to wait a few seconds while you check. Student B, the passenger: return the greeting and say your name and that you are reporting missing luggage; give the information Nonito Pimentel, flight number 178, October 30, only one missing bag; say the color, brand and approximate size; say no problem. A sample:

examples.text: Magandang hapon po, Cebu Pacific po ito. Ano po ang maitutulong ko sa inyo?
examples.translation: Receptionist: Good afternoon, this is Cebu Pacific. How may I help you?

examples.text: Magandang hapon po. Ako po si Nonito Pimentel. Nag-uulat po ako ng nawawalang bagahe.
examples.translation: Passenger: Good afternoon. I am Nonito Pimentel. I am reporting missing luggage.

examples.text: Sige po, matutulungan ko kayo. Puwede po bang ulitin ang buong pangalan ninyo, ang flight number, ang petsa at ilan ang bagahe?
examples.translation: Receptionist: Sure, I can help you. May I ask again for your full name, the flight number, the date and how many bags?

examples.text: Nonito Pimentel po, flight isa pito walo, Oktubre trenta, at isa lang po ang nawawala.
examples.translation: Passenger: Nonito Pimentel, flight one seven eight, October thirtieth, and only one is missing.

examples.text: Ano po ang itsura ng bagahe?
examples.translation: Receptionist: What does the luggage look like?

examples.text: Kulay itim po ito, may tatak na Samsonite at mga dalawang talampakan ang taas.
examples.translation: Passenger: It is black, a Samsonite brand and about two feet tall.

examples.text: Salamat po sa impormasyon. Maghintay po kayo ng ilang segundo at titingnan ko kung nasa opisina namin ang nawawalang bagahe.
examples.translation: Receptionist: Thank you for the information. Please wait a few seconds and I will check whether the missing luggage is in our office.

examples.text: Walang problema po.
examples.translation: Passenger: No problem.

explanations.title: Activity 13: challenge yourself
explanations.body: Narrate your personal experiences about airports. Do one of the following. 1. Talk about one bad or good experience at the airport (for example the handling of delayed, lost or missing luggage, the professionalism of air and land crew, flight schedules, airline beverages or overall service). 2. You are MAJ Espino, a Philippine Marine officer; call a local airport and thank the receptionist for finding your luggage and sending it to your home address (open task, left out).

explanations.title: More adverbial time words and phrases (the book’s sentences)

examples.text: Sa isang taon pa kami bibiyahe sa Pilipinas.
examples.translation: We will travel to the Philippines not until next year.

examples.text: Magbabakasyon kami sa probinsiya sa susunod na taon.
examples.translation: We will vacation in the province the following year.

examples.text: Balak naming pumunta ng Europa sa darating na taon.
examples.translation: We plan to go to Europe this coming year.

examples.text: Sana, magkita tayo balang araw.
examples.translation: I hope we meet someday.

examples.text: Sa hinaharap po, asikasuhin ninyo nang mas maaga ang pagpapa-renew ng pasaporte ninyo, nang hindi kayo maperwisyo.
examples.translation: In the future, please take care of renewing your passport earlier, so you won’t be inconvenienced.

examples.text: Naku, Miss, mapapaso na ang inyong pasaporte sa makalawa.
examples.translation: Oh dear, Miss, your passport will expire the day after tomorrow.

examples.text: Gusto ko pong magpareserba ng kuwarto para sa Biyernes.
examples.translation: I would like to reserve a room for Friday.

examples.text: Sa linggong darating, papasyal ang mga kamag-anak natin mula sa Hawaii.
examples.translation: This coming week our relatives will visit from Hawaii.

explanations.title: Words and phrases for experiences at the airport (the book’s sentences)
explanations.body: Nawawalang bagahe, titingnan, pasaporte, gaano … katagal, pakay ng pagbisita, balido and patingin, each in an example:

examples.text: Kailan ninyo ini-report ang inyong nawawalang bagahe?
examples.translation: When did you report your missing luggage?

examples.text: Titingnan ko po sa logbook kung may nagbalik ng inyong bagahe.
examples.translation: I will check the logbook whether someone returned your luggage.

examples.text: Ihanda ang pasaporte at tiket pagpunta sa counter.
examples.translation: Prepare the passport and ticket when going to the counter.

examples.text: Gaano ka katagal mamamasyal dito sa Davao?
examples.translation: How long will you be sightseeing here in Davao?

examples.text: Ang pakay ng pagbisita ko ay upang magpahinga at mamasyal sa magagandang tanawin.
examples.translation: The purpose of my visit is to rest and tour the beautiful sights.

examples.text: Balido po ang visa ko nang para sa sampung taon.
examples.translation: My visa is valid for ten years.

examples.text: Patingin nga po ng lisensiya ninyo sa pagmamaneho.
examples.translation: May I please see your driver’s license.

units.title: Chapter 11 · Lesson 1: Simple directions

lessons.title: 182. C11 L1 · Walking to the CCP: simple directions
lessons.subtitle: Puwede bang lakarin? · Dumiretso lang po kayo · Ano po ang palatandaan?

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: By the end of the lesson you can extract information from reading and listening passages about giving directions; identify words and expressions related to giving directions and instructions; translate and transcribe expressions related to directions and instructions; and give and follow directions using the expressions learned. The structures are the core vocabulary, um verbs for giving directions and instructions, the conjunctions at, pagkatapos, pero and kasi, and the use of pa, pa+um or patungo with direction words. In the book a mind map of direction words (kumaliwa, lumiko and others) opens the lesson and you add more in Tagalog.

explanations.title: Presentation 1A: a commuter sees a traffic jam and walks
explanations.body: Seeing the traffic jam and trying to save time, a commuter decides to walk. He asks the jeepney driver for directions. Remember to use “boss,” “sir” or “ma’am” when talking to strangers.

examples.text: Boss, malayo pa ba ang CCP? Maglalakad na lang ako at baka mahuli na ako, e. Puwede bang lakarin?
examples.translation: Commuter: Boss, is the CCP still far? I will just walk because I might be late already. Can it be walked?

examples.text: Puwede pero medyo malayo mula dito hanggang CCP.
examples.translation: Driver: You can, but it is a bit far from here to the CCP.

examples.text: Paano ba makakarating dun?
examples.translation: Commuter: How do I get there?

examples.text: Dumiretso lang po kayo sa kalyeng ito. Pagkatapos makikita po ninyo ang unang ilaw trapiko. Tuluy-tuloy lang po nang mga tatlong bloke pa.
examples.translation: Driver: Just go straight on this street. Afterwards you will see the first traffic light. Just keep going continuously for about three more blocks.

examples.text: Ano po ang palatandaan?
examples.translation: Commuter: What is the landmark?

examples.text: Makikita niyo po ang Harrison Plaza. Kumaliwa po kayo. Makikita n’yo po ang malaking gusali ng Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas. Malapit po doon ang CCP sa kahabaan ng Roxas Boulevard.
examples.translation: Driver: You will see Harrison Plaza. Turn left. You will see the big building of the Central Bank of the Philippines. The CCP is near there along Roxas Boulevard.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Variations of the second line include Puwede bang lakarin?, Kaya bang lakarin? and Maaari bang lakarin? Boss and sir are honorifics normally used with strangers. CCP means “Cultural Center of the Philippines.” Makararating is another form of makakarating. Harrison Plaza, opened in 1976, was the first shopping mall in the Philippines; it covers 75,000 square meters, has 180 stores and service outlets and is the closest shopping mall to the CCP. Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas is the Central Bank of the Philippines.

rows: the length of, the stretch of
1. The three questions of the commuter
Puwede bang lakarin? (Is it walking distance?) Paano ba makakarating dun? (How to get there?) Ano po ang palatandaan? (What is the landmark?)

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Bumuwelta and bumalik are synonyms. Bumuwelta, bumalik, lumipat, umabante, tumabi, gumitna, umatras, lumampas and huminto are um verbs related to giving directions or instructions (discussed in the grammar lesson). The affixes pa and pa+um in paakyat, pababa, pahilaga, patungong hilaga, pumasilangan, pumatimog and pumakanan mean “go in the direction of” or “in the manner of” (also in the grammar lesson). Avenida Rizal is one of Manila’s major thoroughfares, named after the national hero Jose Rizal.

rows: go to the side, get out of the way
to go in the center, occupy the middle

explanations.title: Giving directions: the five instructions in English (the book’s key)
explanations.body: 1. Transfer to the left lane then go forward. Go to the side of the street. Do not go in the center. That’s prohibited. 2. You drove past our house. Go back two blocks or if not just stop right there. I’m heading towards your location (I’ll be there shortly). I’m getting out of the house now. 3. That road is wrong (not right). Drive back up to Mabini. Pass through the highway. Go towards the east for about two miles then go towards the south for ten miles. 4. Drive going north and when you get to Quezon City, go towards the west. 5. Keep driving for about 100 meters. Rizal Avenue is still far from there. Go right for about 50 feet until you see an alley. The road goes uphill.

explanations.title: Presentation 2A: notes on directions to Max Fried Chicken
explanations.body: A written note: Direksiyon papuntang Max Fried Chicken. In the book the first line is printed with the numeral 1; here it is written in words.

examples.text: Kunin mo ang Highway isa Timog.
examples.translation: Take Highway 1 South.

examples.text: Lumabas sa Carmona exit.
examples.translation: Exit at Carmona.

examples.text: Pagkatapos, kumanan sa ilalim ng unang tulay.
examples.translation: Afterwards, turn right under the first bridge.

examples.text: Tuluy-tuloy lang nang mga tatlong kilometro.
examples.translation: Just continue for about three kilometers.

examples.text: Nasa kabilang daan ang resto.
examples.translation: The restaurant is on the opposite side of the road.

examples.text: Bawal kasi ang mag-u-turn kaya lumiko ka sa kanan saka mag-u-turn.
examples.translation: Making a U-turn is prohibited so turn right and then make a U-turn.

examples.text: Pagkatapos, kumanan ulit sa unang kanto sa panulukan ng Rizal at Josephine St.
examples.translation: Afterwards, turn right again at the first corner at the corner of Rizal and Josephine St.

examples.text: Pumarada ka na lang diyan at lumakad ka na lang.
examples.translation: Just park there and walk.

examples.text: Wala kasing sariling parking ang resto.
examples.translation: The restaurant has no parking of its own.

examples.text: Lampasan mo lang ang sakayan ng bus at gasolinahan.
examples.translation: Just walk past the bus station and gas station.

examples.text: Nasa bandang kaliwa lang ang Max Fried Chicken sa tabi mismo ng isang panaderya.
examples.translation: Max Fried Chicken is just to the left, exactly next to a bakery.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions (A)
explanations.body: Umexit is a synonym for lumabas. Resto is short for restaurant. Lumabas, dumiretso, kumanan, kumaliwa, lumiko and pumarada are um verbs. Kanto (corner) is often used interchangeably with bloke (block).

rows: the opposite side of the road, opposite lane

explanations.title: Presentation 2B: common expressions used in asking for directions
explanations.body: Where the book gives alternatives (sa address, sa estasyon ng pulis, sa ospital, sa himpilan ng radyo, sa hotel), each is listed as its own question.

examples.text: Paano po ba makarating sa address na ito?
examples.translation: How do I get to this address?

examples.text: Paano po ba makarating sa estasyon ng pulis?
examples.translation: How do I get to the police station?

examples.text: Paano po ba makarating sa ospital?
examples.translation: How do I get to the hospital?

examples.text: Paano po ba makarating sa himpilan ng radyo?
examples.translation: How do I get to the radio station?

examples.text: Paano po ba makarating sa hotel?
examples.translation: How do I get to the hotel?

examples.text: Saan po ba ang sakayan ng bus papuntang Pangasinan?
examples.translation: Where is the bus station for Pangasinan?

examples.text: Gaano po ba kalayo ang paliparan mula dito? Paano po sumakay? Saan po sasakay?
examples.translation: How far is the airport from here? How do I ride? Where do I get on?

examples.text: Malayo pa po ba ang sakayan? Ilang kilometro po mula dito?
examples.translation: Is the station still far? How many kilometers from here?

examples.text: Saan po puwedeng magtanong ng direksiyon?
examples.translation: Where can I ask for directions?

examples.text: Alam n’yo po ba ang daan papuntang Embahada ng Amerika?
examples.translation: Do you know the way to the American Embassy?

explanations.title: Notes and expressions (B)
explanations.body: Estasyon and himpilan (station) are synonyms. Paano, gaano, saan and ilan are question words. Estasyon, pulis, kilometro, direksiyon, embahada and Amerika are cognates. The preposition sa in sa address na ito, sa estasyon ng pulis, sa ospital, sa himpilan ng radyo and sa hotel means “to.”

explanations.title: Comprehension check, notes on directions (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Main idea: a note providing directions to a restaurant (a driving instruction on how to go to a restaurant). Landmarks: bus station, gasoline station, bakery. The ten details: take Highway 1 South; exit at Carmona; turn right under the bridge; continue for 3 kilometers; the restaurant is on the opposite side of the road; making a U-turn is prohibited so turn right first then U-turn; turn right again at the first corner along Rizal and Josephine St.; park and walk because the restaurant has no parking space; walk past the bus station and gas station; the restaurant is on the left, next to a bakery.

explanations.title: Comprehension check, asking for directions (the book’s key)
explanations.body: The six questions ask: how to get to a specific address, police station, radio station or hotel; where the bus station for Pangasinan-bound buses is; how far the airport is and how and where to ride; the distance of the bus or jeepney station in kilometers; where to ask for directions; and the direction to the US Embassy.

explanations.title: Activity 1: a DLI student and a teacher (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Main idea: the conversation is about the new Filipino bakery that recently opened in downtown Monterey. Distance: about one mile. Directions: walk straight from the Franklin gate, go all the way until you see a bank, go past the bank after passing Tyler St., turn onto Figueroa St., turn right on Church St.; the bakery is on the left.

examples.text: Gng. Ong, may bagong bukas na panaderyang Pilipino daw dito sa Monterey.
examples.translation: Student: Mrs. Ong, there is said to be a newly opened Filipino bakery here in Monterey.

examples.text: Oo. Meron nga. Gusto mo bang pumunta?
examples.translation: Teacher: Yes. There is indeed. Do you want to go?

examples.text: Siyempre po. Saan po ba ’yon?
examples.translation: Student: Of course. Where is it?

examples.text: Madali lang. Mga isang milya lang mula rito sa DLI. Paglabas mo sa Franklin gate, tuloy-tuloy ka lang.
examples.translation: Teacher: It’s easy. Only about a mile from here at DLI. When you come out of the Franklin gate, just keep going.

examples.text: Tapos po?
examples.translation: Student: And then?

examples.text: Makikita mo ang bangko. Lampasan mo ang bangko pagkatapos ng kalye Tyler. Lumiko ka sa kalye Figueroa. Kumanan ka sa kalye Church, sa bandang kaliwa ang bagong panaderya.
examples.translation: Teacher: You will see the bank. Go past the bank after Tyler Street. Turn onto Figueroa Street. Turn right on Church Street; the new bakery is on the left.

examples.text: Maraming salamat po, Gng. Ong. Paalam po.
examples.translation: Student: Thank you very much, Mrs. Ong. Goodbye.

lessons.title: 185. C11 L1 · Um verbs for directions, pa/pa+um/patungo and the conjunctions at, pero, pagkatapos, kasi
lessons.subtitle: Kumanan ka · Pumasilangan ka · Pahilaga, pumahilaga, patungong hilaga · At, pero, pagkatapos, kasi

explanations.title: A. Um verbs for giving directions and instructions
explanations.body: One use of um verbs is giving directions and instructions. Three things are instructive. (1) The infinitive form of the verb is used. (2) Unlike in English, “you” (ka, kayo) is not optional in ordinary speech or writing; only in printed directions and military commands is the word omitted. (3) “You” comes right after the verb, except in the presence of a few words such as lang (“just”) when used with the plural kayo (as in Dumiretso lang po kayo).

examples.translation: Make a right on the first street.

examples.text: Umakyat ka sa bahay.
examples.translation: Go up to the house (go inside the house).

examples.text: Tumuloy kayo sa gusali.
examples.translation: Go into the building.

explanations.title: The um verbs in the presentations
explanations.body: Identify the um verbs in these sentences and translate them. The um verbs are dumiretso, kumaliwa, kunin, lumabas, kumanan, lumiko, kumanan, kumaliwa and pumarada. (Where the book writes lumakad or limakad in the last line, the lesson writes maglakad, which is the form the dialog used; both mean “walk.”)

examples.text: Dumiretso lang po kayo sa kalyeng ito.
examples.translation: Just go straight on this street.

examples.text: Kumaliwa po kayo.
examples.translation: Make a left turn, sir or ma’am.

examples.text: Kunin mo ang Highway isa Timog.
examples.translation: Take Highway 1 South.

examples.translation: Exit at Carmona.

examples.translation: Turn right and make a U-turn again.

examples.translation: Afterwards, make a right again at the first corner, then turn left.

examples.translation: Just park there and walk.

explanations.title: Additional um verbs: past, present, future
explanations.body: Practice conjugating these verbs. The past and the infinitive share the same form (the um goes after the first consonant); the present repeats the first syllable after the um; the future repeats the first syllable of the root. Verbs whose root begins with a vowel start with um: umabante, umaabante, aabante.

explanations.title: B. Pa, pa+um and patungo with direction words
explanations.body: To express “go in the direction of” or “in the manner of” use pa, pa+um or patungo with direction words. With pa: papunta (going to), pababa (going down), pahilaga (going north), paakyat (going up). You can add pa to other direction words: pasilangan (going east), pakanluran (going west), patimog (going south). To form pa+um simply add um after the letter p: pa + um = pumasilangan. Patungo means “going in the direction of”; with a direction word it takes the linker ng: patungong hilaga.

examples.text: Papunta na ako diyan.
examples.translation: I’ll be going there now, or I’m on my way there now.

examples.text: Pababa na ako ng bahay.
examples.translation: I’m going down now from the house.

examples.text: Mag-drive kang pahilaga.
examples.translation: Drive going to the north.

examples.text: Paakyat ang daan diyan.
examples.translation: The road there is going up.

examples.translation: Go towards the east for about two miles.

examples.text: Tapos pumatimog ka ng sampung milya.
examples.translation: Then go towards the south for ten miles.

examples.text: Pumakanluran ka.
examples.translation: Go towards the west.

examples.text: Pumakanan ka ng mga singkuwenta piye.
examples.translation: Go right for about fifty feet.

examples.text: Mag-drive kang patungong hilaga.
examples.translation: Drive towards the north.

explanations.title: The direction words with pa, pa+um and patungo
Practice
explanations.body: As a class, give a command or direction to the classmate on your right, using ka or kayo as appropriate; the class judges whether the task was done correctly (a classroom activity, left out).

explanations.title: C. The conjunctions at, pero, pagkatapos and kasi
explanations.body: Conjunctions (pangatnig in Tagalog) connect words, phrases or whole clauses. At can mean “and” or “because.” Pero means “but”; it is a Spanish cognate; subali’t, nguni’t and datapwa’t mean the same but are used in higher-level discourse or formal prose. Pagkatapos means “after,” “afterwards” or “then.” Kasi means “because.”

examples.translation: Because it is forbidden to make a U-turn, turn right and then make a U-turn again.

examples.translation: Because the restaurant does not have its own parking.

lessons.title: 186. C11 L1 · Practice: um verbs, conjunctions, transcribing and a gist of directions
lessons.subtitle: Lumipat kayo · Lumiko o liliko? · Kumaliwa po kayo sa David Ave. · Paano ba ang pagpunta sa bangko?

explanations.title: Activity 2: identify the um verb and translate (the book’s key)

rows: Lumabas ka sa kanan sa Broadway.
Exit to the right at Broadway.
Pumunta kayo sa estasyon ng bus.
Tumuloy ka sa unang kalye sa kanan.
Go or proceed to the first street on the right.
Tumabi po kayo sa tabi ng kalsada.
Go to the side of the street.

explanations.title: Activity 3: choose the correct verb form (the book’s key)
explanations.body: The key: 1. Lumiko; 2. Dumeretso; 3. Kumanan; 4. Lumiko; 5. Umabante. Items 1 and 2 use a past verb (kanina, kahapon); the others are commands, which use the infinitive.

explanations.title: Activity 4: choose the best conjunction (the book’s key)
explanations.body: The key: 1. at; 2. at; 3. pagkatapos; 4. kasi; 5. kasi.

examples.text: Kumaliwa po kayo sa David Ave. at dumeretso sa Forest Ave.
examples.translation: Turn left on David Ave. and go straight on Forest Ave.

examples.text: Nasa bandang kanan ang malaking palengke ng bayan.
examples.translation: The big town market is on the right side.

examples.translation: The new church can be seen in front of the gasoline station.

examples.translation: Your landmarks are Plaza Miranda and the Quiapo church.

explanations.title: Activity 6: Marissa and Alan, translate the underlined phrases (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Key for the five underlined phrases: 1. How do you go to the bank from DLI? 2. From here at Franklin Gate, go straight to Franklin St. 3. You will see the bank on the right. 4. After Tyler St., turn right into the bank parking lot. 5. The bank is on the right side.

examples.text: Sir, puwede bang magtanong?
examples.translation: Marissa: Sir, may I ask something?

examples.text: Opo, ano iyon?
examples.translation: Alan: Yes, what is it?

examples.text: Gusto naming pumunta sa Bank of America. Paano ba ang pagpunta sa bangko mula sa DLI?
examples.translation: Marissa: We want to go to Bank of America. How do you go to the bank from DLI?

examples.text: Madali lang po. Mula rito sa Franklin Gate, dere-deretso lang kayo dito sa Franklin St. at makikita n’yo ang bangko sa kanan, malapit sa Tyler at Washington St.
examples.translation: Alan: It is easy. From here at Franklin Gate, just go straight along Franklin St. and you will see the bank on the right, near Tyler and Washington St.

examples.text: Pagkatapos ng Tyler St., kumanan kayo sa paradahan ng bangko. Nasa kanan ang bangko.
examples.translation: Alan: After Tyler St., turn right into the bank’s parking lot. The bank is on the right side.

examples.text: Maraming salamat po sa inyo.
examples.translation: Marissa: Thank you very much.

examples.text: Wala pong anuman.
examples.translation: Alan: You’re welcome.

explanations.title: Activity 7: directions from the San Carlos Cathedral (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Give the gist in one or two sentences. Key: the directions are from the San Carlos Cathedral to the speaker’s family’s house, which is on Airport Rd., number 234, with a white fence.

lessons.subtitle: Dumeretso lang po kayo sa kalye Mabini · Kunin mo ang SLEX · Magbus kayo sa Lawton

explanations.title: Activity 8: complete the map (the book’s scripts)
explanations.body: In the book you listen to the two segments and write the names of the establishments and landmarks on a map, starting from a blue arrow (the map and audio are left out). The scripts follow. Landmarks in order: on Mabini Street the bank on the left, a big building on the right and a new bakery at the left corner of Mabini and San Juan; then on San Juan and Quirino Streets a church on the left, the cemetery behind the church on Burgos Street, and the turo-turo next to the cemetery at the corner of Burgos and San Juan.

examples.text: Dumeretso lang po kayo sa kalye Mabini.
examples.translation: Just go straight on Mabini Street.

examples.text: Sa pangalawang bloke makikita n’yo ang bangko sa kaliwa at isang malaking gusali naman sa kanan.
examples.translation: At the second block you will see the bank on the left and a big building on the right.

examples.text: May bagong bukas na panaderya rin sa may kaliwang kanto ng kalye Mabini at Kalye San Juan.
examples.translation: There is also a newly opened bakery at the left corner of Mabini Street and San Juan Street.

examples.text: Kumanan po kayo sa kalye San Juan.
examples.translation: Turn right on San Juan Street.

examples.text: Tapos, kumanan kayo sa kalye Quirino.
examples.translation: Then turn right on Quirino Street.

examples.text: Sa bandang kaliwa makikita n’yo ang isang simbahan.
examples.translation: On the left you will see a church.

examples.text: Sa likod mismo ng simbahan, sa may Kalye Burgos, makikita n’yo ang sementeryo.
examples.translation: Right behind the church, along Burgos Street, you will see the cemetery.

examples.text: Katabi lang po ng sementeryo ang turu-turo sa kanto ng Kalye Burgos at Kalye San Juan.
examples.translation: Right next to the cemetery is the turo-turo (eatery) at the corner of Burgos Street and San Juan Street.

explanations.title: Activity 9: a conversation between friends (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Teacher note: before this activity the book introduces SLEX (South Luzon Expressway), Mercury Drug Store (the biggest chain of botika in the Philippines), Sucat Road in Parañaque City (next to Makati City) and the basketball courts found along residential streets. Key: 1. Alice informs Enrico there will be a party at Gary’s house for the baptism of Gary’s son, at lunchtime on Sunday, and invites Enrico. 2. Take SLEX, exit at Sucat Road (not at the bridge), the Mercury Drug Store is the landmark on the right, go more than three blocks on Sucat Road then turn left; that is Goodwill Subdivision. 3. At Rainbow Drive the church is on your left; go straight until you see a basketball court; across it, on the right, you will see a yellow and white painted gate, which is Gary’s house. 4. Enrico asks Alice to tell Gary he will arrive at about 1:00 p.m. In the book the house is also written Block 9 Lot 11.

explanations.title: Activity 10: two people giving directions to their homes (the book’s script)
explanations.body: The book prints multiple-choice items and no key; the answers below follow from the script (my key). Passage 1: 1. b, the jeepney station in Tejero is beside the gasoline station; 2. c, the speaker will pick up his friends in Malabon. Passage 2: 1. a, go to the front of an elementary school; 2. b, the speaker’s house is across the elementary school.

examples.text: Magbus kayo sa Lawton. Kunin ninyo ’yung bus na tuluy-tuloy ng Tejero.
examples.translation: Take a bus at Lawton. Take the bus that goes straight through to Tejero.

examples.text: Sa Tejero, puntahan ninyo ang sakayan ng dyip para sa Malabon, nasa tabi lang ng gasolinahan ng Seaoil.
examples.translation: In Tejero, go to the jeepney station for Malabon, just beside the Seaoil gasoline station.

examples.text: Susunduin ko kayo sa simbahan ng Malabon, mga labinlimang minuto lang ang biyahe mula sa sakayan ng dyip.
examples.translation: I will pick you up at the Malabon church; the trip from the jeepney station is only about fifteen minutes.

examples.text: Mula sa kanto ng F. B. Harrison at F. Redemptorist, kumanan ka.
examples.translation: From the corner of F. B. Harrison and F. Redemptorist, turn right.

examples.text: Lumakad ka hanggang sa gasolinahan.
examples.translation: Walk until the gasoline station.

examples.text: Sa tapat ng gasolinahan ang kalye Bagong Ilog. Puntahan mo iyon.
examples.translation: Bagong Ilog Street is across from the gasoline station. Go there.

examples.text: Lumakad ka hanggang Bagong Lipunan. Tapos, kumanan ka at dumiretso hanggang makarating ka sa harap ng P. Cuneta Elementary School.
examples.translation: Walk until Bagong Lipunan. Then turn right and go straight until you reach the front of P. Cuneta Elementary School.

examples.text: Nasa tapat lang ang bahay namin.
examples.translation: Our house is just across.

explanations.title: Activity 11: guided conversation, finding a seamstress
explanations.body: You have been stationed in Barangay Tinagong Dagat, Narra, Palawan, and your new uniform needs alterations. You ask your neighbor for directions to a known seamstress or tailor. A (the soldier): ask how to get to the address; ask the street’s name; say you’re afraid you’d get lost; thank your neighbor. B (the neighbor): say it is easy, take a jeep for Barangay Bato-Bato, San Isidro, get off at the gasoline station across from the market, there’s a small street to the left of the gasoline station; say you don’t know the street’s name; emphatically say no, just follow the street until he sees a big mango tree, turn right and he will see a small eating place (karinderya) and next to it Aling Iska’s or Mang Isko’s house; say you’re welcome. A sample:

examples.text: Magandang araw po. Paano po ba makakarating sa bahay ng mananahi?
examples.translation: Soldier: Good day. How can I get to the seamstress’s house?

examples.text: Madali lang. Sumakay ka ng dyip papuntang Barangay Bato-Bato, San Isidro. Bumaba ka sa gasolinahan sa tapat ng palengke. May maliit na kalye sa kaliwa ng gasolinahan.
examples.translation: Neighbor: It’s easy. Take a jeepney bound for Barangay Bato-Bato, San Isidro. Get off at the gasoline station across from the market. There is a small street to the left of the gasoline station.

examples.text: Ano po ang pangalan ng kalye?
examples.translation: Soldier: What is the name of the street?

examples.text: Hindi ko alam.
examples.translation: Neighbor: I don’t know.

examples.text: Baka po maligaw ako.
examples.translation: Soldier: I’m afraid I might get lost.

examples.text: Hindi! Sundan mo lang ang kalye hanggang makita mo ang malaking puno ng mangga. Kumanan ka at makikita mo ang maliit na karinderya. Katabi nito ang bahay ni Aling Iska.
examples.translation: Neighbor: No! Just follow the street until you see a big mango tree. Turn right and you will see a small eating place. Next to it is Aling Iska’s house.

examples.text: Maraming salamat po.
examples.translation: Soldier: Thank you very much.

examples.text: Walang anuman.
examples.translation: Neighbor: You’re welcome.

explanations.title: Activity 12: role play, directions to a restaurant in Tayabas
explanations.body: You want to thank the Filipino family in Tayabas, Quezon who invited you for dinner by treating them to a restaurant next weekend. A friend suggested Kamayan sa Palaisdaan. You call for driving directions from your hotel and make a reservation (the book’s map and menu are left out). Student A: greet the reservations clerk, ask for landmarks and street names and make a reservation. Student B, the clerk: return the greeting, say the restaurant’s name, ask what you can do, and give specific directions including at least three landmarks, an intersection and at least two street names. A sample:

examples.text: Magandang hapon po. Gusto ko pong malaman ang direksiyon papunta sa Kamayan sa Palaisdaan mula sa hotel namin.
examples.translation: Customer: Good afternoon. I would like to know the directions to Kamayan sa Palaisdaan from our hotel.

examples.text: Magandang hapon din po. Kamayan sa Palaisdaan po ito. Ano po ang maitutulong ko sa inyo?
examples.translation: Clerk: Good afternoon too. This is Kamayan sa Palaisdaan. How can I help you?

examples.text: Ano po ang mga palatandaan at pangalan ng mga kalye?
examples.translation: Customer: What are the landmarks and street names?

examples.text: Mula sa plaza, dumeretso po kayo sa Rizal Street hanggang sa unang kanto. Kumanan po kayo sa Mabini Street. Makikita ninyo ang simbahan, ang paaralan at ang gasolinahan. Nasa tabi po ng gasolinahan ang restawran namin.
examples.translation: Clerk: From the plaza, go straight on Rizal Street to the first corner. Turn right on Mabini Street. You will see the church, the school and the gasoline station. Our restaurant is next to the gasoline station.

examples.text: Gusto ko rin pong magpareserba para sa Sabado.
examples.translation: Customer: I would also like to make a reservation for Saturday.

examples.text: Sige po. Para sa ilang tao po?
examples.translation: Clerk: Certainly. For how many people?

explanations.title: Activity 13: challenge yourself
explanations.body: a. With a current map of Monterey, Carmel or Pacific Grove, be ready to ask for and give directions (at least five each) to classmates. b. With an identical map of a town, draw lots for establishments (bank, hotel, school, bus station) and give directions by landmarks (in front of, beside, next to, across from) and by starting and end points (street names, turn right or left, go straight); the class guesses which establishment it is (map-based class activities, left out).

units.title: Chapter 11 · Lesson 2: Daily activities

lessons.title: 189. C11 L2 · A son’s journal: my daily routine
lessons.subtitle: Gumigising ako nang maaga · Nagbabaon lang ako para makatipid · Bunso kasi ako

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: By the end of the lesson you can extract information from reading and listening passages about one’s daily activities; identify words and expressions related to a person’s daily activities; transcribe and translate expressions related to daily activities; and relate your daily activities using the expressions learned. The structures are the core vocabulary, the mang verbs, the conjunctions kaya, kapag and para, and the mag verbs in the present form. In the book a mind map of daily action words (nagluluto, nag-aaral and others) opens the lesson and you add more in Tagalog.

explanations.title: Presentation 1A: a son’s journal outlining his daily routine

examples.text: Mahirap pala kapag malayo sa nanay.
examples.translation: It turns out it is hard when you are far from your mother.

examples.text: Nag-aadjust pa ako dito.
examples.translation: I am still adjusting here.

examples.text: Gumigising ako nang maaga.
examples.translation: I wake up early.

examples.text: Pagkagising ko, nagdadasal, nagsisipilyo, naliligo, naghihilamos, nagbibihis, nag-aalmusal.
examples.translation: Right after waking up, I pray, brush my teeth, take a shower, wash my face, put on clothes and have breakfast.

examples.text: Tapos pumapasok sa klase.
examples.translation: Then I go to class.

examples.text: Kadalasan sa iskul na ako nanananghalian.
examples.translation: I usually have lunch at school.

examples.text: Nagbabaon lang ako para makatipid.
examples.translation: I just bring my own food to save money.

examples.text: Pagkatapos ng klase sa hapon, nagla-library muna ako, nag-re-research, at nag-aaral din.
examples.translation: After class in the afternoon, I first go to the library, do research and also study.

examples.text: Minsan nagluluto din ako.
examples.translation: Sometimes I also cook.

examples.text: Nung nasa probinsiya ako, si nanay lahat ang gumagawa para sa akin.
examples.translation: When I was in the province, Mother did everything for me.

examples.text: Minsan si Ate ang naglalaba ng mga damit ko.
examples.translation: Sometimes Ate washed my clothes.

examples.text: Hindi ko nga naranasan ang humawak ng balde o palanggana.
examples.translation: I never even experienced holding a pail or a basin.

examples.text: Bunso kasi ako.
examples.translation: Because I am the youngest.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Nag-aadjust, nagla-library and nagre-research are examples of mag verbs with cognates (English words). Kapag and para are conjunctions (explained in the grammar section). In the first paragraph the affix pagka in pagkagising means “right after,” so pagkagising means “right after waking up.”

explanations.title: Comprehension check, Journal A (the book’s key)

rows: Waking up early, praying, brushing the teeth, taking a shower, washing the face, putting on clothes, having breakfast.
2. Two things the son normally didn’t do

He didn’t normally cook and do laundry; his mom and older sister did those chores for him. He doesn’t even know how to hold a pail and basin. He is the youngest in the family and was spared those chores.
3. What he says about being away from his family
It is not easy to live far away from his mom, and he is still adjusting.

explanations.title: Culture note: harana
explanations.body: Harana is the Filipino name of a traditional form of courtship in which a man woos a woman’s affection by singing underneath her window. This traditional culture is still alive and typically common in rural areas. In metropolitan cities one may request harana online for a fee.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Nangangaso, nanghuhuli, nanghaharana, namimitas, nanghihiram, namamangka, namimingwit, nananahi and nangangalap are mang verbs in the present form (see the grammar section). A baryo (barrio), now referred to as barangay (according to the 1987 Philippine Constitution), is the smallest administrative division in the Philippines; a baryo is equivalent to a village or a small suburban place. Punit (torn) na damit can also be used for sirang damit. Isla, a Spanish cognate, is a synonym of pulo.

rows: fishing with a hook and line

explanations.title: Comprehension check, Journal B (the book’s key)
explanations.body: A typical day in the barrio, seven details: hunting wild boar; catching crab and shrimp; gathering empty clamshells on the seashore; taking a stroll by the lake with family; exploring the bigger caves; (sometimes) serenading; joining my older sister in picking wild flowers in the meadow; borrowing someone else’s boat and going boating; fishing with hook and line; sewing torn clothes and pants; recruiting new volunteers to help clean the church.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Kumusta and kamusta may be used interchangeably. The long nang precedes an expression of clock time (nang alas-singko). Na-le-late is a ma verb using a cognate. Notice the repeated use of lang and naman in the dialog. Nakakainip is a synonym of nakakabagot.

explanations.title: Culture note: the Philippine National Police Academy
explanations.body: The PNPA was created to provide preparatory education and training for the three uniformed bureaus of the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG): the Philippine National Police (PNP), the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) and the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP).

rows: to do at the same time

explanations.title: Comprehension check (the book’s key)
explanations.body: 1. Luis’s typical day: he wakes up very early, does physical training at about 5 a.m., returns to the barracks immediately, takes his meal and puts on clothes, then runs to class because he doesn’t want to be late. 2. His experience: it is not easy to study and do the training at the same time. 3. What he was doing at the time of the conversation: the book prints no key; from the dialog he is on a Christmas vacation and is telling his friend about the academy. 4. What Sonia noticed: he lost weight.

explanations.title: Activity 1: Brandon’s email to his younger brother Jake (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Brandon outlines his daily routine as an OJT (on-the-job trainee) at ABS-CBN in Manila. The book notes that ABS-CBN is a major commercial television network in the Philippines and that its international channel is TFC, The Filipino Channel. Key: 1. In the morning Brandon takes a shower, brushes his teeth, goes to work, has breakfast and wakes up; he does not comb his hair, wash his face, cook breakfast or pray (in the email). 2. He wishes his parents would visit him. 3. His first week was not easy.

lessons.title: 192. C11 L2 · Mang verbs, the conjunctions kaya, kapag and para, and mag verbs in the present
lessons.subtitle: Nananahi, namimingwit, nangangaso · Kaya · Kapag · Para · Naglalaba, nagluluto

explanations.title: A. Mang verbs
explanations.body: Mang verbs focus on the doer in the sentence and can be both transitive and intransitive. The majority of mang verbs express negative actions (you will learn those in future lessons). In some cases mang verbs denote something that is done repeatedly but not as a habit. Mang has three variants, man, mam and mang, depending on the initial syllable of the root word. 1. For roots beginning with D, L, R, S or T, man is the prefix and the first letter of the root is dropped (tahi becomes manahi). 2. For roots beginning with B or P, mam is the prefix and the first letter of the root is dropped (bangka becomes mamangka). 3. For roots starting with other letters, mang is used; only the first letter of a root starting with k (kalap) is dropped, and the rest keep their form (huli becomes manghuli; aso becomes mangaso; harana becomes mangharana). The book’s table prints naghaharana for the present of harana; the correct form is nanghaharana, as in the reading.

rows: pitas (gathering from a tree or plant)

explanations.title: B. The conjunction kaya
explanations.body: In complex sentences, kaya may begin the dependent phrase with the meaning “so,” “therefore” or “that’s why.” Review of lesson 1: Hindi ko naranasan iyan kasi ako ang bunso (I did not experience it because I was the youngest); Mabuti at may bakasyon ka (Good, because you have vacation leave).

explanations.title: The conjunctions kung, kapag and pag
explanations.body: Kung, kapag or pag mean “during,” “in” or “whenever” in recurring time periods; they also mean “when” in the present and future. The three are interchangeable in these sentences.

examples.text: Mahirap pala kapag malayo sa nanay.
examples.translation: It is very difficult whenever mother is far away.

examples.text: Nagha-hiking kami ng pamilya ko sa Yosemite kapag tag-init.
examples.translation: My family goes hiking in Yosemite during summer.

examples.translation: Their place has ice and snow during winter.

examples.text: Mag-aral ka kapag may oras ka.
examples.translation: Study when you have the time.

examples.text: Kapag wala kang ginagawa, sumama ka sa amin ng kuya mo sa sine.
examples.translation: When you are not busy go with us and your brother to the movies.

explanations.title: The conjunction para
explanations.body: Para means “so that” (in order to).

examples.text: Nagbabaon lang ako para makatipid.
examples.translation: I just bring my own lunch in order to save.

examples.text: Magluluto na ako ngayon para mamayang gabi kakain na lang ako.
examples.translation: I’ll cook now so that this evening I’ll just eat.

explanations.title: C. Review of mag verbs
explanations.body: To narrate one’s daily activities, the present form of mag is used. Mag is also used to verbalize nouns and can be translated “let’s do,” depending on the context; you can put it in front of English nouns. The reading’s mag verbs, and their tenses:

explanations.title: Activity 8: a conversation between two colleagues (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Write at least five essential elements of information. Key: 1. Sandra is inviting her friend Stella to relax during a day off. 2. Both have multiple chores and two jobs. 3. They hardly have time for relaxation. 4. Stella has no time for breakfast because she has two jobs. 5. Sandra has hardly had time to relax because she is also taking care of her kids.

examples.text: Stella, mag-relax tayo! Lagi ka na lang nagtatrabaho.
examples.translation: Sandra: Stella, let’s relax! You are always working.

examples.text: ’Mareng Sandra, wala akong oras. Dalawa ang trabaho ko. Wala akong pahinga! Nag-aalmusal nga ako habang nagluluto at naglilinis ng bahay, e.
examples.translation: Stella: Comadre Sandra, I have no time. I have two jobs. I have no rest! I even eat breakfast while cooking and cleaning the house.

examples.text: ’Mare, ako rin dala-dalawa ang trabaho ko. Nag-aalaga pa ako ng mga anak ko. Pero kailangan rin nating magpahinga at mag-relax paminsan-minsan.
examples.translation: Sandra: Comadre, I too have two jobs each. I also take care of my children. But we also need to rest and relax once in a while.

examples.text: Sige na nga, day off naman ngayon.
examples.translation: Stella: All right then, it’s a day off today anyway.

explanations.title: Activity 9: a Tagalog language student talks about her routine at DLI (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Write the activities in the morning and afternoon columns. Morning: wakes up at 5 a.m.; brushing teeth; washing the face; military training at 6:00 a.m.; goes to class at 7:30 a.m. Afternoon: goes home at 3:45 p.m.; jogging or running with fellow soldiers at 5:00 p.m.; eats at the Chow Hall; does homework at night.

examples.text: Napakahirap ng schedule ko mula Lunes hanggang Biyernes.
examples.translation: My schedule is very hard from Monday to Friday.

examples.text: Gumigising ako nang alas-singko ng umaga, nagsisipilyo, naghihilamos, nagsasanay militar nang alas-sais, tapos pumapasok sa eskuwela nang alas-siyete y medya.
examples.translation: I wake up at five in the morning, brush my teeth, wash my face, do military training at six, then go to school at seven-thirty.

examples.text: Sa hapon, umuuwi ako nang alas-tres kuwarenta y singko.
examples.translation: In the afternoon I go home at 3:45.

examples.text: Tumatakbo ako at ng iba pang sundalo tuwing alas-singko ng hapon.
examples.translation: The other soldiers and I run every day at five in the afternoon.

examples.text: Tapos, naghahapunan ako sa Chow Hall.
examples.translation: Then I have supper at the Chow Hall.

examples.text: Sa gabi, gumagawa ako ng homework.
examples.translation: At night I do homework.

explanations.title: Activity 10: the typical day of a student at DLI (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Write the present-tense verb for each activity in its time frame. The verbs in the book’s table, grouped by the script (my key): 5:00 a.m. to 7:00 a.m.: gumigising, naghihilamos, nagsisipilyo, nagbibihis, nag-jo-jogging, naliligo, nag-aalmusal, bumibili. 7:30 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.: pumapasok, nagbubus, nag-aaral, natatapos, nanananghalian, umuuwi. 3:30 p.m. to 10:00 p.m.: nagpapahinga, naglilinis, nagsasanay-pisikal, naghahapunan, nanonood, naglalaro, natutulog.

examples.text: Gumigising ako nang alas-singko y medya tuwing umaga.
examples.translation: I wake up at 5:30 every morning.

examples.text: Naghihilamos, nagsisipilyo, at nagbibihis ako.
examples.translation: I wash my face, brush my teeth and dress.

examples.text: May mga araw na nag-jo-jogging kami bago magklase. Kapag ganun, naliligo ako pagkatapos.
examples.translation: On some days we jog before class. When that happens, I shower afterwards.

examples.text: Nag-aalmusal ako nang bandang alas-siyete sa Chow Hall o bumibili ng pagkain sa kapiterya.
examples.translation: I have breakfast at around seven at the Chow Hall or buy food at the cafeteria.

examples.text: Pumapasok ako sa eskuwelahan nang alas-siyete y medya. Nagbubus ako papuntang klase.
examples.translation: I go to school at seven-thirty. I take the bus to class.

examples.text: Nag-aaral kami nang anim na oras araw-araw, umpisa ng alas-siyete singkuwenta y singko nang umaga.
examples.translation: We study for six hours every day, starting at 7:55 in the morning.

examples.text: Natatapos ang klase sa umaga nang alas-diyes kuwarenta y singko.
examples.translation: The morning class ends at 10:45.

examples.text: Tapos, nanananghalian ako. Umuuwi ako ng baraks nang alas-tres n.h.
examples.translation: Then I have lunch. I go home to the barracks at three p.m.

examples.text: Sa hapon, pagkatapos ng klase, kadalasan, nagpapahinga ako.
examples.translation: In the afternoon, after class, I usually rest.

examples.text: Minsan, naglilinis ako ng kuwarto ko. Minsan naman, nagsasanay-pisikal.
examples.translation: Sometimes I clean my room. Other times I do physical training.

examples.text: Naghahapunan ako bago mag-alas-sais n.g.
examples.translation: I have supper before six p.m.

examples.text: Paminsan-minsan, nanonood ako ng TV o naglalaro ng video games. Alas-diyes natutulog na ako.
examples.translation: Once in a while I watch TV or play video games. At ten I am already asleep.

explanations.title: Activity 11: Celia shares her daily activities with her mother (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: The book’s introduction names the student Paulo but the dialog and key use Celia. Key: 1. Celia’s morning: she has breakfast and sometimes cooks to save money. 2. About her mom: she misses her mom’s cooking. 3. About college: it is difficult, even more so because she is away from her parents. 4. When not in class: she studies and does research at the library. 5. Her concept of rest: sleeping early at night.

examples.text: Celia, kamusta ka na? Magkuwento ka naman.
examples.translation: Mother: Celia, how are you? Please tell me about it.

examples.text: Eto po, maaga akong gumigising. Kailangan po, alas-siyete kinse nag-aalmusal na ako. Minsan nagluluto para makatipid po. Nami-miss ko na nga po ang luto n’yo, e.
examples.translation: Celia: Well, I wake up early. At seven-fifteen I have to be having breakfast already. Sometimes I cook to save money. I really miss your cooking.

examples.text: Hindi bale, malapit na ang bakasyon.
examples.translation: Mother: Never mind, the vacation is near.

examples.text: Gusto ko na nga hong magbakasyon. Mahirap pala ang college. Mas mahirap kasi malayo kayo ni Tatay. Kapag walang klase, nasa library po ako nag-aaral, nag-re-research.
examples.translation: Celia: I really want to take a vacation already. College is hard, it turns out. It’s harder because you and Father are far. When there is no class I am at the library studying and doing research.

examples.text: Nagsisimba ka ba? Nagpapahinga ka pa ba?
examples.translation: Mother: Do you go to church? Do you still rest?

examples.text: Siyempre po. Nagsisimba po ako tuwing Linggo. Natutulog po ako nang maaga. ’Yun na po ang pahinga ko.
examples.translation: Celia: Of course. I go to church every Sunday. I sleep early. That is my rest.

explanations.title: Activity 12: guided conversation with a friend at DLI
explanations.body: You visit your high school friend, a DLI language student, and ask how studies, military duties and the daily schedule are going. A: ask how his or her studies and training are going; tell your friend he or she will do just fine and ask about the weekday routine; ask the distance from the barracks to school. B: say it’s tough to study while doing physical training at the same time; say you wake up at around 4:30, do physical training and return to the barracks, then take a shower, eat and dress for class; say the school is a bit far, about a mile, and you usually take the bus or just run. A sample:

examples.text: Kumusta na ang pag-aaral at pagsasanay mo?
examples.translation: You: How are your studies and training going?

examples.text: Mahirap ang mag-aral habang nagsasanay pisikal.
examples.translation: Friend: It’s tough to study while doing physical training.

examples.text: Kakayanin mo iyan. Ano ang ginagawa mo sa mga araw na may pasok?
examples.translation: You: You will manage. What do you do on weekdays?

examples.text: Gumigising ako nang maaga, mga alas-kuwatro y medya. Nagsasanay pisikal ako at bumabalik sa barracks. Tapos naliligo, kumakain at nagbibihis para sa klase.
examples.translation: Friend: I wake up early, at around 4:30. I do physical training and return to the barracks. Then I take a shower, eat and dress for class.

examples.text: Gaano kalayo ang barracks sa paaralan mo?
examples.translation: You: How far is the barracks from your school?

examples.text: Medyo malayo, mga isang milya. Madalas nagbubus ako o tumatakbo na lang.
examples.translation: Friend: A bit far, about a mile. I often take the bus or just run.

explanations.title: Activity 13: role play, a regular student and a DLI student
explanations.body: You are a student at Monterey Peninsula College and your friend, a DLI student, has a slightly different routine. Use eight to ten present-tense verbs to describe your hourly activities on weekdays. Student A: greet your partner, ask about the regular routine at DLI, say your schedule is different and easier, include three things you do after waking up and before class, two during class and three after class, and ask what time he or she wakes up, the time of the training and three other things. Student B: greet in return, say it is a little difficult to study with physical training every day, tell the time you wake up, the time of the training and three things before, during and after school, say your partner’s schedule is better, and ask about it. A sample:

examples.text: Kumusta! Ano ang regular na gawain mo sa DLI?
examples.translation: A: Hello! What is your regular routine at DLI?

examples.text: Medyo mahirap ang mag-aral habang nagsasanay pisikal araw-araw. Gumigising ako nang alas-singko. Ang pisikal na pagsasanay ay nang alas-sais.
examples.translation: B: It’s a little hard to study while doing physical training every day. I wake up at five. The physical training is at six.

examples.text: Iba ang iskedyul ko at mas madali kaysa sa iyo. Pagkagising ko, nagsisipilyo ako, naliligo at nag-aalmusal.
examples.translation: A: My schedule is different and easier than yours. After waking up, I brush my teeth, shower and have breakfast.

examples.text: Mas maganda at mas madali ang iskedyul mo kaysa sa akin. Anong oras ka gumigising?
examples.translation: B: Your schedule is better and easier than mine. What time do you wake up?

explanations.title: List of verbs with sample sentences from the book
explanations.body: The book’s glossary sentences. The sample under naghihilamos is printed with the root dasal by mistake (the root is hilamos), and kabibe is printed for kabibi; both are kept as the book prints the sentence.

examples.text: Gumagawa siya ng kanyang asignatura.
examples.translation: He is doing his assignment.

examples.text: Gumigising ang mga sundalo ng maagang-maaga.

examples.text: Humawak ka baka ka mahulog.
examples.translation: Hold on or you might fall.

examples.text: Mag-ayos ka naman nang konti, magsisimba tayo.

examples.translation: Please tell me about your vacation in the Philippines.

examples.text: Ayos na ang buhok mo, huwag ka nang magsuklay.

examples.text: Mahirap ang buhay nila pero natapos niya ang kanyang pag-aaral.
examples.translation: Their life is hard but he finished his studies.

examples.text: Hindi siya makatipid kasi gala siya nang gala.
examples.translation: He can’t save money because he keeps going out.

examples.text: Lagi ka bang nag-aalmusal sa cafeteria?
examples.translation: Do you always have breakfast in the cafeteria?

examples.text: Ang sipag-sipag mo naman, lagi kang nag-aaral.

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: By the end of the lesson you can extract information from reading and listening passages about weekend activities; translate and transcribe sentences with conjunctions about weekend activities; identify expressions learned about weekend activities; and use the expressions and conjunctions in speaking about weekend activities. The structures are the core vocabulary, the pseudo verbs maaari, puwede, kailangan, dapat and gusto/ayaw, the conjunctions kung and kung hindi, and a review of mag verbs. In the book a mind map of future-tense action words (magmamaneho, maglilibot, mga plano ngayong weekend) opens the lesson.

explanations.title: Note on gala nang gala
explanations.body: Gala nang gala means “to prowl”; gala refers to the travel patterns and movements of free-spirited, untamed wild animals and birds.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Note the time words nang maaga, sa umaga, sa hapon, kinabukasan and sa gabi. Magsisipilyo, mag-aahit, maghihilamos, magsasanay-militar, mag-aalmusal, magrerenta, magpapahinga and maglalaro are all mag verbs in the future tense. Filipinos commonly use the term “swimming pool” rather than palanguyan. Gusto, kailangan, maaari, puwede and dapat are pseudo verbs (explained in the grammar section).

explanations.title: Comprehension check, the narration (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Saturday: wake up early in the morning; brush teeth; shave; wash face; attend military training; have breakfast; rent a car; go strolling with his girlfriend; drive to Big Sur; (if not) go fishing at Fisherman’s Wharf; rest. Sunday: wake up early in the morning; go to the Monterey Sports Center; swim; play basketball; study; go to sleep early.

explanations.title: Comprehension check, the dialog (the book’s key)
explanations.body: 1. The invitation was to go to San Francisco this coming Saturday. 2. The woman will study this Saturday; she can’t relax because she wants to pass and get a better grade. Her mom doesn’t really want her to settle for just a passing mark, and her father doesn’t want her to just go out having fun.

explanations.title: Presentation 2A: a conversation between siblings
explanations.body: Edu is the older brother (kuya); his younger sibling is going on a first date.

explanations.title: Culture note: dating and the chaperone
explanations.body: In Filipino dating culture, some parents allow their young daughters to date as long as they have chaperones. A chaperone for a date is usually a household helper, a sibling, a cousin or someone trusted by the family. Practices are changing because of the influence of Western culture in Philippine cities, especially in the capital, Manila.

explanations.title: Presentation 2B: two friends are talking
explanations.body: In the book the woman’s first answer has two forms: Kung manlilibre ka sasama ako, or Kung libre sasama ako.

examples.text: Gusto kong kumain sa labas ngayong weekend. Gusto mo bang sumama?
examples.translation: Man: I want to eat out this weekend. Do you want to come?

examples.text: Kung manlilibre ka sasama ako.
examples.translation: Woman: If you treat me I will come.

examples.text: Kung libre sasama ako.
examples.translation: Woman: If it is free I will come (the book’s alternative).

examples.text: ’Eto na lang. Manlilibre ako sa Sabado kung tuturuan mo akong sumayaw.
examples.translation: Man: Here’s what we’ll do. I will treat you on Saturday if you teach me to dance.

examples.text: Yun lang? Oo naman. Bukas na bukas din tuturuan kitang sumayaw.
examples.translation: Woman: That’s it? Of course. Tomorrow, right away, I will teach you to dance.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Tayo na means “let’s go.” Saglit is a time word meaning “a second.” Lalabas means “to go on a date”; in another context it means “to exit” or “to go.” Walang pasok means “there is no work or no office” (or school). Kumain sa labas means “to eat outside.” ’Eto na lang means “Here’s what (we will do).” Yun lang? means “That’s it?” The enclitic din in Bukas na bukas din emphasizes that the promise to teach the man to dance will happen immediately tomorrow; another example is Ngayon din (right now).

rows: will go to the rest room
to eat outside, to eat at a restaurant
to pay for someone else’s bill

explanations.title: Comprehension check, Dialog A (the book’s key)
explanations.body: 1. Familial terms: oldest brother (kuya), oldest sister (ate), father (papa) and niece or nephew (the book’s list; the dialog itself has kuya, ate and papa). 2. The younger sibling is excited about his first date with Irene. 3. The meeting place is Irene’s house. 4. After picking up Irene, they will have dinner at a restaurant and then watch a concert. 5. On Sunday they will go biking, horseback riding and ziplining in Tagaytay along with others.

explanations.title: Comprehension check, Dialog B (the book’s key)
explanations.body: The man is inviting the woman to eat at a restaurant this weekend. The woman agrees if he pays for her meal. The man accepts the counter proposal provided the woman teaches him how to dance. The woman agrees.

lessons.title: 198. C11 L3 · Pseudo verbs: gusto, ayaw, puwede, maaari, kailangan, dapat
lessons.subtitle: Gusto, ayaw, kailangan · Pseudo verb plus infinitive · Hindi kailangang mag-aral · Ni Danny, si Danny

explanations.title: A1. The pseudo verbs and their meanings
explanations.body: Gusto, ayaw, puwede/maaari, kailangan and dapat are called pseudo verbs in Tagalog because, unlike regular verbs, they cannot show different aspects (past, present and future). The synonyms for gusto are ibig and nais, but gusto is more commonly used; nais is formal and rarely used in speech. Ayaw is the negative equivalent of gusto.

rows: do not like, do not want

explanations.title: A2. Pseudo verbs combined with main verbs
explanations.body: When a pseudo verb is combined with a main verb, the main verb is in the infinitive form. If the word preceding the verb or noun ends in a vowel, n or ng may be added (the linker); nothing is added for dapat since it ends in a consonant.

examples.translation: Can you (just) study on Sunday instead?

examples.text: Kailangang mag-aral ako sa Sabado.
examples.translation: I need to study this Saturday.

examples.text: Gusto mo bang sumama sa San Francisco ngayong Sabado?
examples.translation: Do you like to come to San Francisco this Saturday?

examples.text: Gusto mo bang kumain sa labas ngayong weekend?
examples.translation: Do you want to eat out this weekend?

examples.text: Dapat mag-relax ka naman kapag weekend.
examples.translation: You should relax too during the weekend.

explanations.title: A3. Pseudo verbs with hindi
explanations.body: Hindi is used to form a negative sentence. With pseudo verbs it is placed before the pseudo verb.

examples.text: Hindi ko kailangang mag-aral.
examples.translation: I don’t need to study.

examples.text: Hindi niya gustong pumunta sa San Francisco.
examples.translation: She or he doesn’t like to go to San Francisco.

examples.text: Hindi ako puwedeng bumagsak sa exam.
examples.translation: I cannot fail in the exam.

examples.text: Hindi ako maaaring mamasyal.
examples.translation: It is not possible for me to go strolling.

explanations.title: A4. Pseudo verbs with doer-focus verbs and proper nouns as doers
explanations.body: Pattern: pseudo verb + linker + main verb + Set II doer marker (ni) + doer + Set II object marker (ng) + object or the rest of the sentence. Columns 4 and 5 can be interchanged with columns 6 and 7, as the speaker prefers. To negate, add hindi before the pseudo verb. Sentence 4 with ayaw is already negative and doesn’t need hindi. The same sentences also work with the Set I doer marker si. (The book prints Gutong for Gustong in one sentence; the lesson writes Gustong.)

explanations.title: A6. Pseudo verbs used by themselves: indefinite objects
explanations.body: Pseudo verbs can be used by themselves. The objects here are marked with Set II markers and are translated “a” or “an.”

examples.text: Gusto ni Soledad ng bagong uniporme.
examples.translation: Soledad wants a new uniform.

examples.text: Ibig nina Gracia at Blessie ng malaking bahay.
examples.translation: Gracia and Blessie want a big house.

examples.text: Nais niya ng mahal na damit.
examples.translation: She or he would like an expensive dress.

examples.text: Ayaw nila noon.
examples.translation: They don’t want that.

examples.text: Kailangan nito ng pagkain.
examples.translation: This person needs food.

explanations.title: A6. Pseudo verbs by themselves: definite objects
explanations.body: If you want the object to be definite, Set I markers, pronouns and demonstratives are used (ang, and Set I demonstratives like iyan).

examples.text: Gusto ni Soledad ang bagong uniporme.
examples.translation: Soledad wants the new uniform.

examples.text: Ibig nina Gracia at Blessie ang malaking bahay.
examples.translation: Gracia and Blessie want the new house.

examples.text: Nais niya ang mahal na damit.
examples.translation: She or he would like the expensive dress.

examples.text: Kailangan nito ang pagkain.
examples.translation: This person needs the food.

examples.text: Gusto ko iyan.
examples.translation: I like that (not something else).

explanations.title: A7. Pseudo verbs as “intensified” verbs
explanations.body: Pseudo verbs can be repeated to intensify their meaning. Na or ng is placed after the first pseudo verb.

examples.text: Gustung-gusto kong pumunta pero wala akong oras.
examples.translation: I really want to go but I don’t have time.

examples.text: Ayaw na ayaw ni Nanay ng pasado lang.
examples.translation: My mom really doesn’t want just a passing grade.

examples.text: Kailangang-kailangan kong mag-aral.
examples.translation: I really need to study.

examples.text: Pagkatapos nating mag-aral puwedeng-puwede na tayong mamasyal.
examples.translation: After we study we really can go strolling.

explanations.title: B1. Kung hindi
explanations.body: Kung hindi means “if not.”

examples.text: Kung hindi, baka mangingisda na lang kami sa Fisherman’s Wharf hanggang tanghali.
examples.translation: If not, we might go fishing at Fisherman’s Wharf until noon.

examples.text: Kung hindi ka sasama, hindi na lang rin ako pupunta.
examples.translation: If you won’t come, I might as well not go.

explanations.title: B2. Kung
explanations.body: Kung means “if.”

examples.text: Papayag lang kasi ang Papa ni Irene kung sasama ang ate niya.
examples.translation: Irene’s Papa will only agree if her older sister will go with them.

examples.text: Kung may oras, susubukang magzipline.
examples.translation: If time permits, we will try ziplining.

examples.text: Kung manlilibre ka, sasama ako.
examples.translation: If you pay for the bill, I will go.

examples.text: Manlilibre ako sa Sabado kung tuturuan mo akong sumayaw.
examples.translation: I will pay for the bill this Saturday if you teach me how to dance.

explanations.title: C. Review of mag verbs in the future form
explanations.body: To narrate one’s future activities, the future form of mag is used. Identify the mag verbs and translate the sentences. The book’s key: 1. I will brush my teeth, shave and wash my face (magsisipilyo, mag-aahit, maghihilamos). 2. I will have physical training at five o’clock in the morning (magsasanay). 3. Afterwards, I will have breakfast (mag-aalmusal). 4. I will rent a car and visit places with my girlfriend (magrerenta, mamamasyal). 5. We will drive and tour Big Sur (magmamaneho, maglilibot). 6. In the afternoon I will rest already (magpapahinga). 7. In the afternoon, I will play basketball even though it is cold (maglalaro). 8. In the evening, I will study and sleep early (mag-aaral). 9. I will just go to the bathroom for a while (magbabanyo). 10. We will meet (magkikita). 11. We will go biking and horseback riding in Tagaytay (magbibisikleta, mangangabayo). The book’s key numbers its items slightly differently from the exercise list.

examples.text: Magsisipilyo, mag-aahit, at maghihilamos ako.
examples.translation: I will brush my teeth, shave and wash my face.

examples.text: Magsasanay militar ako alas-singko nang umaga.
examples.translation: I will have military training at five o’clock in the morning.

examples.text: Pagkatapos, mag-aalmusal ako.
examples.translation: Afterwards, I will have breakfast.

examples.text: Magrerenta ako ng sasakyan at mamamasyal kasama ang nobya ko.
examples.translation: I will rent a car and visit places with my girlfriend.

examples.text: Magmamaneho kami at maglilibot sa Big Sur.
examples.translation: We will drive and tour around Big Sur.

examples.text: Sa hapon, magpapahinga na ako.
examples.translation: In the afternoon I will rest already.

examples.text: Sa hapon, maglalaro ako ng basketball kahit na malamig.
examples.translation: In the afternoon, I will play basketball even though it is cold.

examples.text: Sa gabi, mag-aaral at matutulog ako nang maaga.
examples.translation: In the evening, I will study and sleep early.

examples.text: Magbabanyo lang ako saglit.
examples.translation: I will just go to the bathroom for a while.

examples.text: Saan nga pala tayo magkikita?
examples.translation: By the way, where will we meet?

examples.text: Magbibisikleta kami at mangangabayo sa Tagaytay.
examples.translation: We will go biking and horseback riding in Tagaytay.

explanations.title: Activity 9: Liza’s voice message to her friend Nadia (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key (essential elements of information): 1. Liza is inviting Nadia to the Tagaytay Picnic Grove for a family outing. 2. Liza will be with her family. 3. They will drive to Tagaytay and will pick up Nadia if she wants. 4. The outing will be on Sunday. 5. Liza’s mom will bring dessert. 6. Liza’s husband will prepare barbecue. 7. Liza will cook pancit and chicken adobo. 8. The family just wants to rest and chat. 9. The kids would like horseback riding and ziplining.

examples.translation: I miss our outings already.

examples.translation: I will make pancit and chicken adobo.

examples.translation: We will just rest there. Like before, we will chat.

examples.translation: The children want to go horseback riding and ziplining.

explanations.title: Activity 10, segment 1: mother and daughter plan their vacation in Palawan (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: 1. They will rest first. 2. The mother decides to rent a car to save on cost. 3. The daughter wants to swim at the beach.

examples.text: Pagdating sa hotel, magpapahinga muna tayo.
examples.translation: Mom: When we arrive at the hotel, we will rest first.

examples.text: Walang problema, Nay, sa hapon na tayo mamamasyal.
examples.translation: Daughter: No problem, Mom, we will tour in the afternoon already.

examples.text: Oo. Magrerenta na lang tayo ng kotse para makatipid. Maglilibot tayo sa bayan.
examples.translation: Mom: Yes. We will just rent a car to save money. We will go around town.

examples.text: At gusto kong maligo sa dagat.
examples.translation: Daughter: And I want to bathe in the sea.

explanations.title: Activity 10, segment 2
explanations.body: Key: 4. The next morning they will have breakfast at the hotel and swim at the pool. 5. In the afternoon they will go fishing, swim at the beach, have a snack and rest.

examples.text: Nay, ano po pala ang gagawin natin bukas?
examples.translation: Daughter: Mom, by the way, what will we do tomorrow?

examples.text: Sa umaga, mag-aalmusal tayo dito sa hotel at maliligo sa languyan.
examples.translation: Mom: In the morning, we will have breakfast here at the hotel and swim in the pool.

examples.text: Sa hapon po?
examples.translation: Daughter: In the afternoon?

examples.text: Sa hapon mangingisda tayo, lalangoy sa dagat, magmimiryenda, at magpapahinga.
examples.translation: Mom: In the afternoon we will fish, swim in the sea, have a snack and rest.

explanations.title: Activity 11: two dialogs about weekend plans (the book’s scripts and key)
explanations.body: Conversation 1, two office workers: a trip to Tagaytay’s Picnic Grove for the long weekend; verbs in the future tense: dederetso, magkokotse, sasakay, magpapahinga, magtatraysikel, makikita, mag-aalmusal, lalakad, kukuha, magzi-zipline. Conversation 2, two friends: training for the team trials in cycling; verbs: babalik, magbibisikleta, magsasanay, papasok, manonood, bibili.

examples.text: Mare, sumama ka sa amin ni Veronica sa Picnic Grove. Dederetso tayo sa Tagaytay mula opisina sa Biyernes.
examples.translation: A: Friend, come with Veronica and me to Picnic Grove. We will go straight to Tagaytay from the office on Friday.

examples.text: Magkokotse ba tayo?
examples.translation: A: Will we go by car?

examples.text: Hindi. Sasakay lang tayo ng bus sa Cubao. Tapos magpapahinga tayo sa mga pinsan ni Veronica. Kinabukasan, magta-traysikel tayo. Makikita natin ang Taal. Sa Picnic Grove, mag-aalmusal tayo sa Alamat Restaurant, lalakad sa eco-trail, kukuha ng retrato, bibili ng souvenirs.
examples.translation: B: No. We will just take a bus at Cubao. Then we will rest at Veronica’s cousins’. The next day we will take a tricycle. We will see Taal. At Picnic Grove we will have breakfast at Alamat Restaurant, walk the eco-trail, take photos, buy souvenirs.

examples.text: Mag-zizipline ba tayo?
examples.translation: B: Will we zipline?

examples.text: Kung hindi ka natatakot, sige.
examples.translation: A: If you are not afraid, sure.

examples.text: Ramil, saan ang lakad mo sa Sabado?
examples.translation: A: Ramil, where are you going on Saturday?

examples.text: Babalik kami sa Quezon Memorial Circle at magbibisikleta. Malapit na kasi ang team trials.
examples.translation: B: We will go back to Quezon Memorial Circle and ride bikes. The team trials are near.

examples.text: Good luck, pare! Siguradong papasok kayo sa finals.
examples.translation: A: Good luck, pare! You will surely get into the finals.

examples.text: Salamat! Manonood ka ba ng trials?
examples.translation: B: Thanks! Will you watch the trials?

examples.text: Siyempre.
examples.translation: A: Of course.

examples.text: Kailan ka bibili ng tiket?
examples.translation: B: When will you buy a ticket?

examples.text: Sa susunod na suweldo na.
examples.translation: A: On the next salary.

explanations.title: Activity 12: two weekend plans to compare (the book’s scripts and key)
explanations.body: The book has two groups each listen to one audio, share the information in Tagalog and decide which plan is more interesting. Plan 1, San Francisco day tour: DLI bus, $45.00 round trip; go around San Francisco’s popular spots, eat in Chinatown, ride a cable car, shop at Union Square; one day, back at DLI by 5 p.m. Plan 2, scuba-diving course in Monterey (Cannery Row and Monterey Bay): $300.00, equipment included; learn scuba diving (train in a pool near Cannery Row and then in the sea); two weekends (Saturdays and Sundays, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.).

examples.text: Mamamasyal ako sa San Fran.
examples.translation: I will go touring in San Francisco.

examples.text: Sasakay ako sa bus ng DLI.
examples.translation: I will ride the DLI bus.

examples.text: Apatnapu’t limang dolyar lang ang bayad, balikan na ’yon.
examples.translation: The fare is only forty-five dollars, round trip already.

examples.text: Puwede kong puntahan ang iba’t ibang lugar sa San Fran, Fisherman’s Wharf, Golden Gate Park.
examples.translation: I can visit different places in San Francisco, Fisherman’s Wharf, Golden Gate Park.

examples.text: Kakain ako sa Chinatown. Sasakay ako sa cable car. Mamimili rin ako sa Union Square.
examples.translation: I will eat in Chinatown. I will ride the cable car. I will also shop at Union Square.

examples.text: Aalis ang bus ng DLI nang alas-tres sa San Fran. Makakarating ako sa Presidio nang alas-singko.
examples.translation: The DLI bus will leave San Francisco at three. I will reach the Presidio at five (the book’s key says back at DLI by 5 p.m.).

examples.text: Mag-aaral ako ng scuba diving nang dalawang linggo.
examples.translation: I will study scuba diving for two weeks.

examples.text: Buong araw ng Sabado’t Linggo ang klase.
examples.translation: The class is all day Saturday and Sunday.

examples.text: Magsisimula nang alas-otso n.u. hanggang alas-singko n.h.
examples.translation: It starts at 8 a.m. until 5 p.m.

examples.text: Lahat-lahat, tatlong daang dolyar ang bayad.
examples.translation: Altogether, the fee is three hundred dollars.

examples.text: Hindi na ako magrerenta ng equipment. Kasama rin ’yon sa bayad.
examples.translation: I will no longer rent equipment. That is included in the fee too.

examples.text: Magsasanay kami sa pool malapit sa Cannery Row at sa dagat. Pagkatapos nito kukuha ako ng iba pang klase.
examples.translation: We will train in the pool near Cannery Row and in the sea. After this I will take other classes.
