explanations.title: Activity 13: role play, plans for this coming weekend
explanations.body: Ask about your partner’s plans, who will do activities with him or her, what time he or she will wake up and have breakfast, five other things with the siblings and four things before bed; give your own plans: four things before the activities with friends, four with friends and two before sleep. Student B: greet, say you will spend the weekend with your older brother and younger sister and that you will drive to San Francisco, tour important places, shop, have dinner with a former classmate and go home at about eight in the evening; ask your partner about his or her weekend. A sample:

examples.text: Kumusta! Ano ang plano mo ngayong weekend?
examples.translation: A: Hello! What are your plans this weekend?

examples.text: Kumusta! Gugugulin ko ang weekend kasama ang kuya at bunsong kapatid ko. Magmamaneho kami sa San Francisco, mamamasyal sa mahahalagang lugar, mamimili, magdidinner kasama ang dating kaklase, at uuwi nang mga alas-otso ng gabi.
examples.translation: B: Hello! I will spend the weekend with my older brother and younger sibling. We will drive to San Francisco, tour important places, shop, have dinner with a former classmate and go home at around eight in the evening.

examples.text: Sino ang kasama mo sa mga gagawin mo?
examples.translation: A: Who is with you in the things you will do?

examples.text: Ang kuya at kapatid ko. Ikaw, anong oras ka gigising, at sino ang kasama mo sa Sabado?
examples.translation: B: My brother and sibling. You, what time will you wake up and who is with you on Saturday?

explanations.title: Activity 14: pair work
explanations.body: Ask each other about your plans this coming weekend or future plans during an upcoming holiday or event. Use as many future-form verbs as possible and practice the Tagalog question words (open pair work, left out).

explanations.body: Share (a) your plans for the coming weekend, including the things you must do or need to do, or (b) your plans for a special holiday (Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Day), using as many verbs as possible including pseudo verbs (open tasks, left out).

lessons.subtitle: Nananakit ang kalamnan ni Junior · Parang trangkaso · Binigyan ko ng salabat

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: By the end of this lesson you can extract information from reading and listening passages about common ailments; formulate and answer simple questions about common ailments; describe symptoms of common ailments and simple medical interventions; and transcribe and translate phrases and sentences with vocabulary on common ailments. The structures are the core vocabulary, doer-focus ma verbs related to illness, and in/hin/nin verbs. In the book a mind map of common ailments (sipon, ubo and others) opens the lesson and you add more in Tagalog.

explanations.title: Culture note: folk healers and health centers
explanations.body: Many rural areas in the Philippines suffer from an acute lack of modern medical services. There are instances in which people die without even seeing a doctor. Because the medical needs are so enormous and treatment is so expensive, reliance on folk healers and native shamans is still popular. Hence the albularyo, mantatawas, hilot and manghihilot thrive everywhere. They charge low fees or no fees at all. Health centers are the most common type of medical facility in rural areas; most of them, however, have no doctors or nurses and may lack sufficient medical supplies.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Center refers to the health center found in every barangay in the Philippines. Albularyo (colloquially, “quack doctor”) refers to an herbalist or a medicine man; other names associated with the albularyo are mantatawas, manghihilot and hilot. Akapulko (Acapulco) is a shrub found throughout the Philippines, known as katanda, andadasi or palochina depending on the region; it is a medicinal herb used to treat fungal infections.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Nilalagnat, sinalat, kinuha, binasa, niyakap, niluto, inayos, nilinis, hinele, binisita and hinilot are in/hin/nin verbs (see the grammar section). Inorasyunan is a synonym of dinasalan.

explanations.title: Comprehension check, the narration (the book’s key)
explanations.body: What five things did the mother do? She took his temperature; put a wet face towel on his forehead; hugged him very tight saying get well, son; cooked his favorite food, tinola (chicken soup); cleaned and fixed his room; even when tired she sang him a lullaby until he slept.

explanations.title: Presentation 2: a mother and a corpsman at a free medical mission
explanations.body: An excerpt of a conversation between a mother and a corpsman during a free medical mission conducted by joint Philippine and U.S. military personnel as part of the Balikatan exercise.

examples.text: Nanunuyo ang labi ni Cindy at mataas ang lagnat n’ya dahil sa tetano. Tapos, may singaw pa siya. Namamaga din ang lalamunan niya. Painumin ng isang kutsaritang antibiotic pagkatapos kumain. Mainam kung dalasan ang pag-inom ng tubig.
examples.translation: Corpsman: Cindy’s lips are drying and her fever is high because of tetanus. Then she also has a canker sore. Her throat is also swollen. Have her drink one teaspoon of antibiotic after eating. It is better if you make her drink water frequently.

examples.text: E, ano po ’yang butlig na tumutubo sa braso niya? Bulutong ho ba ’yan?
examples.translation: Mother: And what is that blister growing on her arm? Is it chicken pox?

examples.text: Opo. May sanggol po ba o buntis sa bahay n’yo? Ilayo muna si Cindy sa kanila para hindi sila mahawa.
examples.translation: Corpsman: Yes. Is there a baby or a pregnant woman in your house? Keep Cindy away from them first so that they won’t be infected.

examples.text: Opo, meron po. Ano pong gagawin? Nangangati siya lagi.
examples.translation: Mother: Yes, there is. What should we do? She is always itchy.

examples.text: Huwag kamutin ang mga butlig. Kasi magpepeklat ito ’pag natuyo. Para maibsan ang pangangati, bigyan n’yo po ng Benadryl.
examples.translation: Corpsman: Don’t scratch the blisters. Because they will scar when they dry. To ease the itching, give her Benadryl.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Magpepeklat is the short form of magiging peklat, “will become a scar.” Natuyo, maibsan, nanunuyo, namamaga and nangangati are ma verbs related to illness (see the grammar lesson).

rows: will become, develop into a scar

explanations.title: Comprehension check, the corpsman’s advice (the book’s key)
explanations.body: 1. For the tetanus: take one teaspoon of antibiotic medicine after meals and drink a lot of water. 2. For the blisters: do not scratch, because they will develop into scars when they dry; take Benadryl to alleviate the itching. 3. Cindy’s symptoms and illnesses: dry lips, high fever, canker sore, swollen throat, chicken pox, blisters, tetanus. 4. The corpsman instructed the mother to isolate Cindy from others, especially babies and pregnant women, because chicken pox is a contagious disease.

explanations.title: Activity 1 (the book’s Activity 8): advice on sticky notes (the book’s key)
explanations.body: On each sticky note a family member left a message for another family member who is ill. The notes are pictures, so only the book’s completed table is kept. The teacher note corrects typos in the notes: in note 1 katihin should be kamutin; in note 2 namamalat can stand alone and na lalamunan should not be there; in note 3 the marker ang needs to come before boses; in note 4 maghigop should be humigop.

rows: Avoid scratching the blisters. Apply ointment when the blisters are almost dry to prevent scarring. Rest and take a lot of fluids.
Gargle with a glass of lukewarm water mixed with half a teaspoon of salt. Drink hot tea or fresh ginger tea.
Stop smoking for now. Eat soft food and avoid salty food. Don’t sing for now; rest your voice.
Take your medicine on time. Drink hot soup. Go to bed early and avoid working on the computer.

explanations.title: A. Doer-focus ma verbs related to illness
explanations.body: These ma verbs focus on the doer and are used mostly to express feelings, emotions, physical conditions or states of being. The focus uses a Set I pronoun; with nouns a Set I marker (ang, si) is used. A vast majority are intransitive, but a few are transitive; the direct object then uses Set II pronouns (nito) and markers (ng). Natutuyo is the form; nanunuyo is colloquial.

examples.translation: Junior’s muscles ache.

examples.translation: His or her throat is also swollen.

explanations.title: A1. Formation and conjugation
explanations.body: Ma verbs are conjugated very much like mag verbs. Matutuyo has the colloquial form manunuyo.

explanations.title: A2. Grammatical structure
explanations.body: Pattern: verb + marker + doer + (marker + direct object) + rest of the sentence. The book’s five sentences and their translations:

examples.text: Namamalat si Eliseo dahil malamig kagabi.
examples.translation: Eliseo has a sore throat because it was cold last night.

examples.text: Biglang nawala ang lagnat ng bata dahil sa gamot.
examples.translation: The child’s fever suddenly disappeared due to the medicine.

examples.text: Natulog nang mahimbing ang mga anak mo dahil napagod sila sa paglalaro.
examples.translation: Your children slept soundly because they were exhausted from playing.

examples.text: Nanginig ang mga bata sa takot.
examples.translation: The children trembled in fear.

examples.text: Namamaga ang lalamunan niya.
examples.translation: His or her throat is swollen.

explanations.title: A3. Other ma verbs
explanations.body: Other ma verbs for medical situations. The last one is irregular (a consonant change).

explanations.title: B. In/hin/nin verbs
explanations.body: You learned mag and um verbs, which are doer-focus verbs. In/hin/nin verbs are also called object-focus or goal-focus verbs. Their formation follows the same rules of reduplication and affixation (prefix, infix and suffix) as um and mag verbs. In irregular and borrowed words, however, the rule may not apply.

explanations.title: B1. Past and present: three rules
explanations.body: 1. Roots beginning with a vowel: prefix IN to the root. 2. Roots beginning with a consonant: infix IN into the root. 3. Roots beginning with L, Y or R: invert IN to NI and prefix it to the root.

explanations.title: B2. Formation and conjugation of the verbs in the reading
explanations.body: The book asks you to complete the last three rows; they are filled in here (the infinitive ends in -in or -hin).

explanations.title: B3. Grammatical structure
explanations.body: Pattern: verb + Set II marker (or Set II pronoun or demonstrative for the doer) + doer + Set I marker + object (the goal) + adjunct. A few of the book’s examples (the book prints ni bunson for ni Bunso in one row):

explanations.title: B4. Tagalized (borrowed) in/hin/nin verbs
explanations.body: For reference; you may use these verbs in speaking. Tsekin and korekin are used for marking or grading test papers; the Tagalog wastuhin (to make things right) does not always convey the idea of checking test papers.

explanations.body: Example in the book: Nagtsek si Josepa ng mga tests becomes Tsinek ni Josepa ang mga tests.

explanations.title: Activity 3: seasonal ailments
explanations.body: Write down seasonal ailments you had in the past twelve months and the treatment you received, then exchange the information with three classmates. The book’s guide dialog: A: Ano’ng nangyari sa iyo nitong nakaraang labindalawang buwan? B: Namaga ang tonsil ko. A: Ano’ng ginawa mo? B: Nagmumog lang ako ng suka. (a classroom activity, left out).

explanations.title: Activity 4: chain story
explanations.body: Sitting in a circle, each student continues a story, the first, third and fifth sentences containing a ma verb; then the class votes for the best story. The book’s example: Gabi na akong natulog kagabi. Bakit? Napupuyat ka na ba? Oo, at saka namamaga ang mga paa ko. Ano’ng ginawa mo? Wala naman, pero namimilipit ako sa sakit. Ang dami mong nararamdaman! (a class activity, left out).

explanations.title: Activity 6: translate the underlined phrases (the book’s key)
explanations.body: A newspaper passage on the medicines in a first-aid kit (adapted from a Philstar article; the book gives the doses with numerals). Key for the five underlined phrases: 1. one tablet every 4 to 6 hours; 2. for headaches or body aches; 3. one capsule 2 or 3 times a day; 4. take mefenamic acid after a meal; 5. just avoid long-term use of this medicine (past a few weeks; the book’s key says one week).

examples.text: Heto ang mga gamot na pangkaraniwang ginagamit sa first-aid kit.
examples.translation: Here are the medicines commonly used in a first-aid kit.

examples.text: Para sa lagnat, uminom ng Paracetamol limandaang miligram, isang tableta kada apat hanggang anim na oras.
examples.translation: For fever, take Paracetamol 500 mg, one tablet every four to six hours.

examples.text: Ang Paracetamol ay puwedeng inumin para sa sakit ng ulo o ng katawan.
examples.translation: Paracetamol can be taken for headaches or body aches.

examples.text: Kung may bata sa bahay, bumili rin ng Paracetamol syrup para sa bata at Paracetamol drops para sa sanggol naman.
examples.translation: If there is a child at home, also buy Paracetamol syrup for the child and Paracetamol drops for the baby.

examples.text: Para sa matinding sakit ng katawan, puwedeng uminom ng Mefenamic Acid limandaang miligram, isang capsule dalawa o tatlong beses sa maghapon.
examples.translation: For severe body pain, you can take Mefenamic Acid 500 mg, one capsule two or three times a day.

examples.text: Inumin ang Mefenamic Acid pagkatapos kumain para hindi humapdi ang tiyan.
examples.translation: Take Mefenamic Acid after eating so that the stomach doesn’t sting.

examples.text: Umiwas lang sa matagalang pag-inom nito dahil puwede itong makaapekto sa ating bato.
examples.translation: Just avoid long-term use of it because it can affect our kidneys.

explanations.title: Activity 7: a voice mail from Ramon’s mother (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Ramon is sick with flu and is at home; his sister Linda is taking care of him while the mother is at work. Key: Ramon’s mother left a message for Linda, reminding her to give Ramon his medicine, which is on the table by his bed. She asked Linda to take his temperature and to call her if the fever is high, and to give Ramon soup before his nap. Ramon should get some sleep and rest. The mother will call later.

examples.text: O, Linda, Ramon, si Mommy ito.
examples.translation: Oh, Linda, Ramon, this is Mommy.

examples.text: Linda, binigyan mo na ba ng gamot si Ramon?
examples.translation: Linda, have you given Ramon his medicine already?

examples.text: Nandoon ang gamot niya sa mesa, sa tabi ng kama niya.
examples.translation: His medicine is there on the table beside his bed.

examples.text: Kunan mo siya ng temperatura at sabihin mo sa akin kung sakaling tumaas ang lagnat niya.
examples.translation: Take his temperature and tell me in case his fever goes up.

examples.text: Bigyan mo rin siya ng sopas bago siya matulog sa hapon.
examples.translation: Also give him soup before he naps in the afternoon.

examples.text: Hayaan mo siyang matulog at magpahinga.
examples.translation: Let him sleep and rest.

examples.text: O, tatawag ulit ako mamaya.
examples.translation: Okay, I will call again later.

lessons.title: 208. C12 L1 · Listening: a doctor’s visit, two home-remedy dialogs and a message from a mother
lessons.subtitle: May trangkaso ka · Uminom ka kaagad ng salabat · Salamat sa halamang akapulko

explanations.title: Activity 8, segment 1: a doctor and a patient (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: 1. the patient suffers from body aches (muscle pain), joint pain, trembling (feeling cold), cold, cough and a severe headache; 2. the symptoms started the other night; 3. he does not know what medicine to take (the book’s key says “she”).

examples.text: O, ano ba’ng nangyari?
examples.translation: Doctor: Well, what happened?

examples.text: Dok, masakit po ang kasu-kasuan ko at nananakit ang kalamnan ko. Nanginginig po ako sa ginaw. Ang sakit din po ng ulo ko. At may ubo at sipon din ako.
examples.translation: Patient: Doc, my joints hurt and my muscles ache. I am trembling from the cold. My head also hurts a lot. And I have a cough and a cold too.

examples.text: Kailan pa?
examples.translation: Doctor: Since when?

examples.text: Nung isang gabi lang po, dok.
examples.translation: Patient: Only the other night, doc.

examples.text: May gamot ka bang iniinom?
examples.translation: Doctor: Are you taking any medicine?

examples.text: Wala pa po. Hindi ko po kasi alam kung ano’ng iinumin ko.
examples.translation: Patient: Not yet. I don’t know what to take.

explanations.title: Activity 8, segment 2
explanations.body: Key: 4. the diagnosis is flu; 5. the doctor’s recommendations: take paracetamol for muscle and joint pain, rest, drink a lot of water.

examples.text: Mataas ang lagnat mo ngayon. At sa sinabi mo, may trangkaso ka.
examples.translation: Doctor: Your fever is high now. And from what you said, you have the flu.

examples.text: Ano po ang gagawin ko, dok?
examples.translation: Patient: What should I do, doc?

examples.text: Uminom ka ng paracetamol para sa sakit ng kalamnan at kasu-kasuan. Kailangan mo ring magpahinga at uminom ng maraming tubig.
examples.translation: Doctor: Take paracetamol for the muscle and joint pain. You also need to rest and drink lots of water.

examples.text: Salamat po, dok.
examples.translation: Patient: Thank you, doc.

explanations.title: Activity 8 (second): two dialogs about ailments and remedies (the book’s scripts and key)
explanations.body: Key: 1. mother and daughter: sore throat; drink fresh ginger tea and gargle with lukewarm salt water. 2. husband and wife: chicken pox; take Paracetamol for the fever and Benadryl for the itching. The book’s task also asks for at least five future-tense verbs from each dialog.

examples.text: Nay, ang sakit ng lalamunan ko, parang namamaga.
examples.translation: Daughter: Mom, my throat hurts so much, it seems swollen.

examples.text: Kailan pa ’yan?
examples.translation: Mom: Since when?

examples.text: Paggising ko po ngayong umaga.
examples.translation: Daughter: When I woke up this morning.

examples.text: Madali lang ’yan. Uminom ka kaagad ng salabat. At magmumog ka ng maligamgam na tubig na may konting asin.
examples.translation: Mom: That’s easy. Drink ginger tea right away. And gargle with lukewarm water with a little salt.

examples.text: Sige po, ’Nay, gagawin ko po agad.
examples.translation: Daughter: Okay, Mom, I will do it right away.

examples.text: Hon, tingnan mo nga ’tong mga butlig sa braso ko. Ang kati kasi, e.
examples.translation: Husband: Hon, look at these blisters on my arm. They’re so itchy.

examples.text: Naku, bulutong ’yan. At saka, mainit ka a. Mukhang may lagnat ka.
examples.translation: Wife: Oh no, that’s chicken pox. And you’re warm. You seem to have a fever.

examples.text: Ano ang gamot dito?
examples.translation: Husband: What is the medicine for this?

examples.text: Mag-Paracetamol ka para sa lagnat at mag-Benadryl ka para maibsan ang pangangati. Huwag mong kamutin at magpepeklat ’yan ’pag natuyo.
examples.translation: Wife: Take Paracetamol for the fever and Benadryl to ease the itching. Don’t scratch or it will scar when it dries.

explanations.title: Activity 10: a voice message from a mother to her son (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Give the gist. Key: the mother thanked her son for the acapulco plant, which cured his sister’s skin diseases, and advised him, on the other hand, not to eat salty foods so that he gets over his canker sore faster.

examples.text: Anak, salamat sa halamang akapulko.
examples.translation: Son, thank you for the akapulko plant.

examples.text: Gumaling na ang buni at alipunga ni Trisha.
examples.translation: Trisha’s ringworm and athlete’s foot have healed.

examples.text: Hindi na niya kailangang mag-apply ng anu-anong ointment diyan.
examples.translation: She no longer needs to apply all sorts of ointments there.

examples.text: Ikaw, magaling na ba ang singaw mo?
examples.translation: You, is your canker sore better already?

examples.text: Iwasan mong kumain ng maaalat na pagkain para mas mabilis kang gumaling.
examples.translation: Avoid eating salty food so you get well faster.

explanations.title: Activity 11: guided conversation at the doctor’s
explanations.body: You are suffering from flu-like symptoms; consult a doctor for medical advice. A (patient): greet the doctor; say you are not feeling well, you have a cold, cough, joint and muscle pains; say a couple of days ago; say none (no medication); ask what medicine to buy. B (doctor): return the greeting and ask how he is; ask when he started feeling ill; ask if he takes any medication; say he has influenza; say Advil for pain, that he needs to rest and drink a lot of water. A sample:

examples.text: Magandang umaga po, dok.
examples.translation: Patient: Good morning, doctor.

examples.text: Magandang umaga rin. Kumusta ka?
examples.translation: Doctor: Good morning too. How are you?

examples.text: Hindi po maganda ang pakiramdam ko. May sipon po ako, ubo, at masakit ang mga kasu-kasuan at kalamnan ko.
examples.translation: Patient: I am not feeling well. I have a cold, a cough, and my joints and muscles hurt.

examples.text: Kailan pa nagsimula?
examples.translation: Doctor: When did it start?

examples.text: Dalawang araw na po.
examples.translation: Patient: Two days ago.

examples.text: May iniinom ka bang gamot?
examples.translation: Doctor: Are you taking any medicine?

examples.text: Wala po.
examples.translation: Patient: None.

examples.text: May trangkaso ka.
examples.translation: Doctor: You have influenza.

examples.text: Ano po ang bibilhin kong gamot?
examples.translation: Patient: What medicine should I buy?

examples.text: Bumili ka ng Advil para sa sakit. Kailangan mong magpahinga at uminom ng maraming tubig.
examples.translation: Doctor: Buy Advil for the pain. You need to rest and drink a lot of water.

explanations.title: Activity 12: role play, home remedies with a host family
explanations.body: You are an exchange student staying with a Filipino host family and curious about home remedies Filipinos use to cure common illnesses, including home remedies for skin diseases such as ringworm, tinea versicolor and athlete’s foot, sore throat, and cough and cold. Your partner plays the host family (open role play, left out).

explanations.title: Activity 13: challenge yourself
explanations.body: Share your experience or a friend’s experience with a common illness, including the symptoms and any home remedies or other medical intervention (open task, left out).

units.title: Chapter 12 · Lesson 2: First aid

lessons.title: 210. C12 L2 · First aid and the first-aid kit
lessons.subtitle: Napakahalaga ng paunang lunas · Benda, gasa, guwantes · May first aid kit sa bawat bahay

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: By the end of this lesson you can extract information from reading and listening passages about first aid; transcribe and translate phrases and sentences containing vocabulary related to first aid; describe the contents of a first-aid kit and the intended uses for them; and orally provide first aid instructions. The structures are the core vocabulary, an/han/nan verbs and i verbs. In the book a mind map of a first aid kit opens the lesson and you add as many related concepts as possible.

explanations.title: Presentation 1: an excerpt from a health column
explanations.body: Adapted from remate.ph (kahalagahan ng first aid). The book prints the list of supplies in one paragraph; here each supply is on its own line and the semicolons are dropped, since the list is spoken text.

examples.text: Napakahalaga na marunong tayo sa pagbibigay ng paunang lunas.
examples.translation: It is very important that we know how to give first aid.

examples.text: Sa ganitong paraan ay maiiwasang lumala ang sugat o pinsala sa katawan ng isang taong naaksidente gaya ng nasugatan o kaya ay nabalian.
examples.translation: In this way a wound or injury to the body of a person in an accident, such as one who is wounded or has a broken bone, can be kept from getting worse.

examples.text: Mahalaga din na ang bawat bahay ay mayroong first aid kit na naglalaman ng sumusunod.
examples.translation: It is also important that every house has a first aid kit containing the following.

examples.text: Benda, ginagamit ang benda para sa napilayan.
examples.translation: Bandage, the bandage is used for a sprain.

examples.text: Puwede rin sa malalang sugat na kailangang pigilan ang pagdurugo.
examples.translation: It can also be used for a severe wound whose bleeding must be stopped.

examples.text: Perdible para ipirmi ang benda.
examples.translation: Safety pin, to keep the bandage in place.

examples.text: Kuritas at gasa para tapalan ang sugat.
examples.translation: Band aid and gauze, to cover the wound.

examples.text: Gunting para sa paggupit ng gasa o benda.
examples.translation: Scissors, for cutting gauze or bandage.

examples.text: Tiyani na pambunot ng mga salubsob na sugat.
examples.translation: Tweezers for pulling out splinters from wounds.

examples.text: Maskara para maiwasan na matalsikan ng dugo.
examples.translation: Mask, to avoid being splashed with blood.

examples.text: Guwantes para iwas impeksyon, gamitin bago hawakan ang sugat ng pasyente.
examples.translation: Gloves, to avoid infection, use them before touching the patient’s wound.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Gasa (gauze), benda (bandage), guwantes (gloves), impeksyon (infection), pasyente (patient), perdible (safety pin) and maskara (mask) are Spanish cognates. Nasugatan, nabalian, matalsikan, maiwasan and napilayan are ma-an verbs. The ma-an verb affix means “to experience a quality or a condition”: in these examples the doer of an action is the person experiencing the action, state or condition.

rows: to be put in a fixed position, to stabilize, to keep steady
something used to take out a splinter

explanations.title: Comprehension check (the book’s key)
explanations.body: 1. The two main subjects of the passage: the importance of knowledge of first aid, and the uses of a first aid kit. 2. The uses of each first aid supply:

rows: used for fractures and sprains; can also be used to stop the bleeding of a severe wound
used for keeping bandages in place
used for cutting gauze pads or bandages
used for removing splinters from the wound
used to avoid getting splashed with blood

explanations.title: Presentation 2: a patient and a health worker
explanations.body: A conversation between a patient and a healthcare worker (the book’s source is a Cebu government page).

examples.text: Sakali pong makagat ako ng aso, ano ho ang dapat gawin?
examples.translation: Patient: In case I get bitten by a dog, what should be done?

examples.text: Madali lang po. Una, paduguin ang sugat. Pagkatapos, sabunin at hugasan itong mabuti sa dumadaloy na tubig at pahiran ng povidone iodine.
examples.translation: Worker: It’s easy. First, let the wound bleed. Then wash it with soap and wash it well under flowing water and apply povidone iodine.

examples.text: Kailangan ko pa po bang magpatingin sa doktor?
examples.translation: Patient: Do I still need to see a doctor?

examples.text: Opo, Nanay, kumunsulta agad sa doktor para malunasan agad.
examples.translation: Worker: Yes, Mother, consult a doctor right away so that it can be treated right away.

examples.text: Paano po ’yung aso?
examples.translation: Patient: What about the dog?

examples.text: Kailangan alagaan at bantayang mabuti at bigyan ng sapat na pagkain, tubig, at obserbahan ito sa loob ng labing-apat na araw.
examples.translation: Worker: It needs to be taken care of and watched well and given enough food and water, and observed within fourteen days.

examples.text: Paano kung namatay ang aso?
examples.translation: Patient: What if the dog dies?

examples.text: Dalhin ang ulo o katawan ng aso sa laboratoryo para masuri.
examples.translation: Worker: Bring the head or body of the dog to the laboratory to be examined.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Rabies, a fatal but preventable disease, remains a significant public health concern in the Philippines. Dogs are the principal reservoirs of rabies in the country. Nanay (mother) is used here as an honorific for an older woman. Pahiran means “apply”, hence pahiran ng povidone iodine, “apply povidone iodine”. In another context pahiran means “wipe”: Papahiran ko ang bawat luha sa ’yong mga mata (I will wipe away every tear from your eyes).

rows: to squeeze the blood out of the wound
to have oneself checked by a doctor

explanations.title: Comprehension check (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Transcription. 1. The first aid instructions for treating a dog bite, in sequence, in Tagalog and English:

rows: Squeeze the blood out of the wound.
3. Hugasang mabuti sa dumadaloy na tubig.
Rinse the wound well under free-flowing or running water.
The dog that bit the victim is alive
Give the dog sufficient food, water and space and observe the animal for about fourteen days.
The dog that bit the victim has died
Have the head or body checked or examined in a laboratory.

explanations.title: Presentation 2B: excerpts from a first aid manual by a government agency
explanations.body: Mga karaniwang aksidente at mga pangunang lunas (from deped.gov.ph). The book numbers the five accidents; each heading starts its own line here, and the ten minutes is written in words since the line is spoken text.

examples.translation: Loosen the clothing so that blood can flow freely in the body.

examples.translation: Put the bitten part of the body in a low position so that the flow of blood slows down.

examples.translation: Wound. Press the wound to stop the blood.

examples.translation: Cover the wound with gauze or bandage to avoid infection.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Biktima, apektado, gasa, minuto, komportable, posisyon and impeksyon are cognates. In the fainting item, makadaloy nang husto means “to be able to flow freely”. Ilayo, ipirmi, ihiga, itaas, ikonsulta and ilagay are i verbs. Hawakan, alalayan, buhusan, suportahan, luwagan, diinan, lapatan and takpan are an/han/nan verbs; both groups are explained in the grammar lessons.

rows: the site where the burning incident took place

explanations.title: The manual in English (the book’s partner-work key)
explanations.body: The book asks you to give the instructions for two accidents each; here are all five.

rows: Move the person away from the place of the incident. Provide support to the victim. Do not touch the burned area of the skin. Hold the burned area under cool water for ten minutes.

Stabilize and reinforce the sprained part of the body. Put the patient in a comfortable position. Put the feet and arms in an upright position to reduce the flow of blood. Allow the affected area to rest and consult the doctor.
Have the victim lie down. The feet and legs should be elevated higher than the head. Loosen the clothing to allow the flow of blood. Have the patient drink water.
Calm the victim. Put the bitten part of the body in a lower position to reduce the flow of blood.
Press the wound to stop the blood. Apply a cold compress or a cold and wet cloth on the wound. Cover the wound with gauze or bandage to avoid infection.

explanations.title: Activity 1: bites of a rat and other animals (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Read an excerpt from a health column (adapted from philstar.com) and write the first aid instruction in the order presented. The key: use gloves to protect yourself; if the bleeding is severe, put pressure on the wound to control it; thoroughly clean the wound using soap and lukewarm water; you may apply povidone iodine; apply antibiotic ointment; cover the wound with bandage or gauze pads; consult a doctor, especially if the wound is deep.

examples.text: Ito ang first-aid sa kagat ng daga at ibang hayop.
examples.translation: This is the first aid for the bite of a rat and other animals.

examples.text: Kung may kinagat na biktima, magsuot ka muna ng guwantes para protektahan ang sarili.
examples.translation: If there is a victim who was bitten, first put on gloves to protect yourself.

examples.text: Kung malakas ang pagdurugo, i-kontrol ito sa pamamagitan ng pagdiin sa sugat.
examples.translation: If the bleeding is heavy, control it by pressing on the wound.

examples.text: Linising maigi ang sugat ng sabon at maligamgam na tubig.
examples.translation: Clean the wound thoroughly with soap and lukewarm water.

examples.text: Lagyan ng Povidone Iodine ang sugat.
examples.translation: Put povidone iodine on the wound.

examples.text: Pagkatapos, pahiran ng antibiotic ointment bago tapalan.
examples.translation: Then apply antibiotic ointment before covering.

examples.text: Takpan ang sugat nang malinis na benda o gasa.
examples.translation: Cover the wound with a clean bandage or gauze.

examples.text: Kumunsulta sa doktor, lalo na kung malalim ang sugat.
examples.translation: Consult a doctor, especially if the wound is deep.

lessons.title: 213. C12 L2 · An/han/nan verbs
lessons.subtitle: Tapalan, hawakan, pahiran · Alagaan, bantayan, yapakan · Binuhusan, diniinan, tinakpan

explanations.title: A. An/han/nan verbs
explanations.body: An/han/nan verbs are object-focus verbs. The focus is on the indirect object or the object of the preposition, which may be people, places or things. When the verb is transitive, the focus is on the indirect object; when it is intransitive, the focus is on the object of the preposition. When translated into English the result contains a preposition; in Tagalog the preposition is already embedded in the suffixes -an, -han and -nan, which carry the locative focus. In Dalhan mo ng benda o gasa si Raul, Raul is the intended object of the preposition “to”, but the verb dalhan already assumes it. As always, the focus takes a Set I marker (ang, si) or a Set I pronoun.

examples.text: Tapalan ang sugat ng kuritas at gasa.
examples.translation: Patch the wound with band aid and gauze.

examples.translation: Bring bandage or gauze to Raul. Or: Bring Raul bandage or gauze.

explanations.title: A1. Formation and conjugation
explanations.body: The conjugation is like in/hin/nin (bigyan: binigyan, binibigyan), but with the locative function the in/hin/nin infixes are combined with the suffixes -an, -han, -nan. When the root begins with l or y, in changes to ni. The book gives these four rows; the first three are from the reading.

explanations.title: A2. Grammatical structure
explanations.body: Pattern: verb + marker + doer + marker + direct object + marker + indirect object (or object of the preposition) + rest of the sentence. The book’s four sentences, with translations:

examples.text: Binigyan ng doktor ng gamot ang pasyente niya.
examples.translation: The doctor provided medicine to his patient. (The doctor gave his patient medicine.)

examples.text: Tinapalan niya ng kuritas ang nasugatan.
examples.translation: He or she applied band aid on the wounded.

examples.text: Lagyan mo ng gasa ang kagat ng aso.
examples.translation: Put gauze on the wound from a dog bite.

examples.text: Aalagaan mo ang maysakit sa kuwarto.
examples.translation: You will take care of the sick person in the room.

explanations.title: A3. More an/han/nan verbs
explanations.body: The book asks you to conjugate the first three (alalay, buhos, diin); they are completed here. Notes: buhos changes /o/ to /u/ (buhusan); pahid changes /d/ to /r/ (pahiran); takip is irregular, the /i/ is dropped in the infinitive and the conjugation. The book prints sinusuporatahan, a misprint of sinusuportahan.

explanations.title: B. I verbs
explanations.body: You have met object-focus verbs with in/hin/nin and an/han/nan. Here you meet another object-focus verb briefly, the i verb; more examples come in later lessons.

explanations.title: B1. Some rules to remember
explanations.body: The object may be a person or a thing. Some verb roots may take the prefix i or the suffixes in/hin/nin without a change in meaning. The book’s list:

rows: to dance a certain dance or person
to put away something or someone
to roast a pig or fowl

explanations.title: B2. Formation and conjugation
explanations.body: These are the i verbs of the reading. The book asks you to complete the last three rows. If the root begins with l, h or y the book says the in becomes ni; in this list that shows in inilagay and inilayo (in prefixed), while consonants such as t, k and p take the infix with the i prefix kept (itinaas, ikinonsulta, ipinirmi).

explanations.title: B3. Grammatical structure
explanations.body: Pattern: verb + Set II marker (or pronoun) + doer + Set I marker + object (the focus) + rest of the sentence. The book’s four sentences:

lessons.subtitle: Lagyan, samahan, iwanan · Sasamahan kita sa ospital · Diinan ang sugat

explanations.title: Activity 2: the eight sentences and the completed table (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Listen to eight sentences and write the an/han/nan verb you hear in the table, then complete the conjugation. The scripts:

examples.text: Lagyan mo ng tubig ang baso.
examples.translation: Put water in the glass.

examples.text: Sinamahan mo ba ang kuya mo sa klinika?
examples.translation: Did you accompany your brother to the clinic?

examples.text: Iwanan na lang natin ang bote ng gamot sa botika.
examples.translation: Let’s just leave the bottle of medicine at the pharmacy.

examples.text: Lagi mong takpan ang sugat ng gasa.
examples.translation: Always cover the wound with gauze.

examples.text: Hinugasan mo bang mabuti ang sugat bago ito ginamot?
examples.translation: Did you wash the wound well before treating it?

examples.text: Kailangang pigilan ang pagdurugo ng sugat.
examples.translation: The bleeding of the wound must be stopped.

examples.text: Tandaan mong mabuti ang sintomas ng sakit.
examples.translation: Remember the symptoms of the illness well.

examples.text: Kailan kukunan ng dugo ang pasyente?
examples.translation: When will the patient’s blood be drawn?

explanations.title: Activity 3: change the verb to its an/han/nan form (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Partners take turns reading a sentence; the listener repeats it and changes the verb to its an/han/nan form, including the markers and pronouns. The book’s key, with translations:

rows: Ako ang sasama sa iyo sa ospital.
I will accompany you to the hospital.
Bibili si Cirilo ng gamot para sa tatay niya.
Bibilhan ni Cirilo ng gamot ang tatay niya.
Cirilo will buy medicine for his father.
Umiwas sa paninigarilyo para hindi magkasakit.
Iwasan ang paninigarilyo para hindi magkasakit.
Avoid smoking so you won’t get sick.
Naghugas ka ba ng kamay bago mo hinawakan ang sugat?
Hinugasan mo ba ang kamay mo bago mo hinawakan ang sugat?
Did you wash your hands before you touched the wound?
Sumama ka kay Araceli sa parmasya.
Samahan mo si Araceli sa parmasya.
Go with Araceli to the pharmacy.
Magtakip ka ng bibig kung uubo ka.
Takpan mo ang bibig mo kung uubo ka.
Cover your mouth if you are going to cough.
He or she will hold the patient.
Gumawa ka ng paraan habang naghihintay ng tulong.
Gawan mo ng paraan habang naghihintay ng tulong.
Find a way while waiting for help.

explanations.title: Activity 4: complete the sentences in your own words
explanations.body: Use an/han/nan verbs; answers vary (open task, left out). The starters: Maaari po ninyong… Pirmahan ninyo ito para… Baka naman… Huwag… Bawal… Huwag na huwag… Depende sa kondisyon ng pasyente,… Hugasang mabuti ang sugat bago…

examples.text: Lagyan ng benda ang sugat ni Danilo at bigyan natin siya ng gamot.
examples.translation: Put a bandage on Danilo’s wound and let’s give him medicine.

examples.text: Aalagaan ng mga nars ang sampung pasyenteng naging biktima ng aksidente.
examples.translation: The nurses will take care of the ten patients who became victims of the accident.

examples.text: Hugasan at patuyuin mo ang kanyang sugat at pahiran ng povidone iodine.
examples.translation: Wash and dry his or her wound and apply povidone iodine.

examples.text: Tatakpan nila ng malaking kumot ang katawan niya dahil sa lamig.
examples.translation: They will cover his or her body with a big blanket because of the cold.

examples.text: Pinuntahan ng doktor ang mga pasyente sa ward at binigyan ng gamot.
examples.translation: The doctor went to the patients in the ward and gave them medicine.

explanations.title: Activity 6: translate the underlined phrases (the book’s key)
explanations.body: A passage on first aid for people with high blood pressure (adapted from philstar.com). The book prints 140 over 90 and 160 over 100 in numerals; they are in words here. The passage lists the two occasions as (a) and (b). Key: 1. the blood pressure is taken properly; 2. breathe or inhale slowly and deeply; 3. when to give additional medicine to the patient; 4. the blood pressure is over 140 over 90; 5. the blood pressure is already over 160 over 100.

examples.text: Heto ang dapat gawin para sa mga na-high blood.
examples.translation: Here is what should be done for people who have high blood pressure.

examples.text: Siguraduhing tama ang pagkuha ng blood pressure.
examples.translation: Make sure the blood pressure is taken properly.

examples.text: Kapag palagi itong mataas sa isandaan at apatnapu over siyamnapu, ito ang nangangahulugang may high blood ka na.
examples.translation: When it is always higher than 140 over 90, this means you already have high blood pressure.

examples.text: Ipagpahinga ang pasyente nang labinlimang minuto.
examples.translation: Let the patient rest for fifteen minutes.

examples.text: Sabihin sa kanya na huminga nang mabagal at malalim.
examples.translation: Tell him or her to breathe slowly and deeply.

examples.text: Pagkatapos ay kunan muli ng blood pressure.
examples.translation: Then take the blood pressure again.

examples.text: Kung may maintenance medicines ang pasyente para sa high blood pressure, ipainom ito sa kanya.
examples.translation: If the patient has maintenance medicines for high blood pressure, give them to him or her.

examples.text: May dalawang pagkakataon kung kailan puwedeng bigyan ng karagdagang gamot ang pasyente.
examples.translation: There are two occasions when the patient can be given additional medicine.

examples.text: Kapag ang blood pressure ay lampas sa isandaan at apatnapu over siyamnapu at may nararamdaman ang pasyente.
examples.translation: When the blood pressure is over 140 over 90 and the patient feels something.

examples.text: Kapag ang blood pressure ay lampas na sa isandaan at animnapu over isandaan.
examples.translation: When the blood pressure is already over 160 over 100.

explanations.title: Activity 7: Linda and a nurse (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Linda asks a nurse how to give first aid to someone with a wound. Key, four instructions: 1. get a clean piece of cloth and use it to apply pressure to the wound; 2. if the wound is still bleeding, add more cloth and apply a little more pressure; 3. place a bandage on the wound; 4. have the person lie down and take him or her to the nearest hospital if the wound is still bleeding or if stitches are required.

examples.text: Nasugatan po ang kapatid ko sa paa at dumudugo ito. Ano po ang dapat kong gawin, ma’am?
examples.translation: Linda: My sibling’s foot was wounded and it is bleeding. What should I do, ma’am?

examples.text: Kumuha kayo ng isang pirasong malinis na damit at diinan ang sugat sa loob nang sampung minuto. Kung dumudugo pa, dagdagan pa ng damit o benda at diinan pa nang kaunti.
examples.translation: Nurse: Get a piece of clean cloth and press the wound for ten minutes. If it is still bleeding, add more cloth or bandage and press a little more.

examples.text: Sige po. Okay. Tapos na po, ma’am.
examples.translation: Linda: Okay. All right. It’s done, ma’am.

examples.text: Bendahan ninyo ang sugat. Pahigain ang kapatid ninyo at dalhin siya sa pinakamalapit na ospital kung hindi pa tumitigil ang pagdaloy ng dugo.
examples.translation: Nurse: Bandage the wound. Have your sibling lie down and take him or her to the nearest hospital if the blood has not stopped flowing.

lessons.title: 216. C12 L2 · Listening: a dog bite, a first-aid trainer and a radio announcement; speaking and glossary
lessons.subtitle: Nakagat po ako ng aso · Kumpleto na ba ang first-aid kit mo? · Importante ang pangunang lunas

explanations.title: Activity 8, segment 1: a nurse and a patient (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: 1. The patient was bitten by a dog, on her left arm; 2. just now, a while ago; 3. she squeezed the blood out of her wound, washed it with soap and rinsed it thoroughly under flowing water. The book prints the patient as a woman in the key.

examples.text: Ma’am, nakagat po ako ng aso. Dito po sa kaliwang braso.
examples.translation: Patient: Ma’am, I was bitten by a dog. Here on my left arm.

examples.text: Kailan po kayo kinagat?
examples.translation: Nurse: When were you bitten?

examples.text: Kani-kanina lang po.
examples.translation: Patient: Just a while ago.

examples.text: Dapat paduguin agad ang sugat, tapos sabunin at hugasan itong mabuti sa dumadaloy na tubig. Ginawa n’yo po ba ito?
examples.translation: Nurse: The wound should be made to bleed right away, then washed with soap and washed well under flowing water. Did you do this?

examples.text: Opo, ma’am.
examples.translation: Patient: Yes, ma’am.

explanations.title: Activity 8, segment 2
explanations.body: Key: 4. She did not apply povidone ointment (or any ointment) on the wound; 5. the doctor’s instructions: apply povidone ointment; go to a local government hospital and consult a doctor; observe the dog for fourteen days; if the dog dies, take its body to the laboratory for further examination.

examples.text: Pinahiran n’yo na po ba ng povidone iodine?
examples.translation: Nurse: Have you applied povidone iodine?

examples.text: Wala po kami n’yan, ma’am.
examples.translation: Patient: We don’t have that, ma’am.

examples.text: Eto, sa iyo na ’tong ointment. Pahiran mo ang braso mo. Tapos, pumunta ka sa pagamutang bayan at kumunsulta ka agad sa doktor. Namatay ba ang aso?
examples.translation: Nurse: Here, this ointment is yours. Apply it on your arm. Then go to the town hospital and consult a doctor right away. Did the dog die?

examples.text: Hindi po, ma’am.
examples.translation: Patient: No, ma’am.

examples.text: Okey, ganito ang gawin mo. Obserbahan mo ng labing-apat na araw. Kung namatay ang aso, dalhin mo agad ang katawan sa laboratory para masuri.
examples.translation: Nurse: Okay, do it like this. Observe it for fourteen days. If the dog dies, bring the body to the laboratory right away to be examined.

explanations.title: Activity 9, segment 1: a Red Cross trainer and a student-volunteer (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: 1. The trainer asked: do you have a complete first-aid kit? What do you have in your first-aid kit? 2. The volunteer has a bandage, band aids, tweezers and gloves (and in the script also a mask, a flashlight and a thermometer); 3. she does not have safety pins, scissors and an ice pack.

examples.text: Kumpleto na ba ang first-aid kit mo?
examples.translation: Trainer: Is your first-aid kit complete?

examples.text: May kulang pa po.
examples.translation: Volunteer: Something is still missing.

examples.text: Anong meron sa first aid kit mo?
examples.translation: Trainer: What is in your first aid kit?

examples.text: Benda, kuritas, tiyani, guwantes at maskara po. May flashlight at thermometer din po.
examples.translation: Volunteer: Bandage, band aid, tweezers, gloves and a mask. There is also a flashlight and a thermometer.

examples.text: E, ano’ng kulang?
examples.translation: Trainer: And what is missing?

examples.text: Imperdible at gunting po at saka ice pack.
examples.translation: Volunteer: Safety pins and scissors and also an ice pack.

explanations.title: Activity 9, segment 2
explanations.body: Key: 4. The trainer asked: are you ready? What are the uses of the bandage? What are the uses of gloves? 5. The volunteer said the bandage is used for sprains and also to stop the bleeding of a wound.

examples.text: Okey, sige. Handa ka na ba?
examples.translation: Trainer: Okay then. Are you ready?

examples.text: Opo, ma’am.
examples.translation: Volunteer: Yes, ma’am.

examples.text: Saan ginagamit ang benda?
examples.translation: Trainer: What is the bandage used for?

examples.text: Puwede pong gamitin ang benda para sa napilayan at puwede rin po itong pampigil sa pagdurugo ng sugat.
examples.translation: Volunteer: The bandage can be used for a sprain and it can also be used to stop the bleeding of a wound.

examples.text: Para saan naman ang guwantes?
examples.translation: Trainer: And what are the gloves for?

examples.text: Proteksyon po para iwas impeksyon. Kailangan pong gumamit ng guwantes bago hawakan ang sugat ng pasyente.
examples.translation: Volunteer: Protection to avoid infection. Gloves must be used before touching the patient’s wound.

explanations.title: Activity 10: a radio announcement (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: The key: the radio announcer talks about the importance of having knowledge about first aid, especially when accidents happen such as broken bones or injuries. Knowledge of first aid will prevent the injury from becoming serious. He also said it is a must to have a first aid kit in the house or in the car.

examples.text: Importante pong meron tayong kaalaman sa pagbibigay ng pangunang lunas.
examples.translation: It is important that we have knowledge of giving first aid.

examples.text: Mahalaga po ito lalo na kapag naaksident gaya ng nasugatan o kaya nabalian.
examples.translation: This is important especially in an accident, such as getting wounded or having a broken bone.

examples.text: Kapag alam n’yong magbigay ng pangunang lunas, maiiwasan din pong lumala ang sugat o pinsala sa katawan.
examples.translation: When you know how to give first aid, a wound or injury to the body can also be kept from getting worse.

examples.text: At saka dapat din na may first aid kit kayo sa bahay at sa sasakyan n’yo.
examples.translation: And you should also have a first aid kit at home and in your vehicle.

explanations.title: Activity 11: guided conversation at a clinic
explanations.body: You and your friend were riding a bicycle on your way home when you hit a gutter hard enough to injure yourself; tell the nurse what happened. Nurse: ask what happened; ask which part is hurting; say you need to stop the bleeding of the patient’s left arm; say he or she needs to go to the doctor first and ask for medical advice. Patient: describe how you hit a gutter and fell from your bike; point to your left arm, which is bleeding, and your left foot; ask if you need an x-ray to check for broken bones; say you will see the doctor immediately. A sample:

examples.text: Ano po ang nangyari sa inyo?
examples.translation: Nurse: What happened to you?

examples.text: Nabangga po ng bisikleta ko ang kanal at nahulog po ako.
examples.translation: Patient: My bicycle hit the gutter and I fell.

examples.text: Aling bahagi po ang masakit?
examples.translation: Nurse: Which part hurts?

examples.text: Ang kaliwang braso ko po, dumudugo, at ang kaliwang paa ko.
examples.translation: Patient: My left arm, it is bleeding, and my left foot.

examples.text: Kailangan nating pigilan ang pagdurugo ng kaliwang braso ninyo.
examples.translation: Nurse: We need to stop the bleeding of your left arm.

examples.text: Kailangan ko po bang magpa-x-ray para malaman kung may bali?
examples.translation: Patient: Do I need an x-ray to find out if there is a broken bone?

examples.text: Kailangan ninyo munang pumunta sa doktor at humingi ng payo.
examples.translation: Nurse: You need to go to the doctor first and ask for advice.

examples.text: Pupunta po ako agad sa doktor.
examples.translation: Patient: I will go to the doctor right away.

explanations.title: Activities 12 and 13
explanations.body: Activity 12 is a role play: you and a friend are on a brief vacation in Davao City and your friend is bitten by a dog during a stroll in a subdivision. Call a 911 operator, describe your friend’s condition and ask for instructions; your partner plays the operator (a role play, left out). Activity 13 is a challenge: mention at least four items in the first aid kit that you think are most useful and briefly explain the use of each (an open task, left out).

rows: the site where the burning incident took place
to have oneself checked by a doctor
to squeeze the blood out of the wound
something used to take out a splinter

explanations.title: An/han/nan verbs and i verbs with sample sentences from the book
explanations.body: Misprints corrected: pagkapatos is pagkatapos; pagdalo is pagdaloy; koi to is ko ito; the book’s 24 oras is written in words. The ihiga to ikonsulta group are i verbs.

examples.text: Alagaan mo ang aso habang wala ako.
examples.translation: Take care of the dog while I’m away.

examples.text: Alalayan mo si lola baka matalisod.
examples.translation: Support grandmother, she might trip.

examples.text: Bantayan mo ang bata baka umalis ng bahay mag-isa.
examples.translation: Watch the child, he might leave the house alone.

examples.text: Buhusan mo ng malamig na tubig agad para hindi mamaga.
examples.translation: Pour cold water on it right away so it doesn’t swell.

examples.text: Diinan mo ang gasa para huminto ang pagdaloy ng dugo.
examples.translation: Press the gauze to stop the flow of blood.

examples.text: Hawakan mo siya nang maayos baka madapa.
examples.translation: Hold him properly, he might fall.

examples.text: Huwag mo na akong hintayin, lapatan mo agad ng pangunang lunas.
examples.translation: Don’t wait for me, apply first aid right away.

examples.text: Luwagan mo ang pagtali ng benda para maayos ang pagdaloy ng dugo.
examples.translation: Loosen the tying of the bandage so the blood flows properly.

examples.text: Obserbahan mo nang dalawampu’t apat na oras ang pasyente.
examples.translation: Observe the patient for twenty-four hours.

examples.text: Pahiran mo ng ointment ang sugat niya pagkatapos mong hugasan.
examples.translation: Apply ointment on his wound after you wash it.

examples.text: Suportahan mo ang katawan niya baka biglang mawalan ng malay.
examples.translation: Support his body, he might suddenly lose consciousness.

examples.text: Takpan mo ang sugat para maiwasan ang impeksiyon.
examples.translation: Cover the wound to avoid infection.

examples.text: Tapalan mo ng gasa ’yan pagkatapos mong pahiran ng gamot.
examples.translation: Cover that with gauze after you apply medicine.

examples.text: Ihiga mo ang pasyente at bantayan mo.
examples.translation: Lay the patient down and watch him.

examples.text: Ilagay mo nga ang reseta sa bag ko nang hindi ko ito makalimutan.
examples.translation: Please put the prescription in my bag so I won’t forget it.

examples.text: Ilayo mo ang gunting sa bata baka masugatan siya.
examples.translation: Keep the scissors away from the child, he might get hurt.

examples.text: Ipirmi mo ang kaliwang kamay mo para hindi ka lalong mapilayan.
examples.translation: Keep your left hand steady so you won’t sprain it more.

examples.text: Itaas mo ang paa mo nang mas mataas kaysa ulo mo.
examples.translation: Raise your foot higher than your head.

examples.text: Ikonsulta mo agad sa doktor kapag nagkalagnat ulit si baby.
examples.translation: Consult the doctor right away if baby gets a fever again.

explanations.title: First aid kit with sample sentences

examples.translation: How many band aids are you carrying?

examples.text: May pambunot ka ba ng tinik?
examples.translation: Do you have something to pull out a thorn?

examples.text: Nagdala ka ba ng maraming gasa?
examples.translation: Did you bring a lot of gauze?

examples.text: Meron ka pa bang guwantes?
examples.translation: Do you still have gloves?

examples.text: Ilan pa bang maskara ang kailangan natin?
examples.translation: How many more masks do we need?

examples.translation: Can you still order a lot of tweezers?

examples.text: Mag-ingat sa paghawak ng gunting baka magupit mo ang daliri mo.
examples.translation: Be careful holding the scissors, you might cut your finger.

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: By the end of this lesson you can extract information from reading and listening passages about medical emergencies; ask and answer simple questions related to medical emergencies; and transcribe and translate phrases and sentences containing vocabulary related to medical emergencies. The structures are the core vocabulary and ma accidental verbs. In the book a mind map of accident-related emergencies (nalunod, nabaril and others) opens the lesson and you add more.

explanations.title: Culture note: the balisong
explanations.body: The balisong, also known as the butterfly knife, is a folding pocket knife that is proudly made in the Philippines. Sizes vary from a tiny knife that dangles on a key chain to a knife as long as a samurai sword. The balisong is often associated with Batangueños, natives of Batangas province in Luzon. It is considered a symbol of the courage of the Batangueños and is also the central feature of the official emblem of the City of Batangas (Taal.gov.ph).

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: In isinugod si Calixto sa hospital, the prefix i means “to do something to a person”; it expresses various kinds of actions, so the sentence implies that someone else brought Calixto to the hospital. Bag is equivalent to “purse” in the United States; “purse” as Filipinos use it refers to a wallet or a coin purse. Napatay here refers to Calixto, who almost got killed; in another context napatay can be used in fortuitous circumstances, for example, Napatay ang sunog dakong alas nuwebe kuwarenta y singko ng gabi (the fire was contained at about 9:45 in the evening). In ipagdasal, the prefix ipag means “to do something for”, so ipagdasal mo na lang kami means “you just pray for us (exclusive)”.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Napadaan is the past tense of mapadaan. The mapa affix in mapadaan (mapa + daan) means “to do something unintentionally”, so mapadaan means “to pass by mere happenstance or coincidentally”. Other examples are mapasigaw (to shout unintentionally) and mapaiyak (to cry unintentionally). Walang tigil na barilan means “endless shooting”. Salamin by itself means “mirror”; in this context it means “glass”.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Nabundol, napilay, nagupit, nalanghap, nalason, natinik, natapilok, natalisod (the book’s heading; the passage has natisod), natumba, nasuka, nahulog, nakunan, naaksidente and naantala are ma accidental verbs, discussed in the grammar section. The questions Napano ka? and Anong nangyari sa yo? both mean “What happened to you?” Nakunan means “miscarriage”; in another context it means “act of getting, taking or obtaining”: Nakunan ko siya ng video (I was able to take her or his video) and Nakunan ko siya ng pahayag (I was able to get her or his statement). Nawalan ako ng malay means “I lost consciousness”; mawalan ng malay is “to lose consciousness”. Nahimatay and nawalan ng malay are synonyms.

lessons.subtitle: Nabangga si Ben ng motorsiklo · Isinugod ko sa center si Nick · Namimilipit po sa sakit si bunso

explanations.title: Activity 1: four notes (the book’s notes and key)
explanations.body: In each note a family member reports a medical emergency and makes requests. The book prints the money as 1,000; it is written in words here, and PO1 is written as Police Officer One. Note 1 is signed Ate, note 2 Kuya Kanor, note 3 May, note 4 Yanyan.

examples.text: Umiwas siya pero naumpog naman siya sa poste ng MERALCO.
examples.translation: He swerved but then bumped into a MERALCO pole.

examples.text: Nasa ospital ng bayan kami ngayon.
examples.translation: We are at the town hospital now.

examples.translation: Then come to the hospital right away.

examples.translation: Cook a lot of rice and then just buy a dish.

examples.text: Dalhan mo kami ng panghapunan.
examples.translation: Bring us dinner.

examples.translation: Dad, we are at the funeral parlor now, Mom and I.

examples.text: Nasaksak si Tiyo Gardo at hindi na siya nakaabot ng ospital.
examples.translation: Uncle Gardo was stabbed and did not reach the hospital.

examples.translation: Please just tell his children.

examples.text: Pakalmahin n’yo na lang po si Tiya.
examples.translation: Please just calm Aunt down.

examples.translation: Call him because they will ask you something.

examples.text: Lola, namimilipit po sa sakit sa tiyan si bunso.
examples.translation: Grandma, little one is writhing in stomach pain.

examples.text: Nasuntok kasi ng kalaro.
examples.translation: Because a playmate punched him.

examples.text: Hindi ko na po kayo hinintay kasi ang taas pati ng lagnat niya.
examples.translation: I did not wait for you anymore because his fever is also so high.

examples.text: Iyak ho nang iyak kahit pinapakalma ko na.
examples.translation: He keeps crying even though I am already calming him.

examples.text: Habol na lang kayo, Lola.
examples.translation: Just follow later, Grandma.

examples.text: Nasa Ospital ng San Lorenzo po kami.
examples.translation: We are at San Lorenzo Hospital.

examples.text: Magpasama po kayo kay Arthur.
examples.translation: Have Arthur accompany you.

examples.text: ’Wag po kayong umalis mag-isa.
examples.translation: Don’t go alone.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Load is the Philippine word for prepaid mobile phone credit. Isinugod means “rushed” (someone is taken in a hurry to a place). MERALCO is the Manila Electric Company, hence a MERALCO pole is an electric utility post. Bunso is the youngest child.

rows: hit by a motorcycle; tried to avoid it but ran into an electric post
borrow money (one thousand pesos) from Aling Anita; come to the hospital right after; bring a blanket and clothing for Ben; buy me a prepaid phone card
Nick (note from Kuya Kanor to Gardo)
electrocuted while putting up an antenna; burns on his body; also fell off the roof
cook plenty of rice; buy food; bring us food for dinner
Uncle Gardo (note from May to Tay)
stabbed to death; did not reach the hospital alive
inform Uncle Gardo’s relatives; help Uncle Gardo’s wife calm down; call Police Officer Samuel Calderon
severe stomach pain after a playmate punched him or her; very high fever
go to the hospital later; have Arthur accompany you; don’t go alone

explanations.title: Ma accidental verbs
explanations.body: You have studied different uses of the ma prefix in verbs. This lesson presents another use of ma, that of denoting an action which is accidental, unintentional, unplanned or unexpected. These verbs are called ma accidental for short.

explanations.title: A. Some rules to remember
explanations.body: 1. The “victim” of the accident, or of the adverse result of the action, is the focus of ma accidental verbs, and can be a person, place or thing. 2. The focus takes Set I markers or Set I pronouns. The doer or cause of the action is usually implied or understood, but it can also be mentioned, depending on the context. 3. The words “accidentally” and “unintentionally” need not always be mentioned in the English translation. 4. Stand-alone sentences may contain words and phrases that clue in the reader to the accidental, unexpected or unplanned nature of the ma verb. Examples are tuloy (“as a consequence”), nang wala sa panahon (“prematurely”) and nang hindi inaasahan (“unexpectedly”). The expression naku! (“OMG!”, “Oh boy!”, “Shoot!” depending on the context) also implies an accidental occurrence.

explanations.title: Activity 3: translate and change the tense (the book’s sentences)
explanations.body: Partners take turns: one reads a sentence, the other translates it; then the second partner changes the verb to a different tense or to its infinitive with suitable time expressions and the first translates the new sentence. The book’s eight sentences with its translations:

examples.text: Nahulog sa hagdan ang bata.
examples.translation: The child fell from a flight of stairs.

examples.text: Napaso si Hilda nang magluto siya kahapon.
examples.translation: Hilda was scalded when she cooked yesterday.

examples.text: Dahan-dahan kayo at baka maaksidente kayo.
examples.translation: Be careful because you might get into an accident.

examples.text: Nadisgrasya daw si Carlos kaya nasaksak.
examples.translation: Carlos was reportedly involved in an accident that’s why he was accidentally stabbed.

examples.text: Tandaan ninyo, laging nahuhuli ang may kasalanan.
examples.translation: Remember, the criminal always gets caught.

examples.text: Hindi kaya sila mabangga sa may ilog?
examples.translation: I wonder if they would crash by the river.

examples.text: Nahuli ang dating ng ambulansiya.
examples.translation: The ambulance came late.

examples.text: Lagi na lamang nauumpog ang bata sa mesa.
examples.translation: The child always hits his or her head on the table.

explanations.title: Activity 4: complete the questions (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Questions a medical practitioner might ask accident victims or their representatives, completed with the correct verb form. The root is in parentheses in the book: (mahulog), (madala), (masunog), (magupit). Part b, answering the questions in complete sentences, varies (open task, left out).

examples.text: Saan nahulog ang anak ninyo?
examples.translation: Where did your child fall?

examples.text: Nadala na ba siya sa ospital?
examples.translation: Has he or she been taken to the hospital?

examples.text: Anong bahagi ng katawan ang nasunog?
examples.translation: Which part of the body was burned?

examples.text: Paano nagupit ang tenga niya?
examples.translation: How did his or her ear get cut?

explanations.title: Activity 5: choose the correct ma accidental verb (the book’s key)
explanations.body: The book gives the options in parentheses: 1. (mabangga, madisgrasya, mapaso) 2. (nabangga, nasunog, nasaksak) 3. (nadapa, nadisgrasya, nasunog) 4. (nahagip, napaso, naumpog) 5. (nadapa, nahagip, nahuli). The answers: 1. madisgrasya, 2. nabangga, 3. nasunog, 4. naumpog, 5. nahagip. Complete sentences:

examples.text: Iwasan ninyo ang gulo kung ayaw ninyong madisgrasya.
examples.translation: Avoid trouble if you don’t want to have an accident.

examples.text: Hindi tumingin ang tsuper sa daan, kaya nabangga ang trak niya.
examples.translation: The driver did not look at the road, so his truck crashed.

examples.text: Maraming bagay ang nasunog dahil sa kandilang iniwan nila.
examples.translation: Many things burned because of the candle they left.

examples.text: Tumakbo nang mabilis ang bata, kaya naumpog siya sa puno.
examples.translation: The child ran fast, so he bumped into the tree.

examples.text: Hindi sila tumingin sa dinadaaan nila kaya nahagip sila ng dyip.
examples.translation: They did not look where they were going so they were sideswiped by a jeepney.

examples.text: Muntik mahagip ng tren ang bata.
examples.translation: The child was almost hit by a train.

examples.text: Nasunog ang kamay ng binatilyo nang nagpaputok siya.
examples.translation: The teenager’s hand got burned when he set off firecrackers.

examples.text: Nabali ang buto niya nang mahulog siya sa hagdan.
examples.translation: His or her bone broke when he or she fell down the stairs.

examples.text: Nalunod ang bata sa ilog.
examples.translation: The child drowned in the river.

examples.text: Nagte-text siya habang nagmamaneho, kaya nabangga siya sa poste.
examples.translation: He or she was texting while driving, so he or she crashed into a post.

explanations.title: Activity 7: a passage about the ambulance (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Source: negro-occ.gov.ph (Tagalog Wikipedia). Key: the ambulance is a vehicle used to transport sick or injured people. Usually they serve those who have emergencies such as broken bones, chest pains, serious head injuries and injuries obtained from tragedies like those involving vehicular collision.

examples.text: Ang ambulansiya ay isang uri ng sasakyang ginagamit sa pagdadala ng maysakit o nasaktang mga tao.
examples.translation: The ambulance is a type of vehicle used in carrying sick or injured people.

examples.text: Karaniwang pinupuntahan ng nagmamaneho nito ang mga tao kung may emerhensiya gaya ng nabalian ng buto, sakit sa dibdib, seryosong pinsala sa ulo, at mga taong nasaktan dahil sa mga sakunang katulad ng banggaan ng mga sasakyan.
examples.translation: Its driver usually goes to people when there is an emergency such as a broken bone, chest pain, a serious head injury, and people hurt in disasters such as vehicle collisions.

explanations.title: Activity 8: first aid for burns (the book’s key)
explanations.body: The book underlines five phrases to translate: 1. ang nasunog na balat: the burnt skin; 2. para hindi ito mag-impeksyon: so that this will not be infected; 3. diinan ang sugat: press the wound; 4. para mabigyan ng dagdag lunas: so that he or she will be given additional care or treatment; 5. Tandaan: remember. The passage (philstar.com):

examples.text: First Aid sa nasunog.
examples.translation: First aid for burns.

examples.text: Patuluan ng malamig na tubig ang nasunog na balat sa loob ng sampu-labinlimang minuto.
examples.translation: Let cold water drip on the burned skin for ten to fifteen minutes.

examples.text: Pagkatapos, puwede tapalan ng kitchen wrap o cling wrap ang nasunog na parte para hindi ito mag-impeksyon.
examples.translation: Afterwards, the burned part can be covered with kitchen wrap or cling wrap so that it won’t get infected.

examples.text: Huwag tapalan ng madikit na tela o tape.
examples.translation: Do not cover it with sticky cloth or tape.

examples.text: Kung may pagdurugo, diinan ang sugat nang sampung minuto hanggang sa tumigil ang pagdurugo.
examples.translation: If there is bleeding, press the wound for ten minutes until the bleeding stops.

examples.text: Dalhin ang pasyente sa ospital para mabigyan ng dagdag lunas.
examples.translation: Bring the patient to the hospital so that he or she can be given additional treatment.

examples.text: Tandaan, huwag hawakan ang nasunog na parte.
examples.translation: Remember, do not touch the burned part.

examples.text: Huwag lagyan ng lotion, cream at kung anu-ano pa.
examples.translation: Do not put lotion, cream or all sorts of things on it.

examples.text: At huwag din puputukin ang blister sa balat.
examples.translation: And do not pop the blister on the skin either.
