explanations.title: Activity 9, segment 1: two friends talk about Cardo’s family (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: 1. The two friends were talking about Cardo’s family. 2. The bus they were riding had an accident and then crashed into a gasoline station; Cardo did not reach the hospital alive. (The book’s key also says “Carlo died”, a misprint.) 3. His wife was stabbed very recently and is still recuperating in the hospital.

examples.text: Mare, alam mo na ba ang nangyari sa pamilya ni Cardo?
examples.translation: A: Friend, do you know what happened to Cardo’s family?

examples.text: Hindi pa. Bakit?
examples.translation: B: Not yet. Why?

examples.text: Nadisgrasya ang sinasakyan nilang bus kahapon, tapos nabangga ito sa isang gasolinahan.
examples.translation: A: The bus they were riding had an accident yesterday, then it crashed into a gas station.

examples.text: Ganun ba? E, kumusta naman si Cardo at pamilya niya?
examples.translation: B: Is that so? And how are Cardo and his family?

examples.text: Si Cardo hindi na umabot sa ospital. Patay agad.
examples.translation: A: Cardo did not make it to the hospital. Dead right away.

examples.text: Naku, e kamakailan lang nasaksak ’yung asawa niya at nasa ospital pa hanggang ngayon.
examples.translation: B: Oh no, and his wife was stabbed just recently and is still in the hospital until now.

explanations.title: Activity 9, segment 2
explanations.body: Key: 4. Cardo’s oldest son had minor bruises; his mother had a broken arm; his father had a head injury. 5. They don’t know that he died.

examples.text: Sobra namang kamalasan ’yan. E, ’yung mga anak niya kasama ba sa nadisgrasya?
examples.translation: B: That is too much bad luck. And his children, were they in the accident?

examples.text: ’Yung panganay niya, may konting galos lang at nasa bahay na. ’Yung nanay ni Cardo, nabalian ng braso. Nasugatan din sa ulo ’yung tatay niya. Pero hindi naman malala.
examples.translation: A: His eldest has only a few bruises and is already at home. Cardo’s mother had a broken arm. His father was also wounded in the head. But it isn’t serious.

examples.text: E, nasaan na ’yung nanay at tatay ni Cardo ngayon?
examples.translation: B: And where are Cardo’s mother and father now?

examples.text: Nasa hospital pa rin, inoobserbahan pa. Hindi pa nga nila alam na patay na si Cardo.
examples.translation: A: They are still in the hospital, still being observed. They don’t even know yet that Cardo is dead.

explanations.title: Activity 10, segment 1: a caller and a 911 operator (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: 1. The caller requested help immediately. 2. Two buildings are on fire. 3. In Malate St., close to a church located right across a plaza. The book’s role labels are swapped in the printed heading (A: Caller, B: 911 Operator); the roles are as shown here.

examples.text: Sir, magpadala po kayo ng tulong agad, may nangyari pong sunog dito.
examples.translation: Caller: Sir, please send help right away, there is a fire here.

examples.text: Saan po ang lokasyon n’yo?
examples.translation: Operator: Where is your location?

examples.text: Dito po sa may simbahan, sa Malate St. May dalawang gusali pong nasusunog.
examples.translation: Caller: Here near the church, on Malate St. Two buildings are burning.

examples.text: Dalawa ang simbahan diyan sa Malate St. Aling simbahan ka malapit?
examples.translation: Operator: There are two churches on Malate St. Which church are you near?

examples.text: ’Yung simbahan po na katapat ng plasa.
examples.translation: Caller: The church that is right across from the plaza.

explanations.title: Activity 10, segment 2
explanations.body: Key: 4. The operator asked: do you see any wounded victims? Do you see any firemen or police in the area? 5. The caller said: there are wounded and unconscious victims on the street; an old man is bleeding and writhing in pain; there is one fire truck but it is not enough to contain the fire; there are also a few policemen in the area.

examples.text: May nakikita ka bang sugatan?
examples.translation: Operator: Do you see anyone wounded?

examples.text: Meron pong mga sugatan at mga walang malay sa daan. May isa pong lolo na duguan at namimilipit sa sakit.
examples.translation: Caller: There are wounded people and unconscious people in the street. There is an old man who is bloody and writhing in pain.

examples.text: May nakikita ka bang bumbero o pulis diyan?
examples.translation: Operator: Do you see any firefighter or police there?

examples.text: May isang fire truck po pero hindi sapat na maapula ang sunog. May ilang pulis din po.
examples.translation: Caller: There is one fire truck but it is not enough to put out the fire. There are also a few police.

examples.text: Sige, parating na ang tulong.
examples.translation: Operator: All right, help is on the way.

explanations.title: Activity 11: a call from a sister to her older brother (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key, the essential elements: she asked her older brother if he is all right after almost being stabbed in Manila; she advised him not to resist or fight back next time; he should not mind losing his cellphone; it is good Uncle Kaloy saved him; she praised Uncle Kaloy, adding that he also saved Dolor from drowning.

examples.text: Hello, Kuya Sixto, okey ka lang ba?
examples.translation: Hello, Kuya Sixto, are you okay?

examples.text: Narinig ko na muntik ka nang masaksak sa Maynila.
examples.translation: I heard you were almost stabbed in Manila.

examples.text: Sa susunod, huwag ka na kasing lumaban.
examples.translation: Next time, please don’t fight back anymore.

examples.text: Hindi bale nang manakaw ’yang cellphone mo.
examples.translation: It doesn’t matter if your cellphone gets stolen.

examples.text: Mabuti na lang kasama mo si Tito Kaloy, nailigtas ka.
examples.translation: Good thing Tito Kaloy was with you, you were saved.

examples.text: Ang galing naman ni Tito Kaloy ’no?
examples.translation: Tito Kaloy is great, isn’t he?

examples.text: Nung nakaraang reunion natin, nailigtas din niya si Dolor na muntik nang malunod.
examples.translation: At our last reunion, he also saved Dolor, who almost drowned.

explanations.title: Activity 12: guided conversation, calling 911
explanations.body: You heard a loud explosion followed by a commotion; a popular restaurant is on fire and you saw injured bodies on the streets. Call 911 and ask for help. Caller: say you need help immediately; say you saw a restaurant on fire and bodies littered on the streets; say you don’t know the street exactly but you are at a Fil-Am Bank right across the restaurant on fire; say a lot, bloody, and either writhing in pain or unconscious. Operator: ask what happened; ask the exact location; ask approximately how many bodies are on the street; say help is on the way. A sample:

examples.text: Kailangan ko po ng tulong agad!
examples.translation: Caller: I need help right away!

examples.text: Ano po ang nangyari?
examples.translation: Operator: What happened?

examples.text: May nakita po akong restawran na nasusunog at may mga katawang nakahandusay sa kalsada.
examples.translation: Caller: I saw a restaurant on fire and bodies lying in the street.

examples.text: Saan po ang eksaktong lokasyon ninyo?
examples.translation: Operator: Where is your exact location?

examples.text: Hindi ko po alam ang eksaktong kalye pero nasa Fil-Am Bank po ako, kaharap ng restawran na nasusunog.
examples.translation: Caller: I don’t know the exact street but I am at Fil-Am Bank, right across from the burning restaurant.

examples.text: Ilan po ang tinatayang katawan sa kalsada?
examples.translation: Operator: Approximately how many bodies are on the street?

examples.text: Marami po, duguan at namimilipit sa sakit o walang malay.
examples.translation: Caller: A lot, bloody and writhing in pain or unconscious.

examples.text: Parating na po ang tulong.
examples.translation: Operator: Help is on the way.

explanations.title: Activities 13 and 14
explanations.body: Activity 13 is a role play: you and your family ran into a spate of misfortune; tell your best friend, mentioning three to five family relations and the unfortunate incident that befell each, using ma accidental verbs (a role play, left out). Activity 14 is a challenge: narrate a medical-related accident, personal or someone else’s, the type of accident and the emergency response (an open task, left out).

explanations.title: Glossary
explanations.body: The book prints the root of nasaksak as dinig; the root is saksak, and kidnapped is the root given for nakidnap.

rows: to be involved in an accident
to be accidentally sideswiped by a fast moving object
accidentally hit by a moving object
what happened to you, in short
to collide with or crash accidentally
accidentally pierced or pricked by a sharp object, thorn or fishbone
accidentally fell on the floor or ground
accidentally hit or bumped one’s head on something

explanations.title: Self-evaluation
explanations.body: The book closes the chapter with a checklist: you should now be able to extract information from reading and listening passages about common ailments, first aid and medical emergencies; formulate and answer simple questions related to common ailments and medical emergencies; describe symptoms of common ailments and simple medical interventions; transcribe and translate phrases and sentences containing vocabulary on ailments, first aid and medical emergencies; describe the contents of a first-aid kit and its uses; and orally provide first aid instructions. You should have a clear understanding of ma verbs related to illness, in/hin/nin verbs, i verbs, an/han/nan verbs and ma accidental verbs. If not, review the section on your own, find a study partner, or ask your academic counselor or team leader for activities tailored to your learning style.

units.title: Chapter 13 · Lesson 1: Education

lessons.title: 224. C13 L1 · The Philippine educational system
lessons.subtitle: K-12 ang sistema ng edukasyon · May matrikula sa pribadong paaralan · Madrasah

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: By the end of this lesson you can extract information from reading and listening passages about education in the Philippines; formulate and answer simple questions related to the Philippine educational system; transcribe and translate phrases and sentences containing vocabulary related to education; talk about education in the Philippines using the expressions learned; and describe your own school or someone else’s from elementary to college. The structures are the core vocabulary, pa-an/han/nan noun formation, comparison of equality with kasing, magkasing and magkakasing, and nouns with mag denoting relationship. In the book a mind map of education (matrikula, antas and others) opens the lesson and you add more.

explanations.title: Presentation 1A: general description of the Philippine educational system

examples.text: Gaya ng Estados Unidos, K-labindalawa ang sistema ng edukasyon ng Pilipinas.
examples.translation: Like the United States, the education system of the Philippines is K-12.

examples.text: May pribado at pampublikong paaralan sa mababa at mataas na paaralan, at maging sa kolehiyo.
examples.translation: There are private and public schools in elementary and high school, and even in college.

examples.text: Libre ang pampublikong paaralan sa elementarya at sekondarya.
examples.translation: Public schools are free in elementary and secondary.

examples.text: Nitong huli, libre na rin pati sa kolehiyo.
examples.translation: Lately, it is free even in college.

examples.text: Samantalang, may matrikula naman sa mga pribadong paaralan.
examples.translation: Whereas there is tuition in private schools.

examples.text: Kilala ang pribadong paaralan sa mataas na kalidad ng edukasyon sa lahat ng antas o baitang ng pag-aaral.
examples.translation: Private schools are known for the high quality of education at every level or grade of study.

examples.text: Marami sa mga ito ay mga Katoliko at paaralan ng parokya.
examples.translation: Many of them are Catholic and parochial schools.

examples.text: Meron ding madrasah, mga pribadong paaralang Muslim.
examples.translation: There is also the madrasah, private Muslim schools.

examples.text: Itinuturo dito ang pag-aaral ng kaugaliang Islam at pagsulat at pagbasa sa wikang Arabe.
examples.translation: Taught here are the study of Islamic traditions and writing and reading in the Arabic language.

examples.text: Sinusuportahan ito ng lokal na pamayanan at donasyon ng mga bansang Muslim.
examples.translation: It is supported by the local community and donations from Muslim countries.

explanations.title: Note on the madrasah
explanations.body: The Department of Education endorses the Tahderiyyah Curriculum in Islamic community schools operated by the Bangsamoro Development Agency (BDA), giving Muslim preschool children equal access to quality kindergarten education. The Tahderiyyah curriculum was developed for five-year-old Muslim pupils in schools under the BDA. The standards and competencies of the curriculum are aligned with the kindergarten curriculum implemented in all public schools nationwide (deped.gov.ph).

explanations.title: Culture note: the University of Santo Tomas
explanations.body: The Pontifical and Royal University of Santo Tomas, The Catholic University of the Philippines, or simply the University of Santo Tomas (UST), is a private, Roman Catholic research university in Manila. Founded on 28 April 1611 by Miguel de Benavides, Archbishop of Manila, it has the oldest extant university charter in the Philippines and in Asia, and is one of the world’s largest Catholic universities in terms of enrollment found on one campus. Run by the Order of Preachers, UST is also the largest university in Manila.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Note and learn the cognates sistema, edukasyon, kolehiyo, pribado, elementarya, sekondarya, parokya, lokal, Katoliko, matrikula, plaza and donasyon. Paaralan ng parokya, parochial school, means a school under the administration of the parish. The book prints K-12; it is written K-labindalawa here since the line is spoken text.

explanations.title: Note on the schools
explanations.body: AMA University is the first and largest ICT (Information and Communication Technologies) university in Asia and a pioneer in computer education in the Philippines. STI (Systems Technology Institute) is the largest network of for-profit information-technology-based colleges in the Philippines.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Pamantasan, paaralan, pamahalaan, pahayagan and pamunuan are pa-an/han/nan nouns (see the grammar lesson). Pisay is short for Philippine Science High School. Pag-iisipan ko means “I will think about it.” Magpinsan and magkaklase are mag nouns. Magkasintalino, magkakasintalino, kasintaas, magkasintaas and magkakasintaas are examples of comparison of equality.

rows: equally intelligent, for two people or objects
equally intelligent, for more than two people or objects
equally tall, for more than two people or objects

explanations.title: A. The affix pa-an/han/nan
explanations.body: One of the many ways to form nouns is the affix pa-an/han/nan. The structure is: pa + root word + an/han/nan. The nouns from the reading:

explanations.title: 1. The place where the action of the root happens
explanations.body: Nouns formed with pa-an/han/nan can name the place where the action expressed by the root word is performed.

headers: Meaning: the place where the action happens
rows: a school, where studying takes place
a playground, where playing is done
a factory, where people work to make things
a hospital, where treatment with medicine is done
a print shop, where things are printed
a market, where things are bought and sold

explanations.title: 2. A contest or competition
explanations.body: Paligsahan (root ligsa), pagalingan (root galing) and the colloquial patalbugan (root talbog) also refer to a contest or some kind of competition. The root words were introduced in earlier lessons.

explanations.title: Activity 2: derived nouns from ma adjectives (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Write the derived pa-an/han/nan noun. For root words ending in /d/, change /d/ to /r/, then add an/han/nan (the adjective root of malapad is lapad, hence laparan).

lessons.title: 228. C13 L1 · Comparison of equality, and mag nouns for relationships
lessons.subtitle: Kasintaas, magkasintalino, magkakasingganda · Magpinsan, magkapatid, magkakaibigan

explanations.title: B. Comparison of equality: kasing, magkasing, magkakasing
explanations.body: These express equality: “as + adjective + as” (kasing), “equally + adjective” (magkasing, for two) and “all equally + adjective” (magkakasing, for more than two). The ng ending of the prefix changes by assimilation: NG becomes N before roots starting with d, l, r, s or t; NG becomes M before roots starting with b or p; NG stays NG before roots starting with a vowel or with k, g, h, y or w. Some speakers use sing instead of kasing, and magsing in place of magkasing; magkakasing has no such variant. Sing and magsing belong to more poetic language than to everyday conversation.

explanations.title: The three forms for common adjectives (my table, built from the assimilation rules)
explanations.body: The book’s own sentences below use taas, hirap, bait, laki, talino, galing, payat, ganda and pogi; the other rows apply the same rule.

explanations.title: 1. Kasing (as + adjective + as)
explanations.body: Pattern: adjective + ng/ni + basis of comparison + ang/si + person or object being compared. The book’s four sentences:

examples.text: Kasintaas ba ng STI ang matrikula ng AMA?
examples.translation: Is the matriculation fee of STI as high as AMA’s?

examples.text: Kasinghirap ng law ang accounting.
examples.translation: Accounting is as difficult as law.

examples.text: Kasimbait ni Nanay si Tita Malou.
examples.translation: Aunt Malou is as nice as my mom.

examples.text: Kasinlaki ng Basilan ang bansang Israel.
examples.translation: The country Israel is as big as Basilan.

explanations.title: 2. Magkasing (equally + adjective, two only)
explanations.body: Magkasing is used only for two persons or objects. The book’s four sentences:

examples.text: Magkasintalino sila ng kuya niya.
examples.translation: He or she and his or her older brother are equally intelligent.

examples.text: Magkasintaas lang sila ng tuition.
examples.translation: The matriculation fees of AMA and STI are equally high.

examples.text: Magkasinggaling ang mga army at marines.
examples.translation: The army and the marines are equally skillful.

examples.text: Magkasimpayat sina Daisy at April.
examples.translation: Daisy and April are equally slim.

explanations.title: 3. Magkakasing (more than two)
explanations.body: Magkakasing is used for more than two people or objects. In the first sentence lahat refers to the mom and her two kids.

examples.text: Magkakasintalino kayong lahat.
examples.translation: All of you are equally smart.

examples.text: Magkakasintaas ang tuition ng lahat ng mga pribadong paaralan.
examples.translation: The tuition fees of all private schools are all equally high.

examples.text: Magkakasingganda sina Jingjing, Dedeng, at Bingbing.
examples.translation: Jingjing, Dedeng, and Bingbing are all equally beautiful.

examples.text: Magkakasimpogi sina Dingdong, Bongbong, at Junjun.
examples.translation: Dingdong, Bongbong, and Junjun are all equally handsome.

explanations.title: Activity 3: write three sentences using kasing
explanations.body: Fill the table with an adjective, a marker, a basis of comparison, a marker and a person or object being compared (an open writing task, left out).

explanations.title: Activity 4: translate (the book’s key)
explanations.body: The book prints Kasingputi in the last sentence; by the assimilation rule above, p before the root would give m, so kasimputi follows the rule while the book prints kasingputi.

examples.text: Magkasingitim sina Diana at Rose.
examples.translation: Diana and Rose are equally black.

examples.text: Magkakasingkulay-rosas ang mga pisngi ng magkakapatid.
examples.translation: The cheeks of the siblings are all equally pink.

examples.text: Kasingputi ni Pacundo si Procopio.
examples.translation: Procopio is as white, fair in complexion, as Pacundo.

explanations.title: C. Nouns with mag denoting relationship
explanations.body: When used as an affix to a base noun, mag denotes a relationship between two people. To express a relationship between two people, simply add mag before the root word. To express a relationship among more than two people, reduplicate the first syllable of the root word. The book’s table (the first two are from the reading); the exercise of adding more root words is left open:

lessons.subtitle: Pumasa ang bunso mo sa UP · Madrasah · Libre po ang enrolment · Glossary

explanations.title: Activity 8, segment 1: a conversation between mothers (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: UP is the University of the Philippines, the premier government-subsidized university. Key: 1. They are talking about Cynthia’s children. 2. The exam was difficult; many students took it but only a few passed. 3. He or she is smart, recently passed the UP entrance exam, is also a barangay scholar, and is a graduate of Philippine Science High School. 4. The barangay scholar gets a monthly allowance of two thousand pesos.

examples.text: Cynthia, congrats ha? Dinig ko pumasa ’yung bunso mo sa entrance exam sa UP.
examples.translation: A: Cynthia, congrats, okay? I heard your youngest passed the entrance exam at UP.

examples.text: Oo, Tess. Mahirap daw ang exam, sabi niya. Marami silang kumuha pero kokonti ang pumasa.
examples.translation: B: Yes, Tess. The exam was hard, he said. Many of them took it but few passed.

examples.text: Matalino naman ang anak mo, nagtapos ’ata siya sa Pisay. O, libre ka na ng matrikula n’yan.
examples.translation: A: Your child is smart, he graduated from Pisay, I think. Oh, you are free of tuition now.

examples.text: Hindi lang matrikula. Iskolar din siya ng barangay kaya meron siyang buwanang allowance na dalawang libo.
examples.translation: B: Not just tuition. He is also a barangay scholar so he has a monthly allowance of two thousand.

explanations.title: Activity 8, segment 2
explanations.body: Key: 5. The oldest finished high school and attended a semester in college. 6. He or she has no plans to pursue college studies and wants to earn money first.

examples.text: E, yung panganay mo. May plano bang magkolehiyo ’yun?
examples.translation: A: And your eldest. Does he plan to go to college?

examples.text: Wala e, mas gusto niyang kumita muna.
examples.translation: B: No, he would rather earn first.

examples.text: Ano ba’ng trabaho niya ngayon?
examples.translation: A: What is his job now?

examples.text: Tagatahi ng pantalon sa isang malaking kumpanya.
examples.translation: B: A pants sewer at a big company.

examples.text: Natapos ba siya ng high school?
examples.translation: A: Did he finish high school?

examples.text: Oo, at isang semester sa kolehiyo. Tapos huminto na.
examples.translation: B: Yes, and one semester of college. Then he stopped.

explanations.title: Activity 9, segment 1: a Filipino host and a foreign language exchange student (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: 1. They talked about the schools or education of the host and her children. 2. The children are enrolled in a madrasah. 3. A regular curriculum; Islamic teachings; and reading and writing in Arabic.

examples.text: Ate, dinig ko po na nag-aaral ang mga anak nyo sa Madrasah. Ano po ’yun?
examples.translation: Student: Ate, I heard your children study at the Madrasah. What is that?

examples.text: Isa itong pribadong paaralan ng Muslim.
examples.translation: Host: It is a private Muslim school.

examples.text: Iba ho ba ang curriculum nila kaysa sa regular na paaralan?
examples.translation: Student: Is their curriculum different from regular schools?

examples.text: Hindi naman. Bukod sa standard na curriculum, may dagdag lang na turo ng kaugaliang Islam at ang pagsulat at pagbasa sa wikang Arabe.
examples.translation: Host: Not really. Besides the standard curriculum, there is only an addition of teaching Islamic customs and reading and writing in Arabic.

explanations.title: Activity 9, segment 2
explanations.body: Key: 4. The student asked: did you also graduate from a madrasah? Where did you graduate? 5. The host said she is Catholic but married to a Muslim; she attended Xavier University from elementary to college; the tuition fee in a private school is high; however it is worth it because of the quality of education at all levels.

examples.text: Nagtapos din po ba kayo sa Madrasah?
examples.translation: Student: Did you also graduate from the Madrasah?

examples.text: Hindi. Katoliko kasi ako pero Muslim ang naging asawa ko.
examples.translation: Host: No. I am Catholic but my husband became Muslim.

examples.text: Saan po kayo nagtapos?
examples.translation: Student: Where did you graduate?

examples.text: Sa Xavier University mula elementarya hanggang kolehiyo.
examples.translation: Host: At Xavier University from elementary to college.

examples.text: Hindi ho ba masyadong mahal ang matrikula doon?
examples.translation: Student: Isn’t the tuition there too expensive?

examples.text: Mahal din, kasi pribado, pero sulit naman. Kasi mataas ang kalidad ng edukasyon sa lahat ng antas.
examples.translation: Host: Expensive too, because it’s private, but it’s worth it. Because the quality of education is high at all levels.

explanations.title: Activity 10: a radio broadcast (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: the announcement is addressed to parents and all other radio listeners. It is a reminder that enrolment at all levels is now open and will end this month; enrolment is free; the listeners are advised to enrol early.

examples.text: Mga nanay, tatay, mga kababayan, paalala lang po.
examples.translation: Mothers, fathers, countrymen, just a reminder.

examples.text: Nag-umpisa na ang enrolment sa pampublikong paaralan sa lahat ng antas sa mababa at mataas na paaralan.
examples.translation: Enrollment in public schools has started at all levels, elementary and high school.

examples.text: Hanggang sa katapusan nitong buwan lang po ang enrolment.
examples.translation: Enrollment is only until the end of this month.

examples.text: Libre po ito. Walang bayad.
examples.translation: It is free. No payment.

examples.text: Huwag ho tayong mahuli. Agahan ho natin.
examples.translation: Let’s not be late. Let’s be early.

explanations.title: Activity 11: guided conversation
explanations.body: You are a Filipino heritage speaker from the USA searching for a good school to enroll in in the Philippines. A: say you want to enroll in an advanced Filipino language course and ask for a good school; inquire about the difference; ask how expensive; say you will think about it. B: ask if A wants a private or public school; say the difference is in the quality of teaching because there are fewer students in a class; say it is not that much but one private school is close to where A lives. A sample:

examples.text: Gusto ko pong mag-enroll sa advance na kurso ng wikang Filipino. May alam ka bang magandang paaralan?
examples.translation: Heritage speaker: I want to enroll in an advanced Filipino language course. Do you know a good school?

examples.text: Gusto mo ba ng pribado o pampublikong paaralan?
examples.translation: Friend: Do you want a private or public school?

examples.text: Ano ang pagkakaiba?
examples.translation: Heritage speaker: What is the difference?

examples.text: Magkaiba ang kalidad ng pagtuturo kasi mas kokonti ang mga estudyante sa isang klase.
examples.translation: Friend: The quality of teaching is different because there are fewer students in a class.

examples.text: Gaano kamahal?
examples.translation: Heritage speaker: How expensive?

examples.text: Hindi naman gaano, pero may isang pribadong paaralan na malapit sa tinitirhan mo.
examples.translation: Friend: Not that much, but there is a private school close to where you live.

examples.text: Sige, pag-iisipan ko.
examples.translation: Heritage speaker: Okay, I will think about it.

explanations.title: Activity 12: role play, asking about each other’s schools
explanations.body: Ask each other about your schools in high school, including fees, scholarship benefits and quality of education; use pa-an/han/nan nouns when applicable (a partner role play, left out). The book’s sample questions, one per line:

examples.text: Saan ka nag-aral ng elementarya?
examples.translation: Where did you study elementary?

examples.text: Saan ka nagtapos ng sekondarya?
examples.translation: Where did you finish secondary?

examples.text: Saan ka nagtapos ng kolehiyo?
examples.translation: Where did you finish college?

examples.text: Kailan ka nagtapos ng elementarya?
examples.translation: When did you finish elementary?

examples.text: Mahal ba ang matrikula?
examples.translation: Is the tuition expensive?

examples.text: Magkano ang matrikula?
examples.translation: How much is the tuition?

examples.text: Anong taon ka nagtapos?
examples.translation: What year did you graduate?

explanations.title: Activity 13: challenge
explanations.body: Narrate where you finished elementary, high school and college, say the year you graduated, and give two to four descriptions of your school (an open task, left out).

explanations.title: Glossary
explanations.body: The book lists edukasyon and nagtapos twice; each appears once here.

rows: equally tall, for more than two people or objects
equally intelligent, for more than two people or objects
equally tall, for two people or objects
equally intelligent, for two people or objects

explanations.title: Pa-an/han/nan nouns with sample sentences from the book

examples.text: Maganda ba ang kalidad ng mga paaralan sa probinsiya?
examples.translation: Is the quality of the schools in the province good?

examples.text: Wala ni isang pahayagan sa baryo namin.
examples.translation: There is not a single newspaper in our village.

examples.text: Maganda ang pamamalakad ng pamahalaan ngayon.
examples.translation: The government’s management is good now.

examples.text: Mataas din ba ang kalidad ng pamantasan sa kamaynilaan?
examples.translation: Is the quality of the university in the Manila area also high?

examples.text: Mayaman sa kultura ang mga pamayanan ng mga Muslim.
examples.translation: The Muslim communities are rich in culture.

examples.text: Tapos na ba ang paligsahan?
examples.translation: Is the contest over?

examples.text: Malayo ang palaruan mula sa bahay namin.
examples.translation: The playground is far from our house.

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: By the end of this lesson you can extract information from reading and listening passages about jobs; answer comprehension questions about jobs; transcribe and translate phrases and sentences containing vocabulary related to jobs; answer and ask questions related to jobs; describe your job or someone else’s; and ask and answer simple questions about a job and job experience. The structures are the core vocabulary and the mag, taga and mang noun formations. In the book a mind map of jobs (tagaluto, tagasalin and others) opens the lesson and you add the jobs you know.

explanations.title: Note on OFWs
explanations.body: It is estimated that about 10% of 100 million Filipinos worked abroad. They are called OFWs, Overseas Filipino Workers. The government hails them as Bagong Bayani, “New Heroes”, because the money they send to their loved ones in the Philippines helps boost the economy.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions

The phrase may natapos siya means “she is a college graduate.”

lessons.title: 233. C13 L2 · Two friends talk about their jobs
lessons.subtitle: Nakahanap ka na ba ng trabaho? · Tagaluto, tagahugas ng plato, tagalinis · Ka-e-endo ko lang

explanations.title: Presentation 2, dialog A: friends talking
explanations.body: The book prints the carinderia as Aling Tisay’s in the dialog and Aling Tinsay’s in a later sentence; Tisay is used here.

examples.text: Pare, nakahanap ka na ba ng trabaho?
examples.translation: Gardo: Pal, have you found a job yet?

examples.text: Oo, dun sa karinderya ni Aling Tisay, tagaluto, tagahugas ng plato, at tagalinis na rin.
examples.translation: Simon: Yes, at Aling Tisay’s carinderia, cook, dishwasher, and also cleaner.

examples.text: Okey na ’yun. Kaysa naman habambuhay kang tambay.
examples.translation: Gardo: That’s okay. Better than being a layabout for life.

examples.text: Oo nga. At saka nagawa ko na rin ’ata lahat, magbobote, magbabalut, magbubulaklak, maglalako ng kung anu-ano. Ewan, wala namang nangyari. Kahit papano, dito sa karinderya, sigurado ang sahod ko at libre pa ang pagkain. Ikaw, kumusta?
examples.translation: Simon: Right. And I think I have also done everything, selling bottles, selling balut, selling flowers, peddling all sorts of things. I don’t know, nothing came of it. At least, here at the carinderia my pay is sure and the food is even free. How about you?

examples.text: Eto, Ka-e-endo ko lang. Habang naghihintay ng trabaho, nasa bahay muna, tagahatid-sundo ng mga bata, tagalaba, tagasingil ng konting pautang ni Misis, at tagabili ng itinitinda sa maliit naming tindahan.
examples.translation: Gardo: Here, I have just been ended. While waiting for work, I’m at home for now, taking the children to and from school, doing the laundry, collecting a few debts from the small lending business of my wife, and buying the goods sold in our little store.

explanations.title: Note on endo
explanations.body: In the last line, endo in Ka-e-endo is a contracted form of “end of contract.” The Herrera Law allows companies to employ contractual employees. This has become a contentious labor issue in the Philippines.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Tagahugas, tagaluto, tagalinis, tagahatid-sundo, tagalaba, tagasingil and tagabili are taga nouns. Tambay (literally, stand by) is a colloquial term for a jobless person. Magbobote, magbabalut and magbubulaklak are mag nouns. Kung anu-ano is an expression meaning “anything”; kahit papano is an expression meaning “at least.” Magbobote and the like can also be future-tense verbs.

explanations.title: Comprehension check, dialog A (the book’s key)

rows: Two friends are talking about their respective jobs.
Cook, dishwasher and cleaner in a small eatery or carinderia.
Selling bottles, selling balut (fertilized duck eggs), selling flowers, selling anything.
4. Why Simon took the latest job
He had multiple jobs before, yet his life did not improve. At least, at the small eatery, he is assured of income and the food is free.
5. What happened to Gardo’s employment (the book’s key says Cardo, a misprint)
His contract ended and he is currently waiting for another job offer.
6. Four things Gardo does while waiting
Dropping and picking up his kids; doing laundry; collecting debts from his wife’s small lending business; buying items for their small store.

explanations.body: Magtotroso, magbubukid, magsasaka, magbibigas, magkakandila, magtitiket, magbababoy, magbabaka, magmamanok, magkakarne and mag-iisda are mag nouns. Mamamahayag, mananayaw, mang-aawit, manlalaro, mambabarang, mandirigma, mangingikil, manunulat, mambabasa, mambabatas and manlilinlang are mang nouns. Dati siyang manunulat means “He used to be a writer,” “He was a writer before,” or “Previously, he worked as a writer.”

explanations.title: A. Nouns with mag
explanations.body: In Lesson 1 you learned that mag prefixed to a base noun denotes a relationship between two people, as in mag-ina (mother and child) and mag-ama (father and child). In this lesson mag is a noun-forming prefix of another kind: when mag is added to a root word with a reduplicated syllable, the noun denotes a person doing something regularly or as an occupation. The book’s examples from the reading:

rows: one who sells things in the streets

explanations.title: Note on maglalako
explanations.body: Maglalako is used as a verb in the future tense with the accent on the second syllable. Maglalako as a noun means one who sells anything, with the accent on the last syllable. There are other mag nouns that may be used as verbs in the future tense; it is all about context.

explanations.title: B. Nouns with taga
explanations.body: Taga added to a verb root denotes a person doing often or regularly what the root designates. Tagapag and tagapang are variants of taga nouns. There is no hard and fast rule as to when tagapag or tagapang is used, but a native speaker would know. Generally, when the verb root takes both um and mag verb affixes, the derived noun can also be prefixed with tagapag; when it takes a mang, the derived noun can also be prefixed with tagapang. These rules may not apply to all verb roots.

explanations.title: C. Nouns with mang
explanations.body: You learned mang (with its mam and man variants) in relation to verbs. Some mang verbs in the future tense are spelled in the same way as nouns indicating a kind of work or occupation or something a person does often. The stress of mang verbs falls on the second syllable while the stress of mang nouns falls on the first syllable. Mang nouns derived from mang verbs you have learned:

headers: Mang verb in the future tense (root)

explanations.title: Activity 7: qualifications for a PMA cadet (the book’s key)
explanations.body: From pma.ph (Philippine Military Academy). The book’s key for the six underlined phrases: 1. the qualifications to become a PMA cadet; 2. single and never been married; 3. high school graduate; 4. height should be not lower than 5 feet and not over 6 feet and 4 inches; 5. 16 years of age (the passage says seventeen); 6. not a day older than 22 years of age. Misprint noted: the key says 16 for disisiyete, which is seventeen.

examples.text: Ang sumusunod ay ang mga kuwalipikasyon upang maging kadete ng PMA.
examples.translation: The following are the qualifications to become a PMA cadet.

examples.text: Walang kasong kriminal o administratibo.
examples.translation: No criminal or administrative case.

examples.text: Dalaga o binata at hindi pa nakapag-asawa.
examples.translation: Single, a young woman or a young man, and never married.

examples.text: Maayos ang pangangatawan at may good moral character.
examples.translation: In good physical shape and with good moral character.

examples.text: Nakatapos ng mataas na paaralan.
examples.translation: Finished high school.

examples.text: Naipasa ang PMA entrance examination.
examples.translation: Passed the PMA entrance examination.

examples.text: May taas na hindi bababa sa limang talampakan at hindi tataas sa anim na talampakan at apat na dali.
examples.translation: A height of not less than five feet and not more than six feet and four inches.

examples.text: May edad na disisiyete anyos ngunit hindi mas matanda ng isang araw kaysa sa beynte dos anyos sa a-uno ng Abril ng taon pagkatapos ng pagsusulit.
examples.translation: Seventeen years of age but not a day older than twenty-two years on the first of April of the year after the exam.

explanations.title: Activity 8: a news report on summer jobs (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Give four essential elements of information. Key: the Department of Education formally opened summer jobs for students; students want to use their vacation to acquire job experience; they also want to earn money to save for the coming school opening; the Education Secretary announced that one million pesos was set aside for qualified student applicants. The book’s script has the quotation marks and the figure P1; they are written in words here.

examples.text: Pormal nang binuksan ng Department of Education, DepEd, ang pagtanggap nito ng summer jobs para sa mga estudyante.
examples.translation: The Department of Education, DepEd, has formally opened its acceptance of summer jobs for students.

examples.text: Gusto ng mga estudyante na makakuha ng karanasan sa trabaho sa bakasyon nila.
examples.translation: The students want to gain work experience during their vacation.

examples.text: Bukod dito gusto nilang kumita pa ng pera para makaipon sa darating na pasukan.
examples.translation: Besides this they want to earn money to save for the coming school opening.

examples.text: Sa pangunguna ng Education Secretary, inanunsyo niya na mayroong isang milyong piso na pondong ilalaan ang gobyerno para sa sahod ng mga mapipiling kwalipikadong aplikanteng estudyante.
examples.translation: Led by the Education Secretary, he announced that the government has set aside a fund of one million pesos for the wages of the selected qualified student applicants.

explanations.title: Activity 9, segment 1: co-workers (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Teacher notes: remind students about endo (end of contract); there is no exact English translation of tagalaba, the closest is laundry woman. Key: 1. They talk about Pia’s contract or job. 2. Her job contract will end in two months. 3. The friend asked Pia if she wants to work in a small eatery. 4. She doesn’t know how to cook. 5. Two jobs: cook and dishwasher.

examples.translation: Friend: Until when is your contract?

examples.text: Malapit na nga e. Dalawang buwan na lang endo na ako.

examples.text: Gusto mo bang magtrabaho sa karinderya?
examples.translation: Friend: Do you want to work at a carinderia?

examples.text: Tagaluto at taga-hugas ng plato.

explanations.body: Key: 6. She will go to Manila and work for her older sister; her job will be to take her nephews and nieces to school and pick them up, and she will also be in charge of cleaning the house. 7. Three jobs: bringing children to and picking them up from school, laundry woman, house cleaner.

explanations.title: Activity 10, segment 1: neighbors (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Teacher note: the job tagatahi ng basahan has no exact English translation; the closest for tagatahi is seamstress. Key: 1. They were talking about Julia. 2. Julia’s sister is a seamstress of cleaning rags and her brother-in-law is a farmer. 3. Despite their low-paying jobs they managed to send Julia to school, they helped her finish college.

examples.text: Ang galing ni Julia ’no? Tagatahi lang ng basahan ang ate niya pero nagtapos siya ng kolehiyo.
examples.translation: A: Julia is great, isn’t she? Her sister is only a sewer of rags but she graduated from college.

examples.text: Oo nga, ang bait ng ate niya at ng bayaw niya.
examples.translation: B: Right, her sister and her brother-in-law are so kind.

examples.text: Ano ba’ng trabaho ng bayaw ni Julia?
examples.translation: A: What is Julia’s brother-in-law’s job?

examples.text: Magbubukid lang pero tinulungan din niya si Julia nung nag-aaral siya sa kolehiyo.
examples.translation: B: Only a farmer but he also helped Julia when she was studying in college.

examples.text: Wala kasi silang anak.
examples.translation: A: Because they have no children.

explanations.title: Activity 10, segment 2
explanations.body: Key: 4. She got a degree in education. 5. Julia plans to work overseas; it is difficult to find jobs in the Philippines; teachers receive low salaries; she plans to work in Canada as a caregiver.

examples.text: Ano ba ang natapos ni Julia?
examples.translation: A: What did Julia finish?

examples.text: Isa siyang guro. Pero balak niyang mag-abroad.
examples.translation: B: She is a teacher. But she plans to go abroad.

examples.text: Ha? Bakit?
examples.translation: A: What? Why?

examples.text: Mahirap maghanap ng trabaho dito sa Pilipinas. At mababa din ang sahod ng guro.
examples.translation: B: It is hard to find a job here in the Philippines. And a teacher’s pay is low too.

examples.text: Saan at ano’ng trabaho niya?
examples.translation: A: Where and what job?

examples.text: Taga-alaga ng matatanda sa Canada.
examples.translation: B: Caretaker of the elderly in Canada.

explanations.title: Activity 11: a TV commercial (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: an advertisement about overseas jobs. A company in Singapore has openings for translator or interpreter, caregiver, cook, seamstress and cleaner. The company offers a benefit package and a high, competitive salary, and a two-week vacation annually.

examples.text: Gusto n’yo bang magtrabaho abroad?
examples.translation: Do you want to work abroad?

examples.text: Sinabi po ng tagapagsalita ng DOLE na maraming trabaho ang naghihintay sa isang kumpanya sa Singapore.
examples.translation: The DOLE spokesperson said there are many jobs waiting at a company in Singapore.

examples.text: Naghahanap sila ng tagasalin, taga-alaga, tagaluto, tagatahi, at tagalinis.
examples.translation: They are looking for a translator, caregiver, cook, seamstress, and cleaner.

examples.text: Maganda ang benepisyo at mataas ang sahod.
examples.translation: The benefits are good and the pay is high.

examples.text: May dalawang linggong bakasyon bawat taon.
examples.translation: There is a two-week vacation every year.

explanations.title: Activity 12: guided conversation
explanations.body: You are a contractual worker in the Philippines; in preparation talk to friends about available jobs locally or overseas. A: say that your job contract will end soon, in two and a half months; say nothing yet and ask whether he knows of any jobs; ask what types of jobs; say you will think about it. B: ask what his plans are; say there are menial jobs locally; enumerate three to five menial jobs that you learned. A sample:

examples.text: Malapit nang matapos ang kontrata ko sa dalawa at kalahating buwan.
examples.translation: A: My contract will end soon, in two and a half months.

examples.text: Ano ang plano mo?
examples.translation: B: What is your plan?

examples.text: Wala pa. May alam ka bang trabaho?
examples.translation: A: None yet. Do you know of any job?

examples.text: May mga trabahong pang-ordinaryo dito.
examples.translation: B: There are menial jobs here.

examples.text: Ano’ng klaseng trabaho?
examples.translation: A: What type of jobs?

examples.text: Tagaluto, tagahugas ng plato, tagalaba, tagalinis.
examples.translation: B: Cook, dishwasher, laundry worker, cleaner.

examples.text: Sige, pag-iisipan ko.
examples.translation: A: Okay, I will think about it.

explanations.title: Activities 13 to 15
explanations.body: Activity 13 is a role play: ask each other about previous or current jobs, with company name, salary and benefits, using taga and mag nouns (left out). Activity 14 is an individual task: describe in more detail the jobs and professions of your family members, and the jobs each has held (an open task, left out). Activity 15, the challenge, is to create a job advertisement as a radio announcer with the company or country, jobs, salary and benefit package (left out).

explanations.title: Glossary
explanations.body: The book lists magbubukid twice and gives the root of tagaluto as linis, a misprint for luto; each appears once here, the variants as separate entries.

rows: one who sells balut, boiled fertilized duck eggs
one who sells things in the streets
to be able to go to school, to be able to study
one who squanders goods or money often
was able to find a job
one who drops off and picks up a person
one whose job is to bathe another person
variant of tagapaligo, one who bathes another person
one who collects debts, debt collector
one who promotes the welfare of other people, advocate
one who makes a living by sewing
one who plays a musical instrument

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: By the end of this lesson you can extract information from reading and listening passages about a job interview; ask and answer simple questions in a job interview; transcribe and translate phrases and sentences containing vocabulary related to a job interview; use the expressions learned in a job interview; and compare and contrast jobs and job interviews. The structures are the core vocabulary, comparison of inequality, comparison expressing similarity, and adjectives expressing extreme conditions. In the book a mind map of possible interview questions opens the lesson and you add more.

explanations.title: Culture note: job interviews in the Philippines
explanations.body: 1) Generally, job interviews in the Philippines are done in English. Tagalog is used for job vacancies where a bachelor’s degree is not required. 2) During a job interview there is no law prohibiting the interviewer from asking for the interviewee’s personal information such as age, religion, date and place of birth, civil status and number of children. 3) Unlike in the United States, there is no law in the Philippines protecting applicants from being discriminated against during job hiring. It is unfortunate that the culture of “whom you know” prevails over “what you know.” A “good connection” is important in getting a job.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Masipag, matiyaga, malikhain, matapat and masunurin are ma adjectives. Kumpare (from the Spanish compadre) means “a male friend” and has no exact English equivalent. Note and learn the cognates sekretarya, dokumento, disente and pamilya.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: Pinagtrabahuan (root trabaho) is a pag-an/han/nan noun meaning “a place to work.” Other examples: pinagkainan (root kain; where you eat, refers to your plate too); pinagdausan (root daos; the place where a party or event was held); pinagmisahan (root misa; the place where mass was held). Nakapasa and nakalusot are synonyms; the latter is colloquial. Kaluma-lumaan, kamahal-mahalan and kabait-baitan are adjectives expressing extreme conditions, explained in the grammar section.

explanations.body: Compare and contrast the teacher’s previous and current situation:

rows: There are a lot more students enrolled in Bulacan Elementary School than in Malabon Elementary School. The students in both schools are equally respectful.
The prices of commodities are more expensive in Malabon than in Bulacan.
Apartment rentals are more expensive in Malabon than in Bulacan, but the teacher said it’s fine because her current apartment is closer to the school where she works.
The school buildings in Malabon Elementary School are newer compared to Bulacan Elementary School.
The teacher’s co-workers before and at her current workplace are equally the same, all are equally nice.

explanations.body: They were talking about Mike’s current job situation. Mike is pretty new in his current job assignment. He considers himself lucky because his supervisor is nicer than the previous one. His salary is not as high but the benefits are better compared to the previous, especially the health benefits.

lessons.title: 242. C13 L3 · Comparison of inequality and similarity
lessons.subtitle: Hindi kasingtaas · Mas, lalo, higit na · Gaya, tulad, kagaya, ganito, ganyan, ganoon

explanations.title: A. Comparison of inequality
explanations.body: In Lesson 1 you learned comparison of equality with sing, magsing, kasing and magkasing. Here you learn comparison involving inequality. 1. Place the negative word hindi before sing, magsing, kasing, magkasing and magkakasing:

examples.text: Hindi kasindami ang mga mag-aaral dito kaysa sa dati kong pinagtrabahuan.
examples.translation: The students here are not as many compared to where I previously worked.

examples.text: Hindi sila magkasing-ugali pero magkasingganda sila.
examples.translation: They do not have the same attitude but they are equally beautiful.

examples.text: Hindi kasingtaas ng suweldo ko dati pero higit na maganda ang benepisyo dito lalo na ang benepisyong pangkalusugan.
examples.translation: The salary is not as high compared to my previous job but the benefits are far better here, especially health benefits.

explanations.title: A2. Mas, lalo, higit
explanations.body: 2. Use the words mas, lalo plus the linker ng (lalo + ng) and higit plus the linker na with adjectives. They express “more + adjective” or an adjective ending in -er in English. (a) Mas is used in the comparative degree of adjectives. (b) Lalo + ng, higit na and mas are all interchangeable, but mas is the most commonly used and higit na the least. (c) Most of the time, statements using lalo + ng and higit na are preceded by a statement made by another person or by a previous statement, so it is safe to say lalo and higit are much higher in degree than mas.

examples.text: Mas mahal ang bilihin dito sa Malabon kaysa sa Bulacan.
examples.translation: Commodities are more expensive here in Malabon than in Bulacan.

examples.text: Mas mataas ba ang suweldo mo kaysa dati?
examples.translation: Is your salary now higher than before?

examples.text: Higit na bago ang mga gusali dito kaysa sa Mababang Paaralan ng Bulacan.
examples.translation: The buildings here are newer than the ones at Bulacan Elementary School.

examples.text: Lalong mahal ang mga paupahang apartment dito.
examples.translation: The apartment rentals here are more expensive.

examples.text: Mas maganda ang trabaho ni Cielo kaysa kay Juliette.
examples.translation: Cielo has a better job than Juliette.

examples.text: Para sa akin, higit na maganda ang trabaho ni Juliette kaysa kay Cielo.
examples.translation: As for me, Juliette has a better job than Cielo.

explanations.title: B. Comparison expressing similarity: gaya
explanations.body: Gaya means “like” in English and denotes similarities of people and objects. Tulad is a synonym for gaya; you can use them interchangeably. If you want to be specific about the point of similarity, add the adjective at the end of the sentence. Kagaya is a variant of gaya, but less used. When combination pronouns are used, the monosyllabic pronoun comes before the longer pronoun. When gaya is used with the demonstratives nito, niyan and niyon or noon, it changes to ganito, ganyan and ganoon (never ganyon); this rule does not apply with kagaya, there is no kaganito, kaganyan or kaganoon. With ganito, ganyan and ganoon the basis of comparison takes Set II markers and demonstratives.

explanations.title: B2. Sentence construction using gaya
explanations.body: Pattern: gaya + marker + basis of comparison + marker + person or object compared + adjective. The book’s eight rows are spoken here, with my own translations (the book leaves the first three for oral translation):

examples.text: Gaya ng bisor mo ngayon ang bisor mo dati, masungit.
examples.translation: Your supervisor before is like your supervisor now, grouchy.

examples.text: Tulad ng bisor mo ngayon ang bisor mo dati, masungit.
examples.translation: Your supervisor before is like your supervisor now, grouchy (tulad).

examples.text: Gaya ng mga katrabaho ko dati ang mga katrabaho ko ngayon, mababait silang lahat.
examples.translation: My co-workers now are like my co-workers before, they are all nice.

examples.text: Kagaya ng mga estudyante ko dati ang mga mag-aaral dito, magagalang sila.
examples.translation: The students here are like my students before, they are respectful.

examples.text: Gaya mo ako.
examples.translation: I am like you.

examples.text: Gaya niya ka.
examples.translation: You are like him or her.

examples.text: Ganyan ang bag ko, mura lang.
examples.translation: My bag is like that, it’s cheap.

examples.text: Ganito ang luto ko, masarap na masarap.
examples.translation: My cooking is like this, very delicious.

examples.text: Ganoon ang balae ko, napakasungit.
examples.translation: My in-law is like that, very grouchy.

explanations.title: B3. Negating gaya or tulad
explanations.body: To express inequality or dissimilarity, simply add the negative word hindi before gaya. Activity 3 asks for the negative of the last three sentences above and original sentences; the negatives are my key, and the original sentences are left open.

examples.text: Hindi ganyan ang bag ko, mura lang.
examples.translation: My bag is not like that, it’s cheap. (my key)

examples.text: Hindi ganito ang luto ko, masarap na masarap.
examples.translation: My cooking is not like this, very delicious. (my key)

examples.text: Hindi ganoon ang balae ko, napakasungit.
examples.translation: My in-law is not like that, very grouchy. (my key)

explanations.title: Activities 2 and 3
explanations.body: Activity 2: orally translate the first three gaya sentences and then make two or three original sentences with gaya, tulad or kagaya. Activity 3: orally give the negative version of the last three sentences and translate them; write two or three original sentences with hindi ganyan, hindi ganito and hindi ganoon (open tasks, left out).

lessons.title: 243. C13 L3 · Extreme-condition adjectives with ka-an/han/nan, and practice
lessons.subtitle: Kabait-baitan, kamura-murahan, kaluma-lumaan · Kauna-unahan, kahuli-hulihan · Hindi singtalino

explanations.title: C. Adjectives expressing extreme conditions
explanations.body: In the previous lesson you learned pinaka + adjective for the superlative (pinakamatalino, pinakaguwapo, pinakapangit). Here you learn the ka-an/han/nan affixes to express extreme conditions. When using a ma adjective, drop the ma and replace it with ka before the root word, reduplicate the root, then add an, han or nan. For simple (non-ma) adjectives use the complete adjective, reduplicate, then add an, han or nan. When the root ends with a vowel, use han; when it ends with a consonant, use an.

explanations.title: C1. The simple adjectives
explanations.body: In terms of ranking, only una and huli are used with ka-an/han/nan affixes; the book says there are now words like katatlu-tatluhan, kapitu-pituhan and kalima-limahan.

explanations.title: C2. Sentence pattern
explanations.body: Pattern: adjective + marker + person or object described + rest of the sentence. The book’s examples from the reading, with my translations:

examples.text: Kabait-baitan ang bisor ko ngayon.
examples.translation: My supervisor now is the nicest.

examples.text: Kamura-murahan ang mga bilihin at paupahan sa Bulacan.
examples.translation: The goods and rentals in Bulacan are the cheapest.

examples.text: Kaluma-lumaan at kapangit-pangitan na ang mga gusali sa dati kong trabaho.
examples.translation: The buildings at my former job are the oldest and the ugliest.

explanations.title: Activity 4: a narration (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Write down all the superlative adjectives you hear in Tagalog and their meaning. The book’s key lists kauna-unahan, kahuli-hulihan, pinakamahirap, pinakamahaba and kainit-initan; the script also has kasungit-sungitan, which the key leaves out.

examples.text: Ako ang kauna-unahang dumating sa interview kanina pero ako ang kahuli-hulihang na-interview.
examples.translation: I was the very first to arrive at the interview earlier but I was the very last to be interviewed.

examples.text: Ito ang pinakamahirap at pinakamahabang interview ko.
examples.translation: This is my hardest and longest interview.

examples.text: Kasungit-sungitan pa ’yung isang nag-i-interview pero hindi naman siya kagandahan.
examples.translation: One of the interviewers was the grouchiest but she isn’t pretty either.

examples.text: Nakalusot naman ako sa interview.
examples.translation: I got through the interview.

examples.text: Ang sabi, tatawagan na lang raw ako.
examples.translation: They said they will just call me.

examples.text: Umalis at dumiretso na ako sa estasyon ng bus.
examples.translation: I left and went straight to the bus station.

examples.text: Napakatagal kong naghintay ng bus.
examples.translation: I waited a very long time for the bus.

examples.text: Kainit-initan pa naman ng panahon.
examples.translation: And the weather was the hottest, too.

lessons.title: 244. C13 L3 · Listening: a job seeker’s story, interviews and a radio job announcement
lessons.subtitle: Tinanggap ako bilang guro · Pumasa ka ba sa job interview mo? · Interesado ba kayong magtrabaho sa Maynila?

explanations.title: Activity 7: a job seeker’s narration (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Write four to five essential elements of information. The key: 1. the narrator went to an interview at a school; 2. the interviewer, a principal, asked her what her qualifications were; 3. she said she had five years’ experience and was a licensed teacher; 4. she enjoyed teaching children; 5. she saw the vacancy posting on the internet; 6. she got the job as a teacher that day.

examples.text: Pumunta ako sa opisina ng punung-guro dahil siya ang nag-interview sa akin.
examples.translation: I went to the principal’s office because she was the one who interviewed me.

examples.text: Tinanong niya sa akin kung ano ang kuwalipikasyon ko.
examples.translation: She asked me what my qualifications were.

examples.text: Sinabi ko na may karanasan ako at lisensyado sa pagtuturo.
examples.translation: I said I have experience and am licensed in teaching.

examples.text: Limang taon akong guro sa Legarda Elementary School.
examples.translation: I was a teacher at Legarda Elementary School for five years.

examples.text: Masaya ako sa pagtuturo sa mga bata.
examples.translation: I am happy teaching children.

examples.text: Sa internet ko nakita na may bakanteng posisyon.
examples.translation: I saw on the internet that there was a vacant position.

examples.text: Tinanggap ako bilang guro noong araw na ’yon.
examples.translation: I was accepted as a teacher that day.

explanations.title: Activity 8, segment 1: job seekers (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: 1. The passage talks about the result of a job interview, that of Rody. 2. Rody is not sure if he passed because there were a lot of job applicants. 3. The company offers good benefits and a high or competitive salary.

examples.text: Rody, pumasa ka ba sa job interview mo?
examples.translation: Friend: Rody, did you pass your job interview?

examples.text: Baka pumasa. Pero, hindi ako sigurado kasi madami kaming nag-a-apply.
examples.translation: Rody: Maybe. But I’m not sure because there are many of us applying.

examples.text: Sakali, maganda ba ang benepisyo ng kumpanya?
examples.translation: Friend: In case, are the company’s benefits good?

examples.text: Maganda talaga ang benepisyo at mataas pa ang sahod.
examples.translation: Rody: The benefits are really good and the pay is high too.

explanations.title: Activity 8, segment 2
explanations.body: Key: 4. He is hardworking, patient, obedient, and skilled at doing other jobs. 5. He hopes he gets the job; he will be able to give his family a decent life. 6. Next week; the company will call him.

examples.text: Alam mo matatanggap ka, masipag ka, matiyaga, masunurin, at marami kang alam na trabaho.
examples.translation: Friend: You know you will be accepted, you are hardworking, patient, obedient, and you know many jobs.

examples.text: Sana nga. Kasi gusto kong bigyan ng disenteng buhay ang pamilya ko.
examples.translation: Rody: I hope so. Because I want to give my family a decent life.

examples.text: Kailan mo ba malalaman kung tanggap ka o hindi?
examples.translation: Friend: When will you know whether you are accepted or not?

examples.text: Sa susunod na linggo na. Tatawagan nila ako.
examples.translation: Rody: Next week already. They will call me.

explanations.title: Activity 10: a radio broadcast (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: the announcement is about a job opening in a big company in Manila. They are looking for a cook, carpenter, painter, electrician and plumber. The applicant should have six months of related job experience. Call 02 567 6879 for more information. The interview will be from June 4 to 20. The book prints the phone number and the date as figures; they are in words here, and the book’s typo hangggang is hanggang.

explanations.title: Activity 11: role play, applying as a volunteer teacher
explanations.body: You are doing immersion in the Philippines and, as part of your immersion project, you apply as a volunteer teacher in a remote barangay. Your partner plays the interviewer; you may refer to the readings (a role play, left out). A sample interview:

examples.text: Magandang umaga po. Ano ang posisyon na inaaplayan mo?
examples.translation: Interviewer: Good morning. What position are you applying for?

examples.text: Magandang umaga po. Boluntaryong guro po sa liblib na barangay.
examples.translation: Volunteer: Good morning. Volunteer teacher in the remote barangay.

examples.text: Bakit interesado kang magturo dito?
examples.translation: Interviewer: Why are you interested in teaching here?

examples.text: Gusto ko pong makatulong at matuto tungkol sa kultura ng mga Pilipino.
examples.translation: Volunteer: I want to help and learn about the culture of Filipinos.

examples.text: Ano ang mga katangian mo?
examples.translation: Interviewer: What are your qualities?

examples.text: Masipag po ako, matiyaga, at masunurin.
examples.translation: Volunteer: I am hardworking, patient, and obedient.

examples.text: May karanasan ka na ba sa pagtuturo?
examples.translation: Interviewer: Do you have teaching experience?

examples.text: Wala pa po, pero gusto ko pong matuto.
examples.translation: Volunteer: Not yet, but I want to learn.

explanations.title: Activities 12 to 14
explanations.body: Activity 12 is a role play: ask each other about previous job experience, educational background, qualities, purpose or interest in the job applied for, civil status, age and number of children, and contact number, with the question words from grammar (left out). Activity 13: narrate your job experience, compare and contrast your past and current jobs with one or two descriptions of each, and say why you like your job (an open task, left out). Activity 14, the challenge: narrate your previous and current jobs, with the years in previous jobs, your qualities and your educational background (an open task, left out).

explanations.title: Self-evaluation
explanations.body: The book closes the lesson with a checklist covering education, jobs and job interviews, and these features: pa-an/han/nan noun formation; comparison of equality with kasing, magkasing and magkakasing; nouns with mag denoting relationship; mag, taga and mang noun formations; comparison of inequality; comparison expressing similarity; adjectives expressing extreme conditions. If you are not sure of one, review it on your own, find a study partner, or ask your academic counselor or team leader for activities suited to your learning style.

units.title: Chapter 14 · Lesson 1: Branches and ranks

lessons.title: 246. C14 L1 · The Armed Forces of the Philippines
lessons.subtitle: Hukbong Katihan, Himpapawid, Dagat · Heneral, Tenyente Heneral, Medyor Heneral · Sandatahang Lakas ng Pilipinas

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: By the end of this lesson you can extract information from reading and listening passages about branches and ranks; formulate and answer simple questions related to branches and ranks; and transcribe and translate phrases and sentences containing vocabulary related to branches and ranks. The structures are the core vocabulary in the glossary, the recent perfective and a review of enclitics.

explanations.title: Getting started
explanations.body: The book opens with a diagram of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) showing Hukbong Katihan and Hukbong Dagat and asks what the other major services are. The answer is on this page: the Air Force, Hukbong Himpapawid, and the Marines, Hukbong Kawal Pandagat, which belongs to the Navy. Teacher note: lead students toward the lesson topic and make sure they know the target vocabulary first.

explanations.title: Presentation 1: Hukbong Sandatahang Lakas ng Pilipinas
explanations.body: Read the information about the AFP. The book prints a colon after “three branches” and the figures 165,000, 85,000 and 1935; in the spoken text the colon is a comma and the numbers are in words.

examples.text: Binubuo ang Sandatahang Lakas ng Pilipinas ng tatlong sangay, ang Hukbong Katihan, Hukbong Himpapawid at Hukbong Dagat.
examples.translation: The Armed Forces of the Philippines is composed of three branches, the Army, the Air Force and the Navy.

examples.text: Pinamumunuan ang tatlong sangay na ito ng Chief of Staff na may karaniwang ranggong Heneral.
examples.translation: These three branches are headed by the Chief of Staff, who usually holds the rank of General.

examples.text: Sunod nito ang Vice Chief of Staff na isang Tenyente Heneral at ang Deputy Chief of Staff na isa naman Medyor Heneral.
examples.translation: Next is the Vice Chief of Staff, who is a Lieutenant General, and the Deputy Chief of Staff, who is a Major General.

examples.text: Sa kasalukuyang datos, mahigit kumulang isang daan at animnapu’t limang libo ang kasapi ng Sandatahang Lakas.
examples.translation: In the current data, there are more or less 165,000 members of the Armed Forces.

examples.text: Umaabot sa walumpu’t limang libo ang nasa Hukbong Katihan at ang iba ay nasa Hukbong Dagat, Hukbong Kawal Pandagat at Hukbong Himpapawid.
examples.translation: Up to 85,000 are in the Army and the others are in the Navy, the Marines and the Air Force.

examples.text: Ang Kagawaran ng Tanggulang Pambansa ang nangangasiwa sa Sandatahang Lakas ng Pilipinas.
examples.translation: The Department of National Defense supervises the Armed Forces of the Philippines.

examples.text: Pormal na itinatag ang Sandatahang Lakas ng Pilipinas noong panahon ng Commonwealth sa ilalim ng Estados Unidos sa bisa ng National Defense Act ng labing-siyam na raan at tatlumpu’t lima.
examples.translation: The Armed Forces of the Philippines was formally established during the Commonwealth period under the United States by virtue of the National Defense Act of 1935.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: a. The synonym of Hukbong Dagat ng Pilipinas (Philippine Navy) is Hukbong Pandagat. Officially, Hukbong Dagat is used. b. There are several forms of nangangasiwa (supervises, is or are in charge): pangangasiwa (the act of supervising); tagapangasiwa (the person or office tasked with supervising); and pangasiwaan (the structure or office). c. Hukbong Kawal Pandagat ng Pilipinas (Philippine Marine Corps, PMC) is part of the Philippine Navy. Its mission is to provide combined arms units for amphibious operations and other operations of the navy. d. In the last sentence, sa bisa ng means “by virtue of.”

explanations.title: Comprehension check (the book’s key)
explanations.body: The book numbers the fourth question “3.” again; it is number 4 here.

rows: 1. The major services of the AFP
2. The ranks at the helm of AFP leadership
General, lieutenant general, and major general.
In the current data, there are more or less 165,000 members. Of this number, 85,000 are with the army. The rest are with the navy, marines, and air force.
4. The agency that administers the AFP
It was established during the Commonwealth Period under the United States by virtue of the National Defense Act of 1935.

explanations.title: Note: the PNP and the AFP
explanations.body: Under Republic Act 6975, the Philippine National Police (PNP) was handed over the principal task of handling matters affecting internal security, including the suppression of insurgency. But the challenge posed by internal security threats led national authorities, through Republic Act 8551, to return the primary responsibility for internal security to the DND and AFP. The PNP was tasked, through information gathering and the performance of its ordinary police functions, to support the AFP on matters involving suppression of insurgency.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: a. Tungkulin by itself means “duties or responsibilities.” b. However, tungkulin in the phrase mataas din ang tungkulin means “position,” so mataas din ang tungkulin means “also occupying a high position.” c. PNP stands for Philippine National Police. d. Kareretiro (root word retiro), kapo-promote and kaga-graduate express the state of being recent. The repetition of the first syllable of the root word signals that an action or event recently occurred; the grammar section explains it. e. PMA stands for Philippine Military Academy.

explanations.title: A. Recent perfective: definition
explanations.body: The recent-perfective aspect expresses actions completed just before the moment of speaking or before some other specified time in the past. The English equivalent is expressed by the present and past perfect tenses plus the word just: has or have just finished, or had just finished, as applicable.

explanations.title: A2. Formation
explanations.body: a. This verb is formed by prefixing ka, kapag or kapang to the verb root with the first syllable of the root reduplicated, plus the word lang or lamang. Examples from Presentation 2: (1) Tapos kayo, kareretiro lang bilang Kumander ng Hukbong Dagat (then you, sir, had just retired as Commander of the Navy). (2) Kapo-promote lang niya (he had just been promoted). (3) Kaga-graduate lang niya sa PMA (he had just graduated from PMA). Note the prefix ka added to the verb root with the first syllable reduplicated (reretiro, po-promote and ga-graduate). Some verbs have variants, shown in the table. b. Only actor-focus verbs from um-/-um-, ma-, maka-, mag-, magpa- and mang- can be transformed into the recent perfective.

explanations.title: Table 1: recent perfective examples
explanations.body: The variants are as the book prints them. Verbs with magpa are discussed later; examples are given here for completeness. Magluto has more recent perfective forms than magbasa (to read intensively for a long time).

rows: has, have or had just left
has, have or had just arrived
has, have or had just finished
has, have or had just broken
has, have or had just heard
has, have or had just seen
has, have or had just cooked
has, have or had just read
kapapagupit lang, kapagugupit lang, kapagpapagupit lang
has, have or had just had someone cut
kapapasulat lang, kapasusulat lang, kapagpapasulat lang
has, have or had someone write
has, have or had just gathered
has, have or had just given birth

explanations.title: A2 c and d. Mag verbs with pag
explanations.body: c. When a root word takes both an um- and a mag- prefix and a difference in meaning occurs, the recent-perfective form of the mag verb should have a pag in it. Example: magpasok, Kapapagpasok ko lang sa hukbong katihan (I have just joined the army). d. With the majority of mag verbs and in all magpa verbs, the pag is optional and the form without it is preferred. Example: magpadala, Kapapagpadala lang niya ng pera sa Pilipinas, or Kapapadala lang niya ng pera sa Pilipinas (he has just sent money to the Philippines).

explanations.title: A3. Sentence pattern
explanations.body: Verbs in the recent-perfective form are optionally but frequently followed by the enclitic particle pa. The doers and markers of a recent-perfective verb come from Set 2 markers, pronouns and demonstratives. Lang or lamang should be placed after the monosyllabic pronouns used in the sentence.

examples.text: Kapapanguha lang ni Praybeyt Dizon ng mga dokumento sa mesa.
examples.translation: Pvt. Dizon had just gathered the documents from the table.

examples.translation: Gen. Garcia had just left the office when it was burned.

explanations.title: The recent perfective with the past perfect
explanations.body: To form the recent perfective with the past perfect tense, you need two actions: one that was done before another action in the past. Study the examples, then make one or two sentences of your own.

examples.text: Kararating ko lang galing sa trabaho nang umulan.

examples.translation: They had just bought a house when it burned down.

explanations.title: B. Review of enclitics
explanations.body: You learned enclitics in earlier lessons. Here are sentences from Presentation 2: identify the enclitics, then translate.

examples.text: Sundalo rin po ba ang asawa n’yo?
examples.translation: rin po ba. Is your spouse also a soldier, sir or ma’am?

examples.text: ’Yung ama niya mataas din ang tungkulin sa PNP.
examples.translation: din. His or her father also has a high rank in the PNP.

examples.text: Kareretiro lang niya bilang Kumander ng Hukbong Dagat.
examples.translation: lang. He just retired as Commander of the Navy.

examples.text: Oo, noong nakaraang taon lang.
examples.translation: lang. Yes, only last year.

examples.text: Kapo-promote lang niya.
examples.translation: lang. He or she had just been promoted.

examples.text: Kaga-graduate lang niya sa PMA.
examples.translation: lang. He or she has just graduated from PMA.

examples.text: Bukod-tangi nga ang pamilya ninyo.
examples.translation: nga. Your family is indeed one of a kind.

examples.text: Saludo na talaga ako sa inyo.
examples.translation: na. I really salute you, already.

explanations.title: Activity 4: complete with the appropriate enclitics
explanations.body: Other enclitics not in this lesson could be used. The book’s key: 1) rin 2) sana, na, nga or rin 3) pala or na 4) lang 5) pala, din, daw, rin, na or nga 6) Sana. One answer is shown in each sentence below.

examples.text: Sundalo rin ba ang tatay mo?
examples.translation: Is your father a soldier too?

examples.text: Ikaw na ang magiging tenyente.
examples.translation: You will now be the lieutenant. (also sana, nga, rin)

examples.text: Si Heneral Santos pala ang mamumuno sa atin.
examples.translation: General Santos is the one who will lead us, I see. (also na)

examples.text: Kareretiro lang niya bilang kapitan.
