explanations.title: Activity 8, segment 1: a conversation between colleagues (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Key: 1. The two friends are talking about the first speaker’s husband and child serving in the military. 2. Kaloy was recently promoted to captain. He is retiring. 3. The second speaker said Kaloy is still young. 4. Kaloy’s wife said the promotion came too late; Kaloy is retiring this year. The book’s key says Kaloy is “64 years old,” but the script says mag-se-senta’y singko, which is seventy-five.

examples.text: Congrats, Mare, ha. Narinig ko na Kapitan na pala si Pareng Kaloy.
examples.translation: Mare A: Congrats, Mare. I heard that Pareng Kaloy is a Captain now.

examples.text: Hay, naku, Mare. Huli na ’yang promotion na ’yan. Magreretiro na si Kaloy ngayong taon.
examples.translation: Mare B: Oh dear, Mare. That promotion is too late. Kaloy will retire this year.

examples.text: Bata pa naman si Pareng Kaloy a?
examples.translation: Mare A: Pareng Kaloy is still young, isn’t he?

examples.text: Mare, mag-se-senta’y singko na siya ngayong taon.
examples.translation: Mare B: Mare, he will be seventy-five this year.

explanations.title: Activity 8, segment 2
explanations.body: Teacher note: remind students that PMA stands for Philippine Military Academy. Key: 5. The first speaker asked, Isn’t Paulo in the Navy? 6. He is a major in the army. He is now assigned in Jolo. He joined the Army after graduating from PMA. He first thought of joining the navy but changed his mind.

examples.text: Hindi bale, ’yung panganay mo naman nasa serbisyo pa rin.
examples.translation: Mare A: Never mind, your eldest is still in the service.

examples.text: A, oo, si Paulo. Medyor siya sa Hukbong Katihan. Nadestino ngayon sa Jolo.
examples.translation: Mare B: Ah, yes, Paulo. He is a Major in the Army. He is now assigned to Jolo.

examples.text: Hindi ba nasa hukbong dagat siya?
examples.translation: Mare A: Isn’t he in the navy?

examples.text: Nagbago ang isip. Pag-graduate sa PMA mas pinili niyang sumapi sa Hukbong Katihan.
examples.translation: Mare B: He changed his mind. After graduating from the PMA he chose to join the Army.

explanations.title: Activity 9, segment 1: an aunt and her niece (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Key: 1. The speakers are talking about the niece’s plans to join the military service. 2. Lorna is financially hard up; she couldn’t afford to finish her course. 3. The aunt said she is sorry; she can’t help her in her studies because she, too, has financial issues.

examples.text: Bakit hihinto ka? Isang semester na lang tapos ka na sa kurso mo.
examples.translation: Aunt: Why will you stop? Just one more semester and you will be done with your course.

examples.text: Wala na po kasi akong pang-matrikula.
examples.translation: Lorna: Because I no longer have money for tuition.

examples.text: Pasensiya na ha. Hirap din ako sa pera. Hindi kita matulungan sa pag-aaral mo. Ano’ng plano mo ngayon?
examples.translation: Aunt: I’m sorry. I am also short of money. I can’t help you with your studies. What is your plan now?

examples.text: Magsusundalo po ako Tita. May recruitment daw ngayon ang Hukbong Kawal Pandagat.
examples.translation: Lorna: I will become a soldier, Auntie. They say the Marines have recruitment now.

explanations.title: Activity 9, segment 2
explanations.body: Key: 4. Hukbong Kawal Pandagat (Marines); Hukbong Dagat (Navy); and Hukbong Katihan (Army). 5. Navy and Marines. Marines started accepting women applicants in 2006. The spoken year is dos mil sais.

examples.text: Teka muna, Lorna. Tumatanggap na ba ng babae ang Hukbong Kawal Pandagat?
examples.translation: Aunt: Wait, Lorna. Do the Marines accept women now?

examples.text: Huli na po kayo sa balita, Tita. Dos mil sais pa po, tanggap na ang babae.
examples.translation: Lorna: You are behind on the news, Auntie. Since 2006, women have been accepted.

examples.text: Ganun ba, akala ko Hukbong Dagat lang ang tumatanggap. Kailan ka pala mag-a-apply?
examples.translation: Aunt: Is that so, I thought only the Navy accepts. When will you apply?

examples.text: Tatanungin ko muna yung kapitbahay namin. Sarhento ’yun sa Hukbong Katihan.
examples.translation: Lorna: I will first ask our neighbor. He is a Sergeant in the Army.

examples.text: Sige, good luck. Halos pareho naman ’ata ang requirements nila.
examples.translation: Aunt: Okay, good luck. Their requirements are probably almost the same.

explanations.title: Activity 10: introducing a guest speaker (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Key: the guest speaker, LTC Alfredo Guevarra, came from a family of soldiers. His father was a Marine General. His mother was an Army Captain. His deceased grandfather was a Navy Commander. His oldest sibling is a captain in the Air Force.

examples.text: Nanggaling po siya sa pamilya ng mga sundalo.
examples.translation: He came from a family of soldiers.

examples.text: Ang ama niya ay naging Heneral ng Hukbong Kawal Pandagat.
examples.translation: His father became a General of the Marines.

examples.text: Naging Kapitan naman ang kanyang ina sa Hukbong Katihan.
examples.translation: His mother became a Captain in the Army.

examples.text: Ang kanyang nasirang lolo ay naging Kumander ng Hukbong Dagat.
examples.translation: His late grandfather became a Commander of the Navy.

examples.text: Ang panganay niyang kapatid ay kapitan ng Hukbong Himpapawid.
examples.translation: His eldest sibling is a captain of the Air Force.

examples.text: Ang ating guest speaker, si Tenyente Koronel Alfredo Guevarra.
examples.translation: Our guest speaker, Lieutenant Colonel Alfredo Guevarra.

explanations.title: Activity 11: guided conversation
explanations.body: You belong to a civilian work force. You heard that your friend recently got a promotion. Congratulate him and have a brief conversation; your partner plays the friend. Cues: A congratulates the friend, saying you heard that he or she was recently promoted to major in the army. B says thank you, corrects A and says you were promoted to Captain in the navy. A says sorry, you were thinking of his or her father, who is in the army. B says yes, you are right, and says your father just recently retired as colonel in the army. A says great, his or her father can relax and enjoy life, and asks how his or her only sister is. B says she has just recently joined the marines. Here is a sample dialog (my own):

examples.text: Binabati kita! Narinig ko na Medyor ka na pala sa Hukbong Katihan.
examples.translation: Civilian: Congratulations! I heard you are a Major in the Army now.

examples.text: Salamat. Pero Kapitan ako sa Hukbong Dagat.
examples.translation: Friend: Thank you. But I am a Captain in the Navy.

examples.text: Pasensiya na. Ang tatay mo pala ang naisip ko, nasa Hukbong Katihan siya.
examples.translation: Civilian: I’m sorry. I was thinking of your father, who is in the Army.

examples.text: Oo nga. Kareretiro lang ng tatay ko bilang Koronel sa Hukbong Katihan.
examples.translation: Friend: Yes, you’re right. My father just recently retired as a colonel in the Army.

examples.text: Ang galing! Makakapagpahinga na siya at mag-eenjoy sa buhay. Kumusta pala ang nag-iisa mong kapatid na babae?
examples.translation: Civilian: Great! He can relax and enjoy life. By the way, how is your only sister?

examples.text: Kasasapi lang niya sa Hukbong Kawal Pandagat.
examples.translation: Friend: She has just joined the Marines.

explanations.title: Activities 12 and 13
explanations.body: Activity 12, role play: ask each other about your rank, year and branch in the military service, and about other family members or friends in the military, with ranks and branch of service, using Tagalog question words and enclitics (a role play, left out). Activity 13, challenge: narrate about the military service you belong to. What is the US Armed Forces composed of? How are they different in ranks and major services (Army, Navy, Marines and Air Force)? Give a rough estimate of the number of active personnel in your own military unit (an open task, left out).

lessons.title: 253. C14 L2 · A soldier’s duty: passage A
lessons.subtitle: Ang sundalo ang pinakamagandang halimbawa ng lingkod bayan · Para sa Diyos, bayan at tao · Tungkulin niya ang ipagtanggol ang saligang batas

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: When you have completed this lesson you can extract information from reading and listening passages about the duties and responsibilities of AFP personnel; transcribe and translate phrases and sentences containing related vocabulary; answer and ask questions about those duties; and use the expressions learned. The structures are the core vocabulary, ka-an/han/nan, and the comparative forms of adjectives: positive, comparative and superlative.

explanations.title: Getting started
explanations.body: The book shows a picture from the army publication ATN and asks: can you identify some of the duties and responsibilities of AFP personnel? As military personnel, what are your other duties and responsibilities? Offer as many clues as possible. (The picture is left out.)

explanations.title: Presentation 1, passage A
explanations.body: Texts adapted from the Senior NCO Leadership Forum (SNCOLF) manuscript of Major General Rodolfo A. Canieso, AFP (Ret).

examples.text: Ang sundalo ang pinakamagandang halimbawa ng isang lingkod bayan.
examples.translation: The soldier is the best example of a public servant.

examples.text: Ang sundalo ay sumumpa na ang kanyang buhay ay para sa DIYOS, BAYAN at TAO.
examples.translation: The soldier has sworn that his or her life is for GOD, COUNTRY and MANKIND.

examples.text: Matalino, matatag, at matapang ang sundalo.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: a. Kasukal-sukalan and kadulu-duluhan are ka-an adjectives used in extreme conditions. b. Kasundaluhan, kapayapaan, kapahamakan, kaguluhan, kagitingan, katapangan, kadakilaan, kabayanihan, karagatan, kabundukan, kasamahan, kakulangan, kalooban and kaibigan are ka-an/han/nan nouns, explained in the grammar section. c. Kalaban and kaaway are synonyms.

explanations.title: New words
explanations.body: The book glosses kagitingan and katapangan both as “bravery,” and kaaway and kalaban both as “enemy”; they are told apart here by a short gloss.

explanations.title: Comprehension check, passage B (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Give the gist of the passage. The passage talks about the soldier as guardians of peace. Despite the ever present threats to their lives, the passage describes the soldiers as dedicated and always ready to protect the people and the country. Soldiers have strong indomitable will to fight the enemy of the state regardless of the limitations in arms and equipment. They symbolize greatness and bravery. The passage also encourages Filipinos to not forget, to recognize and to remember the heroism of the soldiers.

explanations.title: Culture note: Balikatan
explanations.body: Balikatan in English means “shoulder-to-shoulder” and characterizes the spirit of the exercise and the Philippines-United States alliance. Based on the 1951 Mutual Defense Treaty, the combined joint military exercise is conducted every year as a venue for combined training between the Philippine and U.S. militaries. Its intent is to help maintain the force readiness and interoperability of the two countries’ militaries in response to crises and natural disasters. Shifting toward stronger bilateral military relationships not only with the United States but with neighboring ASEAN countries, the AFP hopes for ongoing partnerships with other countries’ military forces to help achieve its goal of global peace and stability. (dnd.gov.ph; pia.gov.ph)

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: a. Tulad ng dati means “like in the previous” or “same as usual.” b. Siyanga pala (by way of changing the topic) is a cohesive device. d. Note and learn the cognates libre, medikal, misyon, tangke, kasado, sibilyan, oportunidad, probinsiya, trabaho, delikado and proyekto.

explanations.title: A. Ka-an/han/nan noun formation
explanations.body: In earlier lessons you learned a few ways to form nouns. Nouns can be derived from adjectives, verbs and other nouns. The examples are from the reading presentations or from vocabulary you already learned.

explanations.title: A1. Nouns derived from adjectives
explanations.body: Use ka-an/han/nan affixes when forming nouns from adjectives. When forming a noun from a ma adjective, simply drop the ma and add the ka-an/han/nan affixes. When forming a noun from a simple adjective, retain the whole adjective and then add ka-an/han/nan. Most of the nouns end in “ness” in English.

explanations.title: A1b. An act or occurrence

explanations.title: A2. Nouns derived from nouns
explanations.body: Just like nouns derived from adjectives, you can categorize ka-an/han/nan affixes according to usage.

explanations.title: A2a. Abstractness of the idea expressed in the root
explanations.body: Generally, there is no marked difference between the meaning of the root and the derived noun, but the latter expresses a higher degree of abstractness. The book prints mundo as “world/earth” and kamunduhan as “wordliness”; the latter is worldliness.

explanations.title: B. Degree of adjectives
explanations.body: In Tagalog, mas is used before the adjective for the comparative degree. This is equivalent to “er” and “more” in English. The prefix pinaka is used for the superlative degree; the English equivalent is “est” and “most.” The book’s table prints the English of mahirap as “poor, poorest, poorest”; the comparative should be “poorer.”

explanations.title: B1. Sentence structure for the comparative degree
explanations.body: Mas + adjective + marker + person or place described + kaysa + marker + basis of comparison. Read aloud, then translate:

examples.text: Mas magulo ang Basilan kaysa sa Sulu.
examples.translation: Basilan is more chaotic than Sulu.

examples.text: Mas mahirap ang Sulu kaysa sa Basilan.
examples.translation: Sulu is poorer than Basilan.

examples.text: Mas malala ang Sulu kaysa sa Basilan.
examples.translation: Sulu is worse than Basilan.

examples.text: Mas delikado ang Basilan kaysa sa Sulu.
examples.translation: Basilan is more dangerous than Sulu.

explanations.title: B2. Sentence pattern for the superlative degree
explanations.body: Adjective + marker + person or place described + marker + rest of the sentence. Read aloud, then translate:

examples.text: Pinakamahirap ang Sulu sa bansa.
examples.translation: Sulu is the poorest in the country.

examples.text: Pinakamahaba ang baybaying-dagat ng Sulu sa lahat.
examples.translation: The coastline of Sulu is the longest of all.

examples.text: Pinakamagulo sa Basilan.
examples.translation: Basilan is the most troubled.

examples.text: Pinakamaganda ang beach ng Sulu sa Mindanao.
examples.translation: The beach of Sulu is the most beautiful in Mindanao.

explanations.title: Activity 3: the correct form of the adjective (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Complete with the positive, comparative or superlative of the adjective in parentheses: 1. near, 2. tall, 3. intelligent, 4. brave, 5. big, 6. peaceful. Key: 1. Mas malapit; 2. Mas matangkad; 3. Pinakamatalino; 4. Mas matapang; 5. Malaki; 6. Mas mapayapa. The completed sentences:

examples.text: Mas malapit sa Monterey ang Camp Roberts kaysa sa Camp Pendleton.
examples.translation: Camp Roberts is nearer to Monterey than Camp Pendleton.

examples.text: Mas matangkad si Tenyente Soriano kaysa kay Tenyente Gloria.
examples.translation: Lieutenant Soriano is taller than Lieutenant Gloria.

examples.text: Pinakamatalino si Praybeyt Doria sa lahat.
examples.translation: Private Doria is the most intelligent of all.

examples.text: Mas matapang ang mga sundalo dito kaysa sa mga sundalo doon.
examples.translation: The soldiers here are braver than the soldiers there.

examples.text: Malaki ang Clark Air Base sa Pampanga.
examples.translation: Clark Air Base in Pampanga is big.

examples.text: Mas mapayapa ang Pilipinas kaysa sa Afghanistan.
examples.translation: The Philippines is more peaceful than Afghanistan.

explanations.title: Activity 4: ka-an/han/nan nouns (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Listen to the short sentences and write all six ka-an/han/nan nouns and their translations. The nouns are kadakilaan (greatness), kalalakihan (group of men), kasundaluhan (group of soldiers), kabayanihan (heroism), karahasan (violence) and kapayapaan (peace). The book’s introduction says “review the intensified and exclamatory adjectives”; the sentences also contain the ka-an adjectives kahuli-hulihan and kadulu-duluhan.

examples.text: Sa kahuli-hulihan maiisip rin natin ang kadakilaan ng ating mga sundalo.
examples.translation: In the end we will also think of the greatness of our soldiers.

examples.text: Kahuli-hulihan si Tedoro sa pila ng kalalakihan na nag-apply sa akademya.
examples.translation: Tedoro was the very last in the line of men who applied at the academy.

examples.text: Sa kadulu-duluhan man ng Pilipinas o kahit saan pa mang dako, hinaharap ng kasundaluhan ang mga kaaway ng lipunan.
examples.translation: Even at the farthest end of the Philippines or anywhere else, the soldiers face the enemies of society.

examples.text: Huwag nating kalimutan ang kabayanihan ng ating mga sundalo.
examples.translation: Let us not forget the heroism of our soldiers.

examples.text: Sinisiguro ng Hukbong Sandatahan ng Pilipinas ang proteksyon ng mamamayan mula sa karahasan.
examples.translation: The Armed Forces of the Philippines ensures the protection of the citizens from violence.

examples.text: Mahalaga ang kapayapaan upang umunlad ang bayan.
examples.translation: Peace is important so that the country can progress.

explanations.title: Activity 5: translate the sentences (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Items 1 to 3 are translated from English; items 4 and 5 from Tagalog. The book’s item 4 repeats item 2’s sentence, so it is the same pair here.

examples.text: Mas matapang ang sundalong ito kaysa sa sundalong iyan.
examples.translation: This soldier is braver than that soldier.

examples.text: Mas malaki ang kampo namin kaysa sa kampo ninyo.
examples.translation: Our camp is bigger than your camp.

examples.text: Mas mapanganib ang kasalukuyang digmaan kaysa sa nakaraang digmaan.
examples.translation: The present war is more dangerous than the past war.

examples.text: Mas masipag si Tenyente Cruz kaysa kay Tenyente Ramirez.
examples.translation: Lt. Cruz is more industrious than Lt. Ramirez.

explanations.title: Activity 6: listen and transcribe (the book’s key sentences)
explanations.body: Audio left out.

examples.text: Pinakamagandang halimbawa ng isang lingkod bayan ang mga sundalo.
examples.translation: Soldiers are the best example of a public servant.

examples.translation: The soldiers swore that their lives are for God, country and mankind.

examples.translation: The life of soldiers is dangerous if there is war.

examples.text: Kung may kapayapaan, tumutulong ang sundalo sa pagtuturo, pagtatayo ng tulay at paaralan.
examples.translation: If there is peace, the soldier helps in teaching and in building bridges and schools.

examples.text: Higit na limang libong pamilya ang nakinabang sa proyekto ng Balikatan.
examples.translation: More than five thousand families benefitted from the Balikatan project.

explanations.title: Activity 7: Balikatan in Mindanao
explanations.body: Read the passage and translate the underlined parts. Source: philstar.com opinion. The book’s numbers (1) to (4) are left out of the spoken text. The key: 1. the arrival of Balikatan in Mindanao. 2. since the Americans arrived there. 3. the economy and means of living improved. 4. can help our country in a big way.

examples.text: Malaki ang naitutulong ng pagdating ng Balikatan sa Mindanao.
examples.translation: The arrival of Balikatan in Mindanao helps a lot.

examples.text: Naalis ang takot ng mga taga-Basilan at ng Zamboanga City simula nang dumating doon ang mga Amerikano.
examples.translation: The fear of the people of Basilan and Zamboanga City was removed since the Americans arrived there.

examples.text: Gumanda rin ang ekonomiya at pangkabuhayan sa mga lugar na ito, sapagkat maliban sa nabuhay ang mga negosyo na katulad ng mga nightclubs, pumasok ang maraming dolyar na makatutulong nang malaki sa ating bansa.
examples.translation: The economy and means of living in these places also improved, because besides businesses like nightclubs coming alive, many dollars came in that can help our country in a big way.

explanations.title: Activity 8: a passage on Balikatan (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Write 3 to 4 EEIs. The key: (1) Balikatan is still beneficial at this time; (2) the Americans teach Filipino soldiers skills to fight the Abu Sayyaf; (3) the Abu Sayyaf has been a Philippine security problem for a long time; (4) the Filipinos need help in defeating the Abu Sayyaf.

examples.text: Makabubuti pa rin ang Balikatan.
examples.translation: Balikatan is still beneficial.

examples.text: Hindi lamang sinasanay ng mga Amerikanong sundalo ang mga sundalong Pinoy kundi gusto rin nilang matulungan ang ating militar laban sa mga Abu Sayyaf.
examples.translation: The American soldiers are not only training the Filipino soldiers but they also want to help our military against the Abu Sayyaf.

examples.text: Matagal nang sakit ng ulo ito.
examples.translation: This has long been a headache.

examples.text: Kailangan na ang tulong ng mga Amerikano upang mapigil ang kasamaan ng Abu Sayyaf.
examples.translation: The help of the Americans is now needed to stop the evil of the Abu Sayyaf.

explanations.title: Activity 9, segment 1: mother and daughter (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Note: the Army General Hospital is located at Fort Bonifacio, Taguig City. Key: 1. The passage is about a daughter’s desire to join the military service. 2. The mother objected because she is a licensed nurse, and she is scared that her daughter might be assigned in Mindanao, which she described as dangerous. 3. The daughter insisted: she applied at other hospitals but ended up doing volunteer work; there are too many nurses nowadays; at the moment no job is available; and she doesn’t want to miss the opportunity offered by the Army General Hospital.

examples.text: Ano? Gusto mong magsundalo? Lisensiyado kang nurse tapos magsusundalo ka?
examples.translation: Mother: What? You want to be a soldier? You are a licensed nurse and then you will be a soldier?

examples.text: Nanay, naman. May hiring ngayon sa Army General Hospital sa Fort Bonifacio. Sayang naman ho.
examples.translation: Daughter: Mother, come on. There is hiring now at the Army General Hospital in Fort Bonifacio. It would be a waste.

examples.text: Ayaw ko! Baka madestino ka sa Mindanao. Delikado dun. Mag-apply ka sa iba.
examples.translation: Mother: I don’t want it! You might be assigned to Mindanao. It is dangerous there. Apply elsewhere.

examples.text: Nanay, nag-a-apply naman ako sa ibang ospital. Pero puro volunteer work lang po. Ang dami po kasing nurses ngayon. Wala po talagang posisyon na bukas.
examples.translation: Daughter: Mother, I am applying at other hospitals. But it is all just volunteer work. There are so many nurses now. There is really no position open.

explanations.title: Activity 9, segment 2
explanations.body: Key: 4. Steadfastness and bravery. 5. As a licensed nurse she will have the rank of captain, she will receive a higher salary, and the benefits are also good.

examples.text: Naku, anak, mapanganib talagang magsundalo. Kailangan matatag at matapang ka. E, ikaw?
examples.translation: Mother: Oh, child, being a soldier is really dangerous. You need to be steadfast and brave. And you?

examples.text: Nanay, lahat naman ng tao namamatay. Bahala na ang Diyos. Basta, gusto ko ngayon, trabaho.
examples.translation: Daughter: Mother, all people die. God will take care of it. Anyway, what I want now is a job.

examples.text: Bakit, gaano ba kalaki ang matatanggap mo?
examples.translation: Mother: Why, how much will you receive?

examples.text: Dahil lisensiyadong nurse po ako, Kapitan po agad ang ranggo ko, ’Nay. Mataas ang sahod. Maganda rin po ang benepisyo.
examples.translation: Daughter: Because I am a licensed nurse, my rank is Captain right away, Mother. The pay is high. The benefits are also good.

explanations.title: Activity 10, segment 1: a phone conversation between friends (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Note: WESMINCOM means Western Mindanao Command. Key: 1. Two friends talked about their respective assignments or duties. 2. Benjie is in Jolo for the Balikatan. 3. His friend is a medical doctor. The book’s script prints balón with an accent; it is balon here.

examples.text: Hello, Benjie, nasa’n ka ba ngayon?
examples.translation: Doctor: Hello, Benjie, where are you now?

examples.text: Dito ako nadestino sa Jolo ngayon. Kasama ako sa Balikatan. Ikaw, nasa’n ka ngayon?
examples.translation: Benjie: I am assigned here in Jolo now. I am part of Balikatan. And you, where are you now?

examples.text: Nasa Iligan ako ngayon. May medical at dental misyon. Alam mo naman kulang ng doktor ang AFP.
examples.translation: Doctor: I am in Iligan now. There is a medical and dental mission. You know the AFP lacks doctors.

examples.text: Akala ko nga nagbabakasyon ka? Nasa field ka rin pala.
examples.translation: Benjie: I thought you were on vacation? You are in the field too.

explanations.title: Activity 10, segment 2
explanations.body: Key: 4. Fixing bridges, digging wells, medical and dental missions, and constructing water tanks. 5. Fix schools affected by the typhoon and construct five new schools in barangays that have no schools.

examples.text: Oo. Kasama rin namin ang engineering team. Nagkukumpuni sila ng nasirang tulay. Wala ring malinis na tubig dito. Kaya gagawa rin ng balon at magtatayo ng tangke ng tubig. Ikaw ano’ng balita diyan?
examples.translation: Doctor: Yes. The engineering team is with us too. They are repairing a damaged bridge. There is also no clean water here. So they will also make a well and build a water tank. What is your news there?

examples.text: Eto, naghahanda sa pagkukumpuni ng mga paaralan. Marami rin kasing nasira dahil sa bagyo. May ibang barangay na wala talagang paaralan kaya magtatayo kami ng limang bagong paaralan.
examples.translation: Benjie: Here, preparing to repair schools. Many were also damaged by the typhoon. Some barangays really have no school so we will build five new schools.

explanations.title: Activity 11: a radio announcement (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: the announcement is a job advertisement. The AFP is seeking applicants who are willing to pledge their life to God, country, and mankind; who are willing to defend the constitution, protect the citizens, and fight terrorism; and who are smart, steadfast, and brave. Interested applicants can go to the nearest recruitment center.

examples.text: Handa ba kayong sumumpa ng inyong buhay para sa Diyos, bayan, at tao?
examples.translation: Are you ready to pledge your life for God, country and mankind?

examples.text: Kaya n’yo bang ipagtanggol ang saligang batas, proteksyunan ang mamamayan at labanan ang terorismo?
examples.translation: Can you defend the constitution, protect the citizens and fight terrorism?

examples.text: Kayo ba ay matalino, matatag, at matapang?
examples.translation: Are you intelligent, steadfast and brave?

examples.text: Bumisita sa pinakamalapit na recruitment center.
examples.translation: Visit the nearest recruitment center.

examples.text: May malaking hiring ng mga sundalo ang Sandatahang Lakas ng Pilipinas.
examples.translation: The Armed Forces of the Philippines has a big hiring of soldiers.

explanations.title: Activity 12: guided conversation
explanations.body: You are both military personnel previously involved in a Balikatan exercise. Ask your partner about his or her experience. Cues: A greets and asks how B is doing. B says you just came from a successful Balikatan exercise in Iligan. A asks about the projects or activities undertaken by B’s group. B enumerates 4 to 6 activities usually done during Balikatan. A says that’s great, surely the local community will benefit from those activities. B asks how the Balikatan in Jolo was. A says it was successful and enumerates 3 to 5 projects done in Jolo. A sample dialog (my own):

examples.text: Kumusta ka, pare?
examples.translation: Soldier 1: How are you, pare?

examples.text: Mabuti naman. Kauuwi ko lang galing sa matagumpay na Balikatan sa Iligan.
examples.translation: Soldier 2: Fine. I have just come home from a successful Balikatan in Iligan.

examples.text: Ano-ano ang mga proyekto ng grupo mo?
examples.translation: Soldier 1: What were the projects of your group?

examples.text: Nagtayo kami ng paaralan, nagkumpuni ng tulay, gumawa ng balon, nagtayo ng tangke ng tubig, at nagsagawa ng libreng medikal at dental na misyon.
examples.translation: Soldier 2: We built a school, repaired a bridge, made a well, built a water tank, and conducted a free medical and dental mission.

examples.text: Ang galing! Siguradong makikinabang ang komunidad sa mga gawaing iyan.
examples.translation: Soldier 1: Great! Surely the community will benefit from those activities.

examples.text: Salamat. Kumusta naman ang Balikatan sa Jolo?
examples.translation: Soldier 2: Thanks. How was the Balikatan in Jolo?

examples.text: Matagumpay din. Nagtayo kami ng limang paaralan, nagkumpuni ng tulay at gumawa ng balon.
examples.translation: Soldier 1: Successful too. We built five schools, repaired a bridge and made a well.

explanations.title: Activities 13 and 14
explanations.body: Activity 13, role play: ask each other about civilian-military duties and give details of significant events, using Tagalog question words and enclitics; for an extra challenge, use me, meron, mayroon plus ba (left out). Activity 14, challenge: give a narration about some of your duties and responsibilities as a member of the U.S. Armed Forces, with 2 to 4 civilian-military duties and 1 to 2 details of significance to you (an open task, left out).

explanations.title: Glossary
explanations.body: The book glosses kabuhayan and paghahanapbuhay both as livelihood; here kabuhayan is “means of living.” The book prints the root of kalimutan as limot with a stray comma; no roots are given here.

explanations.title: Ka-an/han/nan nouns with sample sentences from the book
explanations.body: The book gives no translations; they are mine. The book’s “ika 9 ng Abril” is spoken as ikasiyam ng Abril.

examples.text: Inalala ang kabayanihan ng isang sundalo na nagbuwis ng buhay kaninang umaga.
examples.translation: The heroism of a soldier who gave his life this morning was remembered.

examples.text: Nasa kabundukan ang mga kuta ng mga kalaban ng pamahalaan.
examples.translation: The hideouts of the government’s enemies are in the mountains.

examples.text: Mga mamamayan ng Lucena, Quezon, kinilala ang kadakilaan ni Jose Rizal.
examples.translation: The citizens of Lucena, Quezon, recognized the greatness of Jose Rizal.

examples.text: Nasa kadulu-duluhan ng Sierra Madre ang kampo ng mga makakaliwang grupo.
examples.translation: The camp of the leftist groups is at the farthest end of the Sierra Madre.

examples.text: Naaalala tuwing ikasiyam ng Abril ang kagitingan ng mga sundalong Pilipino na lumaban sa mga Hapones.
examples.translation: Every ninth of April the valor of the Filipino soldiers who fought the Japanese is remembered.

examples.text: Sampung paaralan ang nasira dahil sa kaguluhan sa siyudad ng Marawi.
examples.translation: Ten schools were destroyed because of the violence in the city of Marawi.

examples.text: Kakulangan sa kagamitan at pasilidad ang pangunahing suliranin ng mga sundalong Pilipino.
examples.translation: Shortage of equipment and facilities is the main problem of Filipino soldiers.

examples.text: May mas matindi tayong mga kalaban, ang ating mga kapwa Pilipino.
examples.translation: We have more serious enemies, our fellow Filipinos.

examples.text: Nauubos ang bala ang kalimitang inirereklamo ng mga sundalo.
examples.translation: Running out of bullets is what soldiers usually complain about.

examples.text: Huwag n’yong kalimutang magdasal bago kayo sumabak sa operasyon.
examples.translation: Do not forget to pray before you go into the operation.

examples.text: Mahalaga sa pinuno ng mga sundalo ang matatag na kalooban.
examples.translation: A steadfast will is important to the leader of soldiers.

examples.text: Madalas nakatalaga sa kanayunan ang mga miyembro ng Hukbong Katihan.
examples.translation: Members of the Army are often assigned in the countryside.

examples.text: Malalagay sa kapahamakan si Kuya kung hindi siya susuko.
examples.translation: Kuya will be put in danger if he does not surrender.

examples.text: Nasusukat ang tunay na katapangan sa pagharap ng mga problema.
examples.translation: True bravery is measured in facing problems.

examples.text: Hindi tayo magkakaroon ng kapayapaan kung hindi tayo mag-uusap.
examples.translation: We will not have peace if we do not talk.

examples.text: Nasa Karagatang Pasipiko ang pinakamadugong digmaan sa dagat sa pagitan ng Hukbong Hapones at Hukbong Amerikano.
examples.translation: The bloodiest sea war between the Japanese forces and the American forces took place in the Pacific Ocean.

examples.text: Nasugatan sa bakbakan ang isang sundalo at tatlo pa niyang kasamahan kahapon.
examples.translation: A soldier and three of his colleagues were wounded in the fighting yesterday.

examples.text: Sa mga kasukalan ng Mindoro naninirahan ang mga kalaban ng gobyerno.
examples.translation: The enemies of the government live in the thickets of Mindoro.

examples.text: Kumpiyansa ang mga kasundaluhan na mababawi nila ang siyudad ng Marawi.
examples.translation: The soldiers are confident that they will retake the city of Marawi.

examples.text: Walang katumbas ang sukat ng katapangan ng mga Pilipinong sundalo.
examples.translation: The measure of the bravery of Filipino soldiers has no equal.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: a. Akademya Militar ng Pilipinas (Philippine Military Academy, PMA). Along with the Development Academy of the Philippines, the Philippine National Police Academy, the Philippine Public Safety College and the National Defense College, the PMA is classified as a Special Higher Education Institution (HEI). Special HEIs are public organizations that offer higher education programs related to public service (census.gov.ph). b. In paragraph 2, line 1, tirahan refers to a “lodging house,” not “address.” c. Matalino, mapagkumbaba, matigas and mahina are adjectives.

explanations.title: Note: the Navy Seal
explanations.body: The Navy Seal, or the Philippine Navy Special Operations Group (NAVSOG), is one of the elite units of the Armed Forces of the Philippines. Its core competencies support its four units: Special Boat Unit, Diving Unit, Naval Explosive Ordnance Unit, and Sea Air Land (SEAL). Its capabilities include operations in reconnaissance, close combat, demolition, counterinsurgency and intelligence, and maritime area and riverine environment (navsog.navy.mil.ph).

examples.text: Anak, mukhang humuhusay ka na sa target practice at mukhang gumaganda at lumalakas na rin ang katawan mo.
examples.translation: Father: Son, it seems you are getting better at target practice and your body is also looking better and getting stronger.

examples.text: Naghahanda lang po. Interesado po akong mag-apply sa PNPA. Gusto ko po sanang maging pulis.

examples.text: Magiging magaling ka nga kung palagi kang nagsasanay.

examples.text: Tatay, hindi kaya tututol si Nanay sa plano kong maging pulis?

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: a. Note and learn the cognates listed with dialog A. b. PNPA means Philippine National Police Academy, which you learned in a previous lesson. c. In dialog B, maging was used as a verb and as an adverb, discussed in the grammar section. In the glossary the book glosses nasira as “deceased”; its ordinary meaning is “broken, damaged,” and nasirang lolo means “late grandfather.”

rows: always, often, on a regular basis
appearing to be weak and feeble

explanations.title: Comprehension check, dialog B (the book’s key)
explanations.body: The son is telling his father about his interest in becoming a policeman. He is not sure, though, if his mom would allow him. His father assured him of his mom’s support because the father and grandfather of his mom are both police officers. His father also advised him that things can be difficult if you think it is difficult. The father wished for his son to become a role model in whatever profession he chose to aspire to or join.

explanations.title: A. Maging as a verb
explanations.body: Maging, a very common helping verb in Tagalog, means “to be” or “to become.” It is placed before a noun or adjective. It expresses a change from one state or condition to the other. It is used in sentences where the FOCUS is on the DOER. The book says “precious lessons” where it means previous lessons.

rows: to become a good role model

explanations.title: Conjugating maging
explanations.body: When conjugated, maging follows the rules on mag verbs.

explanations.title: To become with the um affix
explanations.body: “To become” or “to be” can also be expressed using the um affix, as with the weather verbs you learned (humina, to become weak; uminit, to become hot or warm). Only phrases using maging plus an adjective can be transformed using um. ALL adjectives can be used with maging, but NOT ALL adjectives can be used with the um affix.

rows: maging itim (as printed; maging maitim is usual)

explanations.title: B. Maging as an adverb
explanations.body: Maging has another meaning. As an adverb, it means “even,” “to include,” “no matter who,” “no matter what,” or “alike” in an English sentence.

examples.text: Maging si Lolo Jorge mo, ama ng ina mo, ay isang kilalang pulis.
examples.translation: Even Grandpa Jorge, your mom’s father, was also a well-known policeman.

examples.text: Maging ang nasira mong lolo sa tuhod ay isa ring pulis.
examples.translation: Even your deceased great grandfather was also a policeman.

examples.text: Maging ako ay nagulat nung nalaman ko.
examples.translation: Even I was surprised when I learned about it.

explanations.title: More examples (the book’s)
explanations.body: To show the different meanings of maging in English, the book gives sample sentences with words you already know.

examples.text: Mamahalin pa rin kita maging sino ka man.

explanations.title: C. Review of pseudo verbs and negative words
explanations.body: In earlier lessons you learned about pseudo verbs and negative sentences with hindi and wala. Pseudo verbs are not conjugated. They are used as helping verbs. There is a linker between the pseudo verb and the main verb. The doer in the sentence is from either the Set 1 or the Set 2 pronouns and markers. Identify the pseudo verbs in these sentences from the presentations, then translate. The book’s key for the pseudo verbs: (1) puwede or maaari; (2) puwede or maaari; (3) dapat; (4) dapat; (5) maaari; (6) kailangan; (7) kailangan. The book’s second sentence shows both words in one line; they are split into two sentences here.

examples.text: Hindi ako puwedeng tanggapin sa Marines.
examples.translation: I can’t be accepted in the Marines. (pseudo verb: puwede, also maaari)

examples.text: Maaari akong tanggapin sa Navy.
examples.translation: I can be accepted in the Navy. (my reading of the book’s sentence 2, with maaari)

examples.text: Puwede akong tanggapin sa Navy.
examples.translation: I can be accepted in the Navy. (my reading of the book’s sentence 2, with puwede)

examples.text: Dapat determinado, matalino, marunong magtimpi, at mapagkumbaba.
examples.translation: One should be determined, intelligent, have self-control, and be humble. (pseudo verb: dapat)

examples.text: Dapat hindi mayabang.
examples.translation: One should not be arrogant, proud or boastful. (pseudo verb: dapat)

examples.text: Maaari silang magsilbi sa alinmang sangay ng AFP.
examples.translation: They could serve in any branch of the AFP. (pseudo verb: maaari)

examples.text: Kailangan aktibong miyembro ng Navy.
examples.translation: They need to be active members of the Navy. (pseudo verb: kailangan)

examples.text: Kailangan ng anim na buwang masinsinang pagsasanay para sa mga bagong salta.
examples.translation: Six months of intensive training is needed for the newly arrived recruits. (pseudo verb: kailangan)

explanations.title: Besides hindi, what do the other negative words mean?
explanations.body: Ayaw means “do not, does not, did not want or like.” Ayoko means “I do not, I did not want or like”; the doer, “I,” is built in. These are not conjugated.

explanations.title: Activity 6: listen and transcribe (the book’s key sentences)
explanations.body: Audio left out. The book’s source label for this audio reads T_C14_L1 by mistake.

examples.text: Bakit hindi biro ang pag-aaral at pagsasanay sa loob ng akademya?
examples.translation: Why are study and training inside the academy no joke?

examples.text: Ayaw nilang bigyan ka ng tirahan, pagkain, at buwanang allowance.
examples.translation: They don’t want to give you lodging, food and a monthly allowance.

examples.text: Hindi ka puwedeng magsilbi bilang sundalo kung wala kang bachelor’s degree.
examples.translation: You can’t serve as a soldier if you don’t have a bachelor’s degree.

examples.text: Ayaw niyang pumasok si Lino sa Akademya Militar ng Pilipinas.
examples.translation: He or she doesn’t want Lino to enter the Philippine Military Academy.

examples.text: Kung hindi ka determinado at mapagkumbaba, hindi ka tatanggapin sa akademya.
examples.translation: If you are not determined and humble, you will not be accepted in the academy.

explanations.title: Activity 7: translate the sentences (the book’s key)

examples.text: Hindi puwedeng mahina ang loob ng sundalong nag-aaral sa Akademya Militar.
examples.translation: A soldier studying at the PMA cannot be fainthearted.

examples.text: Ayaw namin ng estudyanteng matigas ang ulo at mayabang.
examples.translation: We don’t want a student who is hardheaded and boastful.

examples.text: Wala silang panahon sa pagsasanay at pag-aaral sa akademya.
examples.translation: They have no time for exercises and studies at the academy.

examples.text: Hindi siya puwedeng magsilbi sa alinmang sangay ng AFP.
examples.translation: He could not serve in any branch in the AFP.

examples.text: Bawal ang matigas ang ulo at hindi marunong magtimpi.
examples.translation: It is forbidden to be hardheaded and to have no self-control.

explanations.title: Activity 8: read the passage and give 3 to 4 EEIs
explanations.body: The book’s key: (1) Many Filipino soldiers want to study at the Philippine Military Academy; (2) they want to graduate as officers of the AFP with a bachelor’s degree in military science; (3) they will have the rank of second lieutenant; (4) they need to be brave, determined, intelligent, humble, and have self-control.

examples.text: Karamihan sa mga sundalong Pilipino ay gustong maging mag-aaral sa prestihiyosong Akademya Militar ng Pilipinas.
examples.translation: Most Filipino soldiers want to become students at the prestigious Philippine Military Academy.

examples.text: Gusto nilang maging opisyal ng Sandatahang Lakas ng Pilipinas.
examples.translation: They want to become officers of the Armed Forces of the Philippines.

examples.text: Pagkatapos ng apat na taon may digri sila sa agham militar.
examples.translation: After four years they have a degree in military science.

examples.text: Magiging pangalawang tenyente sila.
examples.translation: They will become second lieutenants.

examples.text: Alam nila na hindi biro ang pag-aaral sa akademya.
examples.translation: They know that studying at the academy is no joke.

examples.text: Kailangang maging matapang, determinado, matalino, marunong magtimpi, at mapagkumbaba.
examples.translation: They need to be brave, determined, intelligent, self-controlled and humble.

lessons.title: 269. C14 L3 · Listening: applying to the PMA and the PNPA, and a Navy Seal call
lessons.subtitle: Gusto ko sanang mag-exam para sa PMA · Gusto kong maging tulad mo, Kuya · Mag-apply bilang Navy Seal

explanations.title: Activity 9, segment 1: mother and daughter (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Key: 1. The passage talks about the daughter’s desire to apply at the PMA. 2. The mother said her daughter, Dolor, is hardheaded; the mom explained that they don’t have money for college. 3. The daughter said that if she gets accepted in the PMA she will enjoy a lot of benefits: besides the monthly allowance, everything is free (food, schooling, and room and board); after graduation she will have the chance to join any branch of the AFP and will get the rank of 2LT. The book’s dash after “libre po lahat” is a period here.

examples.text: Nanay, gusto ko sanang mag-exam para sa PMA. Pahingi pong pamasahe.
examples.translation: Daughter: Mother, I would like to take the exam for the PMA. Please give me fare.

examples.text: Naku, Dolor, ang tigas naman ng ulo mo. Wala nga tayong perang pang-kolehiyo mo.
examples.translation: Mother: Oh, Dolor, you are so hardheaded. We don’t have money for your college.

examples.text: Nay, kapag nakapasok ako ng PMA, bukod sa buwanang allowance, libre po lahat. Pag-aaral, tirahan, at pagkain. At saka ’Nay ’pag natapos po ako maaari po akong pumasok sa alinmang sangay ng AFP. Opisyal po ako agad, pangalawang tenyente po.
examples.translation: Daughter: Mom, if I get into the PMA, besides the monthly allowance, everything is free. Schooling, lodging and food. And also, Mom, when I finish I can enter any branch of the AFP. I will be an officer right away, a second lieutenant.

explanations.title: Activity 9, segment 2
explanations.body: Key: 4. The mother thinks joining the PMA is dangerous; PMA graduates are deployed mostly in Mindanao. 5. The daughter said, “Life is just a matter of luck. Everyone dies anyway.” 6. The mom is a laundry woman. 7. The daughter promised that if she gets accepted to the PMA she will send her monthly allowance to her parents.

examples.text: Pero anak, hindi ba mapanganib ang PMA na ’yan? Kadalasan sa Mindanao nadedestino.
examples.translation: Mother: But child, isn’t that PMA dangerous? They are mostly assigned in Mindanao.

examples.text: Nanay, suwerte suwerte lang po ang buhay. Sige na, ’Nay, bigyan n’yo muna ako ng pamasahe para makapag-exam na po ako.
examples.translation: Daughter: Mother, life is just a matter of luck. Come on, Mom, give me fare first so that I can take the exam.

examples.text: Sige na nga. Eto, may konting pera dito. Kita ko ito sa paglalaba. Sana anak, makapasa ka.
examples.translation: Mother: All right then. Here, there is a little money. I earned this from doing laundry. I hope, child, that you pass.

examples.text: Opo, ’nay. At ’pag nakapasok ako, ipapadala ko ang buwanang allowance ko sa inyo ni Tatay.
examples.translation: Daughter: Yes, Mom. And when I get in, I will send my monthly allowance to you and Dad.

explanations.title: Activity 10, segment 1: siblings (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Note: PNPA refers to the Philippine National Police Academy. Key: 1. The siblings talked about the sister’s (Daisy’s) desire to join the PNPA. 2. The brother said the training in the academy is no joke, it is not for the fainthearted, and it is also not for the stubborn and bossy. He wonders how his sister will survive in the academy when she is a bit stubborn and bossy.

examples.text: Ano papasok ka ng PNPA? Sigurado ka ba?
examples.translation: Kuya: What, you will enter the PNPA? Are you sure?

examples.text: Siguradong-sigurado Kuya. Gusto kong maging tulad mo.
examples.translation: Daisy: Very sure, Kuya. I want to be like you.

examples.text: Naku, Daisy, hindi biro ang pagsasanay sa loob ng akademya. Hindi puwede ang mahina ang loob. At saka hindi rin ito para sa matitigas ang ulo at mayayabang. E, ikaw, may katigasan ka pa naman ng ulo at may konting kayabangan. Papano ’yan?
examples.translation: Kuya: Oh, Daisy, the training inside the academy is no joke. The fainthearted will not do. And it is also not for the stubborn and arrogant. And you, you still have some stubbornness and a little arrogance. How about that?

examples.text: Kuya naman. Dati po ’yun. Mabait na po ako ngayon.
examples.translation: Daisy: Kuya, come on. That was before. I am nice now.

explanations.title: Activity 10, segment 2
explanations.body: Key (the book numbers these 2 and 3 again): Daisy recently graduated from college. The three requirements for admission into the PNPA: 22 years of age; 5’2” height; and passing the written examination. The heights are in words in the spoken text. In the dialog Daisy is twenty-one and says she does not want to be late for the age requirement of twenty-two.

examples.text: Katatapos mo lang ng kolehiyo. Ba’t hindi ka na lang muna magtrabaho?
examples.translation: Kuya: You have just finished college. Why don’t you just work first?

examples.text: Kuya beynte uno na ako. Beynte dos po ang age requirement sa PNPA. Ayaw ko namang mahuli.
examples.translation: Daisy: Kuya, I am twenty-one already. Twenty-two is the age requirement for the PNPA. I don’t want to be late.

examples.text: Teka, ano bang height mo?
examples.translation: Kuya: Wait, what is your height?

examples.text: Pasado po ako. Lima talampakan at limang pulgada kaya ako. Lima talampakan at dalawang pulgada lang ang kailangan.
examples.translation: Daisy: I pass. I am five feet five inches. Only five feet two inches is needed.

examples.text: Makakapasa ka kaya sa written exam? Kaya mo ba?
examples.translation: Kuya: Will you pass the written exam? Can you?

examples.text: Kuya, matalino yata ’tong bunso mo.
examples.translation: Daisy: Kuya, your youngest sibling is smart, I think.

explanations.title: Activity 11: a radio announcement (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: the announcement is a call for those interested to serve the country by becoming a Navy Seal. To qualify, one must be an active member of the navy; she or he should also be steadfast or committed, brave, smart, and must have strong self-confidence. A Navy Seal offers many great benefits: an additional 50% of the current salary of navy personnel, and an opportunity to be sent overseas for training.

examples.text: Gusto mo bang magsilbi sa bayan?
examples.translation: Do you want to serve the country?

examples.text: Kasalukuyang aktibong miyembro ka ba ng Hukbong Dagat?
examples.translation: Are you currently an active member of the Navy?

examples.text: Determinado ka ba?
examples.translation: Are you determined?

examples.text: Matapang, matalino, at malakas ang loob?
examples.translation: Brave, intelligent, and strong-willed?

examples.text: Mag-apply bilang Navy Seal.
examples.translation: Apply as a Navy Seal.

examples.text: Napakaganda ng benepisyo.
examples.translation: The benefits are very good.

examples.text: May karagdagang singkuwenta porsiyentong sahod sa regular na sahod.
examples.translation: There is an additional fifty percent salary on top of the regular salary.

examples.text: Meron ding oportunidad na mapadala sa ibang bansa para magsanay.
examples.translation: There is also an opportunity to be sent to another country for training.

explanations.title: Activity 12: guided conversation
explanations.body: You are interested in applying for the Philippine Army Candidate Soldier Course. Talk to a friend who is now in the Army and ask what the qualifications are. Cues: B says you learned that A is interested to join the army. A says yes and asks about the age and height requirements. B says A must be between 18 and 26 years old and at least 5 feet in height. A says you are 24 and 5 feet 5 inches tall, so you qualify. B says A needs to pass the PAATB. A asks what the PAATB is. B says PAATB stands for Philippine Army Aptitude Test Battery, and that a score of at least 80 is required to pass. A says thank you. A sample dialog (my own):

examples.text: Nabalitaan kong interesado kang sumapi sa Hukbong Katihan.
examples.translation: Friend: I heard that you are interested in joining the Army.

examples.text: Oo. Ano ang requirements sa edad at tangkad?
examples.translation: Applicant: Yes. What are the requirements for age and height?

examples.text: Dapat nasa pagitan ng disi-otso at dalawampu’t anim na taong gulang at hindi bababa sa limang talampakan ang tangkad.
examples.translation: Friend: You must be between eighteen and twenty-six years old and at least five feet tall.

examples.text: Dalawampu’t apat na taong gulang ako at limang talampakan at limang pulgada ang tangkad ko, kaya pasado ako.
examples.translation: Applicant: I am twenty-four years old and five feet five inches tall, so I qualify.

examples.text: Kailangan mo ring pumasa sa PAATB.
examples.translation: Friend: You also need to pass the PAATB.

examples.text: Ano ba ang PAATB?
examples.translation: Applicant: What is the PAATB?

examples.text: Ang PAATB ay Philippine Army Aptitude Test Battery, at kailangan ng markang walumpu man lang para makapasa.
examples.translation: Friend: PAATB stands for Philippine Army Aptitude Test Battery, and a score of at least eighty is needed to pass.

examples.text: Salamat.
examples.translation: Applicant: Thank you.

explanations.title: Self-evaluation (the end of Chapter 14)
explanations.body: The book closes with a checklist. Can you extract information from reading and listening passages about branches and ranks, formulate and answer simple questions about them, and transcribe and translate phrases and sentences with that vocabulary? Can you extract information from passages about the duties and responsibilities of AFP personnel, transcribe and translate related phrases and sentences, answer and ask questions about them, and use the expressions learned? Can you extract information about military schooling and training, ask and answer simple questions about it, and transcribe and translate its vocabulary? Do you have a clear understanding of the recent perfective, enclitics, degrees of comparison (positive, comparative and superlative), maging as a verb and maging as an adverb? If any answer is no, review the section on your own, find a study partner, or ask your academic counselor or team leader for activities tailored to your learning style and needs.

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: By the end of this lesson you can extract information from reading and listening passages about hospitals and other medical services; formulate and answer simple questions about them; and transcribe and translate phrases and sentences containing related vocabulary. The structures are the core vocabulary and the verb magkaroon.

explanations.title: Getting started
explanations.body: The book shows the medical services offered by government hospitals and local government units to indigents in the Philippines (free operations, free medicines) and asks what other medical services are available. Teacher note: lead students toward the lesson topic; know the target vocabulary first. (The picture is left out.)

explanations.title: Presentation 1: medical services for indigents
explanations.body: An excerpt from laguna.gov.ph. The dash after “mahihirap” in the book is a comma here.

examples.text: Maraming pampublikong hospital sa Pilipinas.
examples.translation: There are many public hospitals in the Philippines.

examples.text: Kadalasan, libre ang serbisyo tulad ng ambulansya at mga gamot.
examples.translation: Most of the time, services such as the ambulance and medicines are free.

examples.text: Walang ginagasta ang mga pasyente.
examples.translation: The patients spend nothing.

examples.text: Tinutugunan ng mga doktor ang lahat ng uri ng karamdaman.
examples.translation: The doctors address all kinds of illness.

examples.text: Karamihan sa kanila ay mga espesyalista sa larangan ng medisina.
examples.translation: Most of them are specialists in the field of medicine.

examples.text: Walang tinatanggihan ang pampublikong mga hospital.
examples.translation: The public hospitals reject no one.

examples.text: Bawal ito.
examples.translation: It is prohibited.

examples.text: May direktiba rin ang mga mayor o alkalde ng lungsod na tanggapin ang kahit sinong pasyente lalo na ang mga nangangailangan o mga mahihirap, silang mga walang kakayahang magpagamot sa mga pribadong hospital.
examples.translation: The mayors or city mayors also have a directive to accept any patient, especially the needy or the poor, those who cannot afford treatment in private hospitals.

examples.text: Kadalasan ang lokal na pamahalaan ay nagsasagawa ng libreng medical mission.
examples.translation: Most of the time the local government conducts a free medical mission.

examples.text: Libreng pagsusuri, libreng gamot, at minsan libreng operasyon sa katarata o bingot ang ipinagkakaloob sa mga residente ng barangay.
examples.translation: Free check-ups, free medicine, and sometimes a free operation for cataract or cleft palate are given to the residents of the barangay.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: a. In paragraph 1, line 2, medisina is the synonym of gamot. b. In paragraph 1, last line, medisina refers to the “field of medicine.” c. Note and learn the cognates serbisyo, pasyente, doktor, medisina, espesyalista, alkalde, direktiba, pribado, residente, lokal and operasyon. The book prints nangngailangan in the table; the word is nangangailangan.

rows: 1. Two free services of government hospitals
Free use of ambulance and free medicines.
The doctors are able to respond to and cure all types of diseases. Most of them are specialists in the field of medicine.
It is prohibited to reject patients. The city mayor issues a directive to accept all patients, especially indigents or the poor, those who cannot afford medical treatment in private hospitals.
Free medicine, free check-up, and free operation (cataract and cleft palate).

lessons.title: 272. C15 L1 · A blog on sickness, doctors and traditional healers
lessons.subtitle: Madalas magkasakit ang maraming Pilipino · Umaasa sa albularyo o hilot · Nabati, nausog, naengkanto

explanations.title: Presentation 2: blog exchanges
explanations.body: Blog comments about medical services and traditional medical practices in the Philippines. The book prints “mga 2-3 beses” as figures and quotation marks around naengkanto, nabati and nausog; the spoken text has words and no quotation marks, and “nabati or nausog” is “nabati o nausog.”

examples.text: Madalas magkasakit, magka-dengue, magkatigdas, magka-TB, at magka-pulmonya ang maraming Pilipino. Ito ang mga karaniwang sakit na naitatala taun-taon. Nakakalungkot nga lang dahil malaki ang kakulangan ng mga duktor sa Pilipinas lalo na sa mga kanayunan. ’Yung mga midwife naman, kadalasan mga dalawa hanggang tatlong beses lang bumibisita sa mga health centers tuwing linggo. Sa amin nga hindi ko alam kung kailan kami magkaka-ospital.
examples.translation: Blogger: Many Filipinos often get sick, get dengue, measles, TB and pneumonia. These are the common diseases recorded every year. It is sad, though, that there is a big shortage of doctors in the Philippines, especially in the countryside. As for the midwives, they usually visit the health centers only about two to three times a week. In our place, I don’t know when we will have a hospital.

examples.text: Kaya nga umaasa na lang ang maraming mahihirap na Pilipino sa mga albularyo o hilot.
examples.translation: Reply 1: That is why many poor Filipinos just depend on herb healers or traditional massage healers.

examples.text: May mga sakit din naman kasi na hindi maipaliwanag. Sabi nga ng mga matatanda, yun bang mga naengkanto o nabati o nausog. Mabuti na lang nga at nandiyan ang PITAHC. Isinusulong nito ang pagbibigay ng pangangalagang pangkalusugan gamit ang tradisyonal at alternatibong medisina na garantisadong ligtas, abot-kaya, at epektibo.
examples.translation: Reply 2: There are also illnesses that cannot be explained. As the elders say, those who were enchanted or nabati or nausog. It is good that PITAHC is there. It promotes giving health care using traditional and alternative medicine that is guaranteed safe, affordable and effective.

explanations.title: Note: barangay health centers
explanations.body: Barangay health centers are community-based centers responsible for healthcare services at the primary level. Most medicine is free, and there is a drug subsidy for expensive medications such as antibiotics and pain killers. Challenges that face many barangay health centers include unavailability of medical staff, inadequate facilities, and insufficient supplies of medicine.

explanations.title: Culture note
explanations.body: Nabati or nausog refers to the cause of an infant or toddler’s illness when it is praised as “cute, pretty, chubby, and the like.” Naengkanto (charm, spell) refers to an illness believed to be caused by supernatural beings. Teacher note: explain and give examples of naengkanto, nabati or nausog.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: a. PITAHC stands for the Philippine Institute of Traditional and Alternative Health Care. It provides safe, effective and affordable traditional and alternative health care products, services and technologies. (The book’s note prints PITACH; the text says PITAHC.) b. In reply 2, line 1, maipaliwanag is a mai able verb. Other examples are maipakita, maipasa and maipasyal. c. In reply 2, line 3, pangangalagang pangkalusugan means “health care.” The book says magkatigdas is “German measles”; tigdas is measles.

rows: to be afflicted with dengue disease

explanations.title: Comprehension check (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Summarize the blogger’s comments and the two responses.

rows: Filipinos often get sick in general and develop illnesses such as dengue fever, measles, and TB. These are common illnesses recorded annually. However, it is disheartening that there are not enough doctors in the provinces. As for midwives, they only report 2 to 3 times a week in health centers.
That is why the majority of poor Filipinos rely on an herb healer or medicine man.

There are actually illnesses that cannot be explained. As older people would say, “There are those who were nabati or naengkanto.” It is good that the government established the Philippine Institute of Traditional and Alternative Health Care (PITAHC). It is providing healthcare using traditional and alternative medicines that are guaranteed safe, affordable, and effective.

explanations.title: Activity 1: a blog posted on the DOH page (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Read the blog and give 5 EEIs. The blog itself is an image in the book, so only the key is given here:

rows: The blogger complains about General Aguinaldo Memorial Hospital in Trece Martirez, Cavite City.
The wards or rooms of patients are too crowded.
The processing of papers for the release of patients is too slow.
Three to four mothers have to cram in a single bed with their newborn babies.
Mothers giving birth by CS (Caesarean section) have difficulty because their mobility is limited.
The blogger asks the DOH to help by visiting the hospital.

explanations.title: Magkaroon
explanations.body: Magkaroon means “to have,” “to get,” “to acquire,” or “to come into possession of something.” Usually it is placed before a noun indicating what it purports to express as “to have.” It has the same meaning as may or mayroon (as the verb to have) that you learned in Chapter 6, Lesson 3. Magka + noun is the short form of magkaroon.

explanations.title: A. Forming phrases and words with magkaroon
explanations.body: Formula: magkaroon + article ng + noun, or magka + noun.

explanations.title: Sentences from the reading presentation

examples.text: Sa amin nga hindi ko alam kung kailan kami magkaka-ospital.
examples.translation: In our place, indeed, we do not know when we will have a hospital.

explanations.title: B. Conjugation
explanations.body: Magkaroon is conjugated like a mag verb. The gerund form is pagkakaroon.

explanations.title: D. Use of hindi with magkaroon
explanations.body: To negate, simply add the word hindi before the word magkaroon. The root words are ones you have learned.

lessons.title: 274. C15 L1 · Magkaroon is doer-focus; practice
lessons.subtitle: Nagkasakit ang mga bata · Magkakaroon uli ng health center · Itanong natin kung magkakaroon tayo ng pagkakataon

explanations.title: C. Magkaroon, a doer-focus verb
explanations.body: Magkaroon is doer-focus. The doer in the sentence is either a Set 1 pronoun or a noun marked by Set 1 markers. The direct object of the verb uses a Set 2 pronoun or marker. Set 1 pronouns: ako, ikaw or ka, siya, tayo, kami, kayo, sila. Set 2: ko, mo, niya, natin, namin, ninyo, nila. Set 1 markers: si, ang (singular); sina, ang mga (plural). Set 2 markers: ni, ng (singular); nina, ng mga (plural).

explanations.title: Activity 2: complete with the correct markers (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Key: 1) ang mga 2) ng 3) ng 4) si 5) ng; ang or ang mga 6) ng or ng mga 7) sina 8) ng. The book prints typos (art for at, naming for namin, a comma for a period). The completed sentences:

examples.translation: There will again be a health center in our village in the coming year.

explanations.title: Activity 3: select the magka or magkaroon verb and its tense (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Key: 1. magkasakit (infinitive) 2. magkakaroon (future) 3. magkakabadyet (future) 4. nagkalisensiya (past).

examples.text: Baka magkasakit tayo.
examples.translation: We might get sick.

examples.text: Magkakaroon daw ng bagong inspeksiyon.
examples.translation: They say there will be a new inspection.

examples.text: Hindi pa rin siguro magkakabadyet para sa isa pang emergency room, ano?
examples.translation: There probably still won’t be a budget for another emergency room, right?

examples.text: Nagkalisensiya na rin sa wakas ang mga nakapasa sa medical board.
examples.translation: Those who passed the medical board finally got their license too.

explanations.title: Activity 4: write the correct form of magkaroon (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Key: 1) Magkakaroon 2) magkakaroon or nagkaroon 3) Magkakaroon or Nagkakaroon 4) magkaroon 5) magkaroon 6) magkaroon or magkakaroon 7) magkakaroon. The book prints kimabukasan in item 5; it is kinabukasan. The completed sentences:

examples.translation: They say there will be a new clinic beside our building in a year.

examples.text: Alam ba ninyo kung kailan magkakaroon ng bahay ang mga Manalo?
examples.translation: Do you know when the Manalos will have a house?

examples.text: Magkakaroon ng problema sa kakulangan ng manggagamot sa bansa ngayong mga panahong ito.
examples.translation: There will be a problem with the shortage of healers in the country in these times.

examples.text: Dapat nga kayong magkaroon ng bagong laboratoryo sa ospital?
examples.translation: You really should have a new laboratory in the hospital?

examples.text: May mga taong gustong magkaroon ng magandang kinabukasan, pero ayaw namang magsikap.
examples.translation: Some people want to have a good future but don’t want to make an effort.

examples.text: Baka magkaroon na raw ng mas mahusay na X-ray machine sa ospital natin sa susunod na taon.
examples.translation: They say we might have a better X-ray machine in our hospital next year.

examples.text: Itanong natin sa kanila kung magkakaroon tayo ng pagkakataong magtanong bago tayo umalis.
examples.translation: Let’s ask them whether we will have a chance to ask questions before we leave.

lessons.title: 275. C15 L1 · Health budget numbers and cheap medicine
lessons.subtitle: Dalawa punto walong bilyon pesos · Murang gamot sa mga ospital at health centers · Hindi dapat isinusugal ang kalusugan

explanations.title: Activity 6: number transcription and gisting (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Listen to excerpts of a documentary about a government initiative, transcribe the numbers in figures, and give the gist. The book prints the numbers as figures; in the spoken text they are in words. Source: ptvnews.ph. The book’s gist: this passage is about what Recto said about the health budget. P2.8 billion was set aside for family health and responsible parenting. This will benefit the poor and also give work to 131 doctors, 22,500 contractual nurses, and 3,000 midwives who will be assigned to health centers and barrios. The government aims to address the needs of 962 barangay health stations, 1,265 provincial health centers, 561 hospitals under the local government, and 60 hospitals under the Dept. of Health.

examples.text: Dagdag pa ni Recto, kabilang sa nilaan na pondong pangkalusugan ng pamahalaan ay ang dalawa punto walong bilyon pesos para sa family health and responsible parenting.
examples.translation: Recto added that among the government’s health funds set aside is 2.8 billion pesos for family health and responsible parenting.

examples.text: Maliban sa mga benepisyong makukuha ng mahihirap nating mga kababayan sa Department of Health, mabibigyan din ng trabaho ang isang daan at tatlumpu’t isang doktor at dalawampu’t dalawang libo at limang daang contractual nurses kasama ng tatlong libong midwives na ma-a-assign sa mga baryo o health centers sa iba’t-ibang panig ng Pilipinas.
examples.translation: Besides the benefits our poor countrymen can get from the Department of Health, 131 doctors and 22,500 contractual nurses will also be given work, along with 3,000 midwives who will be assigned to barrios or health centers in different parts of the Philippines.

examples.text: Layunin ng pangkalusugang pondong nilaan ng pamahalaan ang matugunan ang pangangailangan ng siyam na raan at animnapu’t dalawang barangay health stations, isang libo dalawang daan at animnapu’t limang health centers sa probinsiya, limang daan at animnapu’t isang hospital sa pamamahala ng local governments at animnapung hospital sa ilalim ng Department of Health.
examples.translation: The aim of the government’s health fund is to meet the needs of 962 barangay health stations, 1,265 health centers in the provinces, 561 hospitals under local governments and 60 hospitals under the Department of Health.

rows: hospitals under the Department of Health

explanations.title: Activity 7: a news report on cheap medicine
explanations.body: Read the excerpt and translate the underlined sentences; the book underlines the parts keyed below. Source: philstar.com. The book’s (1) to (4) markers are left out of the spoken text.

examples.text: Magkakaroon na ang mga mahihirap at senior citizen sa Maynila ng mga gamot at direkta na ngayon mabibili sa mga ospital at health centers ang mga mura at de kalidad na gamot.
examples.translation: The poor and senior citizens in Manila will now have medicines, and inexpensive, good-quality medicines can now be bought directly at hospitals and health centers.

examples.text: Ito ang ipinahayag nina Manila Mayor Alfredo Lim at Senator Mar Roxas sa pagbisita ng huli sa tanggapan ng alkalde kaugnay na rin ng pagsusulong ng murang gamot.
examples.translation: This was announced by Manila Mayor Alfredo Lim and Senator Mar Roxas during the latter’s visit to the mayor’s office, also in relation to the promotion of inexpensive medicine.

examples.text: Ayon kay Roxas, nakipag-ugnayan siya kay Lim upang mabigyan ng pagkakataon ang mga mahihirap at senior citizen na mabili ang kanilang mga kailangang gamot na nagsisilbing mga maintenance sa mga sakit tulad ng diabetes o high blood.
examples.translation: According to Roxas, he coordinated with Lim to give the poor and senior citizens a chance to buy the medicines they need that serve as maintenance for illnesses like diabetes or high blood.

examples.text: Anya, dito lamang sa bansa sobra ang mahal ng gamot kung saan tatlong doble ang kita ng mga kompanya ng gamot.
examples.translation: He said it is only in this country that medicine is far too expensive, where drug companies earn triple.

examples.text: Hindi umano dapat na isinusugal ang kalusugan dahil na rin sa mahal ng gamot.
examples.translation: They say health should not be gambled with because medicine is expensive.

rows: can be directly bought now at the hospitals and health centers
in relation also to the promotion of inexpensive drugs or medicines
serves as maintenance for diseases like diabetes or high blood
they say one’s health should not be placed in jeopardy also because of expensive medicine
