explanations.title: Activity 8: quality hospitals (the book’s passage and key)
explanations.body: Source: doh.gov.ph. The key: 1. There are quality hospitals in Metro Manila. 2. Four hospitals in Metro Manila received international accreditation. 3. They are Makati Medical Center, Medical City in Pasig City, St. Luke’s Medical Center in Quezon City, and Chong Hua Hospital in Cebu. 4. There are also specialized hospitals such as the Lung Center of the Philippines, the Philippine Heart Center, the National Kidney and Transplant Institute, and the Philippine Children’s Medical Center. 5. The law prohibits collecting fees from patients in advance, as a condition of medical treatment.

examples.text: Maraming de-kalidad na hospital sa Kalakhang Maynila.
examples.translation: There are many quality hospitals in Metro Manila.

examples.text: Apat sa mga ospital na ito ang nakatanggap ng internasyonal na akreditasyon.
examples.translation: Four of these hospitals received international accreditation.

examples.text: Iginawad ito ng Joint Commission International dahil sa pagbibigay ng de-kalidad na serbisyo sa mga pasyenteng Pilipino.
examples.translation: The Joint Commission International granted it for giving quality service to Filipino patients.

examples.text: Ang mga ito ay ang Makati Medical Center, Medical City sa lungsod ng Pasig, St. Luke’s Medical Center sa lungsod ng Quezon, at Chong Hua Hospital sa Cebu.
examples.translation: These are Makati Medical Center, Medical City in Pasig City, St. Luke’s Medical Center in Quezon City, and Chong Hua Hospital in Cebu.

examples.text: Meron ding mga ospital na may serbisyong pinagkakadalubhasaan tulad ng Lung Center of the Philippines, Philippine Heart Center, National Kidney and Transplant Institute, at Philippine Children’s Medical Center.
examples.translation: There are also hospitals with specialized services such as the Lung Center of the Philippines, Philippine Heart Center, National Kidney and Transplant Institute, and Philippine Children’s Medical Center.

examples.text: Ipinagbabawal ng batas ang pagsingil sa mga pasyente bago mabigyan ng kaukulang serbisyong medikal.
examples.translation: The law prohibits charging patients before they are given the corresponding medical service.

explanations.title: Activity 9: government-owned hospitals in Manila (the book’s scripts)
explanations.body: The book’s key: Passage 1: the Manila Hospital has three ambulances, which patients can use for free; the ambulance picks up the patient and takes the patient home for free. Passage 2: Tondo Hospital is free for Manila residents only; however, the Mayor issued a directive to accept non-residents. Passage 3: the passage describes the hospital’s emergency room; the illnesses and emergencies mentioned are stab wounds, gun-shot wounds, heart attack, stomach ache, and high fever. The book’s “…” is a comma here.

examples.text: Ang Ospital po ng Maynila ay mayroong tatlong ambulansya, at ito po ay ibinibigay po nating libre sa paggamit sa ating mga pasyente. At kahit po sila ay pauwi na, ito po ay inihahatid ng ating mga ambulansya at libre po itong ibinibigay. Kung mangangailangan po ang ating mga kababayan sa Maynila, pupuntahan po namin at susunduin namin ang inyong pasyente.
examples.translation: Passage 1: Ospital ng Maynila has three ambulances, and we give them free for the use of our patients. Even when they are going home, our ambulances take them home and it is given for free. If our countrymen in Manila need it, we will go and pick up your patient.

examples.text: Ang Ospital ng Tondo ay para lang sa mga taga-Maynila. Pero may direktiba ang ating Mayor na kahit hindi taga-Maynila ay inyong tanggapin. Wala kami ditong tinatanggihan. As a public servant, iyon ang aming misyon. Ang Ospital ng Tondo ay taos puso at labis na nagpapasalamat sa ating Mayor, na walang iniisip kundi ang kabutihan ng nakararaming Manileño, lalung-lalo na ang mahihirap. Magpapatuloy pa po, muli, ang aming paglilingkod sa inyo.
examples.translation: Passage 2: Tondo Hospital is only for Manila residents. But our Mayor has a directive that even those not from Manila should be accepted. We reject no one here. As a public servant, that is our mission. Tondo Hospital sincerely and deeply thanks our Mayor, who thinks of nothing but the good of the majority of Manileños, especially the poor. Our service to you will continue again.

examples.text: Sa unang palapag ng ospital ay makikita natin ang emergency room. Dito ay walang patid ang pagpasok, labas, ng mga pasyente na merong mga problema at kailangang malutasan kaagad. Wala pong ginagasta ang mga taong nagpupunta sa emergency room. Dito po yung mga nasaksak, nabaril, inatake sa puso, masakit ang tiyan, mataas na lagnat, lahat po ng uri ng problema ay tinutugunan ng mga doktor dito na pawang mga espesyalista sa iba’t-ibang larangan ng medisina.
examples.translation: Passage 3: On the first floor of the hospital we can see the emergency room. Here patients with problems that need to be solved right away come in and out without stopping. The people who go to the emergency room spend nothing. Here are those who were stabbed, shot, had a heart attack, have a stomach ache, high fever, all kinds of problems are addressed by the doctors here, who are all specialists in different fields of medicine.

explanations.title: Activity 10: a news report on a medical mission (the book’s script and key)
explanations.body: Key: 1. A medical mission was conducted in a barangay in Caloocan City. 2. About 500 residents from Barangay 101 benefited, and residents from nearby barangays too. 3. Free check-up and free medicines. 4. The group Tao Muna and the local government of Caloocan City.

examples.text: Isang medical mission ang isinagawa sa isang barangay sa Caloocan City.
examples.translation: A medical mission was conducted in a barangay in Caloocan City.

examples.text: Aabot sa limang daang mga residente mula sa Barangay isang daan at isa at maging sa mga kalapit-barangay ang naserbisyuhan ng nasabing medical mission.
examples.translation: Up to five hundred residents from Barangay 101 and even from nearby barangays were served by the said medical mission.

examples.text: Libreng check-up at gamot ang ipinagkaloob na tulong sa mga dumalo sa nasabing medical mission.
examples.translation: Free check-up and medicine were the help given to those who attended the said medical mission.

examples.text: Ang medical mission ay isa lamang sa mga outreach programs ng grupong Tao Muna at ng lokal na pamahalaan ng Caloocan.
examples.translation: The medical mission is only one of the outreach programs of the group Tao Muna and the local government of Caloocan.

explanations.title: Activity 11, segment 1: an interview with a hospital administrator
explanations.body: The book’s key: the interviewer introduced the administrator of the Lung Center of the Philippines, Dr. Nestor F. Venida. She said that LCP is one institution serving those who suffer from lung disease, especially those who couldn’t afford to seek treatment in private hospitals. The book’s script misspells Philippines in one place.

examples.text: Ngayon naman Sandro, alam naman natin, ang Lung Center of the Philippines ay isa pong institusyon na siyang umaalalay sa ating mga kababayan na may sakit sa baga, lalo na doon sa mga walang kakayahang magpagamot sa mga pribadong ospital. Kaya naman, this morning, para bigyan pa tayo ng detalye at impormasyon tungkol diyan, makakasama natin mula sa Lung Center of the Philippines ang kanilang Administrator, si Dr. Nestor F. Venida. Good morning, Doc.
examples.translation: Woman: Now, Sandro, we know that the Lung Center of the Philippines is an institution that supports our countrymen with lung disease, especially those who cannot afford treatment in private hospitals. So this morning, to give us more detail and information about that, joining us from the Lung Center of the Philippines is its Administrator, Dr. Nestor F. Venida. Good morning, Doc.

examples.text: Hi, Good morning sa inyong lahat.
examples.translation: Dr. Venida: Hi, good morning to all of you.

explanations.title: Activity 11, segment 2
explanations.body: The book’s key: Dr. Venida explains the type of services offered by LCP. He said the LCP Outpatient Department is giving free consultation. Other free services include confinement, surgery, special procedures, and laboratory work. He said LCP has the means or technologies and various kinds of medicines for free.

examples.text: Sir, ito naman po. Ano naman po yung klase ng tulong na naibibigay po ninyo sa Lung Center sa mga iba’t-ibang problema po ng ating mamamayan, mga kababayan natin.
examples.translation: Sandro: Sir, now this. What kind of help can you give at the Lung Center for the different problems of our citizens, our countrymen?

examples.text: Sa Lung Center, nagbibigay kami ng mga libreng pagsusuri sa Outpatient Department. Meron, siyempre kino-confine din namin yung mga kailangang i-confine. Kung kailangang operahin, ooperahin, kung may mga laboratories na kailangang gawin. Aaa, binibigay natin na libre. Kung mangangailangan silang merong mga special procedures na gawin, ginagawa rin natin. Meron tayong mga paraan, o kaya mga teknolohiya, at saka yung mga iba’t-ibang uri ng gamot na puwede, puwede nating ibigay sa kanila.
examples.translation: Dr. Venida: At the Lung Center, we give free check-ups at the Outpatient Department. There is, of course, we also confine those who need to be confined. If they need an operation, we will operate, if there are laboratories that need to be done. Um, we give them free. If they need special procedures done, we do those too. We have means, or technologies, and the different kinds of medicine we can give them.

explanations.title: Activity 12: interview with a DOH spokesperson
explanations.body: Pair up. You are interviewing a spokesperson of the Department of Health about the department’s modernization program. Using the text below, focus your questions on the number of medical centers nationwide to benefit, the total budget allocated, bed capacity, and the number of health facilities given assistance between 2010 and 2013. Your partner plays the spokesperson. Use the usual courtesy to start and end the conversation and the question words ano, sino, kailan, gaano katagal, sinu-sino and bakit, as appropriate. The book’s text (English, from The Philippine Star, 22 September 2013):

explanations.title: The article for Activity 12
explanations.body: 25 hospitals to benefit from DOH modernization program. By Sheila Crosostomo (The Philippine Star). MANILA, Philippines: Three public hospitals in Cagayan Valley, Bicol and Cotabato City were among the 25 medical centers nationwide to benefit from the P1.03-B modernization program of the Department of Health (DOH). The project is part of an ongoing program that ensures the primary, secondary and tertiary care programs of the DOH become available to all, according to Health Secretary Enrique Ona. The Health chief said 25 DOH hospitals were targeted for modernization under the term of Pres. Aquino. On Thursday, the DOH signed a contract for the project that will benefit the Cagayan Valley Medical Center (CVMC), Bicol Medical Center and Cotabato Regional Medical Center (CRMC). Under the project, a new five-story building will be constructed at the CVMC while its bed capacity will increase by 300 beds. The CRMC will have a new four-story building that will increase its bed capacity by 500, while an eight-story main hospital building was proposed for the BMC. DOH Undersecretary Ted Herbosa said the budget for the projects would come from the agency’s 2012 General Appropriation Act. DOH records showed that from 2010 to 2013, HFEP had spent some P33 billion for 4,518 health facilities, mostly under the supervision of the LGUs. HFEP funding has increased by 317 percent or from P3.25 billion in 2010 to P13.56 billion this year.

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: By the end of this lesson you can extract information from reading and listening passages about common diseases, symptoms and preventions; formulate and answer simple questions about them; and transcribe and translate phrases and sentences containing related vocabulary. The structures are the core vocabulary and the um verbs for bodily motions, functions and emotions.

explanations.title: Getting started
explanations.body: The book shows common diseases in the Philippines with their symptoms and asks whether you know other symptoms; students write them on the smartboard. (The pictures are left out.)

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: a. In paragraph 1, line 5, sakit is the root word of pananakit. b. In paragraph 2, line 4, pinaglalagyan ng tubig means “a place where water is stored.” c. In paragraph 2, lines 4 and 5, para hindi mapangitlugan at pagbahayan ng mga lamok means “so that the mosquitoes will not lay eggs or breed (in the containers with standing water).”

explanations.title: New words
explanations.body: The book prints paborito(ng); the linker ng is added when it modifies a noun.

rows: 1. Two common diseases during the rainy season
Leptospirosis is a disease caused by the leptospira virus. It is transmitted when water that has been contaminated by rat urine comes in contact with cuts or open wounds on a person’s legs or feet.
4. Three other body parts affected by the virus
High fever that lasts until seven days, muscle and joint pains, weakening (of the body or immune system), and rashes.

explanations.title: Activity 1: information about dengue (source: doh.gov.ph)
explanations.body: Read the information and fill in the table. The book shows the filled table as a picture; its content is given here.

rows: Transmitted to humans through the bites of mosquitoes carrying the dengue virus.
High fever within 2 to 7 days; muscle and joint pain; weakening of the body; loss of appetite; skin rash (reddening of the skin); abdominal pain and vomiting; nosebleed and bleeding gums.

Clean and cover drums and other water containers. Turn bottles, tin cans, and other water containers that could be a breeding ground for mosquitoes upside down. Wear long clothing to avoid being easily bitten by mosquitoes. Use insect repellent. Go to a health center and have yourself checked. Do the 4 o’clock habit every day.

lessons.title: 280. C15 L2 · Intransitive um verbs for bodily motions and emotions
lessons.subtitle: Sumuka, dumugo, huminga, umihi · Um bilang unlapi at gitlapi · Paglusong, pagsakit, paghinga

explanations.title: Intransitive UM- verbs for bodily motions, functions and emotions
explanations.body: You have learned several uses of um verbs in Chapters 5, 7 and 11: giving directions (kumaliwa, lumiko, tumawid), weather conditions or acts of nature (bumagyo, umulan, sumikat ang araw) and natural disasters (bumaha, lumindol, pumutok ang bulkan). In this lesson you learn um verbs relating to bodily functions and emotions.

explanations.title: A. Identifying um verbs (sentences from the reading)
explanations.body: Find the um verbs in the sentences below. The book’s key: lumusong, sumasakit, sumuka, dumugo, huminga, umihi, tumae, umubo, suminga, bumahing.

examples.text: Kapag ang isang taong may sugat sa binti at paa ay lumusong sa tubig baha, doon papasok ang virus at makakaranas siya ng lagnat at iba pang sintomas.
examples.translation: When a person who has wounds on his legs and feet steps into flood waters, the virus will enter there and he will experience fever and other symptoms.

examples.text: Ate, sumasakit ang tiyan ni Tatay.
examples.translation: Ate, Father’s stomach is aching. Or: Ate, Father has a stomach ache.

examples.text: Sumuka siya kanina.
examples.translation: He threw up earlier.

examples.text: Tapos ngayon, dumugo naman ang ilong at gilagid niya.
examples.translation: Afterwards, his nose and gums bled.

examples.text: Hirap daw po siyang huminga.
examples.translation: He has difficulty in breathing.

examples.text: Hindi ba nahirapang umihi o tumae si Tatay?
examples.translation: Isn’t Father having a difficult time in urinating and defecating?

examples.text: Sabihin mo na takpan niya ang bibig niya kapag umubo, suminga, o bumahing.
examples.translation: Tell him to cover his mouth while coughing, blowing one’s nose, or sneezing.

explanations.title: Intransitive and transitive
explanations.body: The um verb in this usage is usually intransitive, that is, it does not need a direct object: lumusong sa tubig-baha (to go into floodwaters). Occasionally you see a transitive verb: uminom ng Paracetamol (to take Paracetamol). Uminom, which literally means “to drink,” is used in the context of taking medicine.

explanations.title: B. Um as a prefix and an infix
explanations.body: As you learned in your previous lesson, um is both a prefix (affixed to the beginning of a word) and an infix (affixed in the middle of a word), but never a suffix. If the root begins with a vowel, um is a prefix; if it begins with a consonant, um goes after that first consonant.

explanations.title: C. Um verb, a doer-focus
explanations.body: An um verb is doer-focus. The doer in the sentence is either a Set 1 pronoun or a noun marked by Set 1 markers. The direct object uses a Set 2 pronoun or marker.

explanations.title: Persons and things
explanations.body: Si, sina, ni and nina are used for persons; ang, ang mga, ng and ng mga are used for all other nouns.

explanations.title: D. Conjugation of um verbs
explanations.body: Regardless of usage, um verbs have the same conjugation. The last four rows were left to complete in the book; they are given here.

explanations.title: E. The gerund form of um verbs
explanations.body: Formula: pag + root word. The gerund is hyphenated when the root word begins with a vowel. The first column of the book’s table was done for you; the rest are completed here (my key for the ones the book left blank).

Those marked with an asterisk in the book (umibig, umawit, lumulon and umisip) can be used as transitive verbs, that is, verbs that require a direct object. explanations.title: Activity 5: a news report on measles (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Transcribe, translate and give the gist. The book prints the numbers as figures (Region 11, labing-apat, apatanapu); the spoken text writes them in words. Source: PTVnews.ph. The book’s printed key for item 1 (“Many of the women’s health needs were met”) belongs to a different passage; the translation of item 1 below is mine.

examples.text: Nakaalerto ngayon ang Department of Health sa Region labing-isa.
examples.translation: The Department of Health in Region 11 is on alert now.

examples.text: Ito’y dahil sa biglang pagtaas ng kaso ng tigdas sa Davao City kung saan ay labing-apat na ang kumpirmadong tinamaan ng naturang sakit habang apatnapu pa ang patuloy na minomonitor.
examples.translation: This is because of the sudden rise in measles cases in Davao City, where fourteen are already confirmed to have been hit by the said disease while forty more continue to be monitored.

examples.text: Ayon kay DOH Region labing-isa Director Abdullah Dumama Jr., ang bilang na ito ay nakakaalarma dahil mataas ang bilang na ito kumpara sa mga nakaraang taon.
examples.translation: According to DOH Region 11 Director Abdullah Dumama Jr., this number is alarming because it is high compared with previous years.

explanations.title: Activity 5: the gist (the book’s key)
explanations.body: This passage is about the Department of Health Region 11’s warning to the public that measles is on the rise in Davao City where 40 people are sick with measles. They continue to monitor due to the increase in numbers who got sick from last year.

explanations.title: Activity 6: a news report on cholera (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Give four EEIs. Source: PTVnews.ph.

examples.text: Sa iba pang balita, muling nagbabala ang Department of Health sa sakit na kolera.
examples.translation: In other news, the Department of Health again warned about the disease cholera.

examples.text: Kaugnay nito, walo na ang kompirmadong nasawi sa Alamada, North Cotabato dahil sa kolera.
examples.translation: In connection with this, eight deaths are already confirmed in Alamada, North Cotabato because of cholera.

examples.text: Babala ng DOH sa publiko maging maingat sa iniinom na tubig.
examples.translation: The DOH warns the public to be careful about the water they drink.

examples.text: Samantala, nagpadala na ng mga tauhan ang ahensiya sa Alamada upang tumulong sa lokal na pamahalaan sa pagsusuri at pagbabantay sa mga residente.
examples.translation: Meanwhile, the agency has already sent personnel to Alamada to help the local government in examining and monitoring the residents.

rows: The Department of Health once again warned about cholera.
8 deaths so far in Alamada, North Cotabato were confirmed.
The DOH warned the public to be careful with their drinking water.
Personnel were sent to Alamada to help the local government in examining and monitoring the residents.

explanations.title: Activity 7: a health advisory poster (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Source: doh.gov.ph. The poster is a picture in the book; only the questions and the key are given here.

rows: The germs enter the skin that has a wound from the flood waters, wet ground, or plants that have a rat’s contaminated urine.
(1) Fever; (2) chills; (3) muscle or head aches; (4) red eyes; (5) yellow skin; (6) urine that has tea color; (7) small amount of urine; (8) intense headaches.
3. Four ways of avoiding or controlling the disease

(1) Avoid swimming or walking in contaminated flood waters or dirty water; (2) use boots if you need to walk in flood waters; (3) exterminate the rats at home; (4) maintain cleanliness in the whole house.

lessons.title: 283. C15 L2 · Listening scripts: dengue, leptospirosis and measles
lessons.subtitle: Doblehin ang pag-iingat laban sa dengue · Huwag lumangoy, lumusong, at maglaro sa baha · Walang gamot, bakuna lang

explanations.title: Activity 8: a news report on dengue (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Two segments. Source: a YouTube news report. Teacher note: repeat the audio as needed.

examples.text: Muling nagpaalala ang Department of Health sa publiko na doblehin ang pag-iingat laban sa dengue lalo na ngayong El Nino. Ayon kay Secretary Janet Garin, kahit na mababa ang bilang ng kaso ng dengue ngayong taon kumpara nang nakaraang taon ay posibleng tumaas pa ito sa pagpasok ng tagtuyot.
examples.translation: Segment 1: Again the Department of Health reminded the public to double their precaution against dengue, especially during this El Nino. According to Secretary Janet Garin, even though the number of dengue cases this year is low compared to last year, it could still rise with the coming of the dry spell.

examples.text: Paliwanag ng kalihim dahil sa matinding tagtuyot, nag-iimbak ng tubig ang taong-bayan kung saan madalas itong pangitlugan at pagbahayan ng mga lamok. Kaya naman nagpaalala ang ahensiya sa mga mag-iimbak ng tubig na siguruhing laging may takip ang kanilang pinaglalagyan ng tubig at panatilihin ang malinis na kapaligiran para maiwasan ang pagkakaroon ng dengue.
examples.translation: Segment 2: The secretary explained that because of the severe dry spell, the people store water, where mosquitoes often lay eggs and breed. So the agency reminded those who will store water to make sure that their water container always has a cover and to keep a clean environment to avoid getting dengue.

rows: 1. The DOH’s reminder to the public
To take extra precaution against dengue especially this coming El Nino season.
2. Dengue cases this year compared to last year (2 details)
The dengue case this year is lower compared to last year. However, this will possibly increase because of the coming El Nino.
3. The contributing factor that may increase dengue
The secretary said that during El Nino, people store water which usually becomes a breeding ground for mosquitoes.
Make sure to cover the containers where water is stored and maintain clean surroundings.

explanations.title: Activity 9: a health advisory (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Two segments, from PTV Disaster Watch. The book’s dash after “leptospirosis” is a comma here.

examples.text: Mga paghahanda laban sa sakit ngayong tag-ulan. Iwasan ang leptospirosis. Huwag lumangoy, lumusong, at maglaro sa baha. Gumamit ng bota kung talagang kailangan lumusong. At kapag mataas na ang tubig-baha, sumakay sa mga improvised floating devices o rubber boats kung lilikas ng bahay.
examples.translation: Segment 1: Preparations against diseases this rainy season. Avoid leptospirosis. Do not swim, wade, or play in the flood. Use boots if you really need to wade. And when the floodwater is already high, ride improvised floating devices or rubber boats if you will evacuate the house.

examples.text: Mga palatandaan o sintomas ng leptospirosis, lagnat, panginginig ng katawan o chills, pananakit ng ulo, binti, kalamnan, at kasu-kasuan, pamumula ng mga mata, paninilaw ng balat, at nahihirapang pag-ihi. Kung patuloy ang lagnat sa loob nang dalawang araw, agad nang kumonsulta sa doktor.
examples.translation: Segment 2: Signs or symptoms of leptospirosis: fever, chills, pain in the head, legs, muscles and joints, redness of the eyes, yellowing of the skin, and difficulty urinating. If the fever continues for two days, consult a doctor right away.

rows: The health advisory is about the things to do against disease (leptospirosis) this rainy season.
During rainy season, don’t swim; get into; and play into the flood waters.
Using boots when getting into the water becomes a necessity. When flood waters rise, ride onto improvised floating devices or rubber boats to evacuate.
Fever, chills, headache, leg/muscle and joint pains, red eyes, yellow skin (jaundice), labored urination.

explanations.title: Activity 10: an interview with Dr. Olarte, President of the Philippine Medical Association
explanations.body: Two segments; give the gist. The book’s “…” and “ma…” stumbles are dropped and “(Manila)” is written “sa Manila.”

examples.text: So, sir ano po ba ’yung mga factors kung bakit po nagkakaroon ng measles outbreak?
examples.translation: Host: So, sir, what are the factors why there is a measles outbreak?

examples.text: Well, ang una, is malamig ang panahon. And second is, bago lang tayo nakaranas sa Super Typhoon Yolanda na grabe yung pagkasira ng ating mga environment. At ang ating mga kababayan nasalanta sila. Nawalan sila ng mga tahanan, humina ang kanilang kalusugan. Ang karamihan din sa kanila nagpunta dito sa Metro Manila. So, nagkumpul-kumpol sila sa isang lugar. ’Yung iba naman may mga ubo na galing sa Visayas dito din sa Manila may ubo. So ’yan ay one of the many factors that contributed to the outbreak of measles.
examples.translation: Guest: Well, first, the weather is cold. And second, we just experienced Super Typhoon Yolanda, whose destruction of our environment was severe. And our countrymen were devastated. They lost their homes, their health weakened. Most of them also came here to Metro Manila. So they crowded together in one place. Some of them also have coughs that came from the Visayas, and here in Manila too there is a cough. So that is one of the many factors that contributed to the outbreak of measles.

examples.text: So ito naman siguro para sa ating mga manonood ngayon, ’yung symptoms ba ng measles, ano ba ’to? Gaano kabilis natin nararamdaman ’to para ma-confirm natin na may measles tayo at meron bang kumbaga mga preventive measures, kumbaga may nararamdaman ako ngayong kaunti, meron bang dapat na medicine na puwede ko nang i-take para kumbaga maiwasan ’to o ano po ba dapat ang ginagawa natin?
examples.translation: Host: So this is perhaps for our viewers now: what are the symptoms of measles? How quickly do we feel it so that we can confirm we have measles, and are there, so to speak, preventive measures? I feel a little something now; is there a medicine I can already take to prevent it, or what should we do?

examples.text: Wala talagang medicine para maiwasan natin. Ang talagang kuwan diyan e, mass immunization, vaccination no, to prevent the measles no. Now, ang ating prevention diyan is huwag tayong lumapit sa mga pasyente or mga kaibigan natin na umuubo o merong sintoma na nilalagnat sila ’no? Iwasan natin sila. Ang measles ay nakukuha sa hangin. Halimbawa, sila ay umubo, o suminga, uhm, wag tayong lumapit diyan. At sana’y ’tong mga tao natin, itong mga kababayan natin wag umubo na hindi naman tinatakpan ang kanilang bibig at saka huwag mag-sneeze ’no.
examples.translation: Guest: There is really no medicine for us to prevent it. What is really key there is mass immunization, vaccination, to prevent the measles. Now, our prevention there is not to go near patients or friends who are coughing or who have symptoms, who have a fever, okay? Let us avoid them. Measles is caught through the air. For example, if they cough or blow their nose, um, let us not go near. And I hope our people, our countrymen, do not cough without covering their mouths and do not sneeze, okay.

rows: The speaker or guest talked about the factors that contributed to the measles outbreak. He said that Super Typhoon Yolanda hit the country and destroyed the environment. People were displaced and their health was affected by the displacement. Most of them migrated to Metro Manila. He mentioned people from the Visayas having a cough (or being sick) coming to Manila. (The book’s gist leaves out the typhoon’s name; the script names it.)

The speaker explained preventive measures against getting measles. He said there is no medicine to prevent measles. The only prevention is immunization or vaccination. He advised not to get closer to patients or friends who are coughing or who have a fever. Measles can be transmitted through the air, so stay away from people who are coughing, blowing their nose or sneezing.

explanations.title: Activity 11: a call to a doctor’s office
explanations.body: Pair up. You have a fever and are feeling very sick. Call a doctor’s office and set up an appointment with the receptionist. Be as specific as possible when talking about symptoms. Switch roles and present the conversation aloud in class (role play, left out).

explanations.title: A sample call (my own)
explanations.body: The book gives no key for this speaking task; this is my sample.

examples.text: Magandang umaga po. Klinika ni Doktor Reyes po ito.
examples.translation: Receptionist: Good morning. This is Doctor Reyes’ clinic.

examples.text: Magandang umaga po. May lagnat po ako at masama ang pakiramdam ko. Gusto ko pong magpa-check-up.
examples.translation: Patient: Good morning. I have a fever and I feel very sick. I would like a check-up.

examples.text: Kailan pa po kayo may lagnat?
examples.translation: Receptionist: Since when have you had a fever?

examples.text: Dalawang araw na po. Sumusuka rin po ako at sumasakit ang tiyan ko.
examples.translation: Patient: Two days now. I also vomit and my stomach aches.

examples.text: Puwede po kayong pumunta bukas ng alas-diyes ng umaga.
examples.translation: Receptionist: You can come tomorrow at ten in the morning.

examples.text: Sige po, salamat po.
examples.translation: Patient: All right, thank you.

examples.text: Walang anuman po. Magpahinga po muna kayo at uminom ng maraming tubig.
examples.translation: Receptionist: You’re welcome. Please rest first and drink a lot of water.

explanations.title: Activity 12: share an illness you have had
explanations.body: Think about an illness you have experienced. Include symptoms, what you did to deal with it, and any suggestions for others who might suffer similarly. You may use the terms nagkasakit, may sakit, masama ang pakiramdam, albularyo, nahihilo, nagsusuka, naghihina ang kalamnan, katawan, kasu-kasuan, halamang gamot, tradisyonal na gamot, ubo, sipon, lagnat, sumuka, pagtatae, pagsusuka, uminom, magpatingin sa doktor, magpa-check-up, humingi ng payo, and other terms as appropriate (open speaking, left out).

explanations.title: Intransitive um verbs for bodily motions, functions and emotions: sample sentences
explanations.body: From the book’s table of sample sentences; the translations are mine. The book’s r.w. notes: bahin, hatsing, hinga, lusong, singa, suka, tae or dumi, ihi.

examples.text: Huminga ka ng sariwang hangin para gumaling ka.

examples.text: Huwag kang lumusong sa tubig baha at baka may ihi ng daga ito.
examples.translation: Do not wade into floodwater, as it might have rat urine.

examples.translation: Blow your nose so that your breathing improves.

examples.text: Sumuka nang sumuka si Ellen kagabi.

examples.text: Dumumi si Efren sa likuran ng bahay pagkatapos niyang kumain.

examples.text: Umihi sa kama namin ang sanggol ni Ate.
examples.translation: Ate’s baby urinated on our bed.

explanations.title: Other um verbs for bodily motions, functions and emotions: sample sentences
explanations.body: dighay, higa, kain, luha, lulon, ngiti, tango, tawa, tayo, tingin, iling, inom and iyak are the root words.

examples.text: Dumidighay ako pagkatapos kong uminom ng coke.
examples.translation: I belch after I drink Coke.

examples.text: Humiga na ang pasyente sa kama.
examples.translation: The patient has lain down on the bed.

examples.text: Kakain kami nang kakain sa handaan ni Fe bukas.
examples.translation: We will eat and eat at Fe’s party tomorrow.

examples.text: Lumuha ako sa saya nang manganak ang misis ko.
examples.translation: I shed tears of joy when my wife gave birth.

examples.text: Mahirap lumulon kung masakit ang tonsils ko.
examples.translation: Swallowing is hard if my tonsils hurt.

examples.text: Hindi ngumiti si Amalia kay Daniel.
examples.translation: Amalia did not smile at Daniel.

examples.text: Tumatango si Celso sa doktor sa mga bilin ng doktor.
examples.translation: Celso nods to the doctor at the doctor’s instructions.

examples.text: Tumawa lang ang tatay ko sa mga reklamo ko.
examples.translation: My father just laughed at my complaints.

examples.text: Tumayo ako pagkatapos kong umupo nang matagal.
examples.translation: I stood up after I sat for a long time.

examples.text: Titingin kami bukas ng mga gamot sa botika.
examples.translation: We will look at medicines at the pharmacy tomorrow.

examples.text: Umiiling si Andrew dahil ayaw niya ng bakuna.
examples.translation: Andrew shakes his head because he does not want the vaccine.

examples.text: Uminom ako ng gamot para sa sakit sa ulo.
examples.translation: I took medicine for the headache.

examples.text: Umiyak nang umiyak si Josefa dahil masakit ang tiyan niya.
examples.translation: Josefa cried and cried because her stomach hurts.

lessons.title: 285. C15 L3 · PhilHealth and Universal Healthcare
lessons.subtitle: Inilunsad ang Kalusugang Pangkalahatan · Awtomatikong miyembro ang mga kapuspalad · Minadali ang proseso

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: By the end of this lesson you can extract information from reading and listening passages about health care and benefits; formulate and answer simple questions about them; and transcribe and translate phrases and sentences containing related vocabulary. The structures are the core vocabulary and the in/hin/nin verbs.

explanations.title: Getting started
explanations.body: The book shows the priority beneficiaries of Universal Healthcare in the Philippines and asks whether you know other deserving beneficiaries; students write their answers on the smartboard. (The picture is left out.)

explanations.title: Presentation 1: health care in the Philippines
explanations.body: An excerpt from batangascity.gov.ph. The book prints “Kalusugan Pangkalahatan” in the text and “Kalusugang Pangkalahatan” in the glossary; the glossary form is used in the word list.

examples.text: Inilunsad ng pamahalaan ang programang Kalusugan Pangkalahatan sa pamamagitan ng Philhealth.
examples.translation: The government launched the Universal Healthcare program by means of Philhealth.

examples.text: Layunin nito ang mabigyan ng kakayahan ang bawat Pilipino na makakuha ng serbisyong medikal sa panahon ng kanilang pangangailangan.
examples.translation: Its objective is to give every Filipino the capacity to get medical service in their time of need.

examples.text: May mga pakete ng benepisyo mula sa simple hanggang sa komplikadong sakit.
examples.translation: There are packages of benefits from simple to complicated illnesses.

examples.text: Dapat may hulog na tatlong buwan bago magamit ang benepisyo.
examples.translation: There must be three months of contributions before the benefit can be used.

examples.text: Magbabayad rin ang Philhealth sakaling naospital ka sa labas ng bansa.
examples.translation: Philhealth will also pay in case you are hospitalized outside the country.

examples.text: Sa ngayon, awtomatikong miyembro ang mga kapuspalad, mga may kapansanan, at mga batang inabandona.
examples.translation: At present, the indigents, persons with disability, and abandoned children are automatic members.

examples.text: Ginawa na ring awtomatikong miyembro ang mga may edad na animnapu pataas.
examples.translation: Those aged sixty and above were also made automatic members.

examples.text: Matatamasa na ng lahat ng senior citizens ang benepisyo ng PhilHealth.
examples.translation: All senior citizens will now enjoy the benefits of PhilHealth.

examples.text: Sagot ng pamahalaan ang premium contributions ng mga sektor na ito.
examples.translation: The government shoulders the premium contributions of these sectors.

examples.text: Minadali na rin ang proseso ng pag-apply para maging miyembro ng Philhealth.
examples.translation: The application process to become a Philhealth member has also been made easier.

examples.text: Hindi na kailangan ng katibayan ng pagpapakasal o sertipiko ng kapanganakan.
examples.translation: Proof of marriage or a birth certificate is no longer needed.

explanations.title: Note: PhilHealth’s mandate
explanations.body: PhilHealth’s mandate is to provide health insurance coverage to all Filipinos. Priority is also given to the health care needs of the underprivileged, the elderly, persons with disability, abandoned and neglected children, including those who are not regularly employed in the informal sector. Coverage being made compulsory, social health protection is now extended to the project-based or contractual employees who were previously not considered part of the workforce. (philhealth.gov.ph)

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: a. In paragraph 1, line 5, pakete ng benepisyo means “package of benefits.” b. The book’s note says pinakamahirap means “indigents,” but that word is not in the passage; the passage uses mga kapuspalad. c. Note and learn the cognates simple, komplikado, programa, serbisyo, benepisyo, pakete, awtomatiko, miyembro, retirado, sektor, proseso and edad. d. The Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PhilHealth) was created in 1995 to create universal health coverage for the Philippines. It is a tax-exempt, government-owned and government-controlled corporation (GOCC), attached to the Department of Health. It states its goal as insuring a sustainable national health insurance program for all. (Wikipedia.org)

rows: The government launched the program Universal Healthcare by means of PhilHealth. The objective is to make Filipinos capable of receiving medical services in times of need.

PhilHealth provides a package of benefits ranging from simple to complicated illnesses. You just need to have three monthly contributions to avail of the benefits. PhilHealth will also pay for hospitalization overseas.
3. Sectors whose premium contributions the government pays
The indigents, persons with disabilities, abandoned children, and senior citizens, those with 60 years of age and above.
The application process was simplified or made easy. There is no need for a birth certificate or marriage contract.
5. How health care here differs from your country
Answer may vary (a short paragraph in Tagalog; the book says it can also be a brief speaking activity).

explanations.title: Presentation 2: a phone exchange between siblings
explanations.body: The older sister (B) tells the younger (A) what to do about Junior. The book underlines the in/hin/nin verbs.

examples.text: Ate, ang taas-taas na ng lagnat ni Junior. Baka dengue na ’to.
examples.translation: A: Ate, Junior’s fever is so high already. It might be dengue.

examples.text: Dalhin mo agad sa ospital. Gamitin mo yung Philhealth ko. Kumpleto naman ang hulog ko buwan-buwan. Kunin mo kay Nanay ang member ID ko. Basahin at alamin mo rin yung mga benepisyo sa website. O di kaya, tanungin mo si Aling Biring, sa Philhealth siya nagtatrabaho.
examples.translation: B: Take him to the hospital right away. Use my Philhealth. My contributions are complete every month. Get my member ID from Mother. Read and also find out the benefits on the website. Or else ask Aling Biring, she works at Philhealth.

examples.text: Sigurado po ba kayong sasagutin ng Philhealth lahat ng gastos?
examples.translation: A: Are you sure Philhealth will shoulder all the expenses?

examples.text: Wag mo nang problemahin ’yan. Ang gawin mo, bihisan mo si Junior at dalhin mo na agad sa ospital. Tawagin mo si Uncle Rey siya na ang pa-draybin mo. Singilin mo na rin siya sa utang niya. Sabihin mo kailangan mo ng pera ngayon. Kung wala siyang pera utangin mo muna kay Auntie Fe ang panghospital ni Junior. Tapos, hintayin mo ako bukas.
examples.translation: B: Don’t worry about that. What you do is get Junior dressed and take him to the hospital right away. Call Uncle Rey, have him drive. Ask him to pay his debt too. Tell him you need money now. If he has no money, borrow the money for Junior’s hospital expenses from Auntie Fe first. Then wait for me tomorrow.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: a. In line 8, Wag mo nang problemahin ’yan means “Don’t worry about it.” b. In line 9, tawagin means “to call somebody nearby,” as opposed to tawagan, which means “to call by phone.” c. Dalhin, kunin, gamitin, basahin, alamin, tanungin, sasagutin, problemahin, gawin, singilin, utangin, sabihin and hintayin are in/hin/nin verbs, discussed in the grammar section.

explanations.title: New words

explanations.title: Activity 1: a news report on OFW benefits
explanations.body: Read the report and give the gist. Source: remate.ph. The report in the book breaks off after “sa loob” (“within”); its key finishes the sentence: within 180 days after the worker has been released from the hospital. The book’s key: PhilHealth announced that the OFWs affected by the oil tanker accident in Saudi Arabia will certainly receive their benefits. A total of Filipinos were affected including one who was reportedly killed when an oil tanker crashed into the fireway flyover causing an explosion. PhilHealth suggested that the families of the affected OFWs file a claim at any local branch of PhilHealth within 180 days after the worker has been released from the hospital.

examples.text: INANUNSIYO ng Philippine Health Insurance Corporation o PhilHealth na ang mga apektadong Overseas Filipino Workers o OFWs na nagkakaroon ng mga aksidente sa Saudi Arabia na sila ay siguradong makatatanggap ng benepisyo.
examples.translation: The Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PhilHealth) announced that the affected Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs) who have accidents in Saudi Arabia will surely receive benefits.

examples.text: May kabuuang labing-isang Pilipino ang nagkaroon ng sakuna at isa ang namatay ang naiulat nang isang oil tanker ang nabangga sa fireway flyover na nagresulta sa isang pagsabog.
examples.translation: A total of eleven Filipinos had a mishap and one reportedly died when an oil tanker crashed into the fireway flyover, resulting in an explosion.

examples.text: Iminumungkahi na ang pamilya at mga kamag-anak ng mga nasakunang OFWs ay maghain ng claim sa alin mang local na sangay ng PhilHealth.
examples.translation: It is suggested that the family and relatives of the OFWs in the accident file a claim at any local branch of PhilHealth.

explanations.title: More in/hin/nin verbs
explanations.body: In Chapter 12, Lesson 1, you learned in/hin/nin verbs. They are also called object-focus or goal-focus verbs. In this lesson you review them and meet more examples.

explanations.title: A. In/hin/nin verbs from the reading
explanations.body: Study the sentences from Presentation 2 and find the in/hin/nin verbs. The book’s key: dalhin, gamitin, kunin, basahin, alamin, tanungin, sasagutin, problemahin, gawin, bihisan, dalhin, tawagin, singilin, sabihin, utangin, hintayin. The bracketed “(siya)” in the book’s first and eighth lines is written in the sentence.

explanations.title: Focus and markers
explanations.body: The focus of a sentence is always definite. Thus it takes Set 1 markers when proper names and common nouns are used as objects. When the object is a pronoun or a demonstrative, Set 1 pronouns and demonstratives must be used. Markers, pronouns and demonstratives for the doer of the sentence must come from Set 2.

explanations.title: B. Verb formation: past and present
explanations.body: Recall the important rules for forming the PAST and PRESENT aspects of some in/hin/nin verbs. For verb roots beginning with vowels, prefix IN to the root. The last three rows of the book’s table (antok, api, awat) were left to complete; they are given here.

explanations.title: Roots beginning with consonants
explanations.body: For verb roots beginning with consonants, infix IN into the root (after the first consonant). All the root words are from the reading presentations. The last three rows (tanong, sagot, problema) were left to complete; they are given here as the book’s pattern shows (pINroblema).

explanations.title: Activity 2: object focus to doer focus
explanations.body: Translate the sentences, then change the object-focus verb into a doer-focus verb. Pattern: verb, doer (Set 2 pronoun or marker), direct object (Set 1 pronoun or marker), rest of sentence. The book gives the first example; the doer-focus versions for items 1 to 4 are my key. In the book’s table the doer of items 3 and 4 is bracketed (Lito, Nanay).

examples.translation: I will bring the payment for the hospital bill.

examples.text: Bibilangin ni Lito ang gamot sa kuwarto.

lessons.title: 290. C15 L3 · PhilHealth in the news: private hospitals, membership and OFWs
lessons.subtitle: Umapela ang PhilHealth sa mga pribadong ospital · Nobenta porsyento ng mga Pilipino ay miyembro na · Medicare coverage ng OFWs

explanations.title: Activity 5: PhilHealth and private hospitals (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Transcribe the sentences or phrases, give their meaning and give the gist. The book marks parts (1) to (5); the markers are left out of the spoken text, the double period is a single one, and the parts are keyed in the next card. Source: ptvnews.ph. Teacher note: call students at random for the meaning of a phrase; replay as needed.

examples.text: Samantala umapela ang PhilHealth Insurance Corporation o PhilHealth sa mga pribadong ospital.
examples.translation: Meanwhile, the PhilHealth Insurance Corporation appealed to the private hospitals.

examples.text: Ito’y kaugnay ng pagbibigay ng benepisyo sa kanilang mga miyembro.
examples.translation: This is in connection with giving benefits to their members.

examples.text: Una nang sinabi ng Private Hospitals Association of the Philippines na posibleng hindi pagbigyan ang mga PhilHealth members dahil sa utang ng kumpanya.
examples.translation: The Private Hospitals Association of the Philippines had earlier said that PhilHealth members might not be accommodated because of the company’s debt.

examples.text: Matagal umanong naibibigay ng PhilHealth ang bayad nito sa mga private hospitals gayung naghuhulog naman ang mga miyembro nito.
examples.translation: PhilHealth reportedly takes a long time to give its payment to the private hospitals even though its members do make their contributions.

examples.text: Samantala, nangako naman ang PhilHealth na aayusin ang problema para sa pagbibigay ng mabuting serbisyo.
examples.translation: Meanwhile, PhilHealth promised to fix the problem in order to give good service.

explanations.title: Activity 5: the five parts (the book’s translations)

rows: umapela ang PhilHealth Insurance Corporation sa mga pribadong ospital
The Philippine Health Insurance Corporation appealed to the private hospitals
pagbibigay ng benepisyo sa kanilang mga miyembro
posibleng hindi pagbigyan ang mga PhilHealth members dahil sa utang ng kumpanya
It is possible the Philhealth members may not be granted benefits because of the company’s debts.
naghuhulog naman ang mga miyembro nito
The (Philhealth) members are paying or making contributions.
aayusin ang problema para sa pagbibigay ng mabuting serbisyo
They will fix the problems in giving good services.

explanations.title: Activity 5: the gist (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Philhealth appealed to private hospitals to give benefits to their members. They were not granted this because of the company’s debts. Philhealth has been giving payments to private hospitals for a long time. However, they promised to fix the problems in giving good services to their members.

explanations.title: Activity 6: nearly everyone is a member
explanations.body: Read the passage and give four EEIs. The book prints the act number as “R. Act. No. 9485” and the seal of excellence in quotation marks; the spoken text writes the number in words. Source: YouTube.

examples.text: Halos nobenta porsyento na ng mga Pilipino ang miyembro na ng PhilHealth.
examples.translation: Almost ninety percent of Filipinos are already members of PhilHealth.

examples.text: Kabilang na rito ang nakatira sa malalayong probinsiya partikular sa Mindanao.
examples.translation: Included in this are those who live in far provinces, particularly in Mindanao.

examples.text: Ito na nga raw ang pinakamagandang Christmas gift na natanggap ng ahensiya.
examples.translation: This is reportedly the best Christmas gift the agency has received.

examples.text: Kamakailan lang, nakatanggap din ng seal of excellence ang Philhealth mula sa Civil Service Commission para sa kanilang pagtalima sa Republic Act bilang siyam na libo, apat na raan at walumpu’t lima o anti-red tape act.
examples.translation: Just recently, Philhealth also received a seal of excellence from the Civil Service Commission for its compliance with Republic Act number 9485, or the anti-red tape act.

rows: Ninety percent of Filipinos are now Philhealth members.
Included in this number are those who live in far provinces, particularly in Mindanao.
Philhealth considered this as a Christmas gift to its agency.
Just recently, Philhealth received the “seal of excellence” award from the Civil Service Commission.
The award is in recognition of Philhealth’s compliance with Republic Act number 9485, or the anti-red tape act.

explanations.title: Activity 7: a column on medicare coverage of OFWs
explanations.body: Read the excerpt and give the gist. The book prints a street address in Hong Kong (12-B Perth Apt. 27 Perth St.), which is left out; it also prints the misprints “lgal,” “depndents,” “ng ng” and “walangasawa,” corrected here. Source: philstar.com.

examples.text: Tanong sa PhilHealth ni Jarius Bondoc.
examples.translation: A question to PhilHealth, by Jarius Bondoc.

examples.text: May nag-email sa akin tungkol sa medicare coverage ng OFWs.
examples.translation: Someone emailed me about the medicare coverage of OFWs.

examples.text: Mrs. Josephine Dasalla, Hongkong. Nabasa ko ang kolum ninyo tungkol sa Philhealth.
examples.translation: Mrs. Josephine Dasalla, Hong Kong. I read your column about Philhealth.

examples.text: Para sa aking legal dependents sa Pilipinas, puwede ba akong mag-member kahit nandito ako sa HK? Papaano?
examples.translation: For my legal dependents in the Philippines, can I become a member even though I am here in HK? How?

examples.text: Ipinasagot ko ang mga tanong kay Ms. Linda Laureta, Philhealth manager for corporate communications.
examples.translation: I had the questions answered by Ms. Linda Laureta, Philhealth manager for corporate communications.

examples.text: Sabi niya, baka ang asawa ni Mrs. Dasalla ay member ng Philhealth, ipagpatuloy na lang ang contributions.
examples.translation: She said that maybe Mrs. Dasalla’s husband is a Philhealth member, so just continue the contributions.

examples.text: Sakop na ni Mrs. Dasalla at legal dependents nila.
examples.translation: Mrs. Dasalla and their legal dependents are already covered.

examples.text: Kung hindi naman, puwede niyang pasalihin ang asawa o anak na mayor de edad pero walang asawa, sila naman ni Mrs. Dasalla ang lalabas na dependents.
examples.translation: If not, she can have her husband or an adult child who is unmarried join, and they and Mrs. Dasalla will come out as dependents.

examples.text: Sakop silang lahat.
examples.translation: All of them are covered.

explanations.title: Activity 7: the gist (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Mrs. Dasalla from Hongkong asked if she could be a member of the medicare coverage as an OFW. She needs to know if she could include her legal dependents and how.

explanations.title: Activity 8: an interview in three passages (the book’s scripts)
explanations.body: Source: PTVnews.ph. Teacher note: repeat the audio as needed. Misprints in the book’s scripts are corrected: “japag” is kapag, “magp-submit” is written magsubmit, the bracketed OSCA is written “o OSCA,” and the word “pil-apan” in Activity 9 is written i-fill up (my correction). The three passages:

explanations.title: Passage 1: when can you use the benefits?

examples.text: Kung ikaw magpapamiyembro ka ng Philhealth kaagad-agad makukuha mo ang benefits o kailan po ’yan, dok?
examples.translation: Question: If you become a Philhealth member, will you get the benefits right away, or when is it, doc?

examples.text: Ang general rule natin sa paggamit ng benefits dapat meron kang tatlong buwang hulog sa loob ng anim na buwan bago ang unang araw ng pagkakaospital. So halimbawa po ngayon, January, February, March. Kung bayad ka ng January, February, March by April puwede mo na siyang magamit.
examples.translation: Answer: Our general rule for using the benefits is that you must have three months of contributions within six months before the first day of hospitalization. So for example now, January, February, March. If you have paid January, February, March, by April you can already use it.

examples.text: Sir, matanong ko lamang po para maging maliwanag sa ating mga kababayang OFWs kapag nasa ibang bansa sila habang nagtatrabaho doon sila inabutan ng pagkakasakit ano. Paano po ’yung proseso nito para magamit nila ang Philhealth?
examples.translation: Question: Sir, I would just like to ask, to make it clear for our countrymen who are OFWs, when they are abroad working and illness catches them there, what is the process for them to use Philhealth?

examples.text: Well, para po sa ating mga OFW or hindi man, kahit tayo. Alam n’yo naman ang mga Pilipino ngayon, mahilig mag-travel. Uhm, pag tayo po ang inabutan ng pagkakasakit sa ibang bansa magagamit pa rin natin ang Philhealth. Yun nga lang hindi po siya yung automatic deduction diyan sa mga hospital. Ano po ang gagawin? So, tayo muna ang magbabayad ng ating billing. Tapos po, kailangan nating magsubmit sa Philhealth ng ating medical certificate kung saan nakapaloob doon kung ano ang pagkakasakit, saan na-confine, ilang araw, at ibibigay din po natin ang official receipt ng pinagbayadan.
examples.translation: Answer: Well, for our OFWs, or not, even for us. You know that Filipinos nowadays love to travel. Um, if illness catches us in another country we can still use Philhealth. It is just that there is no automatic deduction at the hospitals there. What do we do? So we pay our billing first. Then we need to submit to Philhealth our medical certificate, which states what the illness is, where we were confined, how many days, and we also give the official receipt of what we paid.

examples.text: What are the process kung paano makapag-register?
examples.translation: Question: What is the process for how to register?

examples.text: Actually, napakadali lang especially sa ating mga senior citizens. Ang kinakailangan lang po ninyo, magpunta po kayo sa tinatawag nating Office of Senior Citizen’s Affairs o OSCA sa inyong mga lugar. At doon po magpi-fill up po kayo ng ating Member’s Registration Form. Ang OSCA na po ang bahalang magpadala sa Philhealth nitong mga papel na ’to. At pagka kayo’y miyembro, ipapa-register na at pagbalik po bibigyan na nila kayo ng tinatawag na member data record. Napakadali lang. Actually even ang member, kasi ang mga senior citizens maaring may sakit na and some of them probably baka nahihirapan nang maglakad. So hindi naman nangangailangan na sila po ang mismong pupunta, puwede namang authorized representative. Puwede rin po ’yun.
examples.translation: Answer: Actually, it is very easy, especially for our senior citizens. All you need to do is go to what we call the Office of Senior Citizen’s Affairs (OSCA) in your area. And there you will fill up our Member’s Registration Form. OSCA will be the one to send these papers to Philhealth. And once you are a member, you will be registered and on returning they will give you what is called a member data record. It is very easy. Actually, even the member, since senior citizens may already be sick and some of them probably have difficulty walking, they do not need to be the ones to come themselves, an authorized representative can do it. That is also fine.

rows: The date of effectivity of Philhealth benefits.
Passage 1, item 2: the general rule (2 details)

The general rule is that you must have 3 months of contributions within a 6-month period before your first day of hospitalization. For example, if you pay your contributions during the months of January, February, and March, you can use the benefits in April.
Passage 2, item 3: what the question was about
In case an OFW gets sick overseas, what is the process or procedure so he or she could avail of Philhealth benefits?
Passage 2, item 4: three steps or requisites

She or he should first pay the medical bills. Then submit to Philhealth a medical certificate indicating the type of illness, place and duration of confinement. She or he should also submit official receipts as proof of payments.
How senior citizens should register for Philhealth membership; the registration process of senior citizens to become Philhealth members.

First, the senior citizen should go to the local office of the Office of Senior Citizen’s Affairs (OSCA). Fill up the Member’s Registration Form (MRF). OSCA will send the form to the Philhealth office. Once a member, you will be registered, then Philhealth will issue a member data record. If a senior citizen is unable to go due to illness, she or he could send an authorized representative.

explanations.title: Activity 9: amendments to the PhilHealth policy (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Source: PTVnews.ph. The year and the Republic Act number are written in words in the spoken text.

examples.text: Noong Hunyo ng taong dalawang libo at labintatlo nagkaroon tayo ng bagong batas, tinatawag na R.A. sampung libo, anim na raan at anim. Ano po yung nandodoon. Unang-una pinadali na po ng batas ang pagpapamiyembro sa Philhealth. Wala na tayong kailangang requirements. So ang kailangan na lang po natin, i-fill up natin ang PMRF o yung Philhealth Member Registration Form, isulat lang yun, kumpletuhin ang impormasyon, i-file sa Philhealth, bibigyan ng numero ng Philhealth, puwede na tayong magbayad. Wala na pong kailangang requirements. So, yung mga birth certificate, marriage contract hindi na natin siya hinihingi ngayon.
examples.translation: Narrator: In June 2013 we had a new law, called R.A. 10606. What is in it? First of all, the law has made becoming a PhilHealth member easier. We no longer need requirements. So all we need is to fill up the PMRF, or the Philhealth Member Registration Form, just write it, complete the information, file it with Philhealth, we are given a Philhealth number, and we can pay. There are no more requirements. So the birth certificate and marriage contract we no longer ask for now.

rows: R.A. 10606 provides for expedited application for membership to Philhealth.

There are no requirements. The applicant only needs to fill up the PMRF, or Philhealth Member Registration Form, complete the information, then submit the form. Philhealth will give the applicant a Philhealth number, then the applicant proceeds to pay the monthly contribution. Marriage contract and birth certificate are no longer required.

examples.text: Magandang gabi, Doc! Eto po ang katanungan, ano. OFW siya for almost walong taon. Puwede ko po bang gamitin sa mother ko ang PhilHealth ko? Hindi ko pa po nagagamit ’yon.
examples.translation: Question: Good evening, Doc! Here is the question. She has been an OFW for almost eight years. Can I use my PhilHealth for my mother? I have not used it yet.

examples.text: Kung ang nanay niyo po ay animnapung taon pataas, hindi PhilHealth member, hindi po siya pensioner, puwede niyo po siyang gamitin as dependent n’yo yung magulang ninyo.
examples.translation: Answer: If your mother is sixty years and above, not a PhilHealth member, and not a pensioner, you can use your parent as your dependent.

examples.text: Ang anak ko ay na-ospital, na-dengue. Walong libong piso po lang ang covered. Ang bill po namin ay pitong libo, limang daan at walumpu’t tatlong piso. Halos lahat ng gamot, kami ang bumili. Tapos nagbayad pa kami ng professional fee na isang libo at anim na raang piso, bukod sa nakalistang dalawang libo at apat na raang piso na billing namin. Walong libong piso lang daw po ba talaga ang covered sa Dengue?
examples.translation: Question: My child was hospitalized with dengue. Only 8,000 pesos is covered. Our bill is 7,583 pesos. We bought almost all the medicine. Then we also paid a professional fee of 1,600 pesos, aside from our listed billing of 2,400 pesos. Is it really only 8,000 pesos that is covered for Dengue?

examples.text: Opo. Ito po ay pakete yung sa Dengue isa po natin na tinatawag, walong libong piso po ang ating benepisyo. At kung ito naman yung tinatawag nating Dengue dalawa, ito po yung mas matindi o yung may mga kumplikasyon na, labing-anim na libong piso po yung ating pakete para diyan.
examples.translation: Answer: Yes. That is the package for what we call Dengue 1, our benefit is 8,000 pesos. And what we call Dengue 2, which is the more severe one or the one with complications, our package for that is 16,000 pesos.

rows: An OFW who had been working overseas for 8 years now would like to know if his or her mom could use his or her Philhealth. The interviewee said if the mom’s age is 60 and above and she is not a Philhealth member and not a pensioner, the mom could use the OFW’s Philhealth as a dependent.

A mom whose child was hospitalized for dengue is asking if Philhealth only covers Php8,000.00 for dengue cases. She said she spent more than the coverage. The interviewee said that the Dengue 1 package covers Php8,000 of expenses and the Dengue 2 package covers Php16,000.

explanations.title: Self-evaluation
explanations.body: Recall the objectives: extract information from reading and listening passages, formulate and answer simple questions, and transcribe and translate phrases and sentences about hospitals and other medical services (including numbers in context), common diseases, symptoms and preventions, and healthcare and benefits. Check your understanding of the verb magkaroon, the intransitive um verbs for bodily motions, functions and emotions, the conversion of um verbs to the gerund form, and in/hin/nin verbs. If you answer “No” to any of them: review the section on your own, find a study partner, or let your academic counselor or team leader know where you need help.

lessons.subtitle: Lutuin mo ang sinigang na baka · Kalabasa at kamote laban sa kanser · Pipino at papaya para sa mata ni Lola

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: By the end of this lesson you can extract information from reading and listening passages about food and nutrition; describe governmental programs on combatting malnutrition; transcribe and translate numbers and sentences related to food and nutrition; and describe steps in preparing meals. The structures are the core vocabulary, object-focus i verbs, reservational phrases and in/hin/nin verbs used in cooking.

explanations.title: Getting started
explanations.body: Work in small groups with the food pyramid (a picture, left out). Tell each other what kind of food and beverage you include in your daily diet and what health benefits you get from them. Teacher note: lead the students toward the lesson 2 topic and ensure maximum participation.

explanations.title: Presentation 1, passage A: instructions of a health buff family member to her younger sibling
explanations.body: Adapted from deped.gov.ph. The book’s “(na walang taba)” is written without parentheses; “mo’yung” is mo ’yung.

examples.text: Bukas, lutuin mo ang sinigang na baka na walang taba sa sampalok para kay Tatay.
examples.translation: Tomorrow, cook the lean beef stew in tamarind for Dad.

examples.text: Isahog mo ’yung sayote, repolyo at tanglad.
examples.translation: Mix in the chayote, cabbage and lemon grass.

examples.text: Maganda raw ’yan para bumaba ang kanyang cholesterol.
examples.translation: They say that is good for lowering his cholesterol.

examples.text: Idagdag mo ’yung berdeng sili.
examples.translation: Add the green pepper.

examples.text: Ihalo mo ’yung sibuyas na berde pagkatapos.
examples.translation: Mix in the green onions afterwards.

examples.text: Magtabi ka na rin para kina Freddie.
examples.translation: Set some aside also for Freddie and company.

examples.text: D’yan sila manananghalian.
examples.translation: They will have lunch there.

examples.text: Kung may tira pa, ilagay mo sa pridyider.

explanations.title: Culture note
explanations.body: “You know you are a Filipino if you call any refrigerator a pridyider, from the brand ‘frigidaire.’” Filipinos have the penchant of using brand names in giving names to a particular object. They would call any toothpaste “colgate,” any camera “kodak,” photocopies “xerox,” any detergent “tide,” and any nail polish “cutex.”

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: a. In paragraph 1, line 1, baka na walang taba means “lean beef.” b. In paragraph 1, line 4, magtabi (set aside) also means “to sit together” or “sitting close together” in another context. c. The prefix i in isahog, idagdag, igisa, ihalo, itsek, imeryenda and ilabas means “to do something to a person or a thing.” It expresses various kinds of actions; it is explained in the grammar section.

lessons.title: 294. C16 L1 · A Bicolano recipe: ginataang talbos ng kamoteng kahoy
lessons.subtitle: Mga sangkap at paraan ng pagluluto · Durugin, pigain, pakuluan · Timplahan ayon sa panlasa

explanations.title: Presentation 1, passage B: a blogger shares a healthy Filipino recipe
explanations.body: The book’s amounts are figures (½ kilo, 10, 2, 4, 2-4); the spoken text writes them in words. The dash after “Bicolano” is a comma here.

examples.text: Ibabahagi ko lang po ang isa sa kilalang pagkain ng mga Bicolano, ang ginataang talbos ng kamoteng kahoy.
examples.translation: I will just share one of the well-known foods of the Bicolanos, cassava tops cooked in coconut milk.

examples.text: Ito po ang mga sangkap.
examples.translation: These are the ingredients.

examples.text: Kalahating kilo ng dahon ng kamoteng kahoy.
examples.translation: Half a kilo of cassava leaves.

examples.text: Sampung butil ng bawang, tinadtad.
examples.translation: Ten cloves of garlic, chopped.

examples.text: Dalawang piraso ng sibuyas, tinadtad.
examples.translation: Two onions, chopped.

examples.text: Dalawang kutsarita ng luya, ginayat.
examples.translation: Two teaspoons of ginger, sliced.

examples.text: Apat na pirasong ginayat na niyog, pigain at salain ang gata.
examples.translation: Four pieces of sliced coconut, squeeze and sieve the milk.

examples.text: Dalawa hanggang apat na siling haba o siling labuyo.
examples.translation: Two to four long chilies or hot chili peppers.

examples.text: Dalawa hanggang apat na kutsaritang patis para pandagdag ng lasa.
examples.translation: Two to four teaspoons of fish sauce to add flavor.

examples.text: Paraan ng pagluluto.
examples.translation: Method of cooking.

examples.text: Una, durugin at pigain ang dahon ng kamoteng kahoy.
examples.translation: First, crush and squeeze the cassava leaves.

examples.text: Isantabi pagkatapos.
examples.translation: Set aside afterwards.

examples.text: Pangalawa, pakuluan ang kakang gata, idagdag ang bawang, sibuyas, luya, at dahon ng kamoteng kahoy.
examples.translation: Second, bring the first coconut milk to a boil, add the garlic, onion, ginger and cassava leaves.

examples.text: Tapos, hayaang kumulo hanggang malambot na ang mga dahon.
examples.translation: Then, let it boil until the leaves are soft.

examples.text: Lagyan ng siling labuyo.
examples.translation: Add the hot chili peppers.

examples.text: Timplahan ng asin, patis at paminta ayon sa inyong panlasa.
examples.translation: Season with salt, fish sauce and pepper according to your taste.

examples.text: Maaring samahan ito ng daing o tuyo na hinimay.
examples.translation: It may be served with shredded daing or tuyo.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: a. Durugin, pigain, tinadtad, ginayat, salain and hinimay are in/hin/nin verbs associated with cooking; they are explained in the grammar section. b. Kakang gata literally means “first coconut milk.” It refers to the first extraction of coconut milk, also called coconut cream. It is much thicker in texture and normally added during the last part of the cooking.

rows: first coconut milk; the first extraction of coconut milk

explanations.title: Comprehension check, passage B (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Provide in English the step-by-step instruction for cooking the recipe. Key: First, crush and squeeze the cassava tops. Then set it aside. Second, boil the coconut cream. Add garlic, onion, ginger and cassava leaves or tops. Allow to boil until the leaves are tender or soft. Add hot chili pepper. Season it with salt, fish sauce or pepper according to your taste. You may eat it with shredded dried fish or tuyo, a type of dried fish.

lessons.title: 295. C16 L1 · A health worker talks to Lola about eating well
lessons.subtitle: Pababa nang pababa ang timbang n’yo · Mayaman sa hibla · Puwede po namang tokwa

explanations.title: Presentation 2, dialog A: a health care practitioner (A) and a patient (B)
explanations.body: Information in the dialog is from deped.gov.ph; the dash after “karne” is a comma here.

examples.text: Lola, pababa po nang pababa ang timbang n’yo. Ano po ba ang lagi n’yong kinakain?
examples.translation: A: Lola, your weight keeps going down and down. What do you always eat?

examples.text: Kanin, itlog at tuyo po halos araw-araw.
examples.translation: B: Rice, egg and dried fish almost every day.

examples.text: Ok po yan pero kailangan nyo pong kumain ng gulay at prutas lalo na yung mayaman sa hibla gaya ng pechay at pinya. Para ho kasi silang walis sa ating bituka. Nililinis nila ang kolesterol sa ating katawan. Nang sa ganun maging maayos ang daloy ng dugo sa mga ugat po ng katawan natin. Lola, para sa kalusugan n’yo ho ito.
examples.translation: A: That is okay, but you need to eat vegetables and fruit, especially those rich in fiber such as pechay and pineapple. They are like a broom in our intestines. They clean the cholesterol in our body, so that the flow of blood in the veins of our body is good. Lola, this is for your health.

examples.text: Wala naman akong pambili, ma’am. Itlog at tuyo lang ang kaya ko.
examples.translation: B: I have nothing to buy it with, ma’am. Egg and dried fish are all I can afford.

examples.text: Naku, Lola, mura po sa palengke ang mabeberdeng gulay, mga butong gulay, o mga pagkaing butil. Sariwa pa. At saka kailangan nyo rin pong kumain ng karne, pampalakas po ito.
examples.translation: A: Oh, Lola, green leafy vegetables, legumes or grains are cheap at the market. They are fresh too. And you also need to eat meat, it gives strength.

examples.text: Mahal po ang karne, ma’am.
examples.translation: B: Meat is expensive, ma’am.

examples.text: Lola, puwede po namang tokwa. Sagana din po ito sa sustansya katulad ng karne. At mas mura pa.
examples.translation: A: Lola, tofu will do. It is also rich in nutrients like meat. And it is cheaper.

explanations.title: Culture note: staple foods
explanations.body: Rice is considered the staple food of Filipinos. However, in the Visayas, especially in Cebu and Bohol, milled corn is the staple food. Thus corn eating is a characteristic of Cebuanos and Boholanos. This cultural preference for food has spread to some areas in Mindanao, brought about by Cebu and Bohol migrants.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: a. In line 1, lagi is short for palagi (often, always). b. In line 2, tuyo (dried fish) literally means “dry.” c. In line 3, mayaman sa hibla means “rich in fiber.” d. In line 5, nang sa ganun means “so that.” e. In lines 7 and 9, pam in pambili and pampalakas means “for.”

explanations.title: Comprehension check, dialog A (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Part b (suggest two or three more recommendations for a healthy, balanced diet and ask a partner) is pair work and is left out.

rows: The health care practitioner observed that the patient continues to lose weight every time she visits the clinic or center.

(1) Chinese cabbage and pineapple are examples of fiber-rich fruit and vegetable; (2) they are like a broomstick in the intestine; (3) they clean the cholesterol in our body; (4) thus they allow the blood to flow smoothly in the veins.
Tofu is also rich in nutrients just like meat. It is also cheaper than meat.
4. Vegetables or foods sold cheap in the market

explanations.title: Culture note: dinengdeng
explanations.body: Dinengdeng (also called inabraw) is a healthy dish of the Ilocano people. It is usually cooked in a banga, a local term for a cooking clay pot used by the descendants of the local settlers in ancient times. Dinengdeng is classified as a bagoong monamon soup-based dish. The Ilocanos in Agoo, La Union officially celebrate the Dinengdeng Festival annually to promote local tourism and pay tribute to their favorite dish. The festival features simultaneous cooking of 101 kinds of dinengdeng prepared by local chefs. (Source: Wikipedia, Philstar)

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: a. Ginigisa, nilalaga, gayatin, hiwain, hatiin, linisin, tanggalin, putulin, hintayin, iniihaw, piniprito, haluin and lutuin are in/hin/nin verbs related to cooking; they are explained briefly in the grammar section. b. Okra is a type of vegetable. c. In the last sentence, Sa wakas is an expression meaning “Finally.”

explanations.title: New words
explanations.body: The book glosses magpakulo and pakuluin both as “boil”; they are separated here. The book spells “moringa” as “moringga.”

explanations.title: Activity 1: tips for a healthy diet
explanations.body: Read an excerpt about tips for a healthy diet, then fill in the table. Source: remate.ph. The book’s table (situation and suggestions, in English) is given in the next card.

examples.text: Mag-aalinlangan ka pa ba? Subukan ang mga sumusunod na tips para sa iyong healthy-diet.
examples.translation: Are you still hesitating? Try the following tips for your healthy diet.

examples.text: Ilagay ang mga prutas sa mga lugar na madali mong makita para maengganyo kang kumain nito. Ilabas ito sa refrigerator.
examples.translation: Put the fruits in places that you can easily see so you are encouraged to eat them. Take them out of the refrigerator.

examples.text: Siguruhin na may gulay at root crops ka tuwing kakain. Sanayin na kalahati ng plato mo ay gulay at sangkapat ang root crop.
examples.translation: Make sure you have vegetables and root crops each time you eat. Get used to half of your plate being vegetables and a quarter root crops.

examples.text: Ugaliin din ang pagmemeryanda ng gulay, prutas at root crops. Ang isang tasa ng melon, piraso ng pipino at nilagang kamote o kamoteng-kahoy at saging ay mainam na pamalit sa isang hiwa ng pizza o cookies.
examples.translation: Make it a habit also to snack on vegetables, fruit and root crops. A cup of melon, a piece of cucumber and boiled sweet potato or cassava and banana are good substitutes for a slice of pizza or cookies.

examples.text: Sumubok ng mga bagong putahe taglay ang gulay lalo na ang mga berdeng gulay at prutas.
examples.translation: Try new dishes that have vegetables, especially green vegetables and fruit.

rows: When trying to motivate yourself to eat fruits
Put the fruits in a conspicuous place or take the fruits out of the refrigerator.
Make sure to have vegetables and root crops in your meal. Make it a habit to have half a portion of vegetables and a quarter of root crop on your plate.
Make it a habit to eat vegetables, fruits and root crops. A cup of watermelon, a piece of cucumber, and boiled sweet potato and banana are good alternatives for a slice of pizza or cookies.
Try a recipe that includes vegetables, especially green leafy vegetables, and fruits.

explanations.title: Grammar: object focus i verbs, reservational phrases, in/hin/nin verbs related to cooking
explanations.body: A. I verbs. 1. Review: you were introduced to i verbs or object-focus verbs in Chapter 12, Lesson 2. I verb as benefactive focus is introduced in Chapter 17, Lesson 3. Important rules: the object may either be a person or a thing; some verb roots may take the prefix i and the suffixes in/hin/nin without any change in meaning; when conjugating i verbs, IN becomes NI when the root words begin with /l/, /h/ or /y/.

explanations.body: Identify the i verbs; the focus is underlined in the book.

explanations.title: A.2 Formation and conjugation
explanations.body: Practice conjugating the i verbs from the reading. In the book’s table the first row printed “sahog / ilabas / inilabas...” by mistake; the correct isahog row is given here (my key).

explanations.title: A.3 Grammatical structure: word order
explanations.body: The sentences can be re-written with the direct object at the end. Example: Isama mo ang sayote sa tinola, or Isama mo sa tinola ang sayote. The verbs here have a doer (Set 2 marker), a direct object (Set 1 marker) and the rest of the sentence. My key for the book’s five sentences:

rows: Isama mo ang sayote sa tinola.
Isama mo sa tinola ang sayote.
Ilabas mo na ang labanos, pipino, pakwan, at papaya sa fridge.
Ilabas mo na sa fridge ang labanos, pipino, pakwan, at papaya.
Ilagay mo ang sinigang sa pridyider.
Ilagay mo sa pridyider ang sinigang.
Igisa mo ang hipon sa kalabasa.
Igisa mo sa kalabasa ang hipon.
Ihalo mo ang sibuyas na berde pagkatapos.
Ihalo mo pagkatapos ang sibuyas na berde.
