explanations.title: B. Reservational phrases
explanations.body: When the action implied is directed toward the benefit of someone, the Set 3 reservational phrase para sa, sa mga, kay or kina (“for…”) is used. explanations.title: A note on prito
explanations.body: It is also common to hear native speakers say “priniprito” instead of “piniprito.” A quick search shows the extent of use of “priniprito.”

explanations.title: C.2 Verb formation and conjugation
explanations.body: See the first three examples of in/hin/nin verbs: luto, putol and halo. Note the change from /o/ to /u/ in the infinitive (lutuin, putulin, haluin) and in the future tense. In the past and present tenses, IN is a prefix to verb roots beginning with vowels (inihaw) and an infix to roots beginning with consonants (pinutol, hinalo, hiniwa, tinanggal). For roots beginning with L, Y and R, invert IN to NI and prefix it to the root (nilaga). When conjugating roots ending in /d/, change /d/ to /r/ in the infinitive and future. The book prints “nilaga” as the infinitive of laga; the infinitive is lagain (my correction).

lessons.title: 300. C16 L1 · Exercise, cooking tips and the importance of vegetables
lessons.subtitle: Benepisyo ng pag-eehersisyo sa umaga · Mga tip sa mas malusog na pagluluto · Gulay, hibla at glow food

explanations.title: Activity 5: benefits of exercise (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Transcribe the phrases, give their meaning and the gist. Source: YouTube. The book marks six parts (1) to (6), keyed in the next card. Teacher note: call students randomly for the meaning of a sentence or phrase; replay as needed.

examples.text: Ano nga ba ang benepisyo ng pag-eehersisyo sa umaga?
examples.translation: What are the benefits of exercising in the morning?

examples.text: Ayon sa pag-aaral ang ehersisyo ay nakakatulong para bumilis at tumalas ang kakayanang mag-isip ng tao apat hanggang sampung oras pagkatapos niyang mag-ehersisyo.
examples.translation: According to a study, exercise helps a person’s ability to think become faster and sharper for four to ten hours after he exercises.

examples.text: Nakakatulong ito para maging natural ang cycle ng ating pagtulog.
examples.translation: It helps our sleep cycle become natural.

examples.text: Dahil maagang nakakatulog maaga ring nagigising at nagiging handa ang ating katawan para sa buong araw na gawain.
examples.translation: Because you fall asleep early, you also wake up early and our body becomes ready for the whole day’s activity.

examples.text: Isang pangkaisipang benepisyo nito ay ang pag-iwas sa hindi masusutansiyang pagkain.
examples.translation: One mental benefit of this is avoiding non-nutritious food.

examples.text: Dahil nagsisimula ang araw mo sa pag-eehersisyo mas magiging maingat ka sa pagpili ng kakainin.
examples.translation: Because your day starts with exercise, you will be more careful in choosing what you eat.

examples.text: At mas iisipin mo kung ano ang mas nakabubuti para sa iyong kalusugan.
examples.translation: And you will think more about what is better for your health.

explanations.title: Activity 5: the six parts and their meaning (the book’s key)

rows: maingat ka sa pagpili ng kakainin

explanations.title: Activity 5: the gist (the book’s key)
explanations.body: This passage is about the benefits of exercising in the morning. It helps sharpen mental ability, adjusts our sleep to a natural cycle, and helps in getting ready for the day’s activities. One should also choose carefully what one eats, avoid non-nutritious food, and always think of what is good for the health.

explanations.title: Activity 6a: healthy cooking tips, first part
explanations.body: Read the passage and give the gist in three to five sentences. Source: philstar.com. The book’s “cooking/eating/working out” is separated with commas. The book’s key: Tips for a healthier lifestyle include: take carbs in the morning, then work out up to lunch. Minimize carbs in the evening and just eat proteins. Measure ingredients, like only one tablespoon of mayonnaise, but vegetables should be unlimited. They are full of vitamins and minerals.

examples.text: Narito ang mga tip sa aking healthier cooking, eating, working out lifestyle.
examples.translation: Here are the tips for my healthier cooking, eating, working out lifestyle.

examples.text: Ang carbs ay dapat sa umaga, pagkatapos magwork-out at hanggang lunch dahil mahaba pa ang oras para i-burn at magamit ito.
examples.translation: Carbs should be in the morning, after a workout and until lunch because there is still plenty of time to burn and use them.

examples.text: Ideally ay mas kaunti na ang carbs habang gumagabi at sa gabi ay protina na lang.
examples.translation: Ideally there are fewer carbs as the evening comes, and at night just protein.

examples.text: Bagama’t sinusukat ko ang mga sangkap, ultimo ang bawat kutsara ng mayonnaise, ang gulay naman ay unlimited.
examples.translation: Although I measure the ingredients, down to every spoon of mayonnaise, the vegetables are unlimited.

examples.text: Napakababa ng calories ng mga gulay ngunit hitik sa sustansya, bitamina’t mineral.
examples.translation: Vegetables are very low in calories but packed with nutrients, vitamins and minerals.

explanations.title: Activity 6b: healthy cooking tips, second part
explanations.body: Summarize in four to five sentences. The book prints “2 liters”; here it is “dalawang litro.” The book’s key: Mangoes and bananas have higher carbohydrate content so just eat these fruits in the morning. Instead of salt or flavoring, try pepper and lemon juice. To get slimmer, use more pepper, chili powder and cayenne pepper. Drink two liters of cold water every day because the body will warm this water. Good effects are fast metabolism, one gets full easily, and eats less.

examples.text: Ang mangga at saging ang may pinakamataas na carbohydrate content sa lahat ng prutas, kaya dapat sa umaga lamang ang mga ito.
examples.translation: Mango and banana have the highest carbohydrate content of all fruits, so they should be eaten only in the morning.

examples.text: Imbes na asin ang pampalasa, subukan ang paminta at katas ng lemon.
examples.translation: Instead of salt as a flavoring, try pepper and lemon juice.

examples.text: Nakakatulong ang maaanghang sa pagpapapayat kaya mas damihan mo pa ang sili, chili powder at cayenne pepper sa pagkain.
examples.translation: Spicy foods help in slimming, so add even more chili, chili powder and cayenne pepper to your food.

examples.text: Uminom ng dalawang litro ng malamig na tubig kada araw.
examples.translation: Drink two liters of cold water every day.

examples.text: Mas malamig, mas mainam dahil puwersado ang katawang painitin ito.
examples.translation: The colder, the better, because the body is forced to warm it.

examples.text: Ang epekto, bibilis ang metabolism, madaling mabubusog, konti ang makakain.
examples.translation: The effect is that the metabolism speeds up, you get full easily, and you eat little.

explanations.title: Activity 7: the importance of vegetables (the book’s scripts)
explanations.body: Listen to passages about the importance of vegetables. (a) Write the gist in English. (b) Write a question for each passage in English. (c) On your teacher’s cue, take turns asking your question in Tagalog and answering a classmate’s in Tagalog using your notes (pair work, left out). The book’s “…” is a comma here; the figures ½ and 1½ are in words.

examples.text: Importante na dapat tayong kumain ng iba’t ibang klase ng gulay araw-araw. So, kung iba’t-iba yung klase ng gulay na kinakain natin araw-araw, makukuha natin yung mga vitamins saka minerals na kinakailangan ng ating katawan para tayo ay mag-function nang maayos.
examples.translation: Passage 1: It is important that we eat different kinds of vegetables every day. So if the kinds of vegetables we eat every day are different, we will get the vitamins and minerals that our body needs to function well.

examples.text: Kaya ang mga gulay ay mayaman sa sinasabi nating fiber. Yung fiber na yan ay hindi ito nada-digest. Ito ay parang walis sa ating intestines, sa ating bituka para malinisan at mawawala yung mga kolesterol sa ating katawan.
examples.translation: Passage 2: So vegetables are rich in what we call fiber. That fiber is not digested. It is like a broom in our intestines, in our bowel, to clean it and get rid of the cholesterol in our body.

examples.text: Para yung mga nerve natin sa ating katawan ay maging maayos, at ganun din yung daloy ng ating dugo, gumanda rin yung ating kutis, luminaw ang ating mga mata, dun natin nakukuha yun sa glow foods, kaya glow food siya.
examples.translation: Passage 3: So that the nerves in our body are in good order, and also the flow of our blood, our skin also becomes beautiful and our eyes become clear, we get that from glow foods, which is why it is a glow food.

examples.text: Ang ideal intake nasa nutritional guidelines natin ay isa hanggang isa’t kalahating cups na vegetables ang kinakailangan natin sa isang araw at kalahati dito ay dapat galing sa mabeberdeng gulay. Ang Filipinos ay meron lang isang cup ng vegetables ang intake nila. So parang nagkukulang pa tayo ng kalahating cup para lang sana ma-meet natin yung requirement natin sa vegetable consumption.
examples.translation: Passage 4: The ideal intake in our nutritional guidelines is one to one and a half cups of vegetables that we need in a day, and half of this should come from green leafy vegetables. Filipinos only have one cup of vegetables for their intake. So we are still short by half a cup just so that we can meet our requirement for vegetable consumption.

rows: It is important to eat different kinds of vegetables every day. If we do, we get the vitamins and minerals that our bodies need to function well.
Vegetables are rich in fiber. Fiber is not digested. It is like a broom in our intestines that cleans and gets rid of cholesterol in the body.

Vegetables make our nerves function well, contribute to good blood circulation, make our skin smooth, make our eyes clear, all of which we get from glow foods. That is why vegetables are called glow food.

Based on nutritional guidelines, we need 1½ cups of vegetables daily, and ½ cup should be green leafy vegetables. Filipinos only have a cup; thus Filipinos need ½ more just to meet the daily required consumption or intake of vegetables.

lessons.title: 301. C16 L1 · Family talk on tofu, workmates’ lunches, speaking and glossary
lessons.subtitle: Tokwa, munggo at murang sustansiya · Baon na lutong gulay · Glossary at mga halimbawang pangungusap

explanations.title: Activity 8: two conversations (the book’s scripts)
explanations.body: Listen to excerpts of a conversation and answer the questions. Source: Katumbas Ay Biyaya / National Nutrition Council, DZRH (a recording from a live stream radio broadcast). The book’s “(Giggles),” “(Chuckles)” and “---” are left out. Passage 1: a conversation between family members.

examples.text: Ay, naku, Inay. Ano po yan inihanda ninyo? Pritong karne po ba ’yan?
examples.translation: Jenny: Oh my, Inay. What is that you prepared? Is that fried meat?

examples.text: Hindi ito karne, anak. Tokwa ito na gawa sa soy beans. Ang sustansiyang dulot nito ay katulad din ng sustansiyang binibigay ng isda o karne.
examples.translation: Salud: It is not meat, child. It is tofu made from soy beans. The nutrients it gives are the same as the nutrients that fish or meat give.

examples.text: Sino naman ang nagsabi sa ’yo niyan, Salud?
examples.translation: Ernie: Who told you that, Salud?

examples.text: E, nabasa ko dun sa clippings na ipinahiram sa akin ni mareng Mina. Naku, marami akong natututunan dun. Gaya nga nitong sustansiyang binibigay ng tokwa ’tsaka yung mga berdeng gulay na mabibili nang mura sa palengke, maging ang mga butong gulay, gaya ng munggo na kasing sustansiya ng ibang karne. Marami palang murang pagkain na mabibili pero sagana sa sustansiya.
examples.translation: Salud: Well, I read it in the clippings that Mareng Mina lent me. Oh, I am learning a lot there. Like the nutrients that tofu gives, and the green vegetables that can be bought cheaply at the market, even legumes, like mung beans that are as nutritious as other meat. So there is a lot of cheap food that can be bought but is rich in nutrients.

examples.text: Kung dati’y tuyo at itlog ang lagi mong baon, ba, ngayon iba na, a. Lutong gulay na, a! At araw-araw iba-iba, ha.
examples.translation: Oliver: If before it was dried fish and egg that you always brought as baon, well, now it is different. It is cooked vegetables now! And different every day, too.

examples.text: Oo, Oliver. At luto ’yan ng misis ko. Kasi ang gusto niya masustansiya ang kinakain ko, dahil nga mabigat ang trabaho natin. Para hindi agad ako nanghihina.
examples.translation: Ernie: Yes, Oliver. And my wife cooked that. She wants what I eat to be nutritious because our work is heavy. So that I do not get weak right away.

examples.text: Napansin ko nga, Ernie. Mas malakas na ang resistensiya mo ngayon, e. Di gaya ng dati.
examples.translation: Oliver: I noticed that, Ernie. Your immunity is stronger now. Not like before.

examples.text: Dahil ’yan kay Mrs.
examples.translation: Ernie: That is thanks to the Mrs.

rows: Three people are talking (mother, father, daughter).
(1) Tofu is made from soy beans; (2) the nutrients from tofu are the same as the nutrients from fish and meat.
She learned that tofu has lots of nutrients; that green leafy vegetables sold cheap in the wet market are also rich in nutrients; and that legumes are as nutritious as meat.

Oliver has been bringing packed meals of vegetable dish every day. He used to bring egg and dried fish. Ernie also noticed that Oliver has a stronger immune system, unlike before. (In the printed script the observer is Oliver and the person observed is Ernie; the book’s key swaps the names.)

explanations.title: Activity 9: a mother’s instruction to her daughter
explanations.body: Listen and write the summary. The book’s key: The mom is asking her daughter, Carol, to make vegetables part of their meal (hers and her children’s), and to avoid junk food. She asks her to buy fresh vegetables in the market like squash because it is good for the eyes. She insists on serving the kids fruits and vegetables, especially those rich in fiber. She said that the eyes will see more clearly, the skin will be smoother, and the immune system will be stronger.

examples.text: Carol, si mommy mo to. Yung mga anak mo ha pakainin mo ng gulay. Wag puro chichirya. Ibili mo sila ng sariwang gulay sa palengke gaya ng kalabasa. Maganda yan sa mata. Basta bigyan mo sila ng gulay at prutas lalo na ’yung mayaman sa hibla. Lilinaw na ang mata nila, gaganda pa ang kanilang kutis at saka lalakas ang resistensya nila.
examples.translation: Mommy: Carol, this is your mommy. Make your children eat vegetables, okay. Not just chichirya. Buy them fresh vegetables at the market like squash. It is good for the eyes. Just give them vegetables and fruit, especially those rich in fiber. Their eyes will become clear, their skin will become even more beautiful and their immunity will grow stronger.

explanations.title: Activity 10: chain story
explanations.body: Teacher note: prepare sheets of paper with words and phrases from the lesson (for example para sa mga sundalo, i-tsek, itabi, pagkaing nagbibigay ng enerhiya). Sit in a circle; each student gets a word or phrase and writes a sentence to begin a story, then passes the paper to the right. Each student adds a sentence to the story received from the left, following the plotline, until the paper returns; then read the story aloud (group work, left out).

explanations.title: Activity 11: preparing healthy meals
explanations.body: At the end of the health and fitness segment of your civil liaison work in Manila, you are tasked with preparing a day’s meal (breakfast, lunch and dinner) for your Filipino counterparts. The meals should promote health and fitness. (a) Individually, think about a healthy breakfast, lunch and dinner, with a short explanation of why they are healthy, and fill in the table (Meal, Menu) in Tagalog. (b) Pair up and tell your partner; the book’s example is below. (c) Present your menus to the class with the rationale. (d) Optional: consolidate the meals into a single menu (open writing and pair work, left out).

examples.text: Ano’ng ihahanda mo para sa hapunan?
examples.translation: A: What will you prepare for dinner?

examples.text: Para sa hapunan, ihahanda ko ang halu-halong gulay at inihaw na bagong-huling isda. Masustansiya ang mga gulay na ito, at walang masyadong taba ang isda. Sariwang prutas ang aming pangmatamis.
examples.translation: B: For dinner, I will prepare mixed vegetables and grilled freshly caught fish. These vegetables are nutritious, and the fish does not have much fat. Fresh fruit is our dessert.

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: By the end of this lesson you can extract information from reading and listening passages about mental and physical fitness; identify activities that promote physical and mental health; recommend or offer advice on fitness and nutrition; and translate phrases and sentences related to mental and physical fitness. The structures are the core vocabulary and ma-an verbs.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: a. In paragraph 1, line 2, makayanan (r.w. kaya) is a ma-an/han/nan verb. The ma-an affix in makayanan means “to feel or experience something.” Makayanan means “to bear.” b. In paragraph 1, line 2, the Spanish cognate for suliranin is problema, which is more frequently used in conversation. c. In paragraph 1, line 3, pang-araw-araw na gawain means “daily activities.”

rows: to be able to do; to be able to execute
Sleep and rest are as important as eating right and exercising. Sleep and rest are essential to physical and mental health.
2. Four benefits of sleep and rest
(1) mental alertness; (2) ability to deal with problems; (3) fulfils daily activities; and (4) energizes the body.

(1) weakening of the body system or immune system; (2) the body becomes vulnerable to infections; (3) tiredness; (4) nervousness; (5) irritability; (6) dizziness; (7) depression; and (8) emotional issues such as a sudden burst of anger and anxiety.

explanations.title: Presentation 2: a dialog between friends
explanations.body: A is the friend and B is Luis. The book labels the last two lines “A,” but they read as Luis’ reply; they are given to B here. Images from philstar.com (left out).

examples.text: Luis, naimbitahan akong sumali sa triathlon. Nasalihan mo na ’to minsan ’di ba? I-share mo naman ang nalalaman mo.
examples.translation: A: Luis, I was invited to join the triathlon. You have joined this once, haven’t you? Please share what you know.

examples.text: Handa ka na bang mahirapan? Kailangan mo ng trainer para masubaybayan kung gumagaling ka. Ituturo niya ang tamang paghahanda para mapagtagumpayan mo ang laban.
examples.translation: B: Are you ready to suffer? You need a trainer to monitor whether you are getting better. He will teach you the right preparation so that you can overcome the contest.

examples.text: Tama ka nga. Gusto kong matutunan ang tamang pamamaraan ng paghahandang pisikal.
examples.translation: A: You are right. I want to learn the right way of physical preparation.

examples.text: Utak at katawan, pare. Balanse dapat lahat. Kailangan mong malaman ang tamang istratehiya para malamangan mo ang kalaban mo.
examples.translation: B: Brain and body, pare. Everything should be balanced. You need to know the right strategy so you can have the advantage over your opponent.

examples.text: Kailangan ko talaga ng focus para malampasan ko ang hirap ng training.
examples.translation: A: I really need focus so that I can get past the hardship of training.

examples.text: Kayang-kaya mo yan, Pare. Malay mo, mabansagan ka pang Hari ng Triathlon! Teka muna, kailangan mo munang kumonsulta sa doktor. Hindi ka puwedeng sumabak na lang sa training nang ganun-ganun na lang.
examples.translation: B: You can easily do it, pare. Who knows, you may even be called the King of Triathlon! But wait, you first need to consult a doctor. You cannot just jump into training just like that.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: a. In line 11, ganun (short for ganoon) in ganun-ganun na lang means “like that.” b. In line 5, tamang pamamaraan means “the right way” or the “right process.” c. Note and learn the cognates balanse, doktor, kumonsulta and pisikal.

explanations.title: Ma-an verb affix
explanations.body: A. Categories of the ma-an verb affix. 1. Ma-an as an “able verb” (ma-an from an/han/nan). In Chapter 12, Lesson 1, you learned an/han/nan verbs. The “able” counterpart of verbs inflected in an/han/nan is ma-an. The affix denotes ability. Formula: MA + infinitive of an indirect-object verb. Because these are an/han/nan verbs, the focus is on the indirect object of the sentence or the object of the preposition. This focus can be a person, place or thing and takes Set 1 markers or Set 1 pronouns.

explanations.title: Examples from your earlier lesson and their ma-an able counterparts
explanations.body: Meaning: “to be able to or happen to…”.

explanations.title: Ma-an able verbs from the presentation
explanations.body: The indirect objects are underlined in the book where expressed. Teacher note: call students to identify the ma-an/han/nan able verb.

explanations.title: 2. Ma-an as a “feeling verb”
explanations.body: In the past you learned ma adjectives related to weather (malamig, mainit), food (maalat, masarap, mahal) and physical appearance (guwapo, pangit, maganda, malaki, maliit). Ma-an feeling verbs are formed with adjectives as root words. See the examples.

examples.text: Ikaw naiinitan pero ako nalalamigan.
examples.translation: You feel warm but I feel cold.

examples.translation: I find the souvenir you bought very expensive.

explanations.title: 3. Ma-an as an “accidental verb”
explanations.body: Unlike ma-an feeling verbs, ma-an accidental uses a verb root. In Chapter 12, Lesson 3, you learned about ma accidental verbs. Some ma accidental verbs may be converted to ma-an accidental verbs. Meaning may change depending on context and the markers used.

rows: Yoyoy offered advice to his sister.
She is sick because of work-related stress.
3. The advice offered to the sister (3-4 sentences)

(1) Don’t be stressed out. Learn to keep your balance. (2) You also need to rest. (3) While you are on leave, rest, relax, get enough sleep, and join Zumba. Anyway, it’s free. (4) Give time to yourself. (5) And do things that will make you happy.
Play the guitar again. It is Yoyoy’s sister’s hobby. Music releases tension and calms the mind.
Avoid doing exercise at night so she would be able to sleep tight.
Don’t drink strong coffee so she can sleep.
Individual, then pair work; answers vary.

explanations.title: Activity 4: sentence strips
explanations.body: Pair up and study the strips provided by your teacher. Partner A reads the first part of a sentence aloud. Partner B conjugates the verb (infinitive and tenses) and completes the sentence by adding a phrase and/or main clause. Continue until all the strips are used. Example: A: Maaasahan ko bang… B: maasahan, naasahan, naaasahan, maaasahan. Maaasahan ko bang magsara ka ng gym pagkatapos mong mag-ehersisyo? The strips are Mauunahan ni Celia, Naabutan na yata ni Conrado, Malulunasan natin kaagad, Hindi na makayanan ni Roberto, Mabibigyan kayo, Paano ba puwedeng maiwasan, Ano’ng maaaring matuklasan, Sino ang malalamangan mo, Mauumpisahan kaya natin, Bakit mapapalitan and Mabibilisan mo kaya (pair work, left out).

explanations.title: Activity 5: numbers about the National Center for Mental Health (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Listen to five sentences with numbers and write only the numbers (some sentences have more than one). Adapted from wikipilipinas.org; the image is from pp.gov.ph. The book prints the numbers as figures; the spoken text writes them in words.

examples.text: May kapasidad na apat na libo at dalawang daang pasyente ang National Center for Mental Health at may humigit kumulang na tatlong libo at apat na raang pasyente.
examples.translation: The National Center for Mental Health has a capacity of 4,200 patients and has roughly 3,400 patients.

examples.text: Itinatag ang Insular Psychopathic Hospital dahil sa Public Works Act tatlong libo dalawang daan at limampu’t walo noong ika-labimpito ng Disyembre, isang libo siyam na raan at dalawampu’t walo.
examples.translation: The Insular Psychopathic Hospital was established because of Public Works Act 3258 on December 17, 1928.

examples.text: Itinatag ang National Center for Mental Health noong ika-labindalawa ng Nobyembre isang libo siyam na raan at walumpu’t anim at pinangalanang National Center for Mental Health ayon sa Memo bilang apatnapu’t walo ng Office of the President.
examples.translation: The National Center for Mental Health was established on November 12, 1986 and named the National Center for Mental Health according to Memo No. 48 of the Office of the President.

examples.text: Nasa apatnapu’t anim punto pito ektarya ang National Center for Mental Health, kasama ang tatlumpu’t limang pavilion at limampu’t dalawang ward.
examples.translation: The National Center for Mental Health covers about 46.7 hectares, including 35 pavilions and 52 wards.

examples.text: Mga isang libo siyam na raan at siyamnapu’t tatlo ang mga tauhan ng National Center for Mental Health, kasama ang isandaan at labing-anim na doktor at tatlong daan at pitumpu’t limang nars.
examples.translation: The National Center for Mental Health has about 1,993 personnel, including 116 doctors and 375 nurses.

explanations.title: Activity 6: the benefits of exercise and walking
explanations.body: Read the passage and translate the underlined parts. Source: philstar.com. The book’s “10-minuto” is written “sampung minuto.” The book underlines parts (1) to (5), keyed in the next card.

examples.text: Alam n’yo ba na ang paglalakad ng sampung minuto kada araw ay nakakapagpataas o nakakapagpaganda ng mood ng tao?
examples.translation: Did you know that walking ten minutes a day raises or improves a person’s mood?

examples.text: Ayon sa isang pag-aaral sa United Kingdom, bukod sa nakakapagpataas ito ng kumpiyansa sa sarili ay napapababa rin nito ang stress o anumang alalahanin mo sa iyong isip.
examples.translation: According to a study in the United Kingdom, apart from boosting self-confidence it also lowers stress or any worries in your mind.

examples.text: Nadiskubre din na ang pag-eehersisyo ay kapwa nakakatulong na mapaganda ang takbo ng iyong katawan at ng iyong utak, lalo na kung ikaw ay nakakaranas ng depresyon at pagiging makakalimutin.
examples.translation: It was also discovered that exercise helps in the smooth running of both your body and your brain, especially if you are experiencing depression and being forgetful.

examples.text: Ang pagtatrabaho sa loob ng bahay at ang paglalakad ay magkaiba.
examples.translation: Working inside the house and walking are different.

examples.text: Ang pagtatrabaho sa loob ng bahay bilang ehersisyo ay mas lalong makakapagpadagdag ng iyong alalahanin kumpara sa ikaw ay maglalakad sa labas ng iyong bahay.
examples.translation: Working inside the house as exercise will further add to your worries compared with walking outside your house.

examples.text: Dito ay malilibang ka at pagpapawisan na magreresulta ng maganda mong pakiramdam.
examples.translation: Here you will be entertained and will sweat, which will result in feeling good.

explanations.title: Activity 7: caffeine
explanations.body: Read the passage and give the gist. Source: philstar.com. The book prints “2-3 tasa”; the spoken text writes it in words. The book’s key: The passage tells the readers to avoid caffeine. It says that having caffeine in one’s body is probably part of life, particularly drinking coffee, because it is effective in waking one up. However, in truth, drinking 2-3 cups of coffee increases the number of cortisol hormones in one’s body. Cortisol is a stress hormone that brings nervousness instead of alertness. The passage says that it is better to just drink cold water when one feels sleepy.

examples.text: Iwasan ang caffeine.
examples.translation: Avoid caffeine.

examples.text: Bahagi na yata ng buhay ng maraming tao ang pagkakaroon ng caffeine sa katawan, partikular na ang pag-inom ng kape dahil ito ay mabisang pampagising.
examples.translation: Having caffeine in the body is probably already part of many people’s lives, particularly drinking coffee because it is an effective wake-up aid.

examples.text: Pero, sa totoo lang, ang pag-inom ng dalawa hanggang tatlong tasa ng kape ay nagpapadami ng bilang ng cortisol hormone sa iyong katawan.
examples.translation: But, in truth, drinking two to three cups of coffee increases the number of cortisol hormones in your body.

examples.text: Ang cortisol ay isang stress hormone at nagdadala ito ng nerbiyos sa halip na maging alerto.
examples.translation: Cortisol is a stress hormone and it brings nervousness instead of making you alert.

examples.text: Mas mabuti pang uminom na lang ng malamig na tubig kapag nakakaramdam ng pagkaantok.
examples.translation: It is better to just drink cold water when you feel sleepy.

lessons.title: 308. C16 L2 · Listening: sleep, exercise and fitness tests
lessons.subtitle: Matulog nang maaga, walong oras · Pagsabak ng mga pulis sa ten story ascension test · Iwas obesity

explanations.title: Activity 8: three passages (the book’s scripts)
explanations.body: Listen to three passages and complete the items. Teacher note: repeat the audio as needed.

examples.text: Juanito, si Nanay ito. Huwag mong kalimutan ang sinabi ko tungkol sa tulog. Sapat na tulog lang ang kailangan mo. Mga walong oras. Matulog ka nang maaga. Kailangan, alas-diyes pa lang natutulog ka na. Gigising ka nang maaga kinabukasan ano? Balita ko maaga kang nagigising. Kailangan mong matulog ng alas-diyes at gumising nang alas-sais. Walong oras na yon. Wag na wag kang uminom ng sleeping pills, ha? Masama iyan. Sapat na tulog lang ang kailangan mo. Tumawag ka o ako na ang tatawag bukas.
examples.translation: Passage 1: a mom’s voice message to her son: Juanito, this is Nanay. Don’t forget what I told you about sleep. Enough sleep is all you need. About eight hours. Go to sleep early. By ten o’clock you should already be asleep. You will wake up early the next day, right? I heard you wake up early. You need to sleep at ten and wake up at six. That is eight hours. Never take sleeping pills, okay? That is bad. Enough sleep is all you need. Call me or I will call tomorrow.

examples.text: Simpleng paglalakad, konting takbo, pag-i-iswimming, pag-ba-bike. Ilan lamang iyan ang nirerekomenda ng maraming espesyalista sa mga taong nakakaramdam na ng negatibo sa kanilang katawan. Maaaring ang ganitong mga aktibidades ay magagaan lamang. Pero malaki na ang naitutulong nito para lumakas ang resistensiya at may panangga na sa mga sakit. Mas lalong makakamit ang inaasahang kalusugan kung sasabayan pa ito ng tamang diet.
examples.translation: Passage 2: an excerpt from a documentary: Simple walking, a little running, swimming, biking. Those are only a few of what many specialists recommend to people who already feel something negative in their bodies. These activities may be light only. But they already help a lot in strengthening immunity and providing protection against diseases. The expected health will be even better achieved if this is accompanied by the proper diet.

examples.text: Nagsasagawa ang Department of Health ng mga kampanyang magbibigay pagpapahalaga sa kalusugan. Isa na nga rito ang Bawas Timbang thru Zumba Fitness. Pinaniniwalaan ding isang epektibong kasangkapan ang pagsasayaw sa paghihikayat sa mga Pilipino, lalo na sa mga kabataan. Hindi lang waistline ang mababantayan at napapangalagaan, kundi pati na rin ang mga malubhang sakit ay maaaring mawala o maiwasan.
examples.translation: Passage 3: an excerpt from a news report: The Department of Health is conducting campaigns that will give importance to health. One of these is Bawas Timbang thru Zumba Fitness. Dancing is also believed to be an effective tool in encouraging Filipinos, especially the youth. Not only the waistline can be watched and cared for, but serious illnesses may also disappear or be avoided.

rows: Mom reminded her son about his sleeping habit.
Passage 1, item 2: the mom’s advice (3 details)
(1) Sleep eight hours, from 10 PM to 6 AM; (2) don’t take sleeping pills; (3) it’s bad for the health; (4) you just need enough sleep.
Passage 2, item 3: three activities recommended by specialists
Passage 2, item 4: one more piece of advice
Passage 3, item 5: what the DOH launched
A campaign for a healthy lifestyle through dancing (Bawas Timbang or Zumba Fitness); giving importance to health through dancing.
Passage 3, item 6: two positive effects of dancing
Care for a (slimmer) waistline; cure or avoidance of acute illnesses.

explanations.title: Activity 9: physical fitness training of the Philippine National Police (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Listen to an excerpt of a news report and complete the chart. Source: ncrpo.pnp.gov.ph and scola.org. The book prints “Kandahingal”; I keep it as printed.

examples.text: Kandahingal po ang mga babae at lalaking pulis sa pagsabak nila sa ten story ascension test. Kasama po sa hamon ng physical test ang mapanhik ng lalaking pulis ang sampung palapag ng gusali sa loob lang ng dalawang minuto at apatnapung segundo. Tatlong minuto at labinlimang segundo naman ang hamon sa kababaihan. Bago pumanhik sa gusali todo push up, sit up at takbo ang mga pulis sa Camp Bagong Diwa, Taguig. Naunang sumalang ang may isandaan at dalawampung pulis sa semestral physical fitness program. Pero absent ang mga matataba at umiwas bumagsak sa exam. At sa paunang resulta, apat na porsyento ng mga opisyal ang lumagpak. Ang ten story ascension test ang gagamiting basehan sa promosyon ng mga pulis.
examples.translation: Reporter: The policemen and policewomen were out of breath in taking the ten-story ascension test. Part of the challenge of the physical test is for a policeman to climb the ten floors of the building in only two minutes and forty seconds. For the women the challenge is three minutes and fifteen seconds. Before climbing the building, the police did all-out push-ups, sit-ups and running at Camp Bagong Diwa, Taguig. About one hundred twenty police went first in the semestral physical fitness program. But the fat ones, who avoided failing the exam, were absent. And in the preliminary result, four percent of the officers failed. The ten-story ascension test will be used as the basis for promotion of the police.

rows: Absent but were supposed to participate
The fat ones who avoided failing the exam
Camp Bagong Diwa, City of Taguig
Policemen should be able to go up the 10-story building in 2 minutes and 40 seconds; the women in 3 minutes and 15 seconds
Four percent of the officers failed

explanations.title: Activity 10: two pieces of advice from SIGLA (Vitality)
explanations.body: From Panahon TV’s program SIGLA. Complete the Venn diagram: differences in the left and right parts and similarities in the middle. Compare your answers with a partner, then write a title or caption for each passage and one for both. The book’s URLs are left out.

examples.text: Para mapanatiling malakas at malusog ang ating mga katawan, uminom ng walong basong tubig araw-araw. Takpan ang ilong kapag nasa labas ng bahay para hindi makalanghap ng polusyon. Maglaan ng isang oras araw-araw para mag-ehersisyo. Sikaping matulog nang walong oras kada araw. At ang pinaka-importante, ugaliing kumain ng masusustansiyang pagkain. Alagaan ang kalusugan upang maka-iwas sa sakit at mapasigla ang pangangatawan.
examples.translation: Passage 1: To keep our bodies strong and healthy, drink eight glasses of water every day. Cover your nose when you are outside the house so you do not inhale pollution. Set aside one hour every day for exercise. Try to sleep eight hours a day. And most important, make it a habit to eat nutritious foods. Take care of your health to avoid illness and to invigorate the body.

examples.text: Paano kung nasobrahan ka na sa pagkain? Isang kondisyon kung saan mayroong sobra kaysa sa kailangang taba ang katawan ng isang tao na maaaring magbunga ng masamang epekto sa kanyang kalusugan. Para maiwasan ito, kumain ng gulay, prutas at mahihiblang pagkain. Iwasan din ang sobrang pagkain. Uminom ng walo hanggang labindalawang baso ng tubig kada araw. Ugaliin ding mag-ehersisyo o maglaan ng oras para sa mga gawaing pisikal gaya ng simpleng paglalakad at paggamit ng hagdan kaysa elevator. Para naman sa may mga malalang kaso ng obesity, kumunsulta sa doktor para malaman kung kailangan nang uminom ng gamot. O kaya nama’y maisailalim sa operasyong tinatawag na bariatric surgery.
examples.translation: Passage 2: What if you have overeaten? A condition where a person’s body has more fat than needed, which may result in bad effects on his health. To avoid this, eat vegetables, fruit and fibrous food. Also avoid overeating. Drink eight to twelve glasses of water a day. Make it a habit also to exercise or set aside time for physical activities such as simple walking and using the stairs rather than the elevator. As for those with severe cases of obesity, consult a doctor to know whether medicine is needed. Or else they may undergo an operation called bariatric surgery.

explanations.title: Activity 10: the diagram’s content (from the book)

rows: Maintain a strong, healthy body. Cover your mouth when out of the house so you don’t inhale pollution. Sleep eight hours each day. Take care of your health to avoid diseases and give vitality to the body.
Drink 8 (or 8 to 12) glasses of water every day. Exercise or do physical activity (an hour a day in passage 1). Eat nutritious foods (fruits, vegetables and fiber-rich foods).

Avoid obesity and its bad effects. Avoid overeating. Do physical activities (walking, using the stairs, not the elevator). Those with severe obesity: consult a doctor to know if you need anti-obesity medicine or surgery.

lessons.title: 309. C16 L2 · Speaking: tips for body and mind; glossary and ma-an sentences
lessons.subtitle: Tips para sa magaang na pakiramdam · Physical and mental tips · Glossary at mga halimbawang pangungusap

explanations.title: Activity 11: two feature articles on better physical and mental health
explanations.body: Discuss the articles and share the tips. (a) Form two small groups of three; Group A reads Article A, Group B reads Article B, and fills in a chart. (b) In Tagalog, tell the other group the content of your article. (c) Discuss the similarities and differences between the tips on a diagram (differences left and right, similarities in the middle). (d) Consolidate the tips in your own words on a flip chart, whiteboard or SmartBoard, categorized by physical and mental health. Teacher note: ask the students to just skim the articles; they are very practical tips, and students have heard them as early as boot camp. Group work, left out; the two articles (adapted from Remate) are given here.

explanations.title: Article A: Tips para sa magaang na pakiramdam
explanations.body: The book’s capital-letter headings are in normal case and the quotation marks are dropped.

examples.text: Huwag Kalimutang Mag-almusal.
examples.translation: Do not forget to eat breakfast.

examples.text: Siyento porsiyentong gagaan ang inyong pakiramdam at gagana pa ang inyong utak.
examples.translation: You will feel one hundred percent lighter and your brain will work too.

examples.text: Huwag Bilisan ang Pagkain.
examples.translation: Do not eat too fast.

examples.text: Nagiging dahilan ng over eating ang mabilis na pagkain.
examples.translation: Eating fast becomes a cause of overeating.

examples.text: Nagiging labis ang kinakain, na nagiging dahilan naman upang bumagal ang pagkilos ng digestive system.
examples.translation: What is eaten becomes too much, which in turn slows the movement of the digestive system.

examples.text: Pero subukan ninyong kumain nang mabagal.
examples.translation: But try to eat slowly.

examples.text: Tiyak ninyong mismong utak ninyo ang magsasabing tama na busog ka na.
examples.translation: Be sure your own brain will say, enough, you are full.

examples.text: Kumain Kapag Nagugutom.
examples.translation: Eat when you are hungry.

examples.text: Ang di pagkain sa loob ng apat o limang oras ay nagiging dahilan ng pagbaba ng blood sugar.
examples.translation: Not eating for four or five hours becomes a cause of a drop in blood sugar.

examples.text: Nawawalan ng enerhiya at nakakaramdam agad ng sobrang pagod at palaging pagkagutom.
examples.translation: You lose energy and immediately feel too tired and always hungry.

examples.text: Kumain Nang Kumain.
examples.translation: Keep eating.

examples.text: May taong kapag naiinis o wala sa mood ay agad nawawalan ng ganang kumain ng heavy meals.
examples.translation: Some people, when annoyed or not in the mood, immediately lose the appetite to eat heavy meals.

examples.text: May mga tao namang takot tumaba at iniiwasang kumain nang madalas.
examples.translation: Other people are afraid to get fat and avoid eating often.

examples.text: Kung gutom, kumain nang kumain at huwag mangamba.
examples.translation: If you are hungry, keep eating and do not worry.

examples.text: Kapag hindi naman, huwag pagbuhusan ng pansin ang chips o cookies.
examples.translation: If not, do not pay attention to chips or cookies.

examples.text: Matulog sa Tamang Oras.
examples.translation: Sleep at the right time.

examples.text: Ayon sa pag-aaral, ang mga taong pagod ay mas marami ang ikinakain kaysa sa ipinapahinga.
examples.translation: According to a study, tired people eat more than they rest.

examples.text: Kaya naman ang kinalabasan, kapag nakakaramdam ng pagkaantok ay agad na nagpapatimpla ng kape o kaya ay umiinom ng soft drinks.
examples.translation: So the result is that when they feel sleepy they immediately have coffee prepared or drink soft drinks.

examples.text: Mainam kung madidisiplina ang sarili, matulog sa tamang oras sa ikagagaan na rin ng pakiramdam.
examples.translation: It is good to discipline yourself, sleep at the right time to also feel lighter.

explanations.title: Article B: Physical and mental tips
explanations.body: The book’s “(the no-brainer),” “(waistline-friendly ang mga ito)” and the figures 30, 4-6 are rewritten for the spoken text.

examples.text: Move it or lose it. Maglaan ng tatlumpung minutong ehersisyo kahit sa paglalakad lang sa park.
examples.translation: Move it or lose it. Set aside thirty minutes of exercise even if only walking in the park.

examples.text: Fruits and veggies. Maglaan ng five to seven servings ng prutas at gulay sa isang araw.
examples.translation: Fruits and veggies. Set aside five to seven servings of fruit and vegetables a day.

examples.text: Hindi lang ito iwas cancer, nakakapagpalusog pa ito ng ating puso, nakakapagbigay rin ito ng fiber, na nakatutulong sa atin upang sumeksi.
examples.translation: They not only prevent cancer, they also make our heart healthier and give fiber, which helps us to look sexy (they are waistline-friendly).

examples.text: Simplify your life, immediately. Minsan hinahayaan nating maging masalimuot at komplikado ang ating buhay.
examples.translation: Simplify your life, immediately. Sometimes we let our life become complicated and complex.

examples.text: Maraming pinagkakaabalahang wala namang kapararakan.
examples.translation: There are many things we are busy with that are worthless.

examples.text: Aba, kung gusto mong maging healthy, bawasan mo ang mga ito.
examples.translation: Well, if you want to be healthy, cut these down.

examples.text: Kinakailangan mo nang baguhin ang iyong lifestyle, mas simple mas maganda, hindi ba?
examples.translation: You need to change your lifestyle now, the simpler the better, right?

examples.text: Take a multi-vitamin. Napaka-basic.
examples.translation: Take a multi-vitamin. Very basic.

examples.text: Kinakailangan talagang mag-take ng vitamins para panlaban sa nakakapagod na pang-araw-araw nating gawain.
examples.translation: We really need to take vitamins to fight our tiring daily activities.

examples.text: Get your Zzzzz’s. Magkaroon ng pito hanggang walong oras na tulog.
examples.translation: Get your Zzzzz’s. Have seven to eight hours of sleep.

examples.text: Improve your attitude. Magbigay ng effort para magkaroon ka ng magandang attitude.
examples.translation: Improve your attitude. Make an effort to have a good attitude.

examples.text: Feed your body well, and feed it often. Kung nais mo nang maraming energy, kumain ng apat hanggang anim a day.
examples.translation: Feed your body well, and feed it often. If you want a lot of energy, eat four to six a day.

examples.text: Kumain ng mga pagkaing mayaman sa protein, fruits and veggies.
examples.translation: Eat foods rich in protein, fruits and veggies.

examples.text: Drink your water! Uminom ng walong baso ng tubig araw-araw.
examples.translation: Drink your water! Drink eight glasses of water every day.

explanations.title: Activity 12: role play, trainer and trainee
explanations.body: Pair up; each pair gets a set of role-play cards. Partner A plays a trainer and Partner B a trainee; study your card and decide what to say, then switch roles. Trainer card: you have been tasked to serve as personal physical-fitness trainer to a junior service personnel in your company. The trainee will ask questions. Respond and tell the trainee about nutritional and medical information relative to physical training, frequency of training, different training exercises for arms, legs, chest, etc., any personal advice, and additional information from your experience. Trainee card: you are tasked to do physical-fitness training under a senior service personnel in your company. Ask about the importance of physical fitness, any nutritional and medical information you need to know before training, how often to train, the best time of day to train, and additional questions (role play, left out).

examples.translation: A person who is healthy and mentally alert can be relied on at work.

examples.translation: Can you invite Miguel and Tasha to our Zumba?

examples.text: Nabansagan si Boyet na mataba ng mga klase niya.

examples.text: Nabigyan nila ng pansin ang mga ugat ng depresyon ni Kuya.
examples.translation: They gave attention to the roots of Kuya’s depression.

examples.translation: Can you bring fruit to Jerico so that his nervousness lessens?

examples.text: Kailangan magawan na ng paraan ang pagbawas ng timbang ko.
examples.translation: A way needs to be found to reduce my weight.

examples.text: Nahihirapan akong gumising ng maaga upang mag-ehersisyo.
examples.translation: I have difficulty waking up early to exercise.

examples.translation: When will you be able to invite Lucy and Jaime to the house?

examples.text: Naintindihan mo ba ang mga itinuro ni Binibining Salazar?
examples.translation: Did you understand what Miss Salazar taught?

examples.text: Hindi kami naiwanan ng hapunan ni Inay.
examples.translation: Inay did not leave us without dinner.

examples.text: Paano mo ba maiiwasan ang sobrang taba sa mga masasarap na pagkain?

units.title: Chapter 16 · Lesson 3: Health concerns and issues

lessons.title: 310. C16 L3 · Malnutrition, sanitation and HIV-AIDS
lessons.subtitle: Kakulangan sa nutrisyon · Kagutuman at kahirapan · Kubeta at kalinisan · HIV-AIDS

explanations.title: Objectives
explanations.body: By the end of this lesson you can extract information from reading and listening passages about health concerns and issues; transcribe numbers and sentences and translate sentences related to health concerns and issues; describe health issues and recommend measures to solve them; and ask and answer simple questions related to health issues. The structures are the core vocabulary and ka-an/han/nan nouns.

explanations.title: Getting started
explanations.body: Look at the pictures (left out). Describe and share what you see in three or four phrases, complete sentences or expressions in Tagalog. Teacher note: lead students toward the lesson topic.

explanations.title: Presentation 1: an excerpt from a module on achieving a healthy lifestyle
explanations.body: Sources: philstar.com and remate.ph. The book’s “27 kaso” is written “dalawampu’t pitong kaso”.

examples.text: Mahigit tatlong milyong bata na may edad limang taon pababa ay nakitaang may kalabisang kakulangan sa nutrisyon bunga ng hindi sapat na pagkain o sustansya.
examples.translation: More than three million children aged five years and below were observed to have acute malnutrition as a result of insufficient food or nutrients.

examples.text: Aabot din sa milyon ang bilang ng mga kulang sa tangkad at kulang sa bigat.
examples.translation: The number of those below normal height and underweight also reaches a million.

examples.text: Dahil sa kahirapan laganap ang kagutuman.
examples.translation: Because of poverty, hunger is widespread.

examples.text: Kung may panustos man, hindi naman ito sapat lalo na sa malaking pamilya.
examples.translation: Even if there is a provision, it is not enough, especially for a big family.

examples.text: Malaki rin ang suliranin sa kalinisan.
examples.translation: The problem with cleanliness is also big.

examples.text: Sa katunayan, tinatayang aabot sa halos tatlumpung milyong Pilipino ang walang kubeta at kung saan-saan na lamang dumudumi.
examples.translation: In fact, it is estimated that almost thirty million Filipinos have no toilet and simply defecate anywhere.

examples.text: Karamihan umano na walang kubeta ay yung mga nasa kanayunan.
examples.translation: Reportedly, most of those without toilets are those in the countryside.

examples.text: Hindi rin lahat ay may kakayahang magkaroon ng sariling palikuran.
examples.translation: Also, not everyone is able to have their own toilet.

examples.text: Nakakaalarma rin ang paglaganap ng HIV-AIDS.
examples.translation: The spread of HIV-AIDS is also alarming.

examples.text: Nasa ikatlong puwesto ang Pilipinas sa buong mundo na may pinakamaraming kaso ng HIV-AIDS.
examples.translation: The Philippines is in third place in the whole world with the most cases of HIV-AIDS.

examples.text: Aabot sa dalawampu’t pitong kaso kada araw ang naitatala sa Pilipinas.
examples.translation: Twenty-seven cases a day are recorded in the Philippines.

examples.text: Kakulangan sa kaalaman ang kadalasang dahilan dito.
examples.translation: Lack of knowledge is often the reason for this.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: a. In paragraph 1, line 1, limang taon pababa means “five years old and below.” b. In paragraph 2, line 2, the synonyms for kubeta are kasilyas, palikuran and banyo. c. Note and learn the Spanish cognates edad, nutrisyon, sustansya, puwesto, kaso and kada. d. The book’s translation of tatlumpung milyong as “3 million” in its grammar section is a slip; tatlumpung milyon is thirty million.

explanations.title: New words
explanations.body: The book prints nakitaan(g) and kabila(ng), with the linker ng in parentheses; they are written nakitaang and kabilang here so they can be read aloud.

rows: observed to have; demonstrated [the symptoms of]

explanations.title: Comprehension check (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Part b asks you to share one or two major health concerns of your own state or country and ask a partner; it is left out.

rows: a.1 Three major health concerns mentioned

(1) More than 3 million children, 5 years old and below, are said to be excessively malnourished as a result of insufficient food or lack of nutrients; (2) also reaching almost 1 million are children who are below normal height and underweight.
(1) Hunger is widespread because of poverty; (2) if there is any food supply or provision, it is not enough, especially for a big family.
a.4 The concern about cleanliness (3 details)

(1) Cleanliness is also one of the health concerns; (2) it is estimated that almost 30 million Filipinos do not have restrooms and they move their bowels anywhere; (3) most of those who do not have restrooms are in the provinces; (4) not everyone can afford to have their own restroom.
a.5 Why HIV-AIDS is a concern
The Philippines is third in the world in the number of HIV-AIDS cases. Every day there are 27 recorded cases. Most often the reason for the increase is lack of information.

lessons.title: 311. C16 L3 · A medical mission
lessons.subtitle: Salamat po sa libreng medical mission · Tipus at pagtatae · Iisa ang poso dito

explanations.title: Presentation 2: a health worker and a local resident
explanations.body: A is the local resident and B is the health worker; during the medical mission by the US and Philippine military forces. The book’s ‘Yung is written Yung. Images from doh.gov.ph (left out).

examples.text: Salamat po sa libreng medical mission. Marami dito ang hindi pa nakakita ng doktor. Yung health center po nasa kabilang isla po, sa kabisera. Wala din silang doktor dun.
examples.translation: A: Thank you for the free medical mission. Many here have not yet seen a doctor. The health center is on the other island, in the capital. They don’t have a doctor there either.

examples.text: Tulong po ito ng DOH kasama ng mga sundalo. May libreng gamot, pagpapagamot, bakuna sa tao at sa hayop.
examples.translation: B: This is help from the DOH together with the soldiers. There is free medicine, treatment, and vaccines for people and for animals.

examples.text: Tamang-tama po. Paparami po kasi ngayon ang namamatay sa tipus at pagtatae dahil sa kontaminadong tubig. Sa ilog pa po kami umiigib. Ang layo pa ng ilog. Bihira nga kaming makapaligo.
examples.translation: A: That is very timely. The deaths from typhoid and diarrhea are increasing now because of contaminated water. We still fetch water from the river. The river is far. We seldom even get to bathe.

examples.text: Sabi nga ni Kapitan, iisa ang poso dito. Wala raw kubeta ang paaralan at pati na rin ang maraming residente dito. Hindi bale, magtutulungan po ang mga kasundaluhan at mga kalalakihan dito na magtayo ng mga palikuran. Gagawa rin po ng poso at maglalagay ng bomba ng tubig.
examples.translation: B: The Captain said there is only one deep well here. They say the school has no toilet and neither do many residents here. Never mind, the soldiers and the men here will help each other build toilets. They will also make a deep well and put up a water pump.

explanations.title: Notes and expressions
explanations.body: a. In line 2, synonyms for kabisera are punong lungsod, kabayanan and kapital. b. In line 3, DOH is Department of Health. c. In line 8, the synonym for poso (deep well) is balon. Poso (deep well) is different from poso negro (sewage).

rows: to be able to take a bath

explanations.title: Comprehension check (the book’s key)
explanations.body: Part c asks you to suggest two or three more recommendations to help the residents; it is pair work and is left out.

rows: 1. Four services offered by the US and Philippine military and the DOH
(1) Free medical check-up and medication; (2) medicines; (3) human vaccine; (4) animal vaccine.
2. Why the medical mission is timely
Because deaths from typhoid fever and diarrhea are increasing.
3. Possible causes of the typhoid and diarrhea outbreak (4)
(1) Contaminated water, with no access to clean water; (2) there is only one deep well; (3) no restroom in the school; (4) most residents do not have toilets.

A lot of local residents haven’t seen a doctor yet. The barangay does not have a health center. The health center is located in the town proper, the capital, which is on the nearby island. Even the health center in the capital does not have a doctor.
The water is contaminated. The residents get water from a river which is far from their place. There is only one deep well in the barangay.

explanations.title: Activity 1: the essential elements (the book’s key, at least seven)

rows: Two barangays in Cebu hit by a typhoid outbreak.
The barangays are Sta. Felomena and Poblacion.
It was believed that the typhoid outbreak is caused by contaminated drinking water.
The contaminated water is said to be coming from a creek.
The provinces are not the only ones suffering from the absence of clean water.
Even Metro Manila residents get their water from deep wells contaminated by animal and human feces.
The water pipes are soaked in dirt and this is what the residents are getting.
The result is illnesses such as cholera, typhoid fever and diarrhea.
There are those who die because they cannot afford to pay hospital bills.

explanations.title: Ka-an/han/nan noun formation
explanations.body: You were first introduced to ka-an/han/nan in Chapter 14, Lesson 2. Nouns can be derived from adjectives, verbs and other nouns. In this lesson you learn more examples. A. Examples from the reading presentation.

explanations.title: Sentences from the presentation (translated)
explanations.body: The book asks you to translate eight sentences; the translations below are the book’s answers, with two slips fixed: sentence 5 says “almost 3 million” (it is thirty million) and sentence 4 says “huger” (it means bigger). Note: kadalasan in sentence 8 is an adverb, not a noun.

examples.text: Mahigit tatlong milyong bata na may edad limang taon pababa ay nakitaang may kalabisang kakulangan sa nutrisyon bunga ng hindi sapat na pagkain o sustansya.
examples.translation: More than three million children aged five years and below were observed to have a severe lack of nutrition due to lack of food and nutrients.

examples.text: Dahil sa kahirapan laganap ang kagutuman.
examples.translation: Due to poverty hunger is widespread.

examples.text: Wala pa rin silang kakayahan na bumili ng masustansiyang pagkain.
examples.translation: They still don’t have the means to buy nutritious food.

examples.text: Malaki rin ang suliranin sa kalinisan.
examples.translation: The problem of cleanliness (sanitation) is also big.

examples.text: Sa katunayan, tinatayang aabot sa halos tatlumpung milyong Pilipino ang walang kubeta.
examples.translation: In fact, it is estimated that almost thirty million Filipinos have no toilets.

examples.text: Karamihan umano na walang kubeta ay yung mga nasa kanayunan.
examples.translation: It is reported that most of those without toilets are those in the countryside.

examples.text: Hindi rin lahat ay may kakayahang magkaroon ng sariling palikuran.
examples.translation: Not everyone has the ability to have their own toilet.

examples.text: Kakulangan sa kaalaman ang kadalasang dahilan dito.
examples.translation: Lack of knowledge is often the reason for this problem.

lessons.title: 313. C16 L3 · Ka-an/han/nan: spelling and suffix rules
lessons.subtitle: O sa u, d sa r, e sa i · An, han at nan · Mula sugnay tungo sa parirala

explanations.title: B. Some rules to remember: 1. Spelling rules
explanations.body: When the last syllable of the root word contains the letter o, change it to u.

explanations.title: The letter d becomes r
explanations.body: When the root word starts or ends with d, change it to r.

explanations.title: The letter e becomes i
explanations.body: When the root word ends in e, change it to i.

explanations.title: 2. Rules for choosing the suffix an/han/nan: an
explanations.body: An is affixed to root words ending in a consonant.

explanations.title: Han
explanations.body: Han is affixed to root words ending in a vowel (see the e to i table above): babae, kababaihan; lalake, kalalakihan; salbahe, kasalbahihan.

explanations.title: Nan
explanations.body: Nan is used mostly for irregular formations, with root words ending in n or with a dropped terminal vowel.

explanations.title: 3. A clause can be converted to a phrase using ka-an/han/nan
explanations.body: The noun clause on the left becomes the phrase on the right.

explanations.title: The markers of ka-an/han/nan nouns
explanations.body: Ka-an/han/nan noun formations, being abstract words, are preceded by the markers ang (Set 1, as the focus of the sentence), ng (Set 2, as a non-focus) and sa (Set 3, as the object of a preposition). In the examples above, dahil sa is Set 3 (preposition) and ang is Set 1 (focus of the sentence).

explanations.title: Activity 2: change the bolded words to ka-an/han/nan nouns
explanations.body: The eleven English sentences are: 1. Mr. Gabriel is a good man. 2. The old sewage system will soon be replaced. 3. Is the old senator still pushing House Bill 1548? 4. According to FNRI reports, children five years and younger are malnourished. 5. The American soldiers were helping clear the streets of mud. 6. The police force is not doing a good job of keeping peace in the town. 7. Many of the towns still have no clean water. 8. Healthy children still need to be seen by their doctors regularly. 9. Do you know how many were reported dead from typhoid fever? 10. Did you just buy a new house? 11. There are many health centers in Greater Manila. For each bolded word, give the Tagalog, then the noun in the right column. The book gives the Tagalog words (mabait, luma, …) and the nouns in the ka-an, ka-han or ka-nan column; the English meanings are mine.

explanations.title: Activity 5: a story told in a circle
explanations.body: Sit in a circle. Your teacher gives you a phrase or clause; use it to create a sentence with a ka-an/han/nan noun to start a story. The classmate on your right continues with a sentence using another ka-an/han/nan phrase, until everyone has had a turn; then start a second story. The teacher’s example is Maraming problema sa mga liblib na bahagi ng bansa; Student A continues with “… dahil walang kapayapaan doon”; Student B with “Isa sa problemang ito ang kawalan ng …”. lessons.title: 315. C16 L3 · HIV-AIDS figures, toilets and food safety
lessons.subtitle: Kaso ng HIV noong dalawang libo at labinlima · Pitong milyon at limandaang libong walang kubeta · Ligtas na pagkain

explanations.title: Activity 6: a news report about HIV-AIDS cases (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Listen to excerpts of a news report. (a) Transcribe the sentences or phrases and numbers, writing numbers in figures. (b) Give the meaning of each sentence. (c) Give the gist. The book prints the numbers as figures (2015, 7,000, 38%, 15%, 11%, 5%, 96%, 25 to 34); the spoken text writes them in words. The audio is left out.

examples.text: Sa iba pang balita, tumaas ang bilang ng kaso ng Human Immuno Deficiency Virus o ng HIV-Virus sa taong dalawang libo at labinlima.
examples.translation: In other news, the number of cases of the Human Immuno Deficiency Virus, or HIV virus, rose in the year 2015.

examples.text: Ayon sa Philippine HIV or Aids registry nasa mahigit pitong libong kaso na ang naitalang HIV cases sa loob lamang ng labing isang buwan sa taong dalawang libo at labinlima.
examples.translation: According to the Philippine HIV or AIDS registry, more than seven thousand HIV cases have been recorded in just eleven months in the year 2015.

examples.text: Tatlumpu’t walong porsiyento ang may HIV sa Metro Manila.
examples.translation: Thirty-eight percent have HIV in Metro Manila.

examples.text: Sinundan naman ito ng CALABARZON na may labinlimang porsiyento, labing-isang porsiyento sa Central Visayas, limang porsiyento naman sa Western Visayas.
examples.translation: It was followed by CALABARZON with fifteen percent, eleven percent in Central Visayas, and five percent in Western Visayas.

examples.text: Sa kabuuan, siyamnapu’t anim na porsiyento dito ay puro lalaki at may edad na dalawampu’t lima hanggang tatlumpu’t apat.
examples.translation: In total, ninety-six percent of these are all male and aged twenty-five to thirty-four.

examples.text: Isandaan at pitumpu’t apat na ang naitalang nasawi dahil sa naturang sakit.
examples.translation: One hundred seventy-four deaths from the said disease have already been recorded.

explanations.title: Activity 6: the gist (the book’s key)
explanations.body: This passage is about the number of HIV cases in 2015. In only 11 months more than 7,000 HIV cases were recorded. 38% have HIV in Metro Manila, followed by CALABARZON at 15%, 11% in Central Visayas, 5% in Western Visayas. 96% are male, ages 25 to 34. 174 HIV deaths were already recorded.

explanations.title: Activity 7: the lack of toilets
explanations.body: Read the news item and translate it. Source: philstar.com. The book’s translation gives “Putting Bato” (the place is Isla Puting Bato) and “toilerts” (toilets); both are corrected here, and its figure 7.5 million is written in words in the spoken text.

examples.text: Nabatid na umaabot sa pitong milyon at limandaang libong Pinoy ang walang kubeta at sa labas na lamang ng kanilang mga bahay nagsisidumi.
examples.translation: It was learned that seven and a half million Filipinos have no toilet and just defecate outside their homes.

examples.text: Karamihan sa mga walang malinis na palikuran ay mga mamamayan sa Masbate, Negros Occidental, Maguindanao, Tawi Tawi at iba pang lugar gayundin sa Luzon.
examples.translation: Most of those without clean toilets are citizens in Masbate, Negros Occidental, Maguindanao, Tawi Tawi and other places, also in Luzon.

examples.text: Sa Maynila, binanggit ang mga matataong lugar gaya ng Isla Puting Bato, Baseco, Radial Sampu, sa Tondo, bahagi ng Quiapo at iba pang naninirahan sa mga gilid ng ilog at mga kalsada.
examples.translation: In Manila, populous places were mentioned such as Isla Puting Bato, Baseco, Radial 10 in Tondo, parts of Quiapo and others who live on the banks of rivers and along roads.

explanations.title: Activity 8: food safety rules from the FDA
explanations.body: Read the excerpts and write down three safety rules. Adapted from philstar.com. The book’s “pangkula” is bleach.

examples.text: Ayon kay Dr. Go, kailangan maging maingat ang publiko sa pagbili ng pagkain at paghahanda nito.
examples.translation: According to Dr. Go, the public needs to be careful in buying and preparing food.

examples.text: Ito ay para makaiwas sa sakit na food poisoning at pagtatae.
examples.translation: This is to avoid food poisoning and diarrhea.

examples.text: Bumili ng pagkain sa mga kilalang tindahan.
examples.translation: Buy food from well-known stores.

examples.text: Hindi natin masisiguro ang kalinisan ng mga karne, hamon at hotdog na gawa lamang sa tabi-tabi.
examples.translation: We cannot be sure of the cleanliness of meat, ham and hotdogs made just anywhere.

examples.text: Suriin maigi na hindi botcha at bilasang isda ang bibilhin.
examples.translation: Check carefully that what you buy is not diseased meat or stale fish.

examples.text: Lagyan ng marka ang botelya at lalagyan ng mga sangkap ng pagkain tulad ng asin, asukal at mantika.
examples.translation: Put a label on bottles and containers of food ingredients such as salt, sugar and cooking oil.

examples.text: Lagyan din ng marka ang mga gamit pambahay tulad ng sabon, pangkula, pamatay ng insekto at gasolina.
examples.translation: Also label household items such as soap, bleach, insecticide and gasoline.

examples.text: Huwag pagtabi-tabihin ang mga nasabing botelya dahil baka malagyan ng lason ang iyong pagkain.
examples.translation: Do not put the said bottles side by side because poison may get into your food.

explanations.title: Activity 8: safety rules (the book’s key; any three)

rows: Be careful in buying and preparing food to avoid food poisoning and diarrhea.
Buy your food from well-known stores. We cannot be sure of the cleanliness of meat, ham and hotdogs that are made in unsafe places.
Examine the meat and fish very well and make sure they are fresh.
Label bottles that are used for food, such as salt, etc.
Also mark cleaning materials like soap, etc.
Don’t place food and cleaning containers together, to avoid placing the wrong ingredients in the wrong containers.

explanations.title: Activity 9: two passages about public health (the book’s scripts)
explanations.body: Listen to the two passages. In Tagalog, identify the phrases or sentences about public health concerns, as specifically as possible; in English, fill in the last column. Sources: philstar.com. The book prints the ratios as 1:50, 1:25, 1:55, 1:93 and the numbers as 1.7 billion, 850 million and 780 million; the spoken text writes them in words. The audio is left out.

examples.text: Isa sa mga pinakamahalagang pangangailangan ng mga mag-aaral ay ang palikuran. Ayon sa World Health Organization, isa sa limampu ang nararapat na toilet pupil ratio para sa mga kalalakihan sa mga pampublikong paaralan, habang isa sa dalawampu’t lima naman ang sa kababaihan. Pero ibang-iba ang nangyayari sa mga pampublikong paaralan sa bansa. Isa sa limampu’t lima ang toilet pupil ratio sa elementarya, habang isa sa siyamnapu’t tatlo naman sa high school. Kulang din ang mga paaralan sa mga hugasan ng kamay. Napakahalaga pa naman ang simpleng health practice na ito para maiwasan ang maraming mga sakit.
examples.translation: Passage 1: One of the most important needs of students is the toilet. According to the World Health Organization, the proper toilet-pupil ratio for males in public schools is one to fifty, while for females it is one to twenty-five. But what happens in the country’s public schools is very different. The toilet-pupil ratio is one to fifty-five in elementary school, and one to ninety-three in high school. The schools also lack hand-washing facilities. And yet this simple health practice is very important to prevent many diseases.

examples.text: Sa nakaraang pag-aaral ng ADB aabot sa isang bilyon at pitong daang milyong tao sa Asya at Pasipiko ang nabubuhay sa maruming lugar. Walong daan at limampung milyon naman ang walang makuhanan ng malinis na inuming tubig habang pitong daan at walumpung milyon naman ang walang sariling palikuran. Habang pinag-uusapan ang kaunlaran ng mga bansa, nais ng ADB na maisama rin sa pag-unlad ang pagsasaayos ng mga palikuran, malinis na pamayanan at malinis na tubig para sa lahat.
examples.translation: Passage 2: In a recent ADB study, up to one billion seven hundred million people in Asia and the Pacific live in dirty places. Eight hundred fifty million have nowhere to get clean drinking water, while seven hundred eighty million have no toilet of their own. While the development of countries is being discussed, the ADB wants the improvement of toilets, clean communities and clean water for all to be included in development as well.

kakulangan ng palikuran sa pampublikong paaralan; kulang ang mga paaralan sa mga hugasan ng kamay.
Passage 2: phrases about public health concerns
1.7 billion people live in dirty places; 850 million have no clean drinking water; 780 million have no toilet of their own.
While they talk about the development of (member) countries, they also want to include in the discussion the provision of toilets, clean communities and clean (drinking) water.

explanations.title: Activity 10: a radio program, Katumbas ay Biyaya
explanations.body: Rey Sibayan, the anchor, discusses with Ms. Rhea Bagagunyo of the National Nutrition Council the issue of health and nutrition, in two segments (DZRH). The book prints ₱5,458.00; the spoken text writes it in words, and the dashes become commas. The two segments are run together.

examples.text: Sa panahon po ngayon, isa sa mabigat na problema talaga, Ms. Rhea, yung kakulangan sa pantustos sa pagkain ng maraming pamilya.
examples.translation: Rey: In these times, one of the heavy problems really, Ms. Rhea, is the lack of funds for food of many families.

examples.text: Sa katunayan, Rey, isa sa bawat sampung pamilya ay kulang ang kakayahan na bumili ng sapat at masustansiyang pagkain. Ang isang pamilya na may limang miyembro ay kailangan ng limang libo apat na raan at limampu’t walong piso kada buwan para matustusan ang kanilang pangangailangan sa pagkain lamang.
examples.translation: Rhea: In fact, Rey, one in every ten families lacks the ability to buy enough nutritious food. A family with five members needs five thousand four hundred fifty-eight pesos a month to meet its need for food alone.

examples.text: Katotohanan ho mga kaibigan. Narinig po ninyo, isa sa bawat sampu ang hindi sapat ang pambili ng sapat na pagkain. So ibig sabihin po nito, ay hindi po lahat ng pamilya ay may sapat na nutrisyon. Hindi po ba, Ms. Rhea?
examples.translation: Rey: That is the truth, friends. You heard it, one in every ten does not have enough to buy enough food. So this means that not all families have enough nutrition. Isn’t that so, Ms. Rhea?

examples.text: Sa katunayan, halos pito sa bawat sampung pamilya naman ay kulang ang kinakain nila para sa pangangailangan sa enerhiya o energy requirements.
examples.translation: Rhea: In fact, almost seven in every ten families do not eat enough for their energy requirements.

examples.text: Ay, yayay. Napabuntong hininga ako nito, e. So, Ms. Rhea, ano-ano po ba ang sanhi ng hindi pagkakaroon ng sapat na pagkain ang ilan sa mga pamilya?
examples.translation: Rey: Oh my. I sighed at this. So, Ms. Rhea, what are the causes of some families not having enough food?

examples.text: Maraming dahilan kung bakit lumalala ang problema sa kagutuman ng maraming Pilipino. Ilan sa mga ito ay kahirapan, ang mahihirap na pamilya ay walang lupa, kagamitan, o pera upang makabili ng pagkain dahil sa kakulangan ng kita sa trabaho o kawalan ng trabaho. Bukod dito ay ang pagkakaroon ng malaking pamilya, kung saan mas maraming miyembro ang mangangailangang maghati-hati sa pagkain. At siyempre, sa pagtaas ng presyo ng pagkain, na lubos na naaapektuhan ang mga pamilyang may maliit na panustos sa kanilang pang-araw-araw.
examples.translation: Rhea: There are many reasons why the problem of hunger among many Filipinos is getting worse. Some of these are poverty, poor families have no land, resources or money to buy food because of insufficient income from work or unemployment. Besides this is having a big family, where more members need to share the food. And of course, the rise in food prices, which greatly affects families with small provisions for their daily needs.

rows: 1. The serious problem Rey wanted to discuss
The shortage of funds to spend on food by many families.
One out of ten families lacks the ability to buy enough nutritious food. A family of five needs ₱5,458 per month for food only.
Since there is very little money to buy the required amount of food, not all families have the required nutrition (families go hungry).
Seven out of ten families do not meet the required energy food intake.
5. At least three reasons for the worsening hunger
(1) Poverty: poor families do not have land, resources or money to buy food; (2) insufficient income, unemployment, and a large family with more people to divide the food among; rising food prices.
(1) kakulangan, shortage; (2) katunayan, in fact; (3) kakayahan, ability; (4) katotohanan, reality (truth); (5) kagutuman, hunger; (6) kahirapan, poverty; (7) kagamitan, provisions (resources).

explanations.title: Activity 11: a news report about a health concern (the book’s script)
explanations.body: Listen to the excerpt and give the gist. The book’s script reads “dalawang milyon at anim na daang batang”; I give it as “dalawang milyon at anim na raang libong batang” to match 2.6 million.

examples.text: Ayon naman sa World Health Organization isa sa anim na bata ang under weight sa developing countries.
examples.translation: According to the World Health Organization, one in six children is underweight in developing countries.

examples.text: Kung kaya’t dalawang milyon at anim na raang libong batang may edad na lima pababa ang namamatay sabi ng UNICEF.
examples.translation: That is why two million six hundred thousand children aged five and below die, says UNICEF.

examples.text: Natatantya naman ng United States Agency for International Development ang isang bilyong tao sa iba’t-ibang parte ng mundo na natutulog ng gutom at dalawang daang milyon dito ay mga bata.
examples.translation: The United States Agency for International Development estimates one billion people in different parts of the world go to sleep hungry, and two hundred million of them are children.

examples.text: Mga kababayan, panahon na tayo ay magtipid sa pagkain at magtulungan, magbigayan upang malabanan ang gutom at maiwasan ang pagsasayang ng pagkain.
examples.translation: Countrymen, it is time for us to save food and help one another, to share with one another, to fight hunger and avoid wasting food.

explanations.title: Activity 11: the gist (the book’s key)
explanations.body: The World Health Organization reported that one in six children is underweight in developing countries. Hence 2.6 million children aged five and below die, according to UNICEF. USAID estimates that there are one billion people in different parts of the world who go to sleep hungry, and two hundred million of them are children. The report appealed to the countrymen not to waste food, to help each other and be generous with each other to fight hunger and avoid food waste.
