lessons.subtitle: Smokey Mountain sa Marikina · Hospital wastes · Kalinisan sagot sa dengue · Glossary

explanations.title: Activity 12: news briefs on health issues
explanations.body: Pair up; each pair reads a news brief, completes a chart with the health issue and recommendations, then shares it with other pairs and the group decides which issue concerns them most. Pair work, left out; the three briefs (excerpted from philstar.com) are given here. The book’s “10 metro” is written “sampung metro” and “100” is written “isandaang”.

explanations.title: Pair A: Smokey Mountain sa Marikina

examples.text: Sumulat sa akin si Ms. Anita Paway, pangulo ng Samahang Kapatiran ng Doña Petra ng Concepcion Uno, Marikina City.
examples.translation: Ms. Anita Paway wrote to me, president of the Samahang Kapatiran ng Doña Petra of Concepcion Uno, Marikina City.

examples.text: Ito ay kaugnay ng matagal nang reklamo ng kanilang organisasyon tungkol sa namumuong bundok ng basura dahil sa illegal dumping operation ng pamahalaang lungsod sa naturang lugar.
examples.translation: This is related to their organization’s long-standing complaint about a growing mountain of garbage because of the city government’s illegal dumping operation in that area.

examples.text: Umaabot na raw sa taas na sampung metro ang tambak ng basurang ito.
examples.translation: This pile of garbage is said to already reach ten meters in height.

examples.text: Sa patuloy at walang puknat na pagtatapon, hindi malayong maging bagong Smokey Mountain ang lugar na iyan.
examples.translation: With continuous and unending dumping, it is not far-fetched that the place will become a new Smokey Mountain.

examples.text: Bukod sa pangit tingnan, nanganganib pa ang kalusugan ng tao hindi lamang sa Marikina kundi sa ibang karatig na lugar dahil ito ay malapit sa baybayin ng ilog.
examples.translation: Besides being ugly to look at, people’s health is also in danger, not only in Marikina but in other neighboring places, because it is near the riverbank.

explanations.title: Pair B: DENR and DOH issue standards for managing hospital wastes
explanations.body: The book’s capitalised first word NILAGDAAN is written in normal case.

examples.text: Nilagdaan ni Secretary Francisco Duque ng Department of Health ang isang Joint Administrative Order na magsisilbing gabay sa mga pagamutan at klinika ukol sa ligtas na pamamahala at pagtatapon ng kanilang mga basura.
examples.translation: Secretary Francisco Duque of the Department of Health signed a Joint Administrative Order that will serve as a guide for hospitals and clinics on the safe management and disposal of their waste.

examples.text: Sinabi ng DOH na ang Pilipinas ay kasamang lumagda sa Bangkok Charter on the Global Conference for the Promotion of Health.
examples.translation: The DOH said the Philippines was among the signatories of the Bangkok Charter on the Global Conference for the Promotion of Health.

examples.text: Ang dokumentadong ito ay panawagan sa isandaang kalahok na bansa na magpatuloy sa magkaparehong layunin na mapabuti ang pamamahala at mga estratehiya ukol sa kalusugan sa pamamagitan ng wastong paghawak, pag-imbak, maayos na pakikitungo sa kalinisan at pagtatapon ng hospital wastes.
examples.translation: This document is a call to one hundred participating countries to continue the shared aim of improving health management and strategies through proper handling, storage, good dealings with sanitation and disposal of hospital wastes.

explanations.title: Pair C: Kalinisan sagot sa lamok na may dengue (QC Health)

examples.text: Niliwanag ng Quezon City health department na tanging ang kalinisan lamang sa kapaligiran ang tanging susi para hindi sumibol ang sakit na dengue sa alinmang lugar sa lungsod.
examples.translation: The Quezon City health department made it clear that cleanliness of the surroundings is the only key to keep dengue from breaking out anywhere in the city.

examples.text: Binigyang-diin ni Dra. Antonieta Enumerable, city health officer, na nasa tao rin naman kung magkaka-dengue sa isang lugar dahil kung marumi ang isang lugar, hindi lamang sakit na dengue ang maaaring umusbong kundi pati na rin ang iba pang uri ng sakit.
examples.translation: Dr. Antonieta Enumerable, city health officer, stressed that it is up to people whether a place gets dengue, because if a place is dirty, not only dengue may arise but other kinds of illness as well.

examples.text: Muling pinaalalahanan ni Enumerable ang publiko na ugaliing linisin ang mga daluyan ng tubig, iwasan ang mga de boteng plorera, alisin ang mga lata at mga bote na di na ginagamit, ipunan ng tubig sa ilalim ng refrigerator at sa ilalim ng lalagyan ng mga pinggan.
examples.translation: Enumerable again reminded the public to make it a habit to clean the water channels, avoid bottled vases, remove cans and bottles that are no longer used, and the water collected under the refrigerator and under the dish rack.

explanations.title: Activity 12: sample answers (my own)
explanations.body: Pair A: health issue, a growing mountain of garbage, about ten meters high, near a river; recommendations: stop the illegal dumping, move the garbage to a proper site. Pair B: health issue, unsafe disposal of hospital waste; recommendations: follow the Joint Administrative Order, train hospital staff in proper handling, storage and disposal. Pair C: health issue, dengue; recommendations: keep surroundings clean, clear water channels, remove cans and bottles, empty water under the refrigerator and dish rack.

explanations.title: Activity 13: role play in a Balikatan exercise
explanations.body: You are in a Balikatan training exercise in Barangay Liwayway, Nueva Ecija, tasked to talk to the barangay captain about prevalent health issues in the region. Ask him what these health issues are; what the barangay is doing, if anything, about them; what aid they receive from other regions, if any; and what specifically they need from you. The captain answers and asks questions of his own (role play, left out).

explanations.title: Ka-an/han/nan nouns: the book’s sample sentences
explanations.body: The book’s glossary of ka-an/han/nan nouns. The translations are mine. The book prints “nguinit” (nguni’t), puts a sentence about the youth under karapatan, and lists the root of kapaligiran as ligid.

examples.translation: The Department of Health issues the guidelines.

examples.translation: There was a disturbance because of contaminated water from the deep well.

examples.translation: A high number of hunger cases was recorded in the province of Samar.

examples.translation: Food makes up the greater part of the expenses of an ordinary Filipino family.

examples.translation: The safety of the community lies in the ability of each of its citizens to follow health policies.

examples.text: Mahalaga ang kalinisan nguni’t kailangan magtulungan ang lahat upang mapanatili ito.
examples.translation: Cleanliness is important, but everyone needs to help one another to maintain it.

examples.translation: Sometimes malnutrition is the cause of a high number of deaths.

examples.translation: Many were observed to have the widespread problems with the surroundings.

examples.translation: It is hard to have peace in the whole world.

examples.translation: Violence is frequent if people are irritable and their emotions are hot.

examples.text: Karamihan sa mga suliranin sa kapaligiran ay ang patuloy na pagtapon ng mga basura sa kalye.
examples.translation: Most of the problems in the environment are the continuous dumping of garbage in the street.

examples.text: Ang mga kabataan sa pamayanan ay ang pag-asa sa hinaharap.
examples.translation: The youth in the community are the hope of the future.

examples.text: Mabuting sundin ang mga karunungan mula sa ating mga nakakatanda.
examples.translation: It is good to follow the wisdom from our elders.

examples.text: Sa katunayan, bihira ang nagsasagawa ng operasyon ng katarata sa Pilipinas.
examples.translation: In fact, few perform cataract operations in the Philippines.

examples.text: Ang kawalan ng malinis na tubig ang naging sanhi nang madalas na pagtatae sa bayan ng San Roque.
examples.translation: The lack of clean water was the cause of the frequent diarrhea in the town of San Roque.

explanations.title: Self-evaluation
explanations.body: Recall the objectives at the beginning of this lesson and mark Yes or No. The book’s self-check covers the whole chapter: extract information from reading and listening passages about food and nutrition; describe governmental programs on combatting malnutrition; transcribe and translate numbers and sentences about food and nutrition; create a story collaboratively; describe steps in preparing meals; extract information about mental and physical fitness; identify activities that promote physical and mental health; translate phrases and sentences about fitness; recommend or offer advice on fitness and nutrition; extract information about health concerns and issues; transcribe numbers and sentences about health concerns and issues; describe health issues and recommend measures; and ask and answer simple questions about health issues. Features to check: object-focus i verbs, reservational phrases, ma-an verbs and ka-an/han/nan noun formations. If you answer No, review the section, find a study partner, or tell your academic counselor or team leader.
